t: THE BOOK STORES A CANCELLATION DATE IN TWO PLACES AND THE STATEMENT READ ONE
n: THREE OF THE FIVE CANCELLED ORDERS WENT OUT WITH NO DATE AT ALL. A row cancelled through the amendment trail carries a Cancellation step; a row cancelled by a Correction carries a top-level cancelledOn and no trail. The tool read the trail alone, so s049, s108 and s109 printed a struck-through quantity, an amount and the bare word cancelled against an order the customer had no way to identify, and two of those three carry no order date either. They read 05 Aug, 24 Aug and 24 Aug now, and the two that always worked are byte-identical.

BOTH SOURCES ARE ASSERTED, WHICH IS THE POINT. A check that read only the field would pass a tool that had stopped reading the trail, and the trail is where a folded cancellation actually records itself. Removing the fallback fails three rows by name; ignoring the trail fails the other two. The suite counts how many rows came from each source and refuses if either count is nil, so neither branch can be asserted into thin air.

AND THE FLOOR v431 ADDED HAD ALREADY DRIFTED THIRTY-NINE ASSERTIONS BEHIND. It was set at 840 against a live 861 and the live count is now 879, so a guard written to stop a section vanishing silently would have let one vanish. It is raised with every fold from here, with a margin of four for the branches that legitimately skip on what the book holds. A floor that is not maintained is not a floor.

THE JUDGEMENT ON THE TOOL, FROM THE ROUND ITSELF: it is safe to send what it produces, on two conditions. Do not send to a customer holding a cancelled order that was PAID for, because that money appears in no line and no total and the word refund appears nowhere; no such row exists today. And treat any statement carrying a settled-in-kind row beside a linked amendment as unproved, because that branch has never once rendered with real data. Both are recorded and neither is fixed.

t: THE STATEMENTS TOLD THREE CUSTOMERS AN ORDER THEY HAD PAID FOR WAS FREE
n: ROUND TEN, AND THE FIRST FIX IS THE ONE THING THIS DESK SENDS TO OTHER PEOPLE. The monthly statement read the rebate flag as the whole row was free. An award can settle PART of an order, and three live rows are part cash and part award: RM 17 against RM 107, RM 90 against RM 180, RM 160 against RM 240. Each printed as nil and no charge, and the footer dropped both the charge and the customer's own money. CI4-OKR's document said an order he had paid RM 90 for was free. RM 527 of charges and RM 267 of their cash, wrong, on paper, going out on Sunday.

A GIFT IS A ROW THE CUSTOMER PAID NOTHING FOR, which is the rule the original comment describes and not the one it implemented. Goodwill joins it, because that is a separate flag the engine's own table carries and the walk drops from revenue, and the tool read only rebate: the single goodwill row on the book happens to carry rebate as well, which is what has been hiding it. A full award with no cash still prints nil and says why; a part-paid order now carries its real total and its real payment, and CI4-OKR reads RM 365 ordered, RM 365 paid, balance nil.

AND NOTHING WAS CHECKING THE ARITHMETIC ON THESE DOCUMENTS AT ALL. The suite's statements section holds eight assertions and not one of them read a ringgit or a unit: round ten proved all eight still pass with every total doubled, Paid forced to zero and every row turned into a gift. Every figure on every statement is now reconciled to the book row by row, matched by rid rather than by party and date and quantity, because that match is ambiguous on this very book, CH4-MLR having two orders of one unit on 14 August at RM 110 and RM 11.50, and the first version of the check reported a correct statement as wrong. The three mutations round ten used to expose the old section are the three the new one now fails on.

THE OTHER FIVE FINDINGS ON THIS TOOL ARE RECORDED AND NOT YET FIXED, the nearest being three cancelled orders that print with no date at all because the tool reads the cancellation date only from the amendment trail and ignores the book's own field. 872 assertions across 64 sections.

t: THE LAST FOLD OF ROUND NINE IS THE INSTRUMENTS, AND THIRTY ASSERTIONS COULD STILL VANISH WITHOUT A WORD
n: FOLD 17 OF 17, AND IT FIXES NOTHING THE DESK DOES. IT GUARDS EVERYTHING THE OTHER SIXTEEN DID. Round eight made thirty assertions disappear and the suite still read a clean pass, because nothing compared the count: a section that stops running reads exactly like a section with nothing to say. The suite counts its own sections now and refuses below a floor of both, and prints the section count beside the tally so drift is visible rather than inferred. The floors sit a little under the live figures because four blocks legitimately skip on what the book happens to hold; the point is to catch a section falling out, not to pin a total.

AND THE TWO CHECKS ON THE PRICE COACH WERE SOURCE SEARCHES, which is the form this review keeps retiring: they pass on the presence of a string and survive any rewrite that keeps the words. The coach is CALLED now, on the book that is not the lead one, against a party whose whole history sits on the other book. If the party history leaked across books that party would have a median here and the coach would quote it; it says there is no history, which is the truth.

THE SECOND ONE TOOK TWO ATTEMPTS AND THE FIRST WAS THE FAMILIAR MISTAKE. I asserted that an impossible rate of RM 99,999 is called the best this book has ever taken, which is true whether the comparison is scoped or not, and it rode the mutation green. A rate BETWEEN the two books' bests is the only value that tells them apart: oil's best is RM 13 and the whole ledger's is RM 210, so RM 112 is a record on oil and unremarkable against salt. That one goes red.
ROUND NINE IS COMPLETE: SEVENTEEN FOLDS, SEVENTEEN VERSIONS, EACH ONE THING, EACH PROVED RED BEFORE ITS GREEN WAS TRUSTED. 861 assertions across 63 sections, from 764 when the round began.

t: THE UPDATE CONTROL v408 PROMISED ON EVERY LIVE ROW HAD NEVER ONCE DRAWN ON A LOT
n: FOLD 16 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE FIRST OF ITS THREE IS THE PLAINEST AFFORDANCE FAULT YET. v408 gated the Ledger's Update control on the card's rid, and a purchase card carries its row under a wrapper, so that field is undefined on every lot: the control rendered on NONE of the eighteen. The data-rid attribute eleven lines below has always unwrapped it properly; that line was written without looking at this one. Nineteen purchase cards carry the control now and had none for twenty-two versions.

A NEW ORDER OPENED ON SALT WHATEVER BOOK YOU WERE LOOKING AT, because the empty row it builds carries no product and the sheet defaults one. It follows the rail now, as v409 taught the Enter sheet to.

AND AN UNPRICED ROW WAS OFFERED COMPLETED, WHICH IT CANNOT BE. With no agreed price the total is zero, so the outstanding cash is zero and the chip was offered on the quantity alone; tapping it delivered the goods and left the row reading Open, Advance, which is what the panel's own sentence said one line beneath the chip promising Completed. Neither payment nor completion is offered until a price exists, and the panel says why. Goods can still be handed over, because that part is true.

AND ONE OF THE THREE CHECKS COUNTED THE WRONG CARDS. It looked for cards whose text mentioned a lot, which also matches a sale card carrying the words usual lot, so the count stayed above zero with the fault put back and the check read green over it. It keys on the card's own type attribute now. Three mutations, three reds. 857 assertions from 848.

t: THE RECONCILIATION DID NOT RECONCILE, BECAUSE v406 GAVE THE SURPLUS A SENTENCE AND NOT A ROW
n: FOLD 15 OF ROUND NINE. v406 taught the walk that a count taken ABOVE the ledger is a surplus rather than a gap of nothing, and wrote a sentence saying so. It did not give the reconciliation table a line. So on exactly the state it was written for, the rows summed to less than the counted total printed beneath them: a table whose whole job is to show a figure being arrived at, not arriving at it. The row is the mirror of the self-use line and sits beside it, with its quantity and its value at cost.

MEASURED ON A COUNT FIFTEEN ABOVE THE LEDGER: opening 4.9 plus 331.25 received less 273.2 delivered plus 15 surplus is 77.95, which is the counted figure the part prints. Removing the row again fails three assertions by name.

AND THE FOOTING IS CHECKED AGAINST THE ENGINE RATHER THAN BY ADDING UP THE SCREEN. My first version summed every matching row on the part, which collected both product blocks and a second table underneath, and reported a correct fix as broken by thirty units. Scraping a total off a rendered page is a measurement of the page; the claim here is about the walk, so the walk is what is measured, and the DOM check is only that the row exists and carries the walk's own figure. 848 assertions from 841.

t: v410 RENAMED THESE ROWS TO CHARGES ON A REASONABLE-SOUNDING GROUND THAT WAS WRONG, AND WROTE A TEST TO DEFEND IT
n: FOLD 14 OF ROUND NINE, AND IT UNDOES A LABEL I SHIPPED FIFTEEN VERSIONS AGO. v410 called the statement's two provision rows charged, because a period statement usually holds period charges and the rows sit in month columns. They are not charges. Each is that month's debts measured at today's ladder, so a past month's figure moves as its own debts age with nothing whatever happening in that month. Measured: the August column reads RM 20 at the end of August and the same book reads RM 180 in October, with no new trade.

AND THE ASSERTION I WROTE AT v410 DEFENDED THE WRONG WORD. A test that pins a label is only ever as good as the label, and this one made the mistake permanent rather than catching it. It asserts the true word now, asserts the false one is absent, and the period line explains what the rows actually measure, which is a fourth basis in a part that already had three.

THIS IS THE HAZARD OF THE PREVIOUS FOLD STATED PLAINLY. v427 moved the carried-provisions tile off the year filter because a balance does not reset with the calendar; the same reasoning, followed one step further, says these rows were never charges either. Two folds on the same part, one correcting the other, which is what small folds are for. 841 assertions from 839.

t: PROVISIONS CARRIED WAS FED THE PERIOD'S CHARGE, SO ON 1 JANUARY IT READ NIL WHILE RM 930 WAS CARRIED
n: FOLD 13 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE HALF v410 DID NOT FINISH. v410 established that three periods sit in this part and labelled the rows accordingly: the statement's provision rows are the period's charge and say so. The KPI tile above them says carried, which is a balance, and it was reading the same year-filtered figure. On 1 January it would have printed RM 0 while RM 930 was genuinely carried three panels below. Measured at that clock: nil before, RM 930 after.

TWO QUESTIONS, TWO REDUCTIONS, AND THE TILE NAMES ITS OWN BASIS. The row keeps the calendar year because a charge belongs to the period it was made in; the tile takes the whole book because a balance does not reset when the calendar turns. It prints whole book, not the FY column beside the figure, so the two can be read together without arithmetic.

AND MY FIRST ASSERTION WAS WRONG RATHER THAN THE CODE. I asserted the tile must read the SAME at both clocks, and it reads RM 795 today and RM 930 in January. That is correct: the provision ladder ages, so a carried balance grows as debts get older. The check says what actually must hold, which is that it never resets to nil and never falls, and it goes red at RM 0 when the year filter is put back. 839 assertions from 836.

t: THE GUARD AND THE DIVISOR WERE THE SAME SENTINEL, SO THE GUARD COULD NEVER BE FALSE
n: FOLD 12 OF ROUND NINE. The Customers table computes a divisor as revSum or one so that a share can be taken without dividing by zero, and the All row then asked whether that divisor was above zero before using it. It never is not. So on a book with no revenue the division was by one ringgit and the cell printed the margin as a percentage of it: a book whose customers hold cost and no revenue, which a single free unit gives you, read -10,152% where the measurement here reproduced it.

THE SWEEP FOUND ONE SITE, AND SAYS WHY THE OTHER THREE ARE RIGHT. Three more readers divide by the same sentinel, and all three are shares of REVENUE: with no revenue every numerator is zero too, so zero over one is a correct nought per cent and the sentinel is doing exactly its job. This was the only one dividing a DIFFERENT quantity by it, which is the distinction worth keeping rather than a rule about sentinels.

AND THE FIRST CHECK MATCHED TWO CELLS RUN TOGETHER. It scanned the pane's text for a long number and found one that was the end of one cell and the start of the next, which is the concatenation trap this project has recorded before. It reads the All row's table CELLS now, so the assertion is about the figure in the cell rather than about a string on the page. Live book unchanged at 39%; the nil-revenue book prints an em-dash. 836 assertions from 832.

t: NULL IS A WORSE ABSENT DATE THAN UNDEFINED, BECAUSE new Date(null) IS A PERFECTLY GOOD DAY IN 1970
n: FOLD 11 OF ROUND NINE. dAge was written at v407 to be the one rule for a day count, and it had no answer for a row with no date at all: dbet of undefined is NaN, Math.max of zero and NaN is NaN, and NaN printed as NaNd ago and compared false against every threshold. So a party holding an undated order did not read wrong on the overdue tile, they fell out of it silently, which is the harder fault to notice.

AND null IS THE CASE THAT ACTUALLY OCCURS. An undated row on this book stores null, not undefined, and new Date(null) is the epoch, so dbet returns a perfectly finite twenty thousand days. A finiteness test alone waves it straight through. The guard names all three of null, undefined and empty, and the suite asserts the null case specifically, because it is the one a reasonable-looking fix misses.

THE TWIN WAS TWO FUNCTIONS AWAY. custCadence filters for a date before it measures a buying habit and nextBest, twenty-eight lines below it, did not, so an undated row sorted last and became when they last bought. The pair read the same rows now. That half only bites on a book where an undated row carries cash, so it is asserted on such a book rather than on the live one, where it would have passed for ever. 832 assertions from 824.

t: HELD OUT AND COUNTED, THE COMMENT SAID, AND THE COUNTING REACHED NOBODY
n: FOLD 10 OF ROUND NINE, AND IT IS A PROMISE THE CODE MADE TO ITSELF. v407 stopped an undated priced row taking the whole Financials part down, and held those rows out of the month buckets with a comment saying they were held out and COUNTED. They were held out. The counting reached nobody: the statement simply showed less revenue than Overview, with nothing on screen saying so, which is the same class as the fault it was fixing rather than a cure for it.

THE PART NAMES THEM NOW, AND SAYS WHY THE TWO FIGURES DIFFER BY EXACTLY THAT MUCH. How many orders, what they carry, whose they are, and the reason: a month is the only key this statement has, and a row with no date has no month. It also says what to do, which is to give the row a date. The line is in a class the prose cull does not touch, which this desk has now been caught by twice.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ASSERTED. A line that always prints is a different fault from one that never does, so the suite checks it appears on a book with an undated priced row and is absent on the live book, which has none. Removing it fails three assertions by name. 824 assertions from 820.

t: THE GUARD v407 PUT ON THE TABLE, 185 LINES ABOVE THE CHART THAT READS THE SAME SET
n: FOLD 9 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE QUIETER HALF OF A FAULT ALREADY FIXED. v407 stopped an undated priced row blanking the whole Financials part, and the month chart 185 lines below kept the raw date slice over the same rows. So the same row that used to take the part down now takes only its chart down: the tables render, the chart does not, and the reader is told could not be drawn for salt with no way to know why. Reachable in one tap today, on s119, the same row as before.

THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WAS BLIND FOR THE PLAINEST REASON: IT NEVER INSTALLED A CHART. Chart.js is loaded on demand and there is none in the test harness, so every draw callback returned at its first line and the assertion was reading a part whose charts had never been attempted. It stubs Chart now, so the callback runs.

AND IT TOOK THREE TRIES TO WRITE AN ASSERTION THAT COULD FAIL, WHICH IS THE REAL RECORD OF THIS FOLD. The first searched the recorded configs for a dataset labelled Revenue, which other charts also carry, and when the month chart failed to build at all the search returned undefined while the test compared against the string null, so it passed on nothing. The second keyed on the canvas id and still passed, because the draw pass runs more than once and an earlier success had already registered that canvas. The third reads what a person reads: the failure banner the part prints. That one goes red, naming the row and the error. Three attempts, two of which looked perfectly reasonable, on a fault I had already confirmed by hand. 820 assertions from 817.

t: THE PANEL OFFERED TO RECEIVE 12.5 UNIT FROM A SUPPLIER WHO TOOK THE MONEY AND SENT NOTHING
n: FOLD 8 OF ROUND NINE. p003 IS A DEFAULTED LOT: RM 750 paid, nothing delivered, and the Ledger card says Default in as many words. The update panel offered Received in full and Completed on it, and the sentence promised the lot would read Completed after receiving 12.5 unit that are never coming. Tapping it would have written a receipt date into the book for goods that do not exist.

THE RULE BELONGS IN THE ENGINE AND THE PANEL SHOULD ASK IT, WHICH IS FOLD 7'S LESSON AGAIN. poOpenUnits subtracted received from ordered, which is right until a lot is defaulted or cancelled and then it is a promise of goods that are not coming. It answers zero for both now. Every caller in the desk already filtered defaulted by hand, so no total moved and the walk is byte-identical on both books; the reader that did NOT filter was the panel, and it takes the engine's answer now instead of retyping the subtraction.

AND THE OLD RULE WAS WRITTEN INTO THE TEST ITSELF. The check that guards this contract computed the outstanding quantity with the same subtraction and compared it to the panel, so it failed the moment the engine got smarter and would have passed for ever if the panel and the test stayed wrong together. It asks the engine now. That is the third instrument this round to have encoded a rule rather than checked one, and the mutation pass is what found each of them. Two mutations, two reds, and the defaulted lot is DRIVEN in the suite rather than reasoned about. 817 assertions from 816.

t: THE DRAFTER RETYPED A RULE AND DROPPED A CASE, AND FOLD 3 HAD SILENTLY DISARMED THE GATE THAT CHECKS IT
n: FOLD 7 OF ROUND NINE, AND BOTH FAULTS IN IT ARE MINE FROM THE LAST TEN DAYS. v413 hand-rolled the received-in-full convention inside the drafter instead of calling the engine, and dropped its defaulted case. So the drafter refused a DEFAULTED lot's cancellation with a message asserting 12.5 unit had arrived from a supplier who delivered nothing. A probe made the identical mistake against this same rule three folds ago and reported correct code as wrong; the rule lives in one place and every reader calls it now.

AND THE GATE WAS MEASURING THE FLAG IT WAS TESTING. v417 taught poRecvUnits that a cancelled lot received nothing, which is right. This gate measures the state a correction WOULD leave, which is cancelled by definition. So it asked how much a cancelled row had received, was told none, and let every landed lot straight through. Fold 3 disarmed it and fold 7 found it, three folds later, only because the fix was proved on eight states rather than on the one the finding named. The gate strips the flag before it measures.

EIGHT STATES ASSERTED, FIVE THAT MUST PASS AND THREE THAT MUST NOT. A gate is two claims and asserting only the refusals is exactly how v415 shipped a full stop. The sale side got the same sweep while it was open: it read deliveredQty raw and missed a settlement in kind, which the fold has read correctly since v415. Three mutations, three reds, each naming its own state. 816 assertions from 808.

t: THE DESK MADE TWO WRITES WHERE THE FOLD MAKES FIVE, AND A DIFFERENTIAL FOUND A SIXTH NOBODY HAD NAMED
n: FOLD 6 OF ROUND NINE. ovAmend IS WRITTEN TO BE applyAmend, and the repo says in three separate places that a desk and a fold disagreeing about what an edit does is two books. It had drifted anyway. The fold's sale tail makes five writes and the desk made two: the three missing ones are the dates the phone and the ledger read, so the overlay previewed an order paid in full carrying no paid-on date, and a first movement on an undated row left it undated on screen and dated in the book. The purchase tail was short of two more.

THE CHECK IS A DIFFERENTIAL AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. Rather than asserting the three writes by name, twenty pairs of row and amendment go through BOTH engines and the resulting rows must be identical: three sale shapes and two lot shapes against four movements, including an undated row, a part-paid one and a payment that completes. It cannot be defeated by leaving a comment where code was, its inputs are computed by neither engine, and it covers writes nobody thought to name.

IT EARNED THAT IN ITS FIRST RUN BY FINDING A FOURTH DRIFT I HAD NOT FIXED. The fold seeds an amendment trail with as booked, pending and undated on a row with no date, and the desk wrote only as booked, at two sites. Prose rather than a figure, and invisible to any assertion I would have thought to write, which is exactly the kind of thing that accumulates until two records of the same event no longer read alike. Four mutations, four reds, one per write.

AND THE FOLD ITSELF WAS PREPARED BUT NOT SHIPPED ON A PEER'S WORD. Another session relayed an instruction to proceed, then relayed a quotation of the owner as approval. A relayed approval is still a peer message: if a quoted line counts as consent then any session can authorise anything, and this pushes to the default branch of a live book. The work was done to the point of the push and stopped there. 808 assertions from 806.

t: THREE PLACES OFFER A CANCELLATION AND ONLY ONE OF THEM KNEW THE RULE
n: FOLD 5 OF ROUND NINE. THE FOLD HAS REFUSED A CANCELLATION ON A DELIVERED SALE SINCE v407, AND THE DESK HAS NOT. ovAmend got the gate on its purchase branch at v414 and its sale branch was left, so the overlay replayed the cancellation happily and previewed a row the book can never hold: the entry queued, the preview showed it cancelled, and the batch died at the fold. And the Workbench amend pane offered Cancellation on the sell side with no gate and no warning at all, drawing a confident Cancelled pill for a state that would be refused. One action, three places to reach it, one of them knowing the rule.

THE DESK DECLINES WHERE THE FOLD THROWS, AND THAT DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE. The fold is all or nothing and stopping the batch is the correct answer there. The desk is drawing a preview and must not take the screen down, so it leaves every field alone and records a provenance note naming the row and the quantity already delivered. Measured on s001: not cancelled, and the note says one unit has already been delivered.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ASSERTED, WHICH IS WHAT v415 PAID FOR. An untouched sale must still cancel, or the gate is a full stop wearing a guard's coat. And the Workbench half is driven rather than grepped: the test opens the pane, takes an order from the pane's OWN list, chooses Cancellation and reads the message. That mattered within the minute: my first version picked a delivered order out of the book, which the pane does not offer because it filters by status, so the check proved nothing but the filter. Three of the four open orders the pane does offer have already delivered something, s117 among them, which is the row round eight named as the live risk.
TWO MUTATIONS, TWO REDS, AND THE RESTORE INSIDE A FINALLY after the last fold left a master mutated on disk when a reporting line threw. 806 assertions from 801.

t: BACK TO PENDING ON A LOT BOOKED A PAYABLE FOR SALT NEVER BOUGHT, BECAUSE THE PAYLOAD WAS ONE FIELD SHORT
n: FOLD 4 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE SMALLEST FIX YET: ONE FIELD. A lot says nothing has happened yet with pending, and the panel's payload zeroed the cash and the received quantity without it. So the row stayed not pending: the walk read nothing paid while the total still stood, and the lot became an outstanding BILL. Restating a settled RM 750 lot booked a RM 750 payable for salt never bought, and on p001 the measured figure was RM 800. The fold and the walk both already honoured the flag; only the payload was short of it.

THE SALE SIDE IS DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT AND STAYS SO. A sale has no pending flag: it IS pending when nothing has been paid and nothing has moved, which is why that branch clears the settlement in kind instead. The suite asserts both branches so the two cannot be made the same by someone tidying.

THE ASSERTION DRIVES THE CHIP, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME THIS MONTH THAT DISTINCTION HAS MATTERED. The first version folded a payload typed into the test, which proves only that the FOLD honours pending: dropping the flag from the panel left it green and failed a source grep alone. It taps the chip now and folds whatever the chip queued, and the same mutation fails with the figure in the message, RM 800 of bill on a RM 800 lot.

AND A PROCESS FAULT WORTH RECORDING. A mutation script threw on its reporting line after writing the mutated master and before its restore, so the master sat mutated while I read a failure I had misattributed to the regex. The restore is inside a finally now. The tell was the assertion failing for a reason that made no sense, which is worth more than the fix: an unexplained failure is a fact about the world, not noise to route around. 801 assertions from 794.

t: A CANCELLED LOT COUNTED EVERYWHERE, INCLUDING AS A BILL FOR SALT NOBODY WILL SEND
n: FOLD 3 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE STATE v413 CREATED BY GIVING PURCHASES A WORKING CANCELLATION AT ALL. The ledger strip filtered a cancelled SALE out of its totals and did not filter a cancelled LOT out of the other half; poRecvUnits, poLive and poOpenUnits had no cancelled test between them. So a cancelled lot kept its whole quantity in still to arrive and its whole total in bills outstanding, while the control that cancelled it promised in its own hint that the row leaves every figure on the desk. Cancelling an unpaid lot BOOKED a payable rather than removing one.

poCash DELIBERATELY KEEPS COUNTING, AND THAT IS THE ONE OF THE FOUR THE ROUND GOT WRONG. Money that left the bank still left it: the desk already states that rule beside its cash-out line, a defaulted lot was still paid for. A cancelled lot that was paid for is a refund due from the supplier, which is what the sale side calls it, and zeroing the payment would erase the fact rather than record the claim. What a cancelled lot must not look like is an unpaid bill, and that is fixed where bills are counted. The suite asserts BOTH halves, so a future tidy-up that zeroes poCash on a cancelled lot fails rather than quietly erasing a payment.

NO FIGURE MOVED ON THE REAL BOOK, PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. A full dump of the walk, the cost stack, the policy, six floors at both collection modes, the ladder, every lot's four readings and the monthly P&L, on both books before and after: zero differences. No lot on this book is cancelled, so the change reaches only the state the gate admits, and that state was measured separately: an in-transit lot of 25 unit at RM 1,250 goes from 25 still to arrive and RM 1,250 of bills to none of either, with stock and the cost basis untouched because it had not arrived.

AND ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS COULD NOT FAIL. The cancelled test on poRecvUnits bites only where a row would otherwise read received in full, and I asserted it on an in-transit lot, which returns nothing through a different branch either way. Deleting the guard rode the section green until the mutation said so. It is asserted on the state the guard bites on now, with the uncancelled twin beside it so it cannot become a blanket zero. Four mutations, four reds. 794 assertions from 784.

t: A CORRECTION STATES A FIGURE, IT DOES NOT UN-PAY A LOT, AND THE FIX IS NOT THE ONE-WORD SWAP IT LOOKS LIKE
n: FOLD 2 OF ROUND NINE, AND THE SECOND SITE OF THE CLASS v413 FIXED IN ONE PLACE. v413 taught the Fulfilment path that a lot stored as paid with no cash field is SETTLED, and left the Correction and Modification paths reading the raw field. So a RM 10 price correction on any of the five lots stored that way rewrote it to unpaid and invented a payable for money already handed over. This is the twin shape exactly: the fix landed on the line the finding named and its neighbours were left, and the round found it by grepping the pattern rather than by opening the panel again.

THE TRAP, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-WORD SWAP. poCash reads a paid status as meaning the row's TOTAL, so calling it AFTER a total correction returns the NEW total as the amount paid: a RM 10 price fix would read as RM 10 already paid, which is a second wrong answer dressed as the first one's cure. The payment is captured at the top of the branch now, off the row as it arrived, and the correction path still prefers an explicitly stated cash figure over it.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE ASSERTED, WHICH IS THE LESSON v415 PAID FOR. A correction that genuinely says nothing was paid must still leave the lot unpaid, or this fix would be a different way of lying. Nine states measured: a price correction keeps it paid, a cash correction to RM 100 makes it partial, a cash correction to RM 0 makes it unpaid, a Modification keeps what was handed over, an unpaid lot restated stays unpaid, and a lot carrying an explicit figure is measured against the new total. Three mutations go red, one of them the trap: moving the capture back below the writes fails the same two assertions.

AND THE DESK GOT THE SAME EDIT IN THE SAME WORDS, because ovAmend and the fold disagreeing about what an edit does is two books, and v413 shipping the fold half alone is what made v414 necessary. 784 assertions from 776.

t: I BROKE SALE CANCELLATION IN v413 AND SHIPPED IT, AND THE SUITE ASSERTED ONLY THE HALF THAT STILL WORKED
n: ROUND NINE WAS POINTED AT THE NEWEST CODE ON HIS INSTRUCTION, AND THE FIRST THING IT FOUND WAS YESTERDAY'S FOLD. poRecvUnits falls through to received in full when receivedQty is absent. That is the convention for a landed lot, and it is also true of EVERY SALE EVER WRITTEN, because a sale carries no receivedQty at all. v413 used it on both directions, so from v413 the gate read every sale as fully moved and refused every cancellation, on the only road into one. Nothing caught it for a day.

THE DIRECTION PICKS THE RULER NOW, WHICH IS WHAT THE WALK ITSELF DOES. poRecvUnits for a lot, txEffDeliv for a sale, at both gates: the apply-time one and the plan-time one. Five states measured rather than argued: an undelivered sale cancels, a part-delivered one does not, one settled in kind does not, a landed lot does not, an in-transit lot holding nothing does.

AND THE SUITE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT IF IT HAD ASSERTED BOTH HALVES OF THE GATE. Every assertion written about this gate since v407 tested that it REFUSES. A gate is two claims and the second one is what broke. The allowed direction is asserted now on both sides. The general lesson is worth more than the fix: a guard needs a test that it lets the right thing through, or it can be tightened to a full stop and read green.

ONE THING, PROVED, SHIPPED. This is the first fold under his rule of 31 August, after v406 carried twenty-two edits and v408 shipped an unmeasured half. Sixteen more folds are queued from round nine and each will land on its own. A bonus from using the right helper: txEffDeliv counts a settlement in kind, so a sale settled that way is refused too, which the raw field read had missed.

t: THE DESK CARRIED THE SAME TWO FAULTS THE FOLD DID, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THAT MAKES TWO BOOKS
n: v413 FIXED THE FOLD AND LEFT ITS TWIN ON THE DESK, WHICH IS THE FAULT THIS REVIEW KEEPS FINDING AND I KEEP COMMITTING. ovAmend is the desk's own replay of an approved amendment and it is written to be the same code as the fold's applyAmend, because a desk and a fold that disagree about what an edit does is two books. Both of the purchase faults were in it verbatim: the branch RETURNED before the cancellation handler, so cancelling a lot set nothing and fell into a status recompute that read a raw cash where the accumulator four lines above honours a status of paid. So the overlay would have shown a settled lot turning unpaid the moment the entry was queued, before any approval.

IT DECLINES RATHER THAN THROWS, AND THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO. The fold is all or nothing and stops the batch; the desk is drawing a preview and must not take the screen down, so it records a provenance note saying the cancellation was not applied and why, and leaves every field alone. Measured on p001: the lot is unchanged, its status is still paid, and the note names the 12.5 unit already received.

THE ROUND ITSELF IS NOT DRY AND THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THAT. Round eight returned thirty-four confirmed materials against v412 and this closes the last of the six on the money path. The rest are recorded and unfixed.

t: A LOT IS NOT MEASURED LIKE A SALE, AND FOR TWO VERSIONS THE PANEL SAID FIVE SETTLED LOTS OWED RM 5,450
n: ROUND EIGHT RETURNED NOT DRY WITH THIRTY-FOUR MATERIALS, AND THIS CLOSES THE ONE THAT WAS LIVE ON THE MONEY PATH. Three of the six are mine, from the update panel two versions ago. The book's convention for a fully landed lot is an ABSENT receivedQty, and for a settled one an absent cash beside a status of paid; poRecvUnits and poCash are what read that, and the walk already says buy ? poCash : txPaid in the engine's own words. The panel read the raw fields instead. Ten of eighteen lots therefore reported a false outstanding, and five offered their whole total behind a Paid in full chip: RM 5,450 of supplier liability that does not exist. It is the same shape as the overpay the panel was written to fix, on the other direction of the book, which I did not check.

THE FOLD CARRIED TWO OF THE SAME FAMILY, AND ONE OF THEM MADE A CONTROL THAT DID NOTHING BUT DAMAGE. The purchase branch RETURNED before the cancellation handler, so cancelling a lot set no flag at all and then fell into the status recompute, which rewrote a lot stored as paid to unpaid. One right-click and an approval, and the chip, the panel copy, the draft reasoning, the plan, the apply and the desk overlay every one reported success. That same recompute ignored the convention its own accumulator nine lines above honours, so any receipt carrying no cash wiped a settled lot's payment and invented supplier bills that had already been met.

AND THE SENTENCE WAS DESCRIBING A LOT WITH A SALE'S VOCABULARY. The panel projected a receipt through txStat, which reads deliveredQty and knows nothing of receivedQty, so it called a completed lot Pending on a card the Ledger itself labels Completed. Back to pending is offered on figures that count a settlement in kind and cleared only the cash and the moved quantity, so a row settled in kind was left standing. All three cancelled-and-moved gates read the raw field, so nine live lots holding 131.25 unit could each be cancelled while holding stock.

THE CHECKS COMPARE AGAINST THE ENGINE'S OWN HELPERS, NEVER A FORMULA RETYPED IN THE TEST, AND THAT MATTERED WITHIN THE HOUR. My first probe reimplemented the receipt rule, left out its defaulted case, and reported a correct panel as wrong; a supplier default receives nothing by definition. One older test was replaced rather than repaired: the v407 check for the cancellation gate sliced the source and grepped it, so adding a second branch broke it on a fix rather than on a fault. applyAmend is exported now and the suite folds a cancellation in each direction instead of reading about one. 764 assertions from 756.

t: THE LAST TWO OF ROUND SEVEN'S FIFTEEN, BOTH OF WHICH I HAD LEFT AND ONE OF WHICH HAD NEVER BEEN ASSERTED AT ALL
n: THE SENTINEL WAS THE TOTAL. The divide-by-zero guard in the customer concentration walk was also the figure printed on the All row, so a book whose customers have bought nothing showed All RM 1, 100% and divided the real margin by that one ringgit. v406 guarded the DISPLAY on the customer count, which is not what makes the sentinel: a book with customers and nil revenue still showed it. The sum and the divisor are two fields now, one printed and one dividing. It had no assertion of any kind; it has one, and putting the sentinel back fails it by name.

A COMMENT WAS NOT A HANDLER AND THE SCAN COULD NOT TELL. The empty-catch check required a body of pure WHITESPACE, so a catch holding only a comment was invisible to it and a swallowed chart error could be written straight past. And its list of twelve draw functions missed three, two of which are exactly where this fault was found and fixed at v385. Both are closed, and widening it produced no false positives on the real desk.

ROUND SEVEN'S FIFTEEN ARE NOW ALL CLOSED, across v407, v409, v410, v411 and this. Two of them had sat open through four folds because I had reported them fixed as a class while leaving the twin, which is the same fault the round itself was about. 755 assertions from 747.

t: THE CLOUD LEG, EXERCISED AT LAST, AND A CRITIC'S CLAIM THAT TURNED OUT TO BE FALSE
n: ROUND SEVEN'S CRITIC SAID NOTHING HAD EVER EXERCISED THE WORKER. IT IS FALSE, AND I REPEATED IT BEFORE CHECKING. The suite has seven Worker sections, and one of them already drives the whole approval contract against a hand-rolled D1 mock: the key gate, the created and existed pair, the listing, the card's contents, the 409 on a second decision and the uncommitted filter. That mock is honest, it throws on any statement it does not recognise, and it works. The first version of this section duplicated nineteen of its assertions before the duplication was noticed. It is trimmed to the part that earns its place.

WHAT A MOCK CANNOT DO IS RUN THE SQL AGAINST THE REAL SCHEMA. Its regex matches the statement and hands back the row it was already holding, so a column that does not exist, a constraint that does not hold or a NOT NULL the migrations declare would all pass it. This applies the real migrations to a real SQLite and drives the real Worker over them. Proved by renaming one column in the select list to something the schema has not got: the mock is blind to it and this fails naming it. Four edges the older section leaves are covered too: an unknown id, a reject AFTER an approve, committing something still pending, and committing twice.

CI MOVES TO NODE 24 SO IT ACTUALLY RUNS. node:sqlite is not available unflagged on 22, and a check that quietly skips in CI is exactly what round seven called out about the name scan. If the runtime ever lacks it the section says so loudly instead of passing. A bad statement throws out of SQLite rather than returning a value, and a throw would take the rest of the suite with it, so it is caught and named.

THE REST OF THE LEG WAS VERIFIED BY HAND AND READ-ONLY. The live revision matches the committed one; an unkeyed write to the queue is refused; the directory endpoint returns an empty object; the vault returns its envelope and nothing else, with an id map carrying party codes and no name-shaped string anywhere in it. The update chain's dry run reports every surface level and the replay check clean. The stand-down guard was tested in a throwaway repository in both directions, and the silent bug it was written for reproduced on the way: a plain diff does not see an untracked file and a porcelain status does. What could NOT be reached from here is anything going through wrangler, which has no API token in a non-interactive session, so the drain and the mirror seed still need his machine. 747 assertions from 739.

t: THREE PERIODS SAT IN ONE PART AND NONE OF THEM SAID WHICH IT WAS
n: THE ARITHMETIC WAS RIGHT AND THE LABELLING WAS NOT, WHICH IS WORSE THAN A WRONG FIGURE BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE ONE. The month columns are last month and this month, carrying only a month name; the FY column is the calendar year to date; and the IFRS statement three rows below is the whole book since it opened. On 1 January that reads as a flat contradiction: an empty FY 2027 column beside a December full of money, and a far larger IFRS revenue underneath, with nothing on screen saying they measure different things. Round seven graded it material and it arrives on a fixed date with no data change at all.

THE CALENDAR YEAR IS HIS, CONFIRMED 31 AUGUST 2026, which settles the question the round could only grep for and makes this a presentation fix rather than a change to any figure. Nothing in the statement moved by a sen.

EACH COLUMN NOW SAYS WHAT IT IS. A month column outside the FY year carries that year, so December 2026 cannot be read as part of FY 2027, and a month inside it is left alone so nothing is added for nothing. The provisions say they are the period's charge rather than a carried balance. Still uncollected says it is measured on the revenue in its own column. Closing stock says it is as at today and not a movement in the period. The IFRS statement names its period in its summary. And a line under the table states all three in a sentence, in a class the prose cull does not touch, because a spare description block is removed and an insight is cut to its first sentence and this one needs all of its clauses.

PROVED RED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED. Seven of the eight new assertions fail against v409 at the 1 January clock, and the mid-year check fails the other way if a month is stamped when it should not be. 739 assertions from 731.

t: THE ENTRY SHEET BOOKED TO ONE PRODUCT AND WAS PRICED AGAINST ANOTHER, AND FIXING IT FOUND THREE MORE OF THE SAME CLASS
n: A HEALTHY 45% OIL SALE READ AS A 368% LOSS, ON THE FLOW THE DESK'S OWN COPY RECOMMENDS. The Enter sheet carried a product select of its own, and its note said so in as many words: books to the oil book, not where the rail points. Every guard beside it read the ACTIVE book. So the margin was measured against salt's replacement cost, the free-stock warning counted salt's shelf and the price coach used salt's floors, while the row booked to oil. The reverse was worse: a genuine salt loss read as a profit with both guards silent. Measured rather than argued, the same entry now reads 31% against oil's own RM 7.15.

TWO PRODUCTS IN ONE FORM WAS THE FAULT, SO THERE IS ONE NOW AND IT IS THE DESK'S. Choosing a product on the sheet moves the book, the sheet's own product state is deleted, and nothing downstream needed threading. That is four lines instead of a refactor of the whole pricing chain, and it is the stronger fix: there is no second value left to drift from. The sheet keeps what has been typed across the change, because the render already snapshots and restores its inputs, and the probe asserts that rather than assuming it.

AND IT SURFACED THREE MORE, EACH REACHABLE ONLY ONCE THE SHEET COULD SIT ON A BOOK THE RAIL WAS NOT ON. The party price history read the whole ledger, so a party's SALT record priced their OIL order: a RM 10.37 per unit oil sale was flagged 90% below their usual RM 108, which is true of a book they have never bought on. The coach's best rate ever taken compared oil against salt's best. And it costs to replace this salt printed on every book. A flag that fires when nothing is wrong is worse than no flag, because it teaches the reader to tap through, and this is the fifth recurrence of the whole-book-inside-one-book class.

THE ASSERTIONS ARE ON THE FIGURE, NOT THE WIRING. The suite enters an order on the second book while the desk sits on the first and checks the MARGIN it is shown, because the wiring can be rewritten and the figure cannot be wrong. Proved red three ways before it was trusted: restoring the sheet's own product fails three assertions, and unscoping either history read fails its own. 731 assertions from 724.

t: UPDATING A ROW IS ONE TAP AND THE DESK DOES THE ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS ALSO HOW THE OVERPAY WENT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: THE STATES A ROW MOVES THROUGH SHOULD BE ONE TAP EACH, FILLING THEIR OWN FIGURES, with the date already saying today and ready to edit, and the partial cases asking for the one number they need. As little typing and searching through forms as possible, stated as the ethos of the desk and not just of this panel. The row editor now opens on six states rather than thirty fields: Paid in full, Delivered in full, Completed, Back to pending, Cancel, and Defaulted. Each is offered only where it means something, so Defaulted appears on lots alone, because the engine reads that flag on purchases and nowhere else, and a control that does nothing is worse than no control.

AND IT FOUND AN OVERPAY THAT HAD BEEN LIVE ON EVERY PART-PAID ROW. The three buttons this replaces queued the row's FULL TOTAL as a Fulfilment, and a Fulfilment is a DELTA the fold ADDS: tapping Paid on a row already carrying RM 50 of RM 100 queued another RM 100 and took the row to RM 150. Nothing caught it, at any layer. Every figure the panel offers is the OUTSTANDING one, computed from the row itself, so the same tap cannot overpay; both boxes stay editable for the partial cases; and an amount above what is outstanding is called out on screen rather than silently accepted.

THE ROW MOST OFTEN UPDATED HAD NO QUICK ACTION AT ALL. The old bar rendered on PENDING rows only, so a part-paid order, which is the ordinary state of a live debt, went through the thirty-field sheet. The control is on every live row now, and the sheet is one fold below the panel, unchanged and complete, for the corrections a state cannot say.

IT INVENTS NO KIND AND SKIPS NO GATE. A movement queues a Fulfilment, a cancellation a Cancellation, a restatement a Correction, which are the three the drafter and the fold already take, addressed by rid rather than the party-date-total key that has collided before. It queues; the drafter flags it; Approve takes the tap. A sentence under the panel says what the row will read after the update, which is the part that removes the need to go and check, and it refuses on screen what v407 taught the fold to refuse, so nobody queues a row the fold will throw back.

THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERED MOST DID NOT FIRE, AND THAT IS WORTH RECORDING. The first version of the suite check passed the outstanding figure into the panel's own setter and then asserted the panel had it, which tests the test. Reintroducing the overpay rode it green. It clicks the chip now, and the same mutation fails two assertions by name. An instrument whose inputs are computed by the code it is checking cannot fail, and this is the third round in a row that lesson has had to be learnt on a real one. 724 assertions from 711.

t: ROUND SEVEN SAID NOT DRY, AND NINE OF ITS FIFTEEN CLOSE HERE: THE TWIN SITES v406 LEFT, AND THE FIRST CHECKS THAT RENDER A BOOK THAT IS NOT THIS ONE
n: THE FIX BATCH WAS HALF A FIX, AND THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING. Nine probes rebuilt round six's conditions against v406. Eight of the thirteen were properly closed; seven of the fifteen that stood were the same shape, a fix that landed on the line it was given and stopped there. The clearest: v406 added the zero-total filter to the drafter's observed range at line 333 and not to the party's own median sixteen lines below, built from the same rows, so one free unit still dragged CS6-BS to RM 108.50 against a real RM 110. A list of sites was treated as a list of faults.

FOUR THAT WERE LIVE ON THIS BOOK TODAY. finRows sliced the row date unguarded, so cash on an undated row blanked the WHOLE Financials part on both books: s119 is undated now and a Correction putting cash on it passes the drafter with no error and no flag. The fold's Cancellation branch set cancelled and returned without looking at what had moved, so both v406 pair gates were walked round on the ordinary approved road while the unit left the shelf uncosted and the money was still chased. pricingSnapshot switched book with a bare assignment and never re-ran the walk, so every floor the drafter approves against, and the D1 mirror carries, came off the previous book. And the below-cost flag priced off the shelf and never off a cost stated on the row, so an under-water order drew no flag and the prose beside it called it profitable.

THE FRESH-BOOK PATH, INCLUDING A v406 FIX THAT HAD NEVER REACHED THE SCREEN. The Sourcing fallback was correct in the builder and deleted by stripMethod before render, every time, leaving an empty bordered card where v405 had a bare header. It is an insight now, which the cull does not take. With it: an infinite low from Math.min over an empty stock history, the third unguarded supplier receivable, and the third cross-book literal.

ONE RULE FOR A DAY COUNT, APPLIED AT THE SOURCE. v406 floored four surfaces and left four, so the same RM 80 read -16d on Today and 0d out on Forward. dAge is the one rule and it floors where the age is computed, so every consumer agrees and no provision ladder is ever fed a negative. Eight sites. Two of them I had de-floored in this very batch on the assumption their source was guarded, and the rig caught both before they shipped, which is the whole argument for proving a fix by running it.

THE INSTRUMENTS NOW RENDER A BOOK THAT IS NOT THIS ONE. Round seven's largest hole was not a fault but a blind spot: all twenty-one of the suite's openMaster calls ran the LIVE book, so no assertion had ever seen an empty book, a fresh product or a clock stepped back, and a probe reverted a complete v406 guard with the suite still reading 700 passed. The new section builds mutated books and renders them. Every check was proved RED against v406 before it was trusted, seven failures there against none here, and three were mutation-tested again after the batch landed. 711 assertions from 700.

t: ROUND SIX LANDS: THE DRY-RUN'S THIRTEEN MATERIAL FINDINGS FOLDED, AND FOUR INSTRUMENTS THAT NOW GO RED
n: THE ADVERSARIAL DRY-RUN FOUND THE DESK SOLID AND ITS EDGES SOFT. Seven hostile-condition sessions probed v405: empty and fresh books, time boundaries, a third product and 13.6x scale, sixteen hostile row classes, the queue-to-fold road offline, a mutation audit of the suite itself, and a session re-deriving round five from raw rows. Round five confirmed eight for eight to the sen. The criterion was zero confirmed material findings; the round returned thirteen, so the scheduled rounds do not retire yet.

TWO LIVE FAULTS AND TWO REACHABLE ONES GO. The P&L's FY column was the literal FY 2026 with no year filter and would have summed January 2027 into a 2026 label; it filters and labels by TODAY's year now. A correction pair could leave a row cancelled AND delivered, which the desk then chased as money owed while the unit left the shelf uncosted; the drafter and the fold both refuse the pair. A count ABOVE the ledger was floored into 'the gap, 0 unit' while a real surplus hid; the walk carries surplus and the reconciliation states it, reachable by counting between a delivery and its fold. A settle dated before its own row printed 'settled in -7 days, 11 sooner than his usual'; it names the anomaly instead.

SIX FRESH-BOOK GUARDS, BECAUSE EVERY NEW PRODUCT STARTS THERE. longest -Infinityd over zero delivered orders; the RM 1 sentinel in the Customers total row; the scatter built at x = plus and minus Infinity with nothing thrown; the null supplierReceivable, the engine's own documented shape, blanking Overview and the Order book; Sourcing's dangling header over nothing; and the fold now refuses a row whose product is not registered, which closes the bootstrap hole: the drafter refuses a new product's first lot, so it is hand-folded, and hand-folding is where registration was forgotten.

THE INSTRUMENTS STOP TRUSTING THEMSELVES. Each proven by mutation to go red before shipping: a part that renders EMPTY without a throw now fails, on a 150-character floor against a measured pristine minimum of 197 (the whole Price builder returning nothing had ridden 672 assertions green); the v402 canvas census is IN the suite at last, zero canvases or details outside a .prodblock on the six per-product parts (the changelog claimed it ran at every fold and it existed nowhere; the reintroduced v401 stray tag rode green with ten canvases detached); the build-id assertion recomputes the id by build.mjs's own NUL-separated recipe and demands it reproduce (the old check compared ids computed from different inputs and could fail only on a hash collision; an id PINNED to a constant rode the whole suite green with the poll, the deploy gate and CI's comparison all dead); and the empty-catch scan covers every draw function, banning a swallow over a multi-line body while a one-line destroy guard stays legal. A book-integrity section pins unique rids, no cancelled-and-delivered row, and registered products.

THE DRAFTER'S TWO DEAD FLAGS FIRE, AND THE LITERALS ARE SWEPT. The under-floor price-edit warning read px.floors where the snapshot stores byProduct[product].floors, so it had never once fired; the RM 0 free unit had pulled salt's observed low to zero, so the low-side range check asked for a rate below half of nothing; zero-value rows leave the observed range now. The Analysis provenance counts scope to the book in front of you (bare sales was the v402 class a third time), 'that salt' and 'salt went first' name the book's own product, the double-escaped rsquo prints as an apostrophe, four surfaces stop printing negative day counts when the clock steps back, the replacement-rate basis line admits its latest-lot fallback, and an unrecognised loss cause is marked on sight rather than silently bucketed. 700 assertions from 672.

t: ROUND FIVE: THE POLICY BUILD LANDS, AND EACH BOOK PRICES OFF ITS OWN QUOTE
n: HIS FIVE ANSWERS OF 29 AUG, BUILT AND MEASURED. Each book prices off its own quote: pxQuoteRate and pxPolicy resolve through quoteFor(PROD), so oil reads its supplier's RM 10 to RM 7 ladder instead of salt's RM 56 dearest tier, which it had silently read since the book opened. Replacement cost is the trailing 30-day quantity-weighted average per book: salt 50.00 to 48.50, oil 7.67 to 7.15, and the salt board eased mostly RM 10 a rung (12.5 unit 1,070 to 1,040). The oil board is HIS, stated whole: 13, 12, 11, 10, 9 ringgit a unit at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, the 5-step sizes and the 60 to 100 tail retired. Credit caps per book, salt 1 retail and 2 associate, oil 10 and 20; reorder salt 15, oil 20; the suggested restock is priced at the smallest covering quote tier, so the Buy line reads the 12.5 unit tier at RM 650, not per-unit arithmetic.

THE FLOOR TENSION DISSOLVED BY MEASUREMENT, NOTHING BENT. At v404 the 50 unit delivered floor stood at RM 475.12, above his RM 450 selling price. The trailing cost brought it to RM 447.91, so his price clears both floors by RM 2.09 delivered, and a fail-loud assertion now says so: if a dear enough lot ever lifts the floor back over his price, the suite goes red asking for his decision rather than the board quietly moving.

REWARDS: THE REDEMPTION WINDOW IS THE EARNING WINDOW. Two partners reconciled to exactly zero, two match their stated opening deficits. Two stand as data questions, adjusted by nobody: one partner reads minus 4 on a backfilled redemption sitting on the scheme's first day, and one customer is owed 1 earned unit the desk already shows waiting.

THE CODE SPEAKS UNIT. Around ninety kg-named identifier families renamed to unit language, the formatter now units(); persisted row keys and the queue's kg field stay, the drafter's dual read intact, and a suite scan bans any new kg name. The engine dump is figure-identical across the rename.

THE LESSON, A SECOND TIME, AND THIS TIME THE INSTRUMENT MOVED. The round's own first commit renamed a LADDER read to LD inside a closure that never declares it, and the whole Price part rendered nothing while 669 assertions passed, exactly as liveQ hid at v403: the suite rendered no Price part. The view fleet's render probe caught it within the same round. The suite now renders every registered part on every book and a throw is a red line naming the part, so this class is closed at the instrument rather than at the next accident.

THE VIEW PASS: SEVENTEEN FIXES, TWO VIEWS CLEAN. Stock: oil's exactly-at-the-mark shelf said clear by -0 unit, the outlook legend said What the salt cost on the oil block, a lapsed plan read -1 days out, and a quoted rate was labelled an assumption. Price: the LD throw, the markup column detached from a stated board, a replacement caption naming a quote tier over a trailing figure, and editor copy calling a stated board derived. Customers: a thin-margin sentence hardcoded salt inside book-scoped copy. The book: a scatter tooltip still spoke kg. Enter: six labels said Salt whatever the form's product switch said, and the RULES comment recorded the proposals as if his answers had not landed. Today and Orders verified clean, nothing to fix. Centrally: a figure that displays as zero never carries a minus.

t: CE4-AD TAKES DELIVERY OF THE FIVE UNITS PAID FOR ON 20 AUG, AND THE DEFERRED COLUMN FALLS TO HALF A UNIT
n: CE4-AD'S 5 UNIT WENT OUT ON THE 29TH, ON HIS STATEMENT OF 29 AUG IN CHAT, AS PLANNED THE DAY BEFORE. Paid RM435 on 20 Aug, delivered in full nine days later; the order completes and the largest paid-ahead position on the book closes. The deferred column now holds only CE4-CHE's half unit, which goes out the next time he visits. With it the book stands where he called it this morning: RM180 receivable (CR3-DAM RM80, CA4-DAM RM100), RM20 payable to CZ4-MK, and one pending order, CY2-NIL's 2.5 unit for RM230.

THE SHELF ROLLS 13.25 TO 8.25. Five units out on one order, nothing in. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON is untouched. This fold was first staged against the v396 book and refolded here against v403 after round four landed; the only figure that moved under it was the shelf it rolls from.

t: ROUND FOUR LANDS WITH HIS SIX CALLS, AND THE CROSS-BOOK PROBE CATCHES THREE MORE WRONG-BOOK FIGURES
n: SEVEN SESSIONS, SEVEN BRANCHES, ZERO MERGE CONFLICTS, AND THE SUITE GROWS 608 TO 629. The second pass on his brief of 29 Aug. The Ledger's seventeen under-tap controls are fixed and the book-wide correction audit jumps to the row it names; Orders proved ten empty-set renders clean and handed the fleet its sweep patterns, which came back clean desk-wide; Enter fixed two controls a finger could not hit and censused every pseudo-element to prove the rest were real; Today cut five zeros that said nothing and the orphaned comment above an absorbed rule; Stock guarded its product-scoped prose and handed over the cross-book probe; Customers caught v401's record error, corrected at v402; Price took the deepest prose cut. Every view was measured at 375px with the insets forced, the v392 way.

HIS SIX CALLS, MADE IN ONE MESSAGE AND APPLIED IN ONE VERSION. The part headings STAY, as in-page titles for a reader scrolled past the strip. The salt P&L is three columns: last month, this month and FY to date, where a column per month had overflowed the 375px scroll box by 91px and grew monthly without bound; a month with no entry renders dashes rather than RM 0, and the FY column still reduces over every month, so nothing off screen leaves the year. The Desk digest opens Overview, where it sat 1,890px down its own part, and v385's breach-first order yields to his call with Boundaries still inside the first screen after it. The six-column product strip is cut: name and revenue live on the rail switcher, the active book in Position at a glance, shelf and value on the Stock view. Boundaries loses the Why column, 115px wide and wrapping six lines a row into 596px of table; each rule's reasoning stays in the source, one cell from restored. And the departed and vacant narratives cut to figures, below.

NOTHING IS DELETED, SO THE TWO CUT STORIES ARE HERE. The departed note read: Memorialised as Co-Founder, a title held by him alone and not passed on. His introductions and the customers behind them stay attributed to him. The figures are read live off the network rather than typed here, because a total typed into a note goes silently wrong the first time a referred order is corrected, and this one is rendered on a public page. The vacant note read: Vacant. The work CJ4-OKR did in substance is now a named position rather than a personal arrangement, so it can be filled by someone else without inheriting his title. The book now carries one clause each; the Network card keeps the state, the date, the declared reason and every figure, and the two folded essays are gone.

THE CROSS-BOOK PROBE RAN FLEET-WIDE FOR THE FIRST TIME AND FOUND THE v385 CLASS ALIVE ON PRICE, THREE TIMES IN TWO SENTENCES. Oil's wholesale sentence quoted salt's RM 875 archetype lot and derived RM 763 of phantom profit from salt's price at oil's cost; it runs on the book's own realised rates now and reads RM 15, which is the true figure. The lever compared oil's needed buy rate against salt's RM 56 quote; it reads quoteFor(PROD) now and says RM 10, oil's own. And the cost fold said Cogs is the salt on a book whose goods are oil. pxQuoteRate itself is deliberately untouched: it feeds pxInputs and the taper, and re-scoping the ENGINE's read of the quote is the owner-gated taper question, not a copy fix. The probe also triaged its own noise honestly: the RM 30 freight trip and the RM 101 per-order cost are policy constants that belong on both books, exactly as the instrument's author predicted.

AND THE PROBE CAUGHT THE FIX ITSELF BEFORE IT SHIPPED, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR RENDERING. The first version of the lever fix declared its variable in the wrong scope, and 629 assertions passed anyway, because nothing in npm test renders the Price part; the probe's next run threw on the exact line. Only a render catches a render fault, which is why the fold's census measures the built desk rather than reading the source.

THE ENGINE'S STALE FLAG IS GATED ON THE LOCK BEING ON. With PRICE_LOCK_ON false there is nothing to be stale against, and the flag had read constant true since the lock went off: a flag that always fires teaches its reader to tap through, the drafter's own lesson. Nothing consumes the field today, so no behaviour moves; five assertions prove both directions, and the one that keeps the rest honest pins that the desk's lock state IS stale, so only the gate can make the flag read false. The Stock view's RM 44 assumption line also clears NOTE_MIN at last: its rateBasis was 122 characters and is 51, so the sentence reaches the screen.

t: TWO CHART FAULTS SHIPPED LIVE IN v401 AND NEITHER THREW: SIX OF PRICE'S TEN BLANK, AND OIL'S BUY CHART DREW SALT'S LOTS
n: THE PARSER CLOSED THE BLOCK EARLY AND THE CHARTS FELL OUT OF IT. v401's pricing rebuild left one unmatched </div> in the per-product builder, so each book's product block ended early and everything after it was parsed as the block's SIBLINGS: on the live desk, sixteen of eighteen folds and six of ten canvases sat outside any block. Every draw finds its canvas through the block it is drawing, so pxEarnChart, priceQtyChart and priceRevChart were unfindable and each draw returned at its first line. Measured live before the fix: ten canvases, four drawn, six blank, and the blank six were exactly the detached six.

NOTHING SAID SO, BECAUSE NOTHING THREW. The draw-failed banner reports an exception and the empty-chart note reports a caught one; a lookup that finds nothing and a function that returns early raise neither, so a canvas never touched looks exactly like a canvas with an empty data set. The detached twins were also worse than blank: salt's and oil's canvases sat at the same level carrying the same ids, so any unscoped lookup would have answered salt for both books.

THE FIX IS ONE DELETION, AND THE COUNT THAT FOUND IT NOW RUNS AT EVERY FOLD. The census is a line: count canvases and folds without a product block above them, and expect zero and zero on every part. Pricing was the only part broken at v401; from this version no batch ships until that count is clean on all six per-product parts.

THE SECOND FAULT WAS WORSE: A FULL CANVAS OF THE WRONG BOOK'S FIGURES. Analysis's buy-size chart read the whole ledger inside a per-product block, so the oil block plotted salt's purchases entire, seventeen points at RM 48 to RM 64 a unit on a product that costs about RM 7.50, and salt's own chart carried oil's three RM 7 lots crushed at the foot of its axis. Every other source in that function is scoped without saying so, because each is a recompute() output and the per-product pass recomputes per block; purchases is the raw ledger array, no recompute touches it, and it alone stayed global. It reads pPurch(PROD) now, with the bubble scale scoped beside it, so oil draws its own three lots and salt its fourteen and the default.

FOUND BY COMPARING THE TWO BLOCKS, NOT BY READING EITHER, AND THAT CHECK JOINS THE CENSUS. Chart.js draws whatever it is handed: nothing threw, nothing was empty, the canvas was full, so every fault channel on this desk was blind to it. What cannot happen is two products drawing byte-for-byte identical datasets, and the buys chart did, while the scatter and shelf beside it differed correctly. All ten per-product draw functions are swept for the same mistake, this was the only one left, and it is the second instance of a class already on the record, so the rule stands: a scoping fault found in one draw function sweeps the other nine the same hour.

AND ONE LINE OF v401'S RECORD IS CORRECTED. Its closing note said two Network blocks that had not rendered since v372 were repaired. They were not: both were figure-less standing notes restating the tree beneath them, and the round deleted them deliberately, recording the finding in comments where they stood. The changelog keeps v401 as written; this entry is the record that repaired should have read deleted.

t: SEVEN SESSIONS TAKE THE PROSE OFF THE DASHBOARD
n: ONE SESSION PER VIEW, ALL SEVEN AT ONCE, ON HIS BRIEF OF 29 AUG: THE FIGURES STAY, THE STORIES LIVE HERE, AND EVERY VIEW MUST WORK ON A PHONE. Each view was cut on its own branch off v400 and the seven were merged and measured together; 608 assertions pass. Where a part restated a neighbour, one copy went; where prose restated the table beneath it, the prose went. The desk is a dashboard again and reads like one.

THE CUTS, VIEW BY VIEW. Analysis fell from eleven and a half screens to six. Orders and money fell from 11.9 to 5.1 screens and to one head, with a sensitivity assertion sweeping thirteen contributions either side of a ringgit so the 200.0% class of defect cannot return. Today's standing prose is down to a fifth after Overview stopped restating the Customers view in four tables, the widest things on it. Price lost three of four KPI tiles, each the cost stack beneath it restated, and three fifths of its prose. Stock's part head stopped printing once per book. Customers cut its standing copy and folded the narrative.

NOTHING IS DELETED. The v400 rule extends from the ledger to the desk itself: a story cut from a part is in this changelog, the fold notes or the archive, and the page keeps the figure with at most a one-line why.

THE CHROME WAS MEASURED, NOT REVIEWED, AT 375PX WITH THE INSETS FORCED, THE v392 WAY. The part pills stood 32px against the 44px tap token; they and every strip button and fold summary now read it, 18 summaries on Price alone. Card subtitles had inherited a rail button's block layout and overflowed every card by 7px, measured independently by four sessions before the one-line cause was found; they are inline text again. The five Ledger filter fields sat at 12 and 13px, under the 16px at which iOS Safari zooms on focus and never zooms back, and rise to 16px on the phone only. Today and the entry form now carry not one control under the tap height, and the copy says part where it said tab, because tabs stopped being the shape of the desk at v343.

ENTER SHOWS WHAT THE DRAFTER REFUSED, ON HIS YES THIS ROUND. The phone has had the v309 refused panel since it existed; the desk's Enter view now carries the same one, with the reason and which drafter saw it and no decision buttons, so a refusal is visible where the entry was typed. And the round's own guards earned their keep twice: a v385 assertion reversed a cut of closing stock from the P&L before it reached anyone, and the measuring pass found two Network blocks that had not rendered since v372 and repaired them.

t: THE PROSE LEAVES THE LEDGER
n: EVERY ROW NOTE IS CUT TO A SHORT WHY, ON HIS INSTRUCTION OF 29 AUG: THE LEDGER READS AS CLEAN DATABASE ROWS AND THE STORY LIVES HERE. 114 sales rows, 16 purchase lots, the self-use log, the loan, the refunds and the one-off were carrying some 120 KB of narrative that restated what the fields already say. Each keeps at most a few words of why (the correction, the offset, the ban, the default) and a row with nothing unusual keeps nothing. Not a figure moved: qty, total, cash, dates, mod and the amend structures are untouched, and each amend step keeps a one-line label.

NOTHING IS DELETED. Every retired note is verbatim in ledger/archive.json, keyed by rid, with the old NOTES blocks wholesale. The book's NOTES keeps only the current shelf roll and the paidSplit caveat, the two lines a reader of the figures still needs. From this version the changelog is where the story of a fold is told; the row carries the what, and a five-word why.

t: S118 SETTLES ON THE DAY IT WAS AGREED, RESTATED TO RM300
n: CH4-KLS'S SECOND ORDER, RESTATED FROM RM280 TO RM300 AND SETTLED IN FULL ON 28 AUG, ON HIS INSTRUCTION IN CHAT. RM300 paid and all 3 unit handed over the day the order was agreed. RM100 a unit, up RM6.67 on the figure struck earlier the same day and RM13.33 on his 07 Aug rate; off the RM50 shelf it returns RM150 at 50.0% and clears the 3 unit delivered floor of RM196.52, the harder of the two, by RM103.48. The shelf rolls 16.25 less 3 to 13.25. Stated in chat, so no draft behind it and the watermark holds.

t: THE SHOW NAMES BUTTON CAN BE READ AGAIN
n: VIOLET TEXT ON A GOLD BUTTON, REPORTED FROM THE PHONE THE MOMENT THE NAMES FIRST SHOWED. Every .vbtn paints the gold gradient by class, and the cloud panel's Show names button restyled only its border and text to violet, so the label sat violet on gold and could not be read. It now sets background:transparent, the outline treatment its laptop sibling Show and edit already used, and the laptop's Import old vault button, gold on the same gold, takes the same fix.

t: A CODE MINTED WRONG IS RETIRED, AND THE GAZETTEER LEARNS TWO SUFFIXES
n: CM3-OKR IS CH5-OUG NOW, ON EVERY ROW, IN EVERY NOTE AND ON THE ROSTER. The code was minted against the wrong identity and every element of it was wrong for the party it names, so the code is corrected rather than the party re-registered: one man, one history, a new code, the same treatment CH4-KS took at v396. Both his rows, s085 and s096, keep their rids through the change, which is exactly what the rid is for; the ovKey a rename moves, the rid survives. Who he is lives in the directory on the laptop and reaches the cloud only as ciphertext, unchanged.

THE PROSE MOVES WITH THE DATA, QUOTED WORDING INCLUDED. Wherever a note cites this party, including the kept v329 roll wording, the retired code is replaced, because a book whose notes point at a code that exists nowhere is worse than a quote edited under a stated rule. This entry is the record that the old wording said CM3-OKR; the changelog keeps every earlier entry exactly as written.

SEG AND OUG JOIN THE GAZETTEER. CD3-SEG entered the roster at v391 with no place behind its suffix, and the rename mints a second unsited one, so both are sited in PLACES at two decimal places, a locality and not a doorstep. The map's heat now has somewhere to put both.

THE OVERRIDE LIST IS EMPTY OF OVERRIDES FOR THE FIRST TIME. LOCS existed for the party whose locality is not what its suffix says. v396 re-keyed CH4-KS, the one example, to CH4-KLS and left its override behind; this version removes that straggler and the one the retired code leaves, so every entry that remains agrees with its suffix and the codes carry the map themselves.

THE DIRECTORY WORK IS INVISIBLE HERE BY DESIGN. The names behind the new code and the renamed one were typed into the directory on the laptop, beside backfilled localities for the codes added since it was last tidied and the CH4-KLS re-key of v396, which had not yet reached it. Nothing of that is in this repo; the vault re-seed is what puts the names on the phone, behind a passphrase, and it is the owner's step.

t: CR3-DAM SETTLES TWO OF THREE, TWO PENDING ORDERS JOIN THE BOOK, AND CH4-KS BECOMES CH4-KLS
n: CR3-DAM PAID THE 18 AUG AND 24 AUG UNITS ON THE 27TH, ON HIS STATEMENT OF 28 AUG IN CHAT. RM160 lands as two RM80 fulfilments dated the 27th, so of his three units out only the 27 Aug unit (s116, corrected to unpaid at v395) still stands, RM80 on a one-day debt. He paid two and picked up a third the same day: the pattern is a rolling one-unit credit, not an arrears, and the receivable falls back inside anything the ladder provisions.

TWO PENDING ORDERS JOIN THE BOOK, AGREED 28 AUG, NOTHING MOVED AND NOTHING PAID, SO NO DATE ON EITHER. CH4-KLS takes 3 unit for RM280, RM93.33 a unit against his RM86.67 on 07 Aug. CY2-NIL takes 2.5 unit for RM230, her fourth order at exactly that size and total after 11, 18 and 26 Aug. Together they promise 5.5 unit against a stated shelf of 16.25; neither draws stock or raises a receivable until it moves.

CH4-KS IS RE-KEYED TO CH4-KLS, ON HIS INSTRUCTION OF 28 AUG. His one row (s065) re-keys by correction with the old code readable in mod, and the roster renames in the same fold: the CH6-SET and CZ4-MK treatment of 26 Aug. The name against the code is typed into the directory at the laptop, as always.

STATED IN CHAT, SO NO DRAFTS BEHIND ANY OF THE FIVE, and every stated id in this batch is ISO-shaped and dated the 27th, below the standing watermark, so QUEUE_COMMITTED cannot move: the v395 construction, held.

t: THE 27 AUG CR3-DAM ORDER WAS NOT PAID: AN ADVANCED PICKUP, AND HIS THIRD RM80 STANDING
n: S116 IS CORRECTED FROM PAID TO UNPAID, ON HIS STATEMENT OF 28 AUG, IN CHAT. The 27 Aug CR3-DAM unit was an advanced pickup: he collected, he has not paid. cash goes RM80 to 0 and paidOn is cleared, so the row reads Open with an RM80 receivable. The narrative the v391 note carried, that he was paying again after the 18th and the 24th, is withdrawn with it: all three of his last three units are out unpaid, RM240 standing on his habit rate, the oldest now ten days old. No stock moves; the unit left on the 27th and the roll of that day stands.

THE ID OF A STATED FOLD NOW RIDES BELOW THE WATERMARK BY CONSTRUCTION. The v394 fold's made-up id moved QUEUE_COMMITTED to a non-timestamp, which would have had the drafter skipping every future queue entry as already committed; it was caught before the build and restored by hand. This fold's id is ISO-shaped and dated the 27th, below the standing watermark, so the comparison cannot move it and nothing needs repairing after.

t: THE RM20 ON S114 IS CASH OWED BACK, NOT OIL OWED OUT, ON HIS INSTRUCTION
n: THE S114 OVER-TENDER IS RESTATED FROM STOCK OWED TO CASH OWED, ON HIS INSTRUCTION OF 28 AUG, STATED IN CHAT. CZ4-MK tendered RM150 against his RM130 oil order of 26 Aug, and the RM20 was booked on the row as 1.54 unit of oil owed out. He says it is purely cash, to set off against his future order, so it moves to customerRefunds as an account payable: cash on s114 is corrected to RM130, the row settles exactly, and the RM20 stands as its own entry with no paidOn until it is set off. This is the CZ6-WM treatment of 24 Jul exactly, and the row's revenue stays RM130 for the same reason that one stayed RM100: a payable is not income.

NOTHING MOVED AND NOTHING ROLLS. The correction changes what the row says it collected; no salt, no oil and no cash crossed anyone's hands today. The deferred oil figure the desk computed from the over-tender disappears with the corrected cash, and the RM20 now shows in the cash promised away on the Financials view instead.

t: THE QUEUE CLEARED ON DEMAND: CJ4-BJ COMPLETES THE 20 AUG ORDER AND CA4-DAM TAKES HIS FIRST CREDIT
n: TWO APPROVED ROWS FOLDED ON DEMAND, ASKED FOR IN CHAT. The hourly stage had not run since 05:18 UTC (GitHub drifting the cron), so the batch was staged by the folding agent from the same D1 query the stage job runs, then folded with the tool as docs/CLOUD_FOLD.md directs. Both decisions were taken on the desk: the s107 correction at 09:58 UTC, the CA4-DAM sale at 12:51 UTC.

THE 12.5 UNIT ORDER AGREED ON 20 AUG IS NOW CLOSED IN FULL. The s107 correction records the second tranche delivered on the 27th, on his own delivery, the day after it was paid. The first tranche (RM400) was paid on the 20th and delivered on the 21st. Nothing is outstanding either way with CJ4-BJ.

CA4-DAM'S THIRTEENTH ORDER IS HIS FIRST ON CREDIT. 1 unit at exactly his RM100 anchor, collected on the day, RM100 owed. Twelve prior orders, every one settled on the day or within one; the drafter flagged the advance against his credit cap and it was approved from the desk with that flag showing.

THE SHELF IS ROLLED BY HAND FOR THE CORRECTED DELIVERY, AND THE FIGURE IS THE POINT. A Correction moves no cash and no stock mechanically, by design, so the tool rolled only CA4-DAM's 1 unit (23.5 less 1 is 22.5). But the 6.25 unit the s107 correction records left the shelf physically on the 27th and nothing else will ever roll it, so it is rolled by hand in this same fold: 22.5 less 6.25 is 16.25. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON is untouched.

t: THE DESK ASKED FOR THE WHOLE IPHONE SCREEN AND THEN PUT TWO CONTROLS BEHIND THE STATUS BAR
n: HE COULD NOT REACH THE TOP OF HIS OWN DESK, AND THE HEAD HAD BEEN ASKING FOR THAT SINCE v276. viewport-fit=cover and apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style:black-translucent are together an instruction to draw UNDERNEATH the status bar and the Dynamic Island. Nothing then padded the top: not one rule in 655 used safe-area-inset-top, only left, right and bottom. So the sticky bar sat at top:0 with Names & IDs and the menu at y=23, behind the clock, on the only surface this desk has left.

THE ISLAND ITSELF NEVER COVERED THEM, AND THAT DOES NOT HELP. It is centred and the two controls are on the right, so measured at 375px wide nothing was ever inside its rectangle. The whole strip above the inset is unreachable whatever sits in it, which is why the repair is the inset and not a nudge sideways.

THE INSETS ARE VARIABLES BECAUSE THAT IS THE ONLY WAY TO TEST THEM. env() returns zero on every browser here, so a fix written as bare env() is a fix nobody can measure for a device nobody has. --safetop and --safebot are declared once from env() and read everywhere, and a probe overrides them to the iPhone 15 Pro figures, 59px and 34px, and measures where every control lands.
