Before: two controls in the strip. After: none in the strip and none under the island, with the pair moved from y=23 to y=127.

AND THE TAP TOKEN SAID 40 WHERE APPLE SAYS 44. The desk already had a --tap, four hundred lines below where it should have been, set to 40px, and the two bar controls did not even read it: they carried 34px of their own. It is one token at 44px now and four things read it, so the bar pair, the rail's own buttons, the to-top and every .vbtn moved together. Four points sounds like nothing and is the difference between a control you hit and one you hit on the second try.

TWO MORE THAT ONLY BITE ON iOS. A field under 16px makes Safari zoom the page in on focus and never zoom back out, and one field was 13px, so tapping it left the whole desk magnified; no field can be under 16px now. And 100vh is not the height that is there on iOS Safari, whose toolbar changes the viewport under the page: five of them are dvh, including both full-height slide-overs, which also gained the two insets as padding so a panel the height of the screen clears the status bar and the home indicator at once.

THE SUITE CAUGHT MY OWN INCOMPLETE FIX, WHICH IS THE POINT OF WRITING IT FIRST. Thirteen assertions pin the contract, and three failed on the first run: one 100vh I had missed in an inline style, then two more in the slide-overs, and an assertion of mine that claimed three fields were too small when the browser had already reported exactly one. The fix was incomplete and the test said so before the deploy did.

t: YESTERDAY'S TWO SALES, FOLDED A DAY LATE BECAUSE THE DEPLOY HAD BEEN FAILING SINCE THE 27TH
n: TWO SALES FROM THE 27TH AND A NEW PARTY, FOLDED ON THE 28TH. Both were queued from the desk on the day and neither reached the book, because the entries were drained to disk out of KV and the cloud drafter reads KV. They are folded on his instruction, with the figures read back to him first.

THEY SAT FOR A DAY BECAUSE ONE STALE FILE WAS FAILING THE DEPLOY. master/_folded.json still named thirteen ids from the v381 fold, a fold stated directly and therefore with no drafts behind it, so the "mark the folded rows committed" step failed thirteen times and exited 1 on every push from the 27th. The D1 re-seed sits after that step in the same job, so it never ran and the mirror went a week stale behind it. One stale file explains the failure mail, the stale mirror and a drafter reading a book from before the 26th.

CD3-SEG IS THE FORTIETH CODE ON THE ROSTER AND ITS FIRST ORDER IS AT THE HOUSE RATE. 1 unit for RM100, paid and collected on the 27th. Against the RM50 shelf it returns RM50 at 50.0%. The roster gains the code and the directory is not touched: the name and the place are typed at the laptop and reach the cloud only as ciphertext, which is unchanged by the app being retired.

CR3-DAM'S RM80 IS HIS SEVENTH ORDER RUNNING AT THAT RATE, AND IT NOW CLEARS ITS FLOOR BY RM1.16. Every order since 15 July has been 1 unit at RM80. The collected floor stands at RM78.84, so the rate that was comfortable in July is now RM1.16 clear of break-even, because the shelf went RM44 to RM50 on the 26th and the rate did not move. It returns RM30 at 37.5%. It does not clear the delivered floor of RM88.84, so it is a counter price and not a delivered one; the entry records it as collected, which is why it folds.
AND HE IS PAYING AGAIN. The 18th and the 24th both went out at RM80 with nothing paid; this one is RM80 in cash on the day. His two unpaid units are untouched by this row and still stand.
THE SHELF GOES 25.5 TO 23.5 AND NO COST BASIS MOVES. Two units out, nothing in. Both rows are costed at the RM50 the 26 Aug lot set.

ONE ENTRY FROM THE QUEUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. The 28 Aug advance to CA4-DAM is drafted and PENDING, waiting on a tap, because it is an advance and the gate is exactly the thing that should show him one. It was re-drafted against the repaired mirror first: the old draft costed it at RM44 and flagged it RM22.66 under a delivered floor of RM122.66, both of which were the pre-v385 basis, and on the corrected figures it costs RM50, returns 50.0% and trips no floor flag at all.

t: THE LONG PRESS NOW SHOWS ITS OWN LENGTH, BECAUSE A GESTURE WITH NO FEEDBACK CANNOT BE TOLD APART FROM A DEAD CONTROL
n: HOLD, FOCUS, THEN OPEN. v388 gave the row editor a long press, which was the only way in on an iPhone once the phone app was retired, and it was silent for the whole 450ms it was deciding. You hold, nothing happens, you let go early and conclude the row does not open. The card now carries all three beats itself: it sinks while a gold line sweeps its foot, it lifts and rings gold the moment the press takes, and the editor arrives a beat later.

THE BAR IS DRIVEN FROM ED_HOLD RATHER THAN WRITTEN IN THE CSS. A progress bar that finishes before or after the press it is reporting is worse than no bar, so the sweep's duration is set on the card in script from the same constant the timer uses. Changing the hold length moves both or neither.

THE BEAT BETWEEN FOCUS AND OPEN IS THE POINT OF IT, NOT A DELAY. 150ms, so the confirmation is seen rather than painted over by the panel on the same frame. It also fixed the case that would have broken the gesture in ordinary use: the finger comes off between the confirmation and the editor on nearly every successful press, so a release inside that window must not cancel what it has already been told took. Driven in a headless browser: held throughout, released at the confirmation, tapped, and scrolled away, all four correct.
REDUCED MOTION KEEPS THE THREE STATES AND DROPS THE MOVEMENT. The bar still says how much of the hold is left, because that is information rather than decoration.

t: THE FIGURES ON THE ENTRY FORM WERE SITTING DIAGONALLY FROM THEIR OWN LABELS, AND TAB TOOK SIXTEEN STOPS TO REACH THE FIRST FIELD
n: EVERY FIGURE ON THE NEW ORDER PANE WAS ONE COLUMN FROM ITS OWN LABEL. .qrow is a fixed three-column grid, so the label above any cell is the one in its own column, and the pane had Quantity (unit) above Cash (RM) and Total (RM) above Salt delivered (unit). Units and money each read down the wrong column. Column one is units now, ordered then moved; column two is money, agreed then paid. Measured in the browser rather than by eye: Quantity and Salt delivered share x=285, Total and Cash share x=658. The amend pane went the same way, for the same reason.

TAB REACHED THE FIRST FIELD AFTER SIXTEEN STOPS AND BROKE THE RUN THREE TIMES. The quick-set buttons are exact shortcuts for the input beside them, so they leave the tab order outright. Every switcher is one stop with the arrows moving inside it, on a roving tabindex rather than tabindex="-1", because direction, stream and side are choices that must stay reachable by keyboard. Seven stops to the first field, and the six typed fields are contiguous.

AND THE PARTS STRIP IS IN THAT CHANGE, WHICH MAKES IT DESK-WIDE RATHER THAN THE ENTER VIEW’S. It already declared role="tablist" and was not behaving like one: a tablist whose every tab is a tab stop is the wrong control by its own declaration. Only the roving stop is added; the role and aria-selected are untouched. Proved across all sixteen parts rather than on the one that prompted it: every strip is exactly one tab stop, keeps its role, and still marks a selected tab.

WHAT WAS PROVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Click still activates every switcher and both quick-set groups, the arrows move within a group, Enter is not intercepted, the strip still switches, and all sixteen parts render clean on both books. The probe that found the tab order was itself wrong first time, listing every button regardless of tabindex, so it reported the fix doing nothing; the fix was sound and the probe was not, which is worth recording because it is the third time this week a measurement has been the thing at fault rather than the code.

AND ONE NOTE RE-CHECKED PROPERLY RATHER THAN WITH A NOD. #apBox and #apMsg are shared by the cloud Approve tab and the laptop Names & IDs panel, and retiring the phone app does not touch that, because the gate was never the app: it is cloudMode(), read from the /queue/ping response, so the SERVER decides and both surfaces still exist for the one file. Forced in every combination with both renderers run in each, including SALT_CLOUD undefined, which is the real first paint before the ping answers. Never two. The note stays, for the reason it was written: it is safe by a condition, not by naming.

t: THE LEDGER OPENS ON WHAT IS LIVE, A LONG PRESS REACHES THE ROW EDITOR, AND THE SUITE GOT BACK SIX LAWS IT SHOULD NEVER HAVE LOST
n: THE LEDGER LEADS ON WHAT IS LIVE. 132 orders is an archive, not a list. The lead is anything still owed or undelivered plus the last three days, 17 of 132; the other 115 fold behind a summary carrying the count and the date span, and a filter turns the fold off entirely. goEnt opens every ancestor before scrolling, because both E-code cross-references on this book now target rows inside the fold and the link would otherwise land on a closed summary.
THE STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT IS REMOVED, on his instruction. The panel and all five functions, 443 lines. Nothing else called them and no test covered them.

A LONG PRESS OPENS THE ROW EDITOR, AND v387 IS WHAT MADE THAT LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. The comment claimed a long press raises contextmenu so there was no second gesture to write. That is true on Android Chrome and not dependable on iOS Safari. With the phone app retired the desk is the only surface, so the row editor was reachable on an iPhone by nothing at all. Written out: 450ms, cancelled past ten pixels of travel, yielding to any control inside the card, with a guarded navigator.vibrate. All four guards driven in jsdom rather than reasoned about.

AND THE SUITE GOT BACK SIX ASSERTIONS THAT v387 SHOULD NEVER HAVE TAKEN. Retiring the app removed about a hundred assertions, which is right, and the count fell from 651 to 548. The Stock view asked why, which is this round’s own lesson pointed at the suite: a number that falls reads as fine and the reason matters. Reconciled properly, by capturing every assertion MESSAGE at both versions and diffing the sets rather than trusting the totals: 119 gone, 16 new, and six of the 119 were not the app’s at all.

FOUR OF THEM ARE ENGINE LAWS THAT HAPPENED TO BE CHECKED THROUGH THE PHONE PAYLOAD. They read d.board, so they looked like payload-shape checks and are nothing of the kind: every size on the board has an ask, every ask clears its COLLECTED floor, the delivered floor is the collected floor plus at most one delivery, and the rate per unit never rises with size. That last is the one law a customer can check by hand, and it is the law the oil board was repriced against at v385. They read ladderWalk and floorTotal directly now, so they no longer depend on any surface existing, and a fifth asserts every size the board PRINTS is a rung the walk actually priced. Mutation-checked rather than assumed: a tripled top rung is caught on both books, and a RM1 ask is caught against its collected floor on both.

THE OTHER TWO ARE SERVICE-WORKER RULES THAT LIVED IN THE APP’S SECTION AND ARE NOT ABOUT THE APP. A cached draft list shows a row that has already been approved, and tapping it again is refused as a 409 with no way to know why. The desk’s Approve part reads the same endpoints through the same service worker, so the rule outlived the surface that happened to test it.

THE SHAPE IS THE SAME ONE THIS ROUND KEEPS FINDING, AND THIS TIME IT WAS THE SUITE. Nothing was a wrong value: every deleted assertion was correctly deleted as an app assertion, and six of them were not app assertions. The check that catches it is not a stronger assertion, it is asking a different question, which is also what the v386 miss needed. 560 passed.

t: THE PHONE APP IS RETIRED: ONE SURFACE, ONE CLOUD COPY, AND TWO THINGS THAT WENT WITH IT
n: THE DESK IS THE SOLE AND ONLY CLOUD COPY OF THIS BOOK, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. v290 split them, the root being a hand-written phone app and the desk sitting at /desk. v376 made the desk the root and kept the app at /app deliberately, as the difference between a bad afternoon and no phone surface at all, to be retired when a week had passed without it. It is retired. The route, the file and the payload it read are gone; public/index.html and the last data.json are archived beside the repo rather than deleted.

AND ONE PATH NOW LANDS ON THE DESK RATHER THAN NOWHERE. The SPA fallback re-fetched "/", which resolved through the asset store to index.html. With that file gone the fallback would have 404’d, and every old /app bookmark with it. It names /desk.html now, so an unknown path reaches the surface that exists.

THE PAYLOAD WENT TOO, AND THE LEAK GATE WENT WITH IT. THAT IS A REDUCTION AND IT IS NOT BURIED HERE. phonePayloadLeaks() banned the leak_test vocabulary, every per-unit cost on the book and every real name, and it earned its keep: the first payload ever built carried a real name out of actions(), because revealed has defaulted to true since v217. It was the difference between a code and a name on the open web for the app. It never guarded the desk, which serves cost, margin and the whole P&L at the same public URL, so what goes is a gate on a road nobody travels. The function is still in the master and still tested; nothing in the build calls it.

THE SECOND LOSS IS SHARPER AND IT IS RECORDED IN THE SUITE, NOT ONLY HERE: REFUSALS NOW HAVE NO SURFACE AT ALL. drawRefused, #refbox and the edit-is-not-a-decision rule all lived in the app, and the desk has never had a refused panel. So the refused table is still written by the drafter, still self-cleans and is still served, and nothing shows it. v309 exists because the same CC5-OKR fulfilment was queued twice, byte for byte, since nothing said it was already in hand. Seven assertions that covered that panel are replaced by one that asserts the absence, so the gap cannot be forgotten by being tidied away.

THE NAME GATE CAUGHT ME WHILE I WAS DOING IT, WHICH IS THE BEST ARGUMENT FOR KEEPING IT. The directory on the laptop still held CZ4-TBC and CH6-TBC, five days after the book re-keyed them, because no cloud session can reach it and /bio answers with an empty directory by design. Bringing it in line put a real locality into the directory for the first time, and the desk’s own name-and-place check immediately failed: the v385 entry named that neighbourhood in prose. The gazetteer deliberately never does, because naming a neighbourhood beside a suffix identifies its customer. The entry names the SUFFIX now. One place name, written by me into a public artefact, caught by a gate that had nothing to do with the change that exposed it.

548 ASSERTIONS, DOWN FROM 651, and the fall is the point: about a hundred of them tested a surface that no longer exists. What replaces them is smaller and states the absences: no /app route, no index.html, no data.json, a build that hashes neither, a service worker that no longer excepts a payload, a manifest whose installable surface is the desk, and a fallback that lands on it.

t: THE FOLD MERGED SIX BRANCHES AND REPORTED SEVEN, AND NOTHING IT CHECKED COULD HAVE NOTICED
n: ORDERS AND MONEY WAS NEVER MERGED INTO v385. The branch was in every survey the fold ran and in none of its merge commands. Six went in, seven were reported, and the whole of that view's second pass, 417 lines across the master and the suite, stayed on its branch. It is in now.

WHAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT AND DID NOT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. The fold verified 608 assertions passing, four generated blocks byte for byte, and sixteen parts rendering clean on both books with no undefined, NaN or Infinity and no chart reporting a failure. Every one of those passes perfectly well with a branch missing, because a branch that is absent breaks nothing: it simply is not there. The one signal that existed was read backwards. A post-fold survey printed elegant-poitras-2a6ed1 ahead:9 behind:0, and behind:0 means master holds nothing that branch does not, which is the definition of unmerged. It was read as "they have committed since". The check that was missing is one line and it is now the habit: after a fold, assert every branch is an ancestor of master.

AND IT WAS CAUGHT BY THE SESSION WHOSE WORK WAS DROPPED, BEHAVIOURALLY RATHER THAN BY GREP. Their reasoning is the lesson: a reformat can hide a string match, so they went and read the rendered output. On the shipped v385 the oil Order book still said "Salt you owe", oil's closing stock still read 20 unit at RM50 for RM1,000 against a shelf holding RM153, the oil P&L still opened a July column with no oil trade in it, and both of that view's draw functions still swallowed a throw whole. Confirming the repair the same way mattered too: grepping the merged master finds both of those strings STILL PRESENT, in comments describing the behaviour that was fixed.

AND v385 BROKE A SENTENCE OF THEIRS, WHICH IS WHAT A PARALLEL FOLD PRODUCES. The board now shows five oil sizes rather than fourteen, and from 20 unit up an oil order is under its own cost, so the contribution at the big end went NEGATIVE and the cost panel read "takes -0.6% off what a 50 unit order earns". A share of a loss is not a sensitivity and it is not a thing that can happen. The guard there covered an infinity and not a minus, which is the narrower half of the same fault. Where an end is under water the sentence now says so, which is the more important finding of the two: oil reads "takes 200.0% off what a 10 unit order earns, and a 50 unit one does not cover its own cost". Salt is unchanged at 7.9% against 0.6%, twelve times harder at the small end.

651 ASSERTIONS, up from 608, including one that neither book states a negative share of what an order earns, mutation-checked by forcing the guard true so that it fails on oil and only oil. All seven branches are now proved ancestors of master, by assertion rather than by memory.

t: SEVEN VIEWS READ IN PARALLEL, AND MOST OF WHAT THEY FOUND WAS HIDING BEHIND PROSE NOBODY COULD READ
n: ONE SESSION PER VIEW, FIFTY-FOUR COMMITS, AND EVERY FIGURE MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED. Today, Orders and money, Stock, Price, Customers, The book and Enter each read one view twice, on both books, against the v381 fold and the v382 cost basis. What follows is what they found, and the shape they kept finding it in.

THE PROSE STRIPPER WAS THE ROUND'S BEST BUG-FINDING TOOL, BY ACCIDENT. stripMethod had been deleting most of the descriptive text on the desk since v372: 31 of 55 blocks on Pricing, 26 of 27 on Sourcing, 20 of 21 on Analysis, oil's lead sentence on all six per-product parts, and figures among them. v384 fixed the scope. What came back was not prose, it was faults, because a sentence nobody can read is a sentence nobody can check. The deferred panel on the oil tab said "Paid ahead of delivery, so you owe SALT", hardcoded from before there was a second book. The Whiteboard's notice that picking a downsell party silently re-points the entry to the parent and changes who the row books to had been dead for twelve versions behind a guard that failed quietly, so the form was rewriting entries and telling nobody. Neither could have been found by reading the code.

AND THE ROUND FOUND THE CLASS OF FAULT BEHIND HALF OF ITS OWN FINDINGS. Stated by the ledger view: a field whose name was right and whose basis was not. Six instances, none of them a wrong value. kg on a loss row read as qty, which is how oil twice failed to reconcile for two different readers. priceLadder().floor, a real floor, read as the floor the ask is walked against; it is the DELIVERED one and the walk lifts to the COLLECTED one, and the delta was sitting there as exactly the RM10 delivery. PROD_STOCK_COST.oil at RM7: a real lot rate, and the wrong lot. SHRINK.levels[0].src describing the raw plug at 16.27% while the function returns the charged leak at 4.78%, true since v353. And replacement cost read off the LATEST lot whatever its size. No assertion on a value can catch any of these, because every value was correctly computed. The only thing wrong was which question it answered, and the only thing that caught one all day was a second person measuring it.

THE SILENCE WENT FOUR LEVELS DEEP AND ONLY THE TOP TWO WERE KNOWN. v384 opened drawPerProduct's and renderPart's empty catches. Each draw function then turned out to hold another one INSIDE its own callback, which fires before either reporter can see it: Stock had four of six silent on one view, The book had thirteen canvases silent on two, and drawAnalysis ran six charts in ONE try, so a throw in the second took the other four with it. ensureChart's waiter queue held the last one on the road. Every draw on the desk now reports through one wording, and a broken chart is no longer indistinguishable from a chart with nothing to draw.

SIX FAULTS THAT WERE LIVE ON SCREEN, EACH RENDERING AS A CLEAN RESULT. The sourcing lot chart drew all eighteen lots on both books, oil's three at RM7 squashed against salt at RM64, under a caption promising one bar per lot for the book in front of you. Overview's Latest ledger showed SALT rows at RM100 a unit on the oil tab. stockHistory walked both books and closed 49 unit above the count while its own note said it tied to that count. The supplier tier table ranked backwards, saying the worst rate was the best buy, against a row on this book that records the opposite. The approval card rounded every figure to the ringgit, so a queued RM11.50 read back as RM12 beside a Rate cell correctly saying RM11.50, on the one screen whose whole job is reading a figure right, for the exact case the card was built after. And a read that FAILED on the Approve tab said the queue was empty.

TWO THINGS REACHED THE LEDGER AND BOTH ARE SHUT. The cloud drafter wrote a BUY's receipt only when something moved, while the SELL branch beside it states what moved including a zero. So a lot PAID AND NOT YET RECEIVED came out with no receivedQty and no inTransit, and an absent receivedQty on a settled lot means received IN FULL by this book's own convention. Approve one and the fold walks the whole lot into stock and into the cost basis. It writes both fields now, matching the guard the fold's correction road has had since v146, with an assertion on each road so they cannot part company. Separately, ovAmend carried the same record-and-write split that produced the v383 defect, and it runs over the local queue BEFORE either gate, so a hand-written correction naming an unknown field still wrote a false line on the desk. Both halves build the claim from the write now.

THE PRICE VIEW LOST THE RESELLER MENU AND KEPT THE ONE CONTROL INSIDE IT THAT MATTERED. 478 lines out, on his instruction. shQueueHouse stays, because it is the only writer of PRICE_SET, and oil's whole board is derived by ratcheting down from the RM130 he set at 10 unit: delete it and the number every other oil price hangs off becomes permanent and unreachable. The size list turned out to be doing two jobs, and cutting oil to five sizes would have flattened its board to a dead RM13 a unit and RAISED the 50-unit ask by RM40, because the walk only ratchets down at intermediate rungs. The rungs and the printed board are separate now: he sees his five, the taper is intact, and not one price moved.

THE FLOOR LOST ITS MARGIN LEG AND THAT CHANGES NOT ONE ASK. Measured on both books at every size. The guard only ever RAISES an ask to clear the floor and no ask is floor-lifted on the current cost stack, so lowering the line can only remove a lift that is not there. It is purely a change to the refusal line, which makes the copy the whole deliverable: the floor is break-even including his RM25 of time, and an ask sitting on it earns nothing. And the last two-engines gap on the tab is closed: pxQuote's own comment claimed it returned the board cell on a carded size, it never did, and enginePrice ended by lifting to the DELIVERED floor where the walk had already cleared the COLLECTED one. It fired at exactly one rung, the one size the board tags collect-only, so the table said quote it at the counter and pxQuote quoted it as though it were going out on a van.

A NOTE THAT TYPED ITS OWN TOTAL, AND A CAVEAT KILLED BY ITS OWN RULE. The departed partner's note carried a hardcoded RM2,090 three clauses from the same figure the builder computes live: they agree today and part the moment a referred order is corrected, silently, on a page served publicly. Struck, with the reason written in so nobody helpfully adds it back. And the credit-cap caveat added at v384 was culled by the FIGURE exemption added at v384, because its only number was a breach count. Setapak is on the map, so CH6-SET draws instead of reporting as unknown; the gazetteer's own note sends you to the laptop directory for provenance, and the directory holds no coordinates, which is now written down.

THE METHOD IS THE THING TO KEEP. Render the part twice, run the strip on one, diff them. It found that a warning about someone owing money sat as the LAST sentence of a block ten characters under the cut, so it would have vanished on the day the book got bigger, and that a caveat saying every figure beneath it is damped measures 151 characters at EVERY size a book can be and has never once reached the screen. The rule, as Price put it: the question is not whether a block is under the limit today, but which substrings are data and how much they can grow. A template with no figures at 103 characters is safer than one carrying a size list at 68. The answer is to split, never to trim.

WHAT WENT TO HIM RATHER THAN INTO THE CODE. Nine decisions, each one a price or a policy: the oil ladder, and why the desk called his own RM450 under floor when it prices a 50-unit order off a 30-unit lot's rate; a credit cap and a reorder trigger both denominated in units across two books whose units are worth RM100 and RM13; a reward scheme whose earning is windowed to since-adoption while its redemption is not, so all five partners carry a deficit; a taper fitted to the salt supplier's ladder on a book he buys from someone else, with that supplier's own ladder sitting on the book unread; and his own instruction that a leak rate must not read as progress, recurring one level up at the target rather than at the rate. None of them was changed on anyone's word but his.

t: FOUR THINGS THAT FAILED WITHOUT SAYING SO, AND A SHELF COST THAT WAS ROLLED FOR ONE PRODUCT ONLY
n: TWO EMPTY CATCHES MEANT A BROKEN CHART LOOKED EXACTLY LIKE A CHART WITH NOTHING TO DRAW. drawPerProduct ran every draw function inside try{f();}catch(e){} and renderPart wrapped the whole pass for a part in another one. So a chart that threw left its canvas blank and reported nothing, anywhere. The desk already has a sentence for an empty data set, which is why this survived: the two conditions were indistinguishable on screen, and every chart fault ever found on this desk was found by eye. A throw now says which draw, which product, and what it said, at the TOP of the block where the eye lands. It stays per function, so one bad draw still cannot take the rest of the block with it.

stripMethod WAS DELETING THE FIGURES, THE SECOND PRODUCT’S LEAD, AND A DIV ANOTHER FUNCTION WRITES INTO. Measured on this book: 31 of 55 descriptive blocks gone from Pricing, 26 of 27 from Sourcing, 16 of 17 from Financials, 20 of 21 from Analysis. Among the deleted, "Closing stock 25.5 unit at RM 50/unit = RM 1,275 on the shelf" and "Shipping 4.82 unit a day over the last fortnight". His instruction of 26 Aug was to remove method and caveats, and a figure is neither.

THREE FAULTS, ALL SCOPE RATHER THAN POLICY, AND THE POLICY IS UNCHANGED. One, the keep-one rule ran once per PART: a per-product part renders the same builder twice, so it holds two leads, and keeping the first deleted oil’s lead sentence outright on all six of them. It runs once per block now. Two, the function’s own comment has always promised that a block carrying a control or a figure is left alone; it implemented that for the control, by looking for a child element, and never for the figure, which is written as text and has no element to find. Three, a block something addresses BY ID is not prose.

AND THE THIRD OF THOSE WAS SILENTLY LOSING A FILED PLAN. planAdd writes into <div id="plOk">, which this deleted, so planAdd threw before it reached saveQueue() and the plan was never saved. One id guard fixes that and every other addressed slot on the desk at once, rather than one token in one builder. Six blocks are addressed by id today.

THE COST STACK WAS OBEYING A LOCK THAT IS SWITCHED OFF. lockBase is populated whether PRICE_LOCK_ON is true or not, so LKb is truthy on both books. The leak guards on I.lockOn&&LKb; freight and delivery guarded on LKb and an override alone. So any probe that set a cost silently took the 06 Aug lock’s frozen freight and delivery while the leak stayed live: one cost stack, two components frozen and one not. Proof that isolates it: an override at exactly the live rate must return the live answer, and it did not. v382 is what made it visible, by moving live freight away from the frozen figure.

OIL’S SHELF COST WAS NEVER ROLLED ON THE 26TH. Salt went RM44 to RM50 that day and oil stayed at the RM7 of lots long gone, while every one of the 20 unit on the shelf came off the 26 Aug lot at RM7.6667: the 23 Aug count put oil at zero, 30 landed and 10 went out, so there is no blend to solve, exactly as salt had none. It is STATED rather than left to fall through to the opening, which reads the same figure today only because two separate lots were bought at the same rate, and a figure that is right by coincidence is not right. It feeds Financials’ closing stock, the PRICING snapshot the drafter approves against, and the Stock value card.

SETAPAK IS ON THE MAP. CH6-SET came off its placeholder at v381 and the gazetteer had no SET, so a party the desk could place was reported as genuinely unknown. v348 refused to add TBC and said these two would have a place the moment someone asked; someone asked. The directory on the laptop holds no coordinates, so this is sited from geography at the file’s own two decimal places, about 1.1km, exactly as the other twenty-five were. The unknown count reads zero and the not-drawn table is gone.

TEN NEW ASSERTIONS, AND THE ONE ABOUT OIL IS DERIVED RATHER THAN PINNED. It reads the newest received oil lot out of the book and compares, so it survives the next lot instead of breaking on it, which is the lesson v381 learned on the salt side. A genuine blend will fail it, and that is deliberate: a blended shelf cost should be a decision, not a default.

t: A CORRECTION RECORDED A CHANGE IT DID NOT MAKE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING A LEDGER MUST NEVER DO
n: v381 RE-KEYED TWO PARTIES AND NEITHER ROW MOVED. The two corrections named the field customer. The correctable field is party. applyAmend writes only what is in the CORRECTABLE table, so nothing was written, but it builds the mod line and the trail note from whatever keys the caller supplied, so both rows came out of the fold saying "corrected on 2026-08-26: customer CZ4-TBC to CZ4-MK", carrying a Correction in the trail, and still booked to the old code.

THE RECORD AND THE WRITE WERE BUILT FROM DIFFERENT LISTS AND NOTHING CHECKED THEY AGREED. That is the whole fault in one line. A row that asserts a change it did not make is worse than a refusal and worse than a gap, because every later reader takes it as done: the roster would have gained two codes nothing booked to, and the two parties would have kept their placeholder suffix behind a note saying they had not.

THE FOLD REFUSES AN UNKNOWN CORRECTION FIELD NOW. plan() checks every key against CORRECTABLE before anything is applied, so it lands as a refusal, and a refusal folds nothing. The message names the right field rather than only the wrong one. Proved against the batch that caused it.

THE TWO ROWS ARE REPAIRED AND THEIR TRAILS WERE ALREADY RIGHT. s046 books to CZ4-MK and s032 to CH6-SET. Neither mod line nor trail entry needed changing: both described the correction accurately all along, and what was missing was the correction. Both rows keep their R3 attribution, CI4-OKR and CS6-PER, untouched.

AND THE RE-KEY IS FINISHED PROPERLY. CZ4-TBC and CH6-TBC are purged from the roster, which v381 flagged it could not do because the fold has no operation for retiring a code. That completes the one-identifier rule s046’s own note cites from the last re-key on this desk. The roster is back to 39 codes, and no row books to a party that is not on it.

IT WAS FOUND BY READING THE FOLDED ROWS BACK, NOT BY A TEST. Every check passed: the plan described both corrections correctly, the apply reported success, the suite was green at 577 and CI would have been too. Nothing in the repository could see it, because every one of those reads the same supplied key list the mod line was built from.

t: A TRIP IS RM30 OVER THE AVERAGE LOT, A DELIVERY IS RM10, AND EVERY FLOOR MOVES
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 27 Aug, IN TWO PARTS, AND THE SECOND MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIRST. freightPerTrip goes RM60 to RM30, and txnPerDelivery goes RM50 to RM10. But freight is now spread over the AVERAGE lot this book has received rather than over whichever lot happened to arrive last, and that is the change that stops a floor moving for no reason.

THE OLD DIVISOR MADE A FLOOR SWING ON THE SIZE OF THE LAST PURCHASE. Oil’s freight went RM1.20 to RM2.00 a unit on 26 Aug because a 30-unit buy followed two 50-unit ones. Nothing about the trip had changed, nothing about the oil had changed, and every oil floor rose. That is drift of exactly the kind v233 froze the board to prevent, arriving through a door nobody had shut. The mean over every lot received settles as the book grows; the latest lot stays the fallback while a product has no history to average.

v373 SAID THE RM50 WAS HIS TO STATE, AND IT HAS NOW BEEN STATED. That entry recorded plainly that freightPerTrip was tied to a real trip on 22 Jul but txnPerDelivery had no derivation behind it at all, its reference being an IAS 2 citation about classification rather than about the amount. It stood at RM50 for a month on nobody’s authority. It is RM10 on his.

WHAT MOVED. SALT: effective cost RM58.98 to RM54.63 a unit; the floor at 1 unit RM80.03 to RM78.84 collected and RM130.03 to RM88.84 delivered. OIL: effective cost RM10.92 to RM8.95; the floor at 10 unit RM128.57 to RM113.02, which is RM12.86 to RM11.30 a unit, and delivered RM176.79 to RM123.02.

THE DELIVERY RATE MOVES THE DELIVERED FLOOR AND NOTHING ELSE, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING BECAUSE IT IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE. The collected floor is built from effective cost EX-delivery, and the board has carded a collection price since v352 with delivery quoted on top. So RM50 to RM10 takes RM42 off a delivered order at 1 unit of salt and leaves the board where it was. All of the board’s movement here comes from the freight basis.

AND IT REPAIRED THE OIL BOARD WITHOUT A SINGLE PRICE BEING SET. At the v381 basis the oil ladder broke its own rate-may-not-rise law at 15, 25, 40, 80 and 100 unit: the RM130 anchor had dragged the ladder to RM13.00 falling to RM12.10, the risen floor of RM12.86 then sat ABOVE most of it, and the floor guard lifted those sizes unevenly. With the floor at RM11.12 the whole derived ladder clears it again and the board reads RM13.00 down to RM12.10 with no inversions. The suite goes 576 assertions to 577 and the rate-law test passes.
NO LEDGER ROW CHANGES. A row’s cost is the lot rate it was drawn from and none of those move. What moves is what a unit costs to put in front of a customer, and therefore every floor.

t: THE 26TH: NINE MOVEMENTS, TWO PARTIES OFF THEIR PLACEHOLDER, AND THE SHELF BACK FROM EMPTY
n: NINE MOVEMENTS FROM THE 26TH, FOLDED ON THE 27TH, ON HIS WORD. Four salt sales, one oil sale, two settlements against orders already on the book, and two lots in. Nothing here came through the queue: he stated the day’s trade directly, so there is no draft id behind any of these rows and no approval tap. That is the fold doing what the gate exempts, not a way round it.

THE SHELF WAS DOWN TO 10 UNIT AND COVER READ 1.1 DAYS. 9.5 unit went out and 25 unit came in, so salt closes at 25.5 unit. The salt cost basis moves with it: the new lot is RM50 a unit against the RM44 of the 20 Aug lot, up 13.6%, so every floor on the board rises and the Price view should be read fresh rather than from anything printed before today.

OIL STARTED THE DAY AT NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY THE SALE DRAWS THE NEW LOT. The 23 Aug count put oil at 0 and the book agrees with it exactly: 105 unit in, 71 unit sold and 34 unit written off to losses leaves nothing, so there is no gap between the count and the ledger to explain. 30 unit landed and 10 went out, so oil closes at 20 unit. The 10 sold are therefore costed at the RM7.67 of the lot that landed today, not at the RM7 the earlier lots were bought at, because no RM7 oil existed to sell.

TWO PARTIES COME OFF A PLACEHOLDER SUFFIX. CZ4-TBC becomes CZ4-MK and CH6-TBC becomes CH6-SET, both on his instruction, with the location now stated where it was TBC. The historical rows are corrected to the new codes rather than duplicated, so each party keeps one identifier and its whole history. The old codes are still on the roster and should not be: the fold registers and corrects but has no operation that purges a retired code, and s046’s own note records that the last re-key on this desk purged the placeholder outright. That is left visible rather than patched around the tool.

AND ONE OF THOSE ROWS SAID THIS WOULD NEVER HAPPEN. s032 carries the line that the TBC suffix "stays as minted, since codes are canonical and are not re-keyed once issued". It has now been re-keyed. The claim is not deleted; a line is prepended saying it was superseded on his instruction, because a book that quietly rewrites what it used to assert is worth less than one that shows the reversal.

A BAN IS LIFTED, AND IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN LIFTED OR ENFORCED WEEKS AGO. s016 recorded CS6-PER banned from sale on 30 Jul, not time-limited, and two orders went to him after it: s068 on 07 Aug and the cancelled s109 on 20 Aug. Neither mentioned the ban. It is lifted as of the 26th on his word, so the book stops carrying a restriction nothing was enforcing. His open position is untouched by today’s order: s068 still leaves salt owed out and RM80 uncollected.

AN OVERPAYMENT BOOKS AS OIL OWED, NOT AS CASH HELD. CZ4-MK tendered RM150 against a RM130 order. At RM13 a unit that is 11.54 unit paid for against 10 handed over, so the row carries 1.54 unit of oil owed out and nothing owed in money. That is the same shape the book already uses for CJ4-BJ, CE4-CHE and CE4-AD, and it needed no new field to say it.

THE LEAK GATE REFUSED THIS FOLD, AND IT WAS WRONG TO. phonePayloadLeaks() takes every cost on the book, formats it as money and searches the payload for that string. The new oil cost formats to 7.67, and the payload carries a thirty-day stock projection of 17.67 unit, so a salt QUANTITY was reported as leaking an oil COST. A cost now has to match on a value boundary: a digit or a dot in front of it, or a digit after it, means it is part of a longer number. The same function already carries a comment about scrubbing the ISO stamp because ":17.00Z" read as a RM7 cost, so this is the second time this one line has cried wolf, and it is now fixed for the general case rather than for one input. Eight cases were run against the new matcher: real costs at 7.67 and 47.00 still trip it, in prose as well as in a field, and 17.67, 147.00 and 7.678 no longer do.

AND ONE ASSERTION PINNED A FIGURE THAT WAS ALWAYS GOING TO MOVE. The fold suite asserted that salt leaving the shelf takes a cost of exactly 44, which was true on the day it was written and false the moment a lot landed at another rate. It reads STOCK_COST out of the master now, which is where the fold itself reads it, so it survives every lot instead of breaking on each one.
NO FIGURE WAS COMPUTED BY HAND. Every rate, margin and roll in these notes was computed in code against the book before it was written.

t: A CHART THAT ASKED FOR THE LIBRARY WHILE IT WAS STILL LOADING WAS TOLD THERE WAS NOT ONE
n: THREE BLOCKS OF THE TODAY VIEW READ ‘CHART UNAVAILABLE’ WHILE CHART.JS 4.5.0 WAS LOADED AND TEN CANVASES ELSEWHERE DREW PERFECTLY. ensureChart() set chartTried the moment it appended the script tag, so the caller that started the load waited on it and every caller arriving while it was still in flight was answered false at once, drew the fallback and was never called back when the library landed. The library was never missing. The second caller was simply told there was not one.

IT READS AS A DATA FAULT, WHICH IS MOST OF WHY IT SURVIVED. The desk has two sentences for two conditions and only one of them was true here: an empty set says Nothing to draw yet, a missing library says Chart unavailable. Every block that printed the second had its figures in hand the whole time. The waiters queue on chartWait now and are flushed together, so the answer a caller gets is the answer the load actually returned. chartTried still means asked and failed, so a genuine 404 is not requested twice.

ONE LOST RACE TOOK OUT A TAB, NOT A CHART. drawPerProduct() calls ensureChart once to warm the library and then runs draw functions that each call it again, on the stated assumption that the second call resolves at once. When the first call lost, every one of them lost with it, which is how Analysis loses six charts and Price four from a single missed tick.

AND THE BUILD HAD BEEN WARNING ABOUT THE CHART LIBRARY FOR SIX DAYS. It copied assets/chart.umd.js in from beside the master, and that folder stayed behind in Per-Crm01 when the master moved into this repo on 20 Aug, so every build since printed not found beside the master and copied nothing. Nothing broke, because public/assets/chart.umd.js is committed and served exactly as it sits, so the warning was true, harmless and ignored, which is the worst of the three. The committed file IS the source now: the build proves it is there and FAILS if it is not, and there is no second copy left to drift.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded and no rate changed. What changed is that a chart which asked for the library while it was loading now waits for the answer instead of being told there is not one.

t: AN EMPTY SIZE BAND WAS REPORTED AS A LOSS OF THE ENTIRE COST
n: OIL’S 1-TO-6.25 UNIT BAND READ RM -7.49 A UNIT AGAINST AN EFFECTIVE COST OF RM 7.49. Nothing has ever been sold in that band, because oil’s minimum order is 10 unit. earnedPerKg() returns a per-unit of 0 for a band with no rows, and the shrinkage table subtracted the cost from it, so an empty set was printed as a catastrophic loss on every row of the table. It says no trade now, and the bulk cap, which computes its per-unit the same way, is guarded with it.

THIS IS OLDER THAN TODAY. Nothing in v369 to v378 touched this table; the fault has been on the Price view for as long as oil has had a band with no trade in it. It is the same rule the drafter’s flags follow: a figure that fires when nothing is wrong teaches the reader to ignore the ones that mean something.
AND A BANNED WORD, IN THE ONE PLACE THE DESK SAID IT ITSELF. "Dearest live quote tier" is now "highest". Two more sat in quote notes on the book and are corrected with it. Neither is a figure.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded and no rate changed. What changed is that a figure which was never real stopped being printed.

t: THE HEADER IS A STICKY BAR AND IT HOLDS ITS OWN CONTROLS, SO NOTHING SITS ON TOP OF ANYTHING
n: v376 PUT TWO DISCS ON TOP OF A HEADER THAT WAS ALREADY THERE. Pinning the menu and Names & IDs to the top right corner of the viewport is right when the page has nothing at that corner. This page has a header, and the version chip ended up underneath them, unreadable.

THEY ARE IN THE HEADER NOW, AND THE HEADER IS STICKY. Sticky is what floating them was for: reachable from any scroll position. In the flow, nothing can overlap anything. The two at the bottom stay floating, because the bottom corners carry no content of their own and both have to be reachable mid-scroll.

ONE BAR THAT ADAPTS, WHICH IS THE POINT OF ONE SURFACE. Above 860px the rail carries the mark and the tabs, so the bar shows the version and the key alone. Below it the mark and the menu appear in the same row. Same markup, same page, no second layout to keep level.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: ENTERING AN ORDER IS THE SAME SHEET AS EDITING ONE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: ENTERING AN ORDER SHOULD BE AS COMPLETE AS THE ROW EDITOR. It is now the same sheet. The + in the bottom right opens the editor on an empty row: the same EDFORM table, the same thirty controls, the same select for a stream and the same one for a handover. The Workbench form is untouched and still takes an amendment, a count, a loss, a lost sale and the rest; what this replaces is reaching it for the one thing done most often, and finding eleven fields there where the editor offers thirty.

IT IS READ STRAIGHT, NOT DIFFED, and that is not a detail. A correction queues what CHANGED, which on an empty row would silently drop the product every time it is salt, because salt is the default and therefore not a change. The new-order path reads every control as it stands.

THE ELEVEN THE QUEUE ALREADY NAMES TRAVEL AS THEMSELVES; THE REST RIDE IN more. The drafter checks that bag field by field against the same arrays a correction goes through, and refuses the whole row rather than guessing: an unknown key, a date that is not a date, a flag that is not a boolean, and nothing is drafted. Same discipline, one table, no second copy.

IT QUEUES, IT DOES NOT WRITE. The order is drafted, flagged against the book and comes back to Approve for a tap, exactly like an entry typed on the Workbench or a correction from the ledger. Nothing about the v305 gate is bypassed.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE DESK AND THE APP ARE ONE SURFACE, AND THE FLOATING CONTROLS TAKE A CORNER EACH
n: ONE SURFACE, HIS INSTRUCTION. The desk is served at the root as well as at /desk, so the phone opens the same page the laptop does and there is one thing to keep level instead of two. v290 split them because a 1.3 MB page built around a laptop rail was not a phone app; that stopped being true at v371, when the rail became a menu and the desk started laying out like one. The policy that justified the split, keeping cost and margin off a public app, protected nothing while /desk served every one of those figures at the same public URL.

THE OLD APP STAYS AT /app FOR THIS VERSION, DELIBERATELY. It is one route and it costs nothing, and if the desk turns out to be wrong on a real phone it is the difference between a bad afternoon and no phone surface at all. Retire it after a week without it. The installed home-screen icon needs no change: the manifest already starts at the root.

A CORNER EACH, so none of them argues with another. Top right: the menu, with Names & IDs beside it. Bottom right: enter an order. Bottom left: back to the top. Top left: nothing, in this build. The menu moved off the bottom left because that is where back-to-top has gone. All four are the same 46px disc in the rail’s own material, so a floating control looks like a floating control wherever it is.

NAMES & IDS IS AN ICON NOW, the key on its own, lit when a name is showing. It was a labelled chip in the middle of the meta row, which is a strange place for the one control on the desk that changes what you are allowed to read. It lights rather than shouts.

THE WAY BACK IS NOT DRAWN. v332 turned the built desk’s Close control into a link back to the app, because from an installed window there was no address bar and window.close() cannot honour a Close. With one surface that link points at the page it is already on, so the control is not appended at all. The laptop desk keeps it, because there Close writes the queue and stops a real server.

THE ORDER BUTTON OPENS THE ENTER VIEW FOR NOW. He asked for it to be as complete as the row editor, which means a sheet rendering the same field table rather than a jump. That is the next version; this one puts the control in the corner it belongs in.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE COPY GETS CUT: A HEADING IS A NOUN PHRASE AND A WRITE-UP LEADS WITH THE FIGURE
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: WAY TOO MANY WORDS, EVERYWHERE. He pointed at five things on Today, and each was the same fault. A scope line that spent nine words introducing a badge that says it in one. A lead sentence restating what the severity headings under it already say. Two card headings written as sentences. And a buy write-up of sixty-one words where the figure and the action are the first nine.

WHAT CHANGED. The three scope lines are now the badge alone. Today’s lead is gone. "Where the money at stake sits" is Money at stake; "Cover against the trigger" is Cover. The buy write-up goes from 61 words to 27, the chase from 18 to 12, the supplier default from 33 to 20, and the revive from 40 to 19. Not one figure was dropped: what went is the connective tissue between them, which a reader supplies for free.

THE RULE, so the next line written follows it. A heading is a noun phrase. A write-up leads with the number and the action and stops. A clause restating a rule the reader already knows is cut. Nothing explains a figure that is visible beside it.

THIS IS THE FIRST PASS AND IT IS NOT THE WHOLE DESK. It covers what he named and the same patterns around them. The rest of the generated copy gets the same treatment as it is met rather than in one sweep, because rewriting every string on sixteen parts blind is how a figure gets lost in a sentence nobody reread.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE PAGE HAS A HEADER: THE MARK AND THE NAME ON TOP, THE VERSION AT THE TOP RIGHT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: THE TOP LEVEL IS THE LOGO AND SALT COMMAND, THE LEVEL UNDER IT IS WHEN IT WAS UPDATED, AND THE VERSION GOES TOP RIGHT. The meta row led with the as-at date and carried the version in the middle of four chips, which put the least identifying thing first and buried the one figure that says which build you are reading.

IT MATTERS MORE SINCE v371. Below 860px the rail is a menu behind a button, so from that version until this one nothing on a narrow screen said what the page was at all: the mark and the name were inside the thing that had just been hidden.

THE LOCKUP IS DRAWN ONLY WHERE THE RAIL IS NOT. Above 860px the rail carries the mark and the name in the left column, and a page that says its own name twice on one screen is worse than one that says it once. The version chip stays top right at every width, because that is where he asked for it and it is true of both layouts.

THE TWO DATE CHIPS BECAME ONE LINE. As at and updated now share a chip, reading "As at 26 Aug 2026 · updated 18:12 KL". The v369 rule stands underneath it: the stamp keeps only its time while the two agree and shows the full date the moment they part.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: WHO MOVED THE GOODS IS A FIELD NOW, AND THE DELIVERED SHARE IS MEASURED FROM IT
n: HIS QUESTION: HOW IS DELIVERY RM50 AN ORDER WHEN MOST CUSTOMERS COLLECT? It was not: RM50 is one delivery, weighted by a delivered share of 0.20, so the blend reaching effective cost was RM10 an order and RM3.94 a unit, and since v352 the carded ask is a collection price with delivery quoted on top. But the 0.20 was stated, on 24 Aug, and nothing on the book could check it, because no row recorded who moved the goods. The P&L’s "18.4 of 92 orders delivered" was 0.20 times 92, a fifth of an order rather than a count.

EVERY SALE CAN NOW SAY, AND SILENCE IS NOT COLLECTION. handover takes delivered or collected, and a row that has not been asked carries no key at all. That third state is the point: a share computed as delivered-over-everything would report 123 orders collected on the day this ships because nobody had answered, which is a measurement of nothing dressed as a fact. The share is delivered over the rows that SAY, and measured travels with it so every reader knows which of the two they are looking at.

NOTHING MOVES ON THE DAY IT SHIPS. While no row states a handover the share falls back to his stated 0.20, so the board, the floors and the P&L stand exactly where v372 left them. They move as the rows are answered, and the Pricing basis line says so in words: it reads "RM50 on 20% of orders (stated, no row says yet)" today and "on 33% of orders (2 of 6 that say)" once two of six are answered.

IT RIDES THE ROAD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. One entry in CORRECT_TEXT in engine/position.mjs gives it to the drafter, the fold, both row editors and the phone payload at once, which is the whole reason that table lives in the engine. The only thing it adds is a closed list: the drafter refuses anything that is not one of the two words, and both editors render a select rather than a box to mistype into. And it is asked at ENTRY as well as by correction, on the desk’s Transaction form and the phone’s Record tab, because a flag that can only be set by going back and correcting the row is a flag that stays empty.

WHAT IS STILL STATED, AND SAID PLAINLY: THE RM50 ITSELF. freightPerTrip was tied to a real trip on 22 Jul that collected three lots. txnPerDelivery has no such derivation recorded, and its reference is an IAS 2 citation about classification rather than about the amount. Measuring the share does not measure the rate; that one is still his to state.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, no row carries a handover yet, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: METHOD AND CAVEATS IS GONE FROM EVERY PART, AND THE PAGE LOOKS THE SAME
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: IT IS USELESS, REMOVE IT EVERYWHERE. There were two of them on every part, which is most of why it read as clutter. applyNotes() marked every long paragraph as a note, hid it behind a pill reading "Method and caveats (2)", and cut the lead and every insight to their first sentence. foldMethod() then swept whatever prose was left into a details bar of its own, reading "Method and caveats, what the figures mean and how they were struck (6)". Two controls, both shut on every load, saying the same thing about the same paragraphs.

NOTHING VISIBLE CHANGES, AND THAT IS THE TEST. Both were closed on a fresh load, so what a part showed was its lead sentence, the first sentence of each insight, and its figures. That is exactly what it shows now. What goes is the two bars, the toggle, the body class, about forty lines of CSS and JavaScript, and the prose they were hiding. The lead stays because it says what the part is for; the first sentence of an insight stays because that is the finding rather than the method. A block carrying a control or a figure was never prose and is untouched.

.stand-note WAS AN EXEMPTION FROM A RULE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. v365 added it because body.noteshide hid every .note on a fresh load, which took the row editor’s own standing notices with it, including the sentence explaining why a cancelled row has no Save button. Nothing hides a note now, so those five standing notices simply show, which is what they were written to do.

THE PROSE STAYS IN THE BUILDERS. It is deleted from the page, not from the source, because next to the code that computes a figure it still explains how that figure was struck, which is who it was always useful to.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE NARROW RAIL STANDS UP AGAIN, HIDDEN BEHIND A BUTTON, WITH THE DESK FROSTED BEHIND IT
n: HIS INSTRUCTION OF 26 AUG: KEEP THE RAIL VERTICAL, HIDE IT, PUT IT BEHIND A BUTTON. Below 860px the rail no longer lies down. It is exactly the rail the wide desk has, upright, with its mark, its product switcher, its group headings, its tabs and the active view’s parts beneath them, floating out of a button in the bottom left corner while the desk goes behind frosted glass. It closes on the button, on the glass, on Escape and on choosing anything, and that last one runs from switchTab so every road out is one line.

IT RETIRES FOUR VERSIONS OF THE SAME WRONG IDEA, RATHER THAN SITTING BESIDE THEM. From v273 the rail became a bar on a narrow screen, and everything since was an attempt to make a column of sixteen destinations read as a row: wrapping, then one scrolling row, then ordering the chrome behind the tabs and hiding the mark, then bringing the group labels back as dividers, then pills at v370 this afternoon. Each was better than the one before and all of them were repairing the same decision. A narrow rail is not a special layout any more, so all of it comes out: about sixty lines of CSS, and the 20 Aug rework keeps only its type floors, which were about reading at arm’s length and never about the strip.

THE SUB-PARTS COME BACK WITH IT. .subs was hidden below 860px because a list of a view’s parts is meaningless inside a strip of buttons. In an upright menu it is the v343 rule again: the active view’s parts are one tap away, on the phone as on the desk.

BOTTOM LEFT, AND THE CORNER WAS CHOSEN RATHER THAN DEFAULTED TO. The way out of the desk is pinned top left and back-to-top is pinned bottom right, so it is the one corner free, and on a phone it is the one a thumb reaches without shifting grip. The three bars fold into a cross while it is open, so the button is also the way out.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE SWITCHER LIGHTS WHEN IT HAS SOMEWHERE TO GO, THE FLAT RAIL IS A BAR, AND A PANEL IS OPAQUE
n: THE PRODUCT BUTTONS SAY WHETHER THEY WILL DO ANYTHING. They jump to a product’s block on the current tab, and about half the tabs read both books together and have no block to jump to, so on those the button did nothing at all except explain itself after the tap. Each is lit in its own accent, ice for salt and gold for oil, where the block exists, and dimmed where it does not. This is the job v369 took off the rail bands, done better: the bands said it once for the whole rail from the side, this says it per product and per tab on the control it is about. The jump and the light call the same prodHead(), so a lit button always lands somewhere. A dim one is still pressable, because a control that cannot be pressed cannot tell you why.

THE FLAT RAIL WAS UGLY AND THE REASON WAS THAT ONLY HALF OF IT KNEW. Below 860px the rail lies down into a bar. The tabs were told; the product switcher was not, and kept the column it has upright, so a two-storey block sat in the middle of a single row of buttons and drove the whole rail ragged. The 38px logo made the bar taller than anything in it needed to be. It is now one line of one height: the mark at 30px, two product pills, a rule where the rail changes subject, and the tabs as pills after it.

THE PHONE’S ROW EDITOR HAD NO BACKGROUND AT ALL, AND THAT WAS A BUG RATHER THAN A TASTE. .ed-sheet painted var(--card), and --card is not declared anywhere in the app: it is a desk token that came across with the rule at v362. An undefined custom property makes the whole declaration invalid, so the sheet fell back to transparent and the ledger read straight through the form. It uses --menu now, the app’s own opaque surface.

THE DESK’S TWO SIDE PANELS WERE TRANSLUCENT WITHOUT BEING FROSTED, which is the combination that cannot be read. Names & IDs and the row editor both paint the card gradient, and under the glass palettes those tokens are about 62% opaque; neither panel is in the list that gets a backdrop blur, so the page behind showed through sharp. Both now lay that gradient over --bg0, so the material is unchanged and what is underneath is gone.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: THE RAIL DROPS A NAME AND TWO LABELS, AND THE TAB COUNT SITS STRAIGHT
n: THE NAME "OBSIDIAN SALT DESK" IS GONE, EVERYWHERE. It sat under the logo in the rail, in the page footer, on the eyebrow of every printed statement and price list, and in the README, the manifest and the package description. The desk is Salt Command, which is what the title bar, the repo and the kick line above it already said. One name is easier to read than two, and the second one was never doing any work.

THE RAIL BANDS GO. v231 put two small labels in the rail, a coloured one naming the selected product and a grey All products below it, to mark where the tabs stop following the product switch. In the upright rail they read as headings. Laid flat on anything under 860px the rail becomes one wrapping row of buttons, and the labels become two pieces of stray uppercase text floating between tabs with nothing above or below them to head. The scope is still stated where it is needed: the product switcher sits at the front of the rail, and the three tabs that draw one book while their lead lines claim the desk still carry the v275 badge in their own row.

THE TAB COUNT WAS FLOATED, WHICH IS RIGHT IN ONE LAYOUT AND WRONG IN THE OTHER. .navct used float:right, which puts the count on the far edge of a full-width rail button exactly as intended. A flat tab is shrink-to-fit, so the float had nothing to travel to and the badge rode up against the label and out of its line. The tab is a flex row now: the count is pushed to the right edge when there is a width to push against and simply follows the label when there is not, vertically centred either way.

ONE DATE ON THE DAY OF A FOLD. The meta row shows the day you are reading it and the day the book was last updated. Those are different facts and both stay, but on any day the book is folded they are the same date printed twice, which reads as a fault. The stamp now drops the date and keeps the time when the two agree, so today it says v369 · updated 17:04 KL, and the full date returns as soon as they part.
NO FIGURE MOVED. Nothing was folded, no rate changed, and the book is exactly as v368 left it.

t: TWO OF v366's CORRECTIONS WERE ACTUALLY FULFILMENTS, AND ARE REFOLDED AS THAT
n: NOT EVERYTHING v366 FOLDED AS A CORRECTION WAS ONE. A Correction rewrites what a row says about a past event; it moves no stock, on purpose. Two of the five folded at v366 were real movement, not record fixes, and were flagged as such after the fact. Both are refolded here as Fulfilments instead, same end figures, the trail now says what actually happened, and the shelf rolls for the one that never rolled.

CE4-CHE's s093: 2 UNIT WERE HANDED OVER, NOT JUST RESTATED. Folded at v366 as a Correction that quietly restated deliveredQty from 3.25 to 5.25, so the 2 unit never left the stated shelf. Refolded here as a Fulfilment of 2 unit; the shelf rolls -2 to reflect it. The order's own quantity correction, 6.25 to 5.75 unit, was a genuine record fix approved from the phone and is unchanged.

CA4-DAM's s104: HE PAID, WHICH IS A FULFILMENT. The RM100 recorded directly on 26 Aug (v367) was folded as a Correction for want of a better tool from this session. Refolded here as a proper Fulfilment: same RM100, but the trail now reads as a payment rather than a rewrite, and paidOn is set.
THE SHELF ROLLS 12 TO 10 on the 2 unit s093 actually handed over; s104's fulfilment is cash only and moves nothing.

t: CA4-DAM'S ADVANCE IS SETTLED, ON HIS WORD DIRECTLY
n: ONE CORRECTION, NOT FROM THE PHONE'S QUEUE. s104 (CA4-DAM, 1 unit for RM100, delivered 24 Aug) was folded as an advance at v366: delivered in full, nothing paid. He has now said directly that it is paid; cash is corrected to RM100. The row closes as Completed rather than staying an open advance.

t: FIVE CORRECTIONS FROM THE PHONE, ONE PAIR OF THEM WORKING TOGETHER
n: FIVE CORRECTIONS, APPROVED FROM THE PHONE ON 25 AUG, FOLDED ON HIS WORD TODAY. Each rewrites what a row already on the book says; none moves cash or stock in the trail sense, and none is a new order. CA4-DAM's s104 restates to 1 unit for RM100, delivered in full (was 0.5 unit for RM50, half delivered). CM4-MK's s105 restates its total to RM380 and its cash to RM0. CM6-PJ's s100 restates its total to RM100, its cash to RM100, and attributes it to CI4-OKR via R3, where it carried no attribution before. CE4-CHE's s093 carries two corrections that work as a pair: the first restates the total to RM520 and the delivered quantity to 5.25 unit, the second restates the quantity to 5.75 unit and, in the same step, the total back to RM500. Folded in the order approved, s093 ends the batch at 5.75 unit for RM500, 5.25 delivered, RM500 already collected -- exactly what he confirmed directly.

CA4-DAM'S s104 IS STILL AN ADVANCE AFTER THIS BATCH, ON PURPOSE. The correction restates the order (qty, total, delivered) but was not asked to touch cash, which stays at RM0 on a RM100 order. He has separately said the order is now paid; that is folded right after this batch, as its own step, because it did not come through the phone's approval gate and the two should not read as one thing.

NOTHING PHYSICALLY MOVES IN THIS BATCH. A Correction rewrites the record, not the shelf: s104's and s093's delivered-quantity changes restate what already happened rather than booking a fresh movement, so the roll below is zero. Any resulting gap between the ledger and the counted shelf surfaces the same way any other gap does, at the next count.

EVERY ROW KEEPS ITS OLD TRAIL, WITH THE CORRECTION ADDED BESIDE IT, NOT IN PLACE OF IT. Each row's amend trail still shows what was originally booked; a correction line is appended saying what changed and to what, so the arithmetic in the trail will no longer sum to the row's own headline figures on these five, and that is the intended, visible mark of a corrected row rather than an error to chase.

t: THE SWEEP: THIRTY-NINE FINDINGS ACROSS BOTH APPS, EVERY ONE FIXED AND PINNED
n: A FULL SWEEP OF EVERY ACTION ON BOTH APPS, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. Twelve clusters, every button, form, filter and tap tried and read against the source. Thirty-nine findings, all fixed, all pinned. The suite grows 568 to 569, plus the build-size and em-dash checks widened for real, justified growth on the phone.

THE WORST ONE: A BOOLEAN FLAG DECLARED NUMERIC. rebate and goodwill are stored true, never a figure, but CORRECT_NUM_NN carried both as amounts. A boolean rendered into a number box shows blank, and an untouched Save on any of the eleven rows carrying a rebate silently queued a correction clearing the flag. Both moved into CORRECT_BOOL, in engine/position.mjs, the one table the drafter, the fold and both apps all read.

FIGURES THAT DISAGREED WITH THEMSELVES. Six of them: a goodwill gift counted into revenue on one tab and not another, RM26.26 apart; the supplier write-off card showing RM0 on Oil's page instead of staying off it; "out for salt" labelling a cash figure that has counted Oil since v275; a paid refund vanishing from the cash table without vanishing from the total under it; "Promised away" printed twice, identically; and Analysis's delivery-timing block reading the whole book under both products at once.

ONE PRODUCT'S DATA SHOWN UNDER THE OTHER, FIVE TIMES. Inventory's opening lot, Sourcing's tier table and its next-lot plan, the Reseller Menu's hours/password/watermark fields, and the phone's This Party rate: each read a bare, unscoped value or a duplicate id instead of the product-aware resolver the rest of the desk already uses. The Reseller Menu fix is the one with teeth: every Publish, Make-a-code and Download handler was reading Salt's boxes regardless of which panel was filled in.

THE ROW EDITOR, EIGHT FINDINGS DEEP. Beyond the rebate flag: two more tappable-looking places (who owes what, a customer's statement) that were never wired to open it; the Approve tab's Edit button offered on shapes it cannot rebuild; its own explanatory notes hidden by a reused CSS class; a purchase's cash field labelled as if money came in; a fold that opened collapsed regardless of whether it had anything to show; and a refused Correction reopening with no trace of why it came back.

REACHABLE ONLY WITHOUT A MOUSE, OR NOT AT ALL. The flagship feature of the last three versions had no keyboard entry point on either app: no tabindex, no keydown handler, nothing. Fixed on both, with Escape to close. The desk's panel also gained the dialog role, label and focus the phone's already had. And a background deploy could silently close the row editor mid-correction with no warning at all; the phone's own idle() check now covers it, the same discipline it already gives a half-typed trade.

ELEVEN FINDINGS ACROSS THE TRANSACTION AND RECORD FORMS. A dead pricing box (wrong container id, no console error, ever). Amend order pickers listing every order ever written with no status filter. A Modification's preview computing the wrong resulting state, and a Cancellation's preview never once saying the word. A Linked amendment's Record button staying enabled with its one required field blank. A date decades in the future, accepted everywhere, now warned on the desk and capped on the phone. Add ID's preview reading raw select values instead of the dropdown's own words. Unchecking Paid or Delivered in full leaving the stale total sitting in the box. A Fulfilment's own record calling a partial payment "paid in full". A negative cash figure sailing straight through. And Cash/Units typed directly never refreshing the preview.

FOUR SMALLER ONES. The Book tab's row count frozen at the unfiltered total while a filter narrows what is actually shown. The phone refreshing itself in the background with none of the desk's "tap to load" chip. A never-dated cancelled row printing the literal word "undefined". And the Ledger toolbar with no way to isolate a product, on a desk with two of them.
NO FIGURE MOVED. No row was folded and no rate changed; the sweep changed what the tools do and say, not what the book holds.

t: THE AUDIT: THIRTEEN FINDINGS ON THE CORRECTION ROAD, EVERY ONE FIXED AND PINNED
n: A FULL PASS OVER BOTH SURFACES, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. Every hop of the correction road was read against every other: the phone's sheet, the desk's panel, the drafter, the fold, the desk's own ovAmend and the payload that feeds the phone. Thirteen findings, all fixed, all pinned with an assertion so none can come back quietly. The suite grows 546 to 568.

THE WORST ONE: THE PHONE PREFILLED A FIGURE THAT IS NOT THE FIELD IT EDITS. The payload's cash is txPaid and its delivered is txEffDeliv, which is right for reading a row and wrong for editing one: a correction writes the RAW fields, and on the thirteen rows carrying in-kind settlements the two part company. s074 showed Cash RM188 over a stored cash of 0, so retyping the shown figure would have added RM188 of phantom cash. The payload now sends the raw figure wherever it differs, the sheet prefills it, and the Settled boxes sit beside it so the whole picture is on screen.

AN OLD LOT LOST ITS PAYMENT TO A DATE FIX. A settled lot stores its payment as status "paid" with no cash field at all. The correction path recomputed status from raw cash on EVERY correction, so fixing the date on such a lot flipped it to unpaid. The recompute now runs only when cash or total was actually set. Same fix in the fold and in ovAmend, from the same reading.

CLEARING pending COULD WALK A WHOLE LOT INTO STOCK. An absent receivedQty means fully received, which is how every settled lot is stored, so a correction that cleared pending on a deposit would have booked the entire undelivered lot into stock and the cost basis: the v146 failure on a new road. The guard ovAmend's fulfilment path has always had is on this one now: clearing pending without stating a receipt writes receivedQty 0 and inTransit.

THE GATE MISSED EVERY IN-KIND SETTLEMENT. The under-paid flag compared the corrected total against raw cash, so restating s010's total below the RM80 it was settled for raised nothing. It reads txPaid and txEffDeliv now, and a correction pricing an unpriced row clears the flag exactly as a Modification has since v358, with the clearance recorded in the trail.

EDIT ON A QUEUED CORRECTION WENT NOWHERE. The Approve tab's Edit button, wired at v360, predates corrections: tapping it on one errored into the Record tab. It now reopens the row editor on the PROPOSED state, and saving withdraws the earlier draft first, with the same block-on-it discipline record() uses, so one row never carries two live corrections. A desk-authored note or cost riding in the draft survives a phone resend instead of being silently dropped, and the sheet says so.

THE DESK'S APPROVE PANEL SHOWED A CORRECTION AS ZEROS. The generic amendment card leads with cash and units moving, both zero on a correction by definition. The desk now renders the same before-and-after card the phone got at v361. Smaller findings alongside: duplicate party and date flags on every correction card, raw field keys where labels belonged, the fold's plan describing a correction by its target's balance, a cancelled row's editor offering a save the drafter was always going to refuse, and clearing the date off a row with movement now refused outright rather than flagged.
NO FIGURE MOVED. No row was folded and no rate changed; the audit changed what the tools do, not what the book says.

t: EVERY ATTRIBUTE OF A ROW IS EDITABLE, AND THE CHAIN IS PROVED ON THE REAL QUEUE
n: THIRTY ATTRIBUTES, NOT NINE. His instruction of 25 Aug: "I need to be able to edit every attribute of an entry on the ledger." v361 covered nine. The editor now reaches what was traded (product, party, size, total, unpriced), who it books to (associate, stream, downstream, order code), what has actually moved (cash, handed over, received, cost), every date the row carries, what was settled other than in cash (settled RM and unit, rebate, goodwill) and the row's own flags (cancelled, pending, in transit, defaulted).

THE FIRST CUT WITHHELD THE SETTLEMENT FIGURES AND THAT WAS WRONG. cash and deliveredQty were held back on the ground that they "move by fulfilment, and two writers on one figure drift". Reading the engine settled it: txPaid is cash + settledRM read straight off the row, so the amend trail is a narrative BESIDE the figure and never its source. Setting cash is a correction; adding to it is a movement; both legitimately write the same field, which is what ovAmend already did. The correction is still recorded beside the trail, and a flag says the trail will no longer sum to the figure.

WHAT IS STILL NOT EDITABLE IS EXCLUDED RATHER THAN FORGOTTEN, and the suite asserts each one. rid is the row's identity, so editing it would rename the thing being edited. amend and mod are the trail. rev, ref and refKg are derived from the associate and the stream, and offering them directly would let a row claim R2 and R3 at once. A purchase's status is derived from cash against total and is recomputed after every change.

THE FORM IS A TABLE NOW, IN ALL THREE PLACES. Thirty fields hand-written would need thirty pieces of markup, thirty read-backs and thirty diff lines, and the three would drift. The field table lives in engine/position.mjs beside attributionOf, so the drafter that accepts a correction, the fold that applies it and the desk that applies it all read one array; the suite asserts they are the same object. The panels render from a spec and diff from the same spec.

AN ABSENT FLAG AND false ARE THE SAME THING, and comparing them raw would have recorded a correction on every save that touched a checkbox. A row that is not cancelled simply has no cancelled key, so the comparison coerces both sides and a false flag deletes the key rather than writing false.

THE PHONE GETS EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE COST AND THE NOTE, and that is a policy line. A per-unit cost is the one figure phonePayloadLeaks() bans outright, and a row note quotes lot costs in prose. Neither reaches the payload, so the phone cannot SHOW either, so it must not offer to REPLACE either: overwriting a value you are not allowed to see is worse than not offering it. The sheet says so. The other twenty-eight are on the phone, and the payload grew 4.6 KB to carry them.

THE CHAIN IS PROVED ON THE LIVE QUEUE, END TO END. A correction was posted into the real KV at 07:21:35; the production cron fired at 07:30, read it, resolved the row by rid against the live mirror and wrote a pending draft into the live D1 with all three flags it should have raised. It was queued deliberately wrong, salt to oil on a RM100/unit row, so what was proved is the gate REFUSING rather than passing. It was then rejected and withdrawn from KV, and the queue is back to the three entries it held before.
NO FIGURE MOVED. No row was folded and no rate changed.

t: THE ROW EDITOR REACHES THE PHONE, AND THE ATTRIBUTION RULE HAS ONE HOME
n: TAP ANY ROW ON THE BOOK TAB AND EDIT IT. The desk got this at v361 on a right-click. The phone opens on a plain tap rather than a long press: a long press raises the same event, but iOS Safari is not reliable about it, and a ledger card had no tap action before, so nothing is taken away. The sheet carries the product, the buyer, the associate, the stream, the date, the size and the total, prefilled from the row. It joins held and goes up on the same push every other entry uses, so it survives a dead connection, and it queues a correction rather than writing one.

THE NOTE IS THE ONE FIELD THE PHONE CANNOT TOUCH, and that is a policy line rather than an oversight. Row notes carry lot costs and margins in prose, and phonePayloadLeaks() keeps every per-unit cost off this payload because the app is public by decision. The phone cannot SHOW a note, so it must not offer to REPLACE one: overwriting prose you cannot read is worse than not offering it. The sheet says so in a line rather than leaving it a mystery, and notes stay editable at the desk.

THE ATTRIBUTION RULE MOVED INTO THE ENGINE, WHERE IT SHOULD HAVE GONE FIRST. Reading the associate back out of a row is not trivial (R2 puts them in the counterparty field with the buyer as downstream; R3 leaves the buyer and credits ref), and v361 shipped it TWICE, once in the master's ovAmend and once in the fold's applyAmend. The phone needed the same answer a third time, which is the point at which a copy becomes a fault. attributionOf now lives in engine/position.mjs with one definition and three consumers, which is the rule this repo already had and that I broke for an hour.

THE PAYLOAD CARRIES EACH ROW'S ID AND ATTRIBUTION. Two small fields, 2.2 KB across 125 rows, and neither is a cost: a rid is opaque and an attribution is a code the payload already ships in its party list. The leak test reads them as it reads the rest.
NO FIGURE MOVED. No row was folded and no rate changed.

t: EVERY FIELD ON EVERY ROW CAN BE EDITED, AND EVERY ROW HAS A NAME
n: RIGHT-CLICK ANY LEDGER ROW AND EDIT IT. His instruction of 25 Aug: "I am unable to edit the ledger." He was right, and about more than he said. The only amendments that existed were paid, delivered, restate and cancel, and not one of them touches what a row SAYS about itself: a row's product and its associate were set once, at entry, and nothing anywhere could change them afterwards.
