The Ledger tab now opens a panel on a right-click, or a long press, with the product, the party, the associate, the stream, the date, the size, the total and the note all typeable. It queues a correction and writes nothing: the drafter checks every field against the book and it comes back to Approve for a tap, exactly like a transaction.

EVERY ROW CARRIES AN ID NOW, AND THE OLD ONE COULD NOT HAVE WORKED. A row was addressed by ovKey, which is party, date and total joined together. That names a row for exactly as long as none of those three changes, and an editor whose job is changing them cannot use it: correct a party and the row's own name no longer finds it. It also already collided, on two SA5-BTR lots dated 22 Jul both for RM350, neither of which could be addressed at all. All 125 rows were given a rid, the fold mints one for every new row, and the drafter, the fold and the desk all resolve by rid first and fall back to ovKey.

THE DRAFTER COULD ONLY REACH SEVEN ROWS, AND NOW REACHES ALL OF THEM. Every amendment resolved its target through the open-order snapshot, so 118 of the 125 rows on this book, every settled one, were beyond any amendment. A correction reads the full book instead. It is the one amendment that does, deliberately: a row is as often wrong once it is closed as while it is live.

AN ASSOCIATE CAN BE ATTRIBUTED FROM THE PHONE. The drafter refused outright any entry carrying associate, stream or downstream fields, on the ground that whose bucket a row books to is a judgement. That was true of the link fields and never true of these three: each is a code the book either knows or does not. They are checked per field now, and R2 and R3 are applied exactly as the desk's own rule applies them. Only linkTo and orderCode stay refused, because which OTHER row a row links to is a judgement no figure settles.

WHAT A CORRECTION IS APPROVED ON IS WHAT CHANGED. The Approve card leads with cash and units moving, both of which are zero on a correction and say nothing. A correction gets its own card: a before-and-after line for every field it touches, the flags the drafter raised on the row as it would then stand, and nothing else. Changing the product re-runs the whole rate check against the new shelf, which is how a RM100/unit row moved to oil is flagged as more than double the highest oil rate this book has carried.
NO FIGURE MOVED. No row was folded and no rate changed. Every row gained a rid and nothing else; the ledger stands exactly where v360 left it.

t: CM4-MK'S SIZE TAPER, CR3-DAM'S STANDARD ADVANCE, AND CA4-DAM GOES OUT
n: THREE ORDERS, ON HIS WORD. CA4-DAM's pending 0.5 unit at RM50 has gone out with the RM50 still owed, an advance rather than a settlement. CM4-MK took 4 unit for RM360, RM90/unit, paid and delivered on the day. CR3-DAM took his standard 1 unit for RM80, delivered with the RM80 still owed.

CM4-MK'S RM90 IS THE SIZE TAPER, NOT A CHEAPER RATE. The drafter flags it 18.2% under his typical RM110/unit, but that figure is drawn from his 2-unit orders; RM360 for 4 unit is the exact size and total he paid on 10 Aug. Nothing about what he is charged has changed.

CR3-DAM'S RM80 IS HIS RATE ON EVERY ORDER THIS BOOK HAS EVER RECORDED FOR HIM, unbroken since June. It flags only because it is an advance: RM80 sits under the RM122.74 delivered floor while clearing the RM72.74 collected one, which is what an advance always does until the cash lands.
THE SHELF ROLLS 17.5 TO 12 UNIT on 5.5 unit physically out: 0.5 to CA4-DAM, 4 to CM4-MK, 1 to CR3-DAM.

t: THE FOUR SET-ASIDE UNIT GO OUT, AND CA4-DAM'S HALF UNIT CLEARS ITS FLOOR BY RM1.13
n: THE FOUR UNIT HE SET ASIDE AT THE v351 COUNT ARE THE FOUR THAT MOVED, AND THE ROLL LANDS EXACTLY ON THE COUNT. The count of 24 Aug read 21.5 on the shelf and said in terms what it was made of: 17.5 free plus 4 set aside, being the 3 unit due to CS6-BS-R and the free unit due to CS6-BS. Both went out on the 24th, so the shelf rolls 21.5 less 4 to 17.5, which is the free figure he counted, to the unit. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON.salt stays at 24 Aug. Of the 17.5 that stand, 8 are already paid for and owed out as deferred deliveries, 3 to CE4-CHE and 5 to CE4-AD, so 9.5 unit are genuinely free to sell.

CS6-BS-R'S 3 UNIT SETTLES IN FULL ON THE DAY IT WAS PRICED. The order was restated from RM0 and Unpriced to RM290 at v358 this morning, and RM290 and all 3 unit moved the same day, so it never spent a day on the order book as a priced pending order. RM96.67 a unit against the RM44 shelf returns RM158, 54.5% on RM290, and it clears the 3 unit collected floor of RM180.35 and the delivered floor of RM218.22 by RM71.78 on the harder of the two. Nothing is outstanding and no receivable is raised.

THE FREE UNIT MOVES AND NO REASON CAME WITH IT, WHICH IS THE ONE THING IN THIS FOLD THAT NEEDS HIS WORD. The row booked on the 24th said plainly that why it is free was not stated and would not be guessed, and that the flag would go on when it moved and he said which. It has moved and he has not said. So it folds unflagged, and unflagged has a consequence: with no goodwill flag on it, 1 unit at a total of RM0 against RM44 of cost is a COMPLETED SALE in the priced set, the first zero-total completed row this book has carried, and it pulls down every rate the desk averages over priced sales. Goodwill belongs out of that set by his own ruling of v280; an advance on his next reseller award belongs against the award, and the network reads him at 0 earned with RM470 of resale still to run. Neither is invented here. One word from him sets the flag and the row is correct either way.

CA4-DAM ORDERS HALF A UNIT AT RM50, PENDING, AND IT CLEARS ITS FLOOR BY RM1.13. His twelfth order and the eleventh struck at exactly RM100 a unit; the only order he has ever taken at another rate is 1.5 unit at RM116.67 on 26 Jul, so the price is not the news. The floor is. At half a unit the v358 snapshot puts the collected floor at RM48.87 and the delivered floor at RM98.87, and the whole RM50 of difference is the per-delivery transaction cost, which falls whole on an order however small it is. He has collected on every order and the book has said so since 01 Aug, so the collected floor is the one that binds and RM50 clears it, by RM1.13. That is the narrowest clearance his standing rate has stood at, and it is worth reading beside the fact that this rate has not moved through a cost basis that has gone RM64 to RM47 to RM56 to RM44: the desk has absorbed every move and he has absorbed none. The next rise in the buying rate takes RM100 a unit under its own floor on the basis he actually trades on. Nothing is paid and nothing has moved, so the row is undated and draws no stock.

t: MODIFICATION GOES THROUGH THE GATE, AND CS6-BS-R'S PRICE LANDS THE SAME WAY
n: A MODIFICATION IS DRAFTED NOW, NOT LEFT FOR A PERSON. His instruction of 24 Aug, after asking whether a queued price restatement could be committed without waiting for the six-hourly fold: since 20 Aug the phone's Restate form already sends the new quantity and total against a specifically tapped order, so what changed has been a figure rather than free text for a while, and the drafter now runs the same rate-against-history-and-floor comparisons on it that a brand new row gets. That is exactly the check that was missing on 17 Aug, when a Modification restated an order to 5 unit for RM50, RM10 a unit against salt that has never gone below RM46, and reached the fold with nothing beside it but a person reading it. Linked and Rewarded amendments stay refused: neither has a phone form that captures a figure to check, only a judgement about which other row or which award applies.

CS6-BS-R'S PENDING 3 UNIT IS PRICED AT RM290, RM96.67 A UNIT. Queued on 24 Aug once the price was worked out; it was RM0 and Unpriced before. The board asked RM86.67 at 3 unit and his own last comparable order was 2.5 unit for RM270 on 03 Aug, RM108 a unit, so RM96.67 sits between the two. The drafter flags it 13.3% under CS6-BS-R's own six-order median of RM111.5, which the order's own history explains rather than contradicts: his rate has fallen through August as the volume through this reseller bucket has grown. RM290 clears the 3 unit collected floor of RM180.35 and the delivered floor of RM218.22 with a great deal to spare, and it costs RM44/unit off the shelf, a 54.5% margin. The order stays PENDING: nothing was paid and nothing moved, only the price was agreed, so it draws no stock and books no revenue until it does.

t: THE PROJECT MOVED, SIX TOOLS DID NOT, AND THE NAME-LEAK GATE WENT QUIET
n: THE PROJECT FOLDER WAS MOVED AND RENAMED WHILE THIS SESSION WAS RUNNING. Projects\Personal\Cow-Crm01_Salt Business became Projects\Personal\Commerce\Per-Crm01_Salt Business. Nothing was lost: the directory, the vault, the menu secret and both queue files all moved intact, and the 39th name added this morning is still in it. SIX PLACES CARRIED THEIR OWN COPY OF THAT PATH and every one of them was then pointing at a folder that no longer existed.

THE WORST OF THEM WAS SILENT AND IT WAS THE ONE THAT PROTECTS NAMES. The test that scans public/desk.html for any customer name or neighbourhood reads the directory to know what to look for, and it SKIPS ITSELF when the file is not on the machine, which is right on a CI runner and wrong here. So it passed on an empty list: the gate that keeps a real name off a public page was off, and the suite still printed green. Repointed, it is scanning again and the suite goes 440 assertions to 447.

THE SECOND WORST INVENTED A FOLDER RATHER THAN FAILING. drain.mjs mkdir'd the dead path and wrote an empty queue into it, so the run reported success while the real queue sat elsewhere. Nothing was lost only because the file it wrote was empty. It now REFUSES: a missing data folder means the project has moved, and creating one hides exactly the fact worth knowing.

ONE CONSTANT NOW, NOT SIX COPIES. PROJECT_DIR and DATA_DIR are exported from tools/book.mjs and imported by drain, drafts, update, seed-vault and the test suite, each still overridable by SALT_PROJECT and SALT_DATA. The next move is one line rather than six, and the tools that cannot find it say so.

ONE THING IS LEFT ON DISK FOR HIM. The old folder still exists at Projects\Personal\Cow-Crm01_Salt Business, holding nothing but the empty queue file the drain wrote into it. It is safe to delete and is not deleted here: the move was his, and undoing half of someone else’s tidy-up is not this desk’s business.

t: THE SHEET IS AMENDABLE BEFORE IT IS SENT, AND v354 WAS IN THE WRONG PLACE
n: v354 PUT AN EDITOR ON THE HOUSE BOARD AND WHAT HE ASKED FOR WAS THE SHEET. His correction of 24 Aug: he wants to download the price list the engine derives and then amend it for certain customers. Editing what the desk quotes everyone is a different act with a different consequence, and it does not need doing before handing one man a sheet. The standalone panel is gone.

ONE TABLE, IN THE PRICE LIST CARD, WHERE THE SHEET IS ACTUALLY SAVED. Every size with a tick for whether it appears at all and a price prefilled from the board. Change a figure, untick a lot, press Save the sheet and the customer receives exactly what is on screen. The party picker above it watermarks the sheet as it always did.

THE DOWNLOAD USED TO IGNORE THE TABLE ENTIRELY, WHICH IS THE FAULT THIS FIXES. mnSaveTier read priceLadder() at every size, so the figures on the panel were decoration: he could amend them and the sheet would still carry the derived ask. shRows() is now the single source, so the number he typed is the number that goes out.

A PRICE UNDER ITS FLOOR IS REFUSED, NOT LIFTED, AND THAT DIFFERS FROM THE BOARD ON PURPOSE. A board must always answer, so v352 lifts an ask to the next step above its floor. A SHEET goes to a named person, and quietly sending a different figure from the one he typed is worse than refusing to send it. It says which size and by how much, and saves nothing.

NOTHING IS STORED, WHICH IS HIS DECISION AND HAS A COST WORTH STATING. Asked whether a customer’s amended prices should be remembered, he chose one-off: no queue, no approval, nothing to fold. The next sheet starts from the board again. The consequence is that a customer who got RM110 last month and RM130 this month will notice, and this desk cannot warn you, because it does not know what it sent. The saved-sheet confirmation now says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.

THE ONE THING THAT STILL REACHES THE LEDGER IS MAKE IT THE HOUSE BOARD, which queues the typed prices as PRICE_SET on the v354 road: drafted, approved, folded, provisional on the board in the meantime. It is refused while a customer is named, because one man’s sheet is not everyone’s board.

t: SALT'S 55.2 UNIT GET A REASON, AND THE PRICED LEAK FALLS BY TWO THIRDS
n: 15:70:15, ON HIS WORD: STORAGE LEAKAGE, PROMOTION, SELF USE. 8.28 unit lost on the shelf, 38.64 given away to win customers, 8.28 used himself. selfUseLog had never carried a salt row, so more than a fifth of everything ever bought was a gap with no reason against it, and it had been that way since the book opened.

THE PRICED LEAK FALLS 17.74% TO 5.32% AND A UNIT COSTS RM47.74 INSTEAD OF RM54.95. The 38.64 unit of promotion leave the price under the v353 rule, because a one-off spent to start selling is not a cost of selling; the 16.56 unit of leakage and self use stay in it, because those are. FLOORS FALL WHERE THE PER-ORDER LEG BINDS AND NOWHERE ELSE: 1 unit goes RM79.95 to RM72.74, 2 unit RM134.90 to RM120.48, and 2.5 upwards do not move at all because the cogs leg already stands above them. NO ASK MOVES.

THE P&L WAS REPORTING A 50:50 SPLIT ON A BOOK THAT NOW STATES 15:70:15. sampleShare has halved every leak since v232, which was an honest stand-in while nothing attributed it, and it survived the attribution. So the accounts said half of salt’s loss was unexplained waste when 70% of it was promotion he chose to give. The split is now READ off selfUseLog wherever the log covers the plug, and assumed only where it does not; the desk says which of the two it used.

AND THERE ARE THREE DESTINATIONS, NOT TWO. Promotion is marketing under IAS 38.69. Leakage and short delivery are abnormal waste under IAS 2.16(a). What he took for himself is a DRAWING and belongs on neither: it now has its own line BELOW operating profit and is deliberately outside it, because netting an owner’s withdrawal off the trading result flatters nothing and hides the withdrawal.

THE NUMBERS. Marketing goes RM1,473.01 to RM2,062.22 on 38.64 unit. Abnormal loss goes RM1,473.01 to RM441.90 on 8.28. Owner’s use appears at RM441.90 on 8.28 and leaves operating profit, which goes RM2,710.95 to RM3,152.85, 13.0% to 15.1%. Nothing was earned by this commit: an assumption about where the salt went was replaced by his account of it.

t: THE BOARD IS EDITABLE, AND THE EDIT TRAVELS THE SAME ROAD AS A SALE
n: EDIT THE BOARD, ON THE PRICE TAB. His instruction of 24 Aug: let him change a price and change which lots are shown, easily. One table, one row per size: the size, a show tick, the price he wants, what the board actually quotes, and the floor beside it. BLANK MEANS DERIVED, so a size he has not set is priced by the ladder, which is where a price should come from unless there is a reason to say otherwise.

IT DOES NOT WRITE THE BOOK, BECAUSE NOTHING ON THIS DESK DOES. It composes a queue entry exactly as a transaction does, and that entry is drafted, approved and folded on the same road. What makes it feel immediate is the OVERLAY: the moment an edit is queued the board is rebuilt with it, marked provisional like every other queued entry, so he can see what a price does to the sizes above it before anyone approves anything. Withdraw the entry and the board goes back. There is no second state to keep in step and nothing to reconcile.

A SET PRICE STILL OBEYS BOTH LAWS AND THE TABLE SAYS SO WHEN IT DOES NOT WIN. The rate may never rise with size, so setting one price moves every size above it. And no ask may sit under its own floor, so a price set too low is lifted to the next step above the floor and tagged lifted rather than quietly honoured. The drafter flags the same thing before anyone approves it, computed off the PRICING snapshot rather than re-derived, because two engines drift.

HIDING A LOT IS REVERSIBLE AND IS NOT A DELETION. `hide` drops a size from the card without taking it out of the ladder, so it stays priceable off the board and comes back by unticking one box. Hiding EVERY size is refused: a board with no sizes on it is not a board.

THE FOLD REPLACES THAT PRODUCT'S ENTRY RATHER THAN MERGING INTO IT. The form on the desk is the whole statement of what he wants the board to be, so a price he cleared is actually cleared and does not survive as a leftover. It moves no stock, no cash and no ledger row. The other product's board is untouched, and there is a test that says so.

t: PROMOTION LEAVES THE PRICE, FINANCING GOES TO 40%, AND HE CAN SET A PRICE AGAIN
n: PROMOTION IS NOT A LEAK AND THE PRICE STOPS TREATING IT AS ONE. His instruction. Every unit that failed to reach a paying customer used to divide the cost of the ones that did, whatever the reason, so a deliberate launch giveaway was recovered from every future customer for ever. That is not a cost of selling, it is a one-off spent to start selling. OIL: the priced leak goes 32.4% to 6.5%, because 27.2 of its 34 unaccounted unit were the launch, and a unit costs RM12.13 to RM8.77. Its floor at the 10 unit minimum falls RM146.27 to RM112.68. IT LEAVES THE PRICE, NOT THE BOOK: the P&L still carries every one as marketing under IAS 38.69, the count still wins, the plug is unchanged. Only the divisor moves.

ONLY WHAT IS LOGGED AS PROMOTION LEAVES, AND SALT HAS LOGGED NOTHING. An unattributed plug is priced in FULL, which is the conservative way round: a leak nobody has explained is a leak until someone does. Salt’s 55.2 unit are still carried whole at 17.74%, so not one salt figure moves on this commit. He has said the salt gap is some storage leakage, mostly promotion and some self use; until those are three numbers rather than three words the price cannot use them. WHEN THEY LAND, SALT’S FLOORS FALL SHARPLY, on the same arithmetic that just moved oil.

FINANCING GOES 12% TO 40% A YEAR, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. 12% was a borrowing rate; 40% is what he says his own capital is worth, which is the right basis for a desk funded out of his own pocket. IT IS SMALLER THAN IT SOUNDS AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING. A 50 unit lot clears in about twelve days at 4.32 a day, so the average unit is held under six, and 40% of RM45.20 over six days is about 29 sen a unit. On credit it bites harder: a customer taking ten days to pay now costs 1.1% of the sale against 0.33%.

HE CAN SET A PRICE AGAIN, AND IT OBEYS THE SAME TWO LAWS. PRICE_SET is the twenty-seventh ledger key: prices he has stated, by product and size, overriding the derived ladder. The board has been fully derived since v326, which is the right default and the wrong absolute, because he is the one who meets the customer. A stated price replaces the markup and nothing else: the rate-may-not-rise walk still runs on it and the floor guard still runs beneath it, so a price set under its own floor is lifted rather than honoured.

OIL’S 10 UNIT IS SET AT RM130, AND IT TAKES THE WHOLE OIL LADDER WITH IT. That is the honest consequence rather than a fault: RM130 for 10 unit is RM13.00 a unit, and a bigger lot may never cost more per unit, so every size above had to come down. 15 unit goes RM210 to RM190, 50 goes RM650 to RM610 and 100 goes RM1,300 to RM1,210, a flat RM13.00 falling to RM12.10. Every one of them still clears its own floor with room. Salt is untouched: all ten asks stand exactly where they were.

t: THE FLOOR GETS HONEST, AND NOT ONE SALT PRICE HAS TO MOVE
n: THE WHOLE LEAK IS CHARGED AND NOTHING IS ABSORBED. SHRINK_ATTRIB goes 0.33 to 1 on his instruction. A unit costs RM54.95 to put on the shelf and the floor was built on RM48.01, so RM6.94 a unit was being carried silently. That is what put the delivered floor BELOW true cost at every size up to 9.7 unit, nearly the whole board, and it is why one sale in eighty-two lost money and thirty-one more would have if they had been delivered. Absorbed cost is now RM0.00.

THE CARD IS A COLLECTION PRICE AND DELIVERY IS QUOTED PER ORDER, ON HIS INSTRUCTION. Four orders in five are collected, so pricing all of them as though they were delivered makes the collectors pay for the deliveries. The board states one floor, the collected one, and one charge, RM50, once. The v344 deliverable flag and the collectOnly list are gone: on the true figures they said the same thing at nearly every size, which is a flag answering a question the board should not be asking.

AN ORDER COSTS HIM RM25 OF HIS OWN TIME AND THE FLOOR NOW SAYS SO. His figure: roughly five hours a week at RM50 an hour over the ten orders a week this book runs at. PER ORDER, NOT PER UNIT, because a half unit and a twelve and a half take about the same handling. Nothing in this stack had ever paid him for the work; the whole margin was doing it, undifferentiated from the return on his capital, so he could not tell profit from wages. Tested against his own eighty-two sales: at RM25 seventy-two still clear, at RM40 fifty-nine would and at RM60 forty-six.

AND NOT ONE SALT PRICE MOVES. All ten asks stand exactly where they were, RM60 at half a unit to RM950 at twelve and a half, because the ask is a markup on landed cost and already cleared the honest floor at every size. ONE OIL PRICE MOVES: the 10 unit minimum goes RM140 to RM150, because it was RM6.27 under its own floor once the leak was charged in full, and 34 of the 105 unit of oil ever bought were given away. ladderWalk now enforces what v263 already wrote down: an ask may never sit under its own floor, and where it would it rises to the next grid step above it, never to the floor exactly.

THE MARGIN CURVE IS ALIVE AGAIN, AND WHAT KILLED IT WAS v344. Its base added one whole delivery to every order. When delivery went from RM16.67 to its real RM50, that flat charge inverted the fit: a RM50 order carrying RM50 of delivery reads at minus 100% margin while a big lot barely notices, so measured margin appeared to RISE with size, the may not rise clamp fired, b went to zero and the curve returned its clamp floor of 18% at every size, with an r-squared of 0. The base is now the goods and nothing else, which is what the ladder actually prices. Measured after: b -0.0881, r-squared 0.340, 51.3% at half a unit falling to 23.0% at twelve and a half. His time is deliberately NOT in it: a flat per-order charge in a regression base inverts the slope for the same reason delivery did.

THE SOURCING PLAN IS 50 UNIT ON THE 28TH, WHICH IS HIS CALL AND NOT THE RECOMMENDATION. The ceiling resets on the 28th and RM2,260 sits well inside it. Landed cost is RM45.20 a unit against RM43.60 at the 100 tier, so the lot costs RM80 more than the same salt at the top step and covers a fortnight rather than three weeks. RM4,360 would have fitted with RM140 to spare. Recorded as a decision, not an error.

t: THE SHELF IS COUNTED AT 21.5, AND 3.75 UNIT ARE GONE
n: COUNTED AT 21.5 UNIT AGAINST 25.25 ON THE BOOK. A count, not a roll, so COUNT_ON.salt moves 20 Aug to 24 Aug. He counted 17.5 free plus 4 set aside on the shelf, being the 3 unit due to CS6-BS-R tomorrow and the free unit to CS6-BS, and confirmed on the question that 21.5 is the WHOLE shelf: the 8 unit owed to CE4-CHE and CE4-AD as deferred deliveries are inside it, not on top of it. v350 held the figure back for exactly this, because the same three words read three ways and two of them wrote a shrinkage that was not there.

THE DRIFT IS MINUS 3.75 UNIT, ABOUT RM170 AT THE RM45.20 LANDED COST, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE COUNT DIFFERENCE THIS BOOK HAS RECORDED. The salt plug goes 51.45 unit to 55.2, and the leak charged into the price goes 5.46% to 5.85%. Effective cost follows, RM51.73 to RM51.93 a unit. THE CARDED FLOORS DO NOT MOVE, and that is not an oversight: since v326 the floor is a markup on the LANDED cost of a lot, not on the leaked-up cost, so a worse leak shows in the margin rather than in the refusal line. 12.5 unit collected still floors at RM751.45.

IT IS UNATTRIBUTED, WHICH IS THE PART TO ACT ON. selfUseLog now carries oil, split 20:80 at v350, and still carries nothing at all for salt. So 55.2 unit of salt, more than a fifth of everything ever bought, is a gap with no reason written against it. Oil's 34 unit took one sentence from him to explain; salt’s 55.2 has never been asked about.

FREE TO SELL FALLS 17.25 TO 13.5 AND COVER TO 3.1 DAYS. Against it stand 10.25 unit of pending orders, CJ4-BJ 6.25, CS6-BS-R 3 and the free unit, so there are 3.25 unit spare and nothing is short. The 100 unit buy at RM4,360 was already the standing recommendation; the shelf is now a day thinner than when it was made.

t: THE OIL LEAK SPLITS 20:80, AND A FREE UNIT GOES ON THE BOOK
n: SIX POINT EIGHT UNIT OF OIL WERE USED AND TWENTY-SEVEN POINT TWO WERE GIVEN AWAY. v348 recorded the whole 34 unit as one row marked other because the split was not known and was not going to be guessed. He has given it: 20:80, in the order the causes were put to him, so self use first. It is now two rows, 6.8 personal and 27.2 sample. The two carry different treatments, a drawing against IAS 38.69 marketing expensed as incurred, which is exactly why one blended row would not do. No figure moves: attribution never overrides a count, and neither row touches revenue, cost, stock or margin.

ONE UNIT, FREE, TO CS6-BS, DUE OUT AND NOT YET MOVED. On the book pending and undated, so it draws no stock and raises no receivable until it goes. A zero total is paid in full by definition, which is right here: there is nothing to pay. WHY IT IS FREE IS NOT STATED AND IS NOT GUESSED. It is not an earned reseller rebate on this book: CS6-BS has applied all three units he has earned and the network reads earned 0 with RM470 of resale still to run before the next. So it is goodwill, or an advance on the next award, and the two are not the same row, because a rebate settles an award in kind while goodwill is excluded from priced sales altogether. The flag goes on when it moves and he says which.

THE SALT COUNT OF 24 AUG IS NOT WRITTEN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. He counted 17.5 free plus 4 set aside, being the 3 unit due to CS6-BS-R tomorrow and the free unit above. IT DOES NOT RECONCILE UNDER ANY READING AND THE GAP IS WORTH RM169. The book holds 25.25 on hand, 8 unit owed out to CE4-CHE and CE4-AD as deferred deliveries already paid for, and 17.25 free. His 17.5 is a quarter of a unit off the FREE figure, not off the shelf. If 21.5 is the whole shelf then 3.75 unit are gone and free is 9.5, not 17.5. If 17.5 is free after the 4 are set aside, the shelf is 29.5 and the book is 4.25 light. A stated stock written on the wrong reading is a false shrinkage on a book whose leak is its largest single loss, so the figure waits one question rather than being taken twice.
PROMISED RISES 17.25 TO 18.25 on the free unit. Free to sell is unchanged at 17.25, so the pending book now exceeds the free shelf by a unit for the first time.

t: THE MAP HAS A REAL OUTLINE, FETCHED ONCE AND COMMITTED
n: THE GEOGRAPHY IS A MODULE IN THE REPO, THE THIRD AFTER THE ENGINE AND THE BOOK. geo/basemap.json holds the drawn outlines with their provenance, geo/places.json the gazetteer that was five hand-typed declarations in this file, and tools/geosync.mjs --sync renders both into the master between markers. CI runs --check, so the copy in the desk is PROVED to be the files rather than trusted to be, exactly as engine/pricing.mjs and ledger/book.json are. The prose that explained each declaration is NOTES in places.json and comes back as comments.

THE OUTLINES ARE REAL AND THEY WERE NEVER REMEMBERED. Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Putrajaya and Negeri Sembilan, from OpenStreetMap via geoBoundaries, pinned to one release, simplified by Douglas-Peucker and rounded to about 11m: 683 points and 13 KB for the four. tools/geofetch.mjs is what fetched them, it is run by hand, and it is never run by CI or by the build. THE RUNTIME RULE IS UNTOUCHED: the desk still loads nothing at run time. v149 refused a coastline because there was no basemap to be had offline and one drawn from memory would be a fabricated fact. It was right about inventing geometry and wrong about the conclusion, because geometry can be fetched, checked and committed.

ODbL, SO THE CREDIT IS PRINTED UNDER THE MAP. That licence asks for attribution wherever the data is shown and /desk is served publicly, so it goes where a reader sees it rather than into a comment. DOSM Malaysia publishes the same boundaries and was the first choice; its repository carries no licence file at all and GitHub reads it as NOASSERTION, so it was not committed into a private ledger on a guess.

THE OUTLINES CARRY NO NAME, AND NOT EVEN INTO THE FILE THE DESK SHIPS. v293 stripped every label from this canvas because a named place beside a party code identifies a customer. The basemap keeps its names in geo/basemap.json, for whoever maintains it, and geosync renders only the kind and the rings. The leak gate caught the first draft: a note explaining the NIL suffix named the locality it stands for, on a public page, which is precisely the disclosure v293 removed. The note now says the locality is in the directory and does not repeat it.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. The territory the frame sits in is drawn brighter with a faint fill, the surrounding states a dim stroke, everything beyond the frame clips itself, and it all sits UNDER the heat so the blobs still read first. Eight new assertions, including one that every point lies inside Malaysia's own bounding box: a hand-typed coastline or a swapped lat and lng cannot pass as real geometry.

t: THE OIL GAP HAS A REASON, AND TBC STOPS READING AS A MISSING GAZETTEER ENTRY
n: THIRTY-FOUR UNIT OF OIL ARE ATTRIBUTED, ON HIS WORD: SELF USE AND THE PROMOTION PERIOD. The oil walk is 5 unit of opening plus 100 bought less 71 sold, and three counts have found the shelf empty, so 34 unit had sat as an unexplained plug since 14 Aug. It was never spillage or short delivery. The oil went out deliberately, partly to himself and partly as promotion while the product was being introduced. selfUseLog had never carried a single row, so every plug on this book was unexplained by construction; this is the first, and salt’s own plug is still unattributed.

THE SPLIT BETWEEN SELF USE AND PROMOTION IS NOT KNOWN AND IS NOT INVENTED. The reason is recorded as other rather than personal or sample, because the two carry different treatments, drawings against IAS 38.69 marketing, and guessing the proportion would put a figure in the accounts nobody stated. Give the split and the row becomes two. The date is the count, 23 Aug, not the day: it went across 06 to 23 Aug and 23 Aug is when it was established.

NO FIGURE MOVES. selfUseLog attributes the plug and never overrides the count, which still wins. It touches no revenue, no cost, no stock and no margin. What changes is that the oil shelf now reads as a product given away on purpose rather than as 34 unit nobody can account for.

TBC MEANS TO BE CONFIRMED, AND THE MAP NOW SAYS THAT INSTEAD OF BLAMING THE GAZETTEER. CH6-TBC and CZ4-TBC were reported as suffix TBC is not in the gazetteer, which invites exactly the wrong repair: putting TBC into PLACES would site two different people at one invented spot and the map would look complete. They still count as genuine gaps rather than exclusions by rule, because a reseller account will never have a place of its own and these two will, the moment someone asks.

t: THE MAP READS THE PLACE OUT OF THE CODE, AND GETS A GRATICULE
n: A PARTY FELL OFF THE MAP THE MOMENT IT WAS ADDED, AND THE REASON PRINTED AGAINST IT WAS WRONG. locOf read one hand-kept list, LOCS, and nothing else, so any party registered since that list was last typed was reported as having no location suffix against a code that plainly ends in one. CK4-SEN, folded onto the roster at v346, did exactly that. v237 put the locality INSIDE the code on purpose, so the desk now reads it. LOCS stays as the override for the party whose locality is not what its suffix says, CH4-KS at KLS, and it still wins.

NILAI JOINS THE GAZETTEER AND CY2-NIL IS SITED AT LAST. The suffix NIL was never a mystery, it was simply not in PLACES, so a party the desk could place was reported as unknown. At 2.81N 101.80E it falls outside the Klang Valley frame, so it is listed rather than drawn: 39km SSE of the frame centre, beside CN5-TAI at 217km NNW and CM6-HCM at 1,017km NNE.

THIRTY-ONE PARTIES ARE NOW DRAWN AND THREE MORE SITED, AGAINST THIRTY AND TWO. Five remain off the map and none of them is a mystery: three are reseller trading accounts, which are the same people as their parent codes and would draw one man twice, and two carry TBC, which is an admission rather than a location. Those two are the only genuine gaps left on the book.

THE GRID WAS NOT A GRATICULE AND NOW IT IS. It drew three lines at a quarter, a half and three quarters of the canvas, which correspond to no coordinate at all: the look of a graticule with none of the information, in a colour barely separable from the background, so the page read as blobs floating in nothing. The lines now sit at round latitudes and longitudes 0.05° apart and are labelled, and the frame has a border. THERE IS STILL NO COASTLINE. This file loads nothing at runtime, so there is no basemap to be had, and a shoreline drawn from memory would be a fabricated fact on a page whose whole claim is that its figures are checked. A graticule is exact.

A CANCELLED ORDER IS NO LONGER A TARGET FOR AN AMENDMENT. tools/fold.mjs matched the row an amendment names by key alone, so a fulfilment queued against an order that had since been cancelled would have folded straight onto it: cash, units and a date written on a row the book says did not happen. Nothing has hit it, but v345 cancelled two live pending orders, so the road was open. It is refused now and left for a person, which is the test every other amendment is measured by.

THE FOOTER STOPPED COUNTING ON ITS FINGERS. Its copy hard-coded two resellers, two buckets, two TBC from the day it was written and read 2 of these is a genuine gap in the plural. It now counts what is there and says which of the two roads fixes it: a real place goes into PLACES, a placeholder has to be learnt first.

t: A THIRD ZERO ON THE OIL SHELF, AND A CUSTOMER ON THE ROSTER
n: CK4-SEN IS ON THE ROSTER AND THE DIRECTORY IS NOT TOUCHED. The code was typed by hand on the phone, drafted into the roster, approved and folded, which is the whole of the cloud route for a registration. The roster goes 38 codes to 39. The name and the place behind the code are typed at the laptop and never travel, so nothing in the cloud holds them. No figure moves: CK4-SEN has no order on the book and shows as a customer with nothing against it until one is queued. What it does change is the drafter’s reading, because a party on the roster stops being flagged unknown, so the first row carrying this code will be judged on its rate rather than on its novelty.

OIL IS COUNTED AT ZERO FOR THE THIRD TIME AND THE STATED SHELF DOES NOT MOVE. 0 unit counted by hand on 23 Aug against 0 on the book, a drift of 0. Stated stays 0 and COUNT_ON.oil moves from 20 Aug to 23 Aug. That is the one difference from the second count of 20 Aug, which agreed with the first on the same day and therefore moved neither figure nor date: this is a fresh look on a fresh day, so the date of the last look moves even though the figure does not.

THE APPROVAL SCREEN SAID NOTHING IS UNACCOUNTED FOR, AND AGAINST THE WALK THAT IS STILL NOT TRUE. The flag reads the count against the STATED figure, where it is exact. Read against the LEDGER it is not: oil walks 5 unit of opening plus 100 bought less 71 sold, which is 34 unit the book says should be on a shelf three counts have now found empty. No oil row has been folded since 14 Aug and v345 touched salt alone, so the gap is unchanged at 34 unit. A count confirms the shelf, not the walk. This is the same finding as v331 and it is written again because the flag will say it again on the next count.

NOTHING ROLLED AND NO OTHER FIGURE MOVED. Neither row is a movement, so the shelf is not rolled at all: salt stands at 25.25 with COUNT_ON.salt still on 20 Aug, and no cash, no unit and no cost basis changed. The watermark moves to the newest id folded, 2026-08-23T15:36:10.986Z. This is the batch that was approved on the 23rd and has been waiting through two versions: v344 folded nothing and v345 was a desk edit, so the staged rows sat where the fold expects to find them until now.

t: AN ORDER AGREED BEFORE ITS PRICE, AND TWO WITHDRAWN
n: CS6-BS-R TAKES 3 UNIT AND THE PRICE IS NOT STRUCK YET. On the book pending and undated, so it draws no stock and raises no receivable. The total is a placeholder zero and the row says so: unpriced. WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS IT SHOULD BE. The ladder asks RM260 at 3 unit, RM86.67 a unit. His own last comparable order was 2.5 unit for RM270 on 03 Aug, RM108 a unit, and the only other 3 unit he has taken was RM285 on 15 Jul, RM95 a unit. The board therefore asks RM25 LESS than he paid three weeks ago for half a unit LESS. Both his own figures and the ask clear the v344 floors, RM180.35 collected and RM193.43 delivered.

THE DESK CAN NOW TELL TWO KINDS OF ZERO APART. A zero total has read as paid in full since the first free unit went out, which is right for a rebate and wrong for an order whose price is still being worked out: it would have read Pending and Paid, nothing owed, on the one row whose whole point is that no figure is agreed. unpriced makes payFull false and labels the row Unpriced. Everything downstream follows without a second rule: undated with nothing moved it is Pending and counts nowhere, and if goods ever go out before a price is agreed it becomes Open and Advance, which is exactly what that would be.

CN6-WM AND CS6-PER ARE CANCELLED ON HIS WORD, AND NEITHER TAKES ANYTHING BACK. Both were agreed, never dated, never paid and never handed over, so both counted nowhere before and count nowhere now. CN6-WM was 1.5 unit for RM185, RM123.33 a unit, which was his dearest direct rate by some way and reversed four orders that had fallen at every step. CS6-PER was 6.25 unit for RM350, RM56 a unit, RM170 under the RM520 ask and RM25.73 UNDER THE v344 COLLECTED FLOOR OF RM375.73: an order this desk could not have filled without a loss. Both rows are kept rather than deleted, because the rate is the record.

PROMISED FALLS 22 TO 17.25 UNIT AND NOW EXACTLY EQUALS FREE STOCK. Minus 7.75 on the two cancellations, plus 3 on the new order. The shelf holds 25.25 with 8 owed out, so 17.25 is free and every one of those units is spoken for. Nothing is short and there is no headroom either.

t: THE TWO MOVEMENT COSTS ARE MEASURED, AND THE CARD IS A COLLECTION PRICE
n: COLLECTION IS RM60 A RETURN TRIP, NOT RM100 A LOT. v325 set it at RM100 and said in terms that it was the line to challenge first. It has been. The key is renamed freightPerTrip because the distinction is real: a trip that collected three lots on 22 Jul cost RM60, not RM180. Landed cost on the 20 Aug 50 unit lot goes RM46.00 to RM45.20, and freight in the accounts goes RM1,300 to RM780 across thirteen lots. One trip per lot is still assumed, because the rows do not say otherwise.

DELIVERY IS TWO NUMBERS, AND THE OLD ONE WAS NEITHER. RM50 is what ONE delivery costs. Four orders in five are collected by the customer, so deliveredShare is 0.20 and the blended cost of an order is RM10. The old RM16.67 charged every order a third of a delivery that most of them never had. delPerOrder is now the full RM50, which is what a delivered order has to carry, while the blended figure is what goes into effective cost: RM3.92 a unit against RM6.54.

THE NET IS RM3.47 A UNIT OFF EFFECTIVE COST. RM55.20 to RM51.73. Goods and freight account for RM0.85 of it and delivery for RM2.62. Floors fall about 1.7% at every size: a 12.5 unit lot collected goes RM764.75 to RM751.45, and a single unit RM61.18 to RM60.12. No ask moved.

THE CARDED ASK IS A COLLECTION PRICE, AND THE BOARD NOW SAYS WHERE IT STOPS BEING ONE. Charging one delivery at its real RM50 shows what the old blend hid: at half a unit the ask is RM60 and the delivered floor is RM73.90, so delivering it loses RM13.90. Oil is the same at its 10 unit minimum, RM140 against RM141.81. Every size now carries deliverable and deliveryGap, and the board lists collectOnly. It is a reported fact and not a new price: nothing refuses an order and nothing moves an ask. What to charge for a delivery is his decision and it is not taken here.

THE P&L RESTATES AND NOTHING ABOUT THE PAST CHANGED. Gross profit goes RM6,925.22 to RM7,346.97, 33.3% to 35.3%. Selling and distribution goes RM1,533.33 to RM920, being 18.4 of 92 orders delivered rather than all 92. Operating profit goes RM1,876.00 to RM2,911.08, 9.0% to 14.0%. An assumption about the past was corrected, not the past.

t: THE PARTS ARE VISIBLE, AND THE PHONE CARRIES THE PEOPLE
n: THE FIFTEEN TABS ARE ONE TAP AWAY AGAIN. v341 folded a view’s other tabs at the foot of its lead, and on a 7,000px lead that is the same as losing them: the Network sat closed under the whole of Customers and was reported missing. Every view now opens with a strip naming each part it holds, the rail lists the active view’s parts beneath it, and one part shows at a time. The old addresses still work: #network opens Customers on the Network.

ADD ID AND APPROVE REACH THE CLOUD DESK. Names & IDs mints a code from a name and a place on the laptop only, so the cloud desk could not register a party at all while its own form said to use a control it did not have. The Enter view now carries Add ID, the phone’s route: a code typed by hand, queued, drafted into the roster, approved, folded. And Approve, which only the phone had since v302, is a part of Enter on the cloud desk, reading the same drafts and writing the same decisions.

THE PHONE GAINS THE PEOPLE, THE NEXT THIRTY DAYS AND THE AGE OF EACH DEBT. A People tab: who is due on his own buying habit, every customer with the desk’s tier and a statement on tap, the associates and what each made, brought and earned, the customer rewards, the demand turned away and the map’s heat. Today carries the forecast per product, the shelf’s dry day on the desk’s own walk, what lands and what is expected in. Who-owes-what says how old a debt is and what the ladder says it is worth. Every figure is read off the desk’s own functions (nextBest without its profit, networkStats, customerRewards as band and units, mapPoints), and the leak test reads the payload as before: no cost, no margin, no profit, no prose.

THE PHONE’S ADD ID SAYS WHAT IT DOES. The Record mode was labelled Party and its road text said the drafter refuses it; the drafter has drafted a registration into the roster since v309, so the mode is named Add ID and the text says it goes through the gate.
NO FIGURE MOVED.

t: THE PHONE ON THE STORYBOARD
n: MOVE 5 OF THE REBUILD: TODAY, THE BOOK AND RECORD FOLLOW THE PRICE TAB. Today leads with the count only when a count is due: a shelf looked at today is one line with its figure, and the card with the instruction is kept for the shelf that has not been looked at. What needs doing follows, and the position, on hand, free, cover and owed to you, moves here from the Book tab as the Watch block, because the question it answers is asked in the morning, not while reading the ledger.

THE BOOK OPENS ON WHO OWES WHAT. Every open order with money or stock still to move, either way, what is due to you first, then what is agreed and not yet moved, read straight off the open orders the desk sends. The ledger itself, with its filters, folds behind a summary that says how many rows it holds, and its method sentence goes inside the fold.

RECORD SAYS WHAT THE PARTY USUALLY PAYS. When a customer is chosen on a sale, one line under the field gives their rate across their orders and the date of the last, from the desk’s own customer figures, so the price being typed is typed against something. The app still computes nothing.
NO FIGURE MOVED. The phone reads the same data.json; only what stands open changed.

t: SEVEN VIEWS OVER FIFTEEN TABS
n: MOVE 4 OF THE REBUILD: THE DESK IS SEVEN VIEWS. Today (with Overview and Forward behind it), Orders and money (the order book, with Financials behind it), Stock (Inventory, with Sourcing behind it), Price, Customers (with Network and the Map behind it), The book (the Ledger, with Analysis behind it) and Enter (the Transaction form, with the Whiteboard behind it). A view leads with one tab open and carries the others as folds that render on first opening; every figure is still here, and the old tab ids still work as addresses and links, opening the fold they name.

THE METHOD PROSE FOLDS ONCE PER TAB. Every standing paragraph that explained what the figures mean is kept, word for word, behind one Method and caveats fold at the top of the tab, each block under the heading it sat beneath. The lead sentence stays, because it says what the tab is for. Measured at 1280px before this change, across the fifteen tabs: 61,700px of page, 5,770 characters of prose standing open, 92 tables. Measured after, the seven views with their folds shut: 29,579px of page and 766 characters of prose standing open, the Enter form’s own copy being most of that. Every view’s figure tokens, with every fold opened, are the same multiset as its tabs produced before: 2,897 tokens across the seven, none missing, none added.

NO FIGURE MOVED. The builders that draw each tab are untouched; the views compose them. The figure tokens extracted from every view with its folds opened are the same multiset as the fifteen tabs produced before the change.

t: THE FOLD IS A DATA WRITE
n: MOVE 3 OF THE REBUILD: AN APPROVED ROW BECOMES A RECORD, WITH ITS NOTE, BY A TOOL. tools/fold.mjs reads the staged batch, says what every row would do and what would leave or land on the shelf, refuses what it must (a Modification, a key that matches nothing or two things, a replay, a row with no note), takes the agent’s notes from one file and writes the book, the master, the version entry and the changelog in one pass, all or nothing. A fulfilment is applied exactly as the desk’s own ovAmend applies it; a count sets the stated shelf and moves COUNT_ON; the roll is written as a sentence into NOTES; the watermark moves to the newest id.

WHAT STAYS WITH THE AGENT IS THE JUDGEMENT. The note on every new row, the trail note on every amendment, the sentence on the roll and the version entry are typed by the agent into master/_fold_notes.json, and the tool refuses to fold without them. What leaves the agent is the syntax: nobody edits twelve thousand lines of a page to add a row again.

PROVED ON A COPY. The suite folds a four-row batch (a new sale, a fulfilment of a pending order, an oil count and a registration) into a copy of the book, checks every figure it moved, syncs it into a copy of the master, builds the phone payload from that and finds the new row on the phone’s ledger at the rolled shelf. It also proves the tool refuses a Modification and a note-less row. The sorter now sorts the book and syncs the block, and the cloud routine’s procedure is rewritten for this in docs/CLOUD_FOLD.md.
NO FIGURE MOVED. The book as it stands is untouched; this version is the tool and its proof.

t: THE BOOK LEAVES THE DESK
n: MOVE 2 OF THE REBUILD: THE BOOK IS DATA. The twenty-six ledger declarations this file used to carry as JavaScript, the rows, the opening, the stated stock, the count dates, the roster, the quotes, the watermark and the rest, now live in ledger/book.json, and the desk carries a generated copy of them in one block near the top of its script, rendered by tools/booksync.mjs. CI fails if the block is not the file. The prose that sat in comments beside the data, the roll of the stated stock, the oil counts, the 07 Aug orders, is kept as NOTES in the same file and rendered back as comments, so nothing written beside a figure is lost.

WHY THIS IS THE MOVE THAT MATTERS. The mirror went stale for two days because the book was a JavaScript file only a browser could evaluate. As a JSON document it is a copy any job can regenerate, the desk and the phone are builds of it, and the fold, from the next version, writes a record rather than editing twelve thousand lines of a page.
THE GATE HELD. The v338 master and this one, built on the same date, produce byte-identical payloads, and the extract read back from the running desk equals the file on every key. No figure moved.

t: THE POSITION LEAVES THE DESK
n: MOVE 1, SECOND SESSION: THE TRANSACTION MODEL AND THE LEDGER WALK ARE A MODULE. Eighteen row helpers, what a row has paid, delivered, deferred and pending, its state and its dates, what a lot has received and paid, and the ageing ladder, are lifted out of the desk verbatim into engine/position.mjs. recompute() becomes walk(): the same pass over a product’s rows, with the globals it set turned into the fields of a record and the facts it read gathered by posInputs(). Cover, the commitments the forecast and the phone read, and the phone’s own row shape and open-order key go with it.

THE DESK KEEPS EVERY NAME. Two hundred and fifty call sites are untouched because each helper is now a one-line wrapper; the walk assigns the same twenty-four globals from the record. Inlined by tools/engine.mjs beside the pricing engine, and CI proves both copies are their files.

THE GATE HELD AGAIN. The committed data.json, every field but the two stamps, is byte for byte what v337 produced: position, ledger, open orders, customers, actions and the board. The tests feed the module the desk’s own inputs on both books and the walk, the cover and the commitments come back equal.
NO FIGURE MOVED. A layout change to the code, not to the book.

t: THE PRICING ENGINE LEAVES THE DESK
n: MOVE 1 OF THE REBUILD: THE ENGINE IS A MODULE. The cost stack, the supplier taper, the markup curve, cogs, the rounding, the walk that holds the rate law, the ask at any size, the lot cost, the floor, the reference ladder and the board, eleven functions, are ported verbatim into engine/pricing.mjs as pure functions of explicit inputs. The desk keeps every name as a one-line wrapper and gains two functions, pxInputs() and pxPolicy(), which gather the book’s facts and the policy into the records the engine takes. Nothing prices on the desk any more.

ONE DEFINITION, PROVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. The desk cannot import a file, because it is one page that opens from disk and loads nothing, so the module is inlined between two markers by tools/engine.mjs and CI fails if the block is not the file to the byte. The tests import the module directly, with no browser, and then feed it the desk’s own inputs and compare: the asks and the floors at every size on both books are the desk’s exactly, and the committed data.json board is byte for byte what it was before the move.

THE DRAFTER PRICES THE EXACT SIZE FROM HERE. The pricing snapshot in the mirror now carries the inputs as well as the carded floors, so a fulfilment or a sale of 1.5 or 7 unit is judged against the floor at that size rather than the nearest carded size below it. An older snapshot still takes the old road.
NO FIGURE MOVED. This is a layout change to the code, not to the book: the shelf, the watermark and every row stand as v336 left them.

t: THE PHONE PRICE TAB, REBUILT AS ONE QUESTION AND ONE ANSWER
n: THE PRICE TAB ON THE PHONE LOOKED UNFINISHED BECAUSE IT WAS. Measured at 375px before this change: 3750px tall, three dropdowns, 345 characters of method prose, thirty-four party cards standing open under the board, and the board itself a bare table with no styling at all, browser default, beside three cards that said the same thing. A report in a dashboard’s clothes.

NOW: THE QUESTION, THE ANSWER, THE LADDER. The tab opens on What do I charge, the product as two pills, and one figure: the ask for the size chosen, its per-unit rate beside it, the floor and the room to move riding on it as chips rather than a sentence. The ladder below is the picker: tap a rung and the answer follows it, so there is one way to choose a size and nothing that duplicates it. A rung under its floor says so on the rung. One dropdown remains, to name a party and see what they usually pay; the full list of thirty-four folds behind a summary that still says how many. Measured after: 1275px, 75 characters of prose, one dropdown, no card open, no sideways overflow.

AND A WAY TO ACT ON IT. The answer carries one button, Record 1.5 unit at RM150, which carries the size and the total into the Record form and switches to it. Nothing is recorded until he taps Record there; it saves typing the two figures he has just read.

NO FIGURE CHANGED AND THE APP STILL COMPUTES NOTHING. Every ask and floor is read from data.json as before; the only arithmetic is the per-unit division beside an ask and the one subtraction for the room. The desk is untouched; this is the phone app alone.

t: THE QUEUE COMMITTED, A DATE CORRECTED, AND ONE ORDER MADE TWO
n: ONE ENTRY IN THE QUEUE, AND IT IS THE REPAIR WORKING. CA5-KER paid RM120 and took his unit on the 22nd, within the hour of the order going on the book. The cloud drafter drafted the fulfilment against the current mirror, the first it has managed since 20 Aug, and it is folded on his instruction to commit the queue. RM76 at 63.3%.
CM6-PJ BOUGHT ON THE 21ST, NOT THE 22ND. v334 dated the sale to the session for want of a day; he has given the day, and the row, its delivery and its payment move to 21 Aug. No figure changes.

THE CJ4-BJ 12.5 UNIT ORDER IS TWO TRANCHES, ON HIS WORD. RM400 for the first 6.25 unit, paid on the 20th and delivered on the 21st, is now a complete row at RM64 a unit, RM125 at 31.3% against the RM44 shelf. RM450 for the next 6.25 unit is its own pending row, undated, counting nowhere until it moves, RM72 a unit and RM70 under the ask. The book no longer shows a half-delivered order with RM450 owing; it shows a sale done and an order waiting.
THE SHELF ROLLS 26.25 TO 25.25 on the CA5-KER unit. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON stays at the 20th. QUEUE_COMMITTED moves to 2026-08-22T11:00:24.409Z.

t: ONE SALE, NOT TWO; A NEW CUSTOMER; AND TWO ORDERS ON THE BOOK
n: THE CS6-BS RM190 ENTRY REPLACED THE RM120 ONE, ON HIS WORD. v331 booked 1 unit for RM120 from the entry queued on the night of the 21st, and v332 folded the RM190 entry of the 22nd as a second sale beside it, with the question asked. The answer is that it was the same sale re-entered at the right figures, so the book now carries one row, 1.5 unit for RM190 paid and delivered on the 21st, restated in place with the trail recording both readings. The shelf gets 1 unit back.

CM6-PJ JOINS THE ROSTER, AT POSTCODE 460, AND TAKES 1 UNIT FOR RM120 PAID AND DELIVERED. Entered by him in the session and dated to the 22nd because no other day was given. RM20 above the ask at 1 unit and the dearest single-unit rate the book records; RM76 at 63.3% against the RM44 shelf. The name and the place went into the directory on the laptop; nothing here carries either.

TWO ORDERS GO ON THE BOOK PENDING. CA5-KER, 1 unit for RM120, an exact repeat of his only other order. CN6-WM, 1.5 unit for RM185, RM123.33 a unit, his dearest direct rate after four orders that had fallen at every step. Neither has paid or taken anything, so neither carries a date or counts anywhere yet. Both were typed in the session rather than queued, so no draft stands behind them.

THE SHELF STANDS AT 26.25, up 1 on the restatement and down 1 on the CM6-PJ unit. A roll and not a count; COUNT_ON stays at the 20th. QUEUE_COMMITTED does not move, because nothing here came through the queue.

t: THE HEADER STRIP FITS THE PHONE
n: THE FOUR CHIPS ABOVE THE TITLE WERE EACH BREAKING INTO THREE LINES ON A 375PX SCREEN, so the date read as a column and the cloud badge as a stack. The row now wraps between chips and never inside one: two lines on a phone, one on a desk. Seen in the Browser pane at phone width straight after v332 shipped. Nothing else moved and no figure changed.

t: FOUR ROWS FOLDED LATE, AND THE REASON THEY WERE LATE WAS A MIRROR NOBODY REFRESHED
n: FOUR ENTRIES FOLDED: THREE FULFILMENTS THE DRAFTER HAD REFUSED AND ONE SALE STILL WAITING FOR A TAP. CA4-DAM took delivery of his half unit and paid RM50 on the 20th. CN6-WM took half a unit on the 21st and the other 1.5 with RM150 on the 22nd. CJ4-BJ took 6.25 of his 12.5 unit on the 21st, leaving 6.25 unit and RM450 outstanding. CS6-BS took 1.5 unit for RM190 on the 21st, paid and delivered, his second row that day. All four draw on the RM44 lot.

THE FULFILMENTS WERE REFUSED BECAUSE THE CLOUD DRAFTER WAS READING A BOOK FROZEN AT v320. The drafter confirms an amendment against the open-order snapshot in the D1 mirror, and the mirror was last seeded on 20 Aug at 12:07 KL, before the eleven versions since it folded. It still carried the CA4-DAM order as 1 unit for RM100, had no CN6-WM order at all and keyed CJ4-BJ to an undated row, so every fulfilment queued after it was refused as matching no open order. The refusal said the order had been settled or folded, which is not what had happened, so the same three fulfilments were typed again on the 22nd: nine entries in the queue for three events and one sale. Nothing was double counted, because a refused entry never drafts; each event is folded once here.

THE FIX IS A STANDING STEP, NOT A ONE-OFF. The deploy job now re-seeds the mirror from the master it has just shipped, so the drafter reads the book as it stands rather than as it stood. The same staleness is why three drafts in a row costed salt at RM56 after the shelf had moved to RM44; from this build the drafter sees the current shelf too.

THE CS6-BS ROW WAS APPROVED BY INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY A TAP, on his word of 22 Aug to commit the whole queue, with the row, the cost and the flag shown in the same session, and the decision is recorded against the draft in those words. The drafter flagged the rate as 16.7% above his RM108.50 habit; RM126.67 a unit is his dearest yet and the flag is the right way round. At RM44 of cost it returns RM124 at 65.3%, not the RM106 at 55.8% the draft implied. If it was meant to replace the RM120 unit queued the night before rather than follow it, it is an amendment and should be said so.

THE SHELF ROLLS 36.5 TO 26.25 on the 10.25 unit that left across the four rows. A roll and not a count, so COUNT_ON stays at the 20th. QUEUE_COMMITTED moves to 2026-08-22T08:09:04.893Z, the newest id folded.

AND THE DESK GROWS A WAY BACK. Opened from the installed phone app, the desk filled a window with no address bar and no back button, and its Close control could not close a window the app had opened, so there was no way out. In the cloud build that control now reads App and returns to the phone app.

t: A SALE THAT BEAT THE BOARD, AND A COUNT THAT CONFIRMED THE SHELF RATHER THAN THE WALK
n: TWO ENTRIES FOLDED: A SALE THAT BEAT THE BOARD, AND A COUNT THAT CHANGED NOTHING. CS6-BS took 1 unit at RM120, paid and delivered on the 21st, and the oil shelf was counted by hand at ZERO for the second time. Both were approved on the phone under the gate.

RM120 IS THE FIRST ROW IN WEEKS TO CLEAR THE ASK RATHER THAN THE FLOOR. The ladder asks RM100 at 1 unit and the floor stands at RM65.32, so this is RM20 above the ask and RM54.68 above the floor. It matches his own high of 15 Jul rather than setting a new one, and it is 10.6% above the RM108 he averages across four salt orders. The drafter flagged it as unusually HIGH, which is a more useful thing for a flag to say than a warning about a cut: a customer has agreed to more than his habit and the next quote should know it.

THE COST WAS DRAFTED AT RM56 AGAIN AND IS FOLDED AT RM44, WHICH MAKES IT A PATTERN RATHER THAN A SLIP. The whole shelf is the 20 Aug lot at RM44 and no RM56 salt remains on it, so the unit returns RM76 at 63.3% rather than the RM64 at 53.3% the approval screen implied. That is the second draft in two days carrying a shelf rate that had already moved. A draft costs against STOCK_COST as it stood when it was written; the fold has to re-read it, and from here that is a standing step rather than a correction.

THE OIL COUNT MOVES NO FIGURE, AND ITS REASONING NEEDED CORRECTING RATHER THAN COPYING. Stated was already 0 and COUNT_ON.oil was already 20 Aug, so a second zero moves neither. The approval screen said nothing is unaccounted for, which is true against the STATED figure and false against the LEDGER: oil walks 5 unit of opening plus 100 bought less 71 sold, so 34 unit are still missing from a shelf now looked at twice and found empty. Counting again confirms the shelf, not the walk. The gap is the finding and it is unchanged.

THE SHELF ROLLS 37.5 TO 36.5 on the one unit that left. A roll and not a count, so salt’s COUNT_ON stays at the 20th. 13.88 unit are owed out, leaving 22.62 free to sell. QUEUE_COMMITTED moves to 2026-08-20T18:12:16.478Z, the newer of the two ids folded.

t: THE BOARD FITS THE PHONE, AND THE FLOOR IT PRINTS IS THE ONE THE PHONE PRINTS
n: THE BOARD DID NOT FIT ON THE PHONE, AND THE COLUMN BEING CUT OFF WAS THE ASK. Measured in Chromium at 375px, the five columns came to 406px inside the 325px a card gives, so the ASK sat half past the edge and the FLOOR was entirely off it. The ask is the number he reads to a customer standing in front of him, so it is the last thing on this desk that should need a sideways scroll. Two changes, both small: the rate and the margin under the ask go on separate lines rather than one, which takes that column from 160px to 84px, and the board alone gets 5px gutters instead of 8px. The table is now 325px in a 325px box, nothing off the edge on either book.

IT WAS ALREADY MUCH BETTER THAN WHAT IT REPLACED, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING. The four-rung board of v324 was 801px in the same 325px box, 476px off the edge. Collapsing it to one ladder at v326 cut that to 81px without anybody aiming at the phone, and this closes the rest. The other tables on the tab still scroll in their own boxes at 342px to 638px over, and that stays deliberate: they are genuinely wide and nobody prices off them at a market stall.

AND THE SCREENSHOT SHOWED A SECOND FLOOR, WHICH IS THE MORE SERIOUS OF THE TWO FINDINGS. priceLadder struck its own floor as cogs times the policy markup. That agreed with floorTotal from 1.5 unit up and disagreed below it, because floorTotal ALSO lifts the floor to what serving the lot costs, and at 0.5 and 1 unit that bites. So the desk board printed RM30.59 at half a unit while the phone, which reads floorTotal through the payload, printed RM40.99 for the same size. Two floors for one lot. floorTotal answers now and the markup beside it is derived back from that answer rather than assumed, so a floor lifted by the cost of serving reports the markup it actually represents.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED, AND THE SWEEP SAYS SO. All fifteen tabs measured at 375px before and after: page overflow ZERO on every one, no clipped text anywhere, and the count of text under 11px unchanged at 174 against 171 before this session began, the three extra being the product chips on the three rows folded at v329. That sub-11px text is a standing gap against the rule set when the desk was tuned for portrait, it is almost all on Ledger at 9px, and it predates this work rather than arriving with it.

t: THREE ROWS FOLDED, AND THE CHEAPEST SALT THIS BOOK HAS EVER SOLD COST RM44 RATHER THAN RM56
n: THREE APPROVED ROWS FOLDED, AND ALL THREE WERE APPROVED WITH FLAGS SHOWING. CM3-OKR took 12.5 unit for RM600, paid and delivered on the day. CN6-WM agreed 2 unit for RM150 and CS6-PER 6.25 unit for RM350, both with nothing paid and nothing moved, so both are PENDING, carry no date and count nowhere. Every one of the three was drafted under the gate, put in front of him with what was wrong with it, and taken anyway. That is the gate working: it is there to make a decision informed, not to make it for him.

THE CM3-OKR ROW IS BOOKED AT RM44 OF COST AND THE APPROVAL SCREEN SAID RM56, WHICH IS THE ONE FIGURE CHANGED IN THIS FOLD. The drafter costed it at 10:42 against STOCK_COST as it then stood and told him it lost money on every unit. It did not. The shelf was COUNTED AT ZERO that morning and the 50 unit lot landed at RM44 the same day, so no RM56 salt existed for the order to draw. At RM44 it returns RM50 at 8.3% rather than losing RM100 at minus 16.7%. He took the trade on the WORSE number, so this corrects the drafter and not his judgement. THE GENERAL LESSON IS TIMING: a draft carries the shelf as it was when it was written, and this one sat four hours while the shelf underneath it changed completely.

RM48 A UNIT IS THE CHEAPEST SALT THIS BOOK HAS EVER SOLD. The previous low on an ordinary sale was RM60, set on 08 Jul and matched on the 17th; the only rates below it anywhere are two REBATE rows at RM46.99 and RM47, and a rebate is goods at cost rather than a price. It is also under floor by RM164.75 and RM360 under the ladder ask. Reported and not repriced, as every under-floor row on this book is.

BOTH PENDING ROWS ARE TO ASSOCIATES, WHICH CHANGES HOW THEY SHOULD BE READ. CN6-WM at RM75 and CS6-PER at RM56 are wholesale rates to people who resell, not retail concessions. CN6-WM has fallen RM25 a unit across three direct orders while doubling his size, and his downstream bucket clears RM67.69 to RM125. CS6-PER at RM56 would be RM4 under his own previous floor. Judge either against what they can get for it rather than against what a retail buyer pays.

ONE OF THE FLAGS HAS ALREADY EXPIRED, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING ABOUT FLAGS. The drafter told him RM150 was under the delivered floor of RM165.98. That was the v326 board; on the ladder as it now stands the 2 unit floor is RM122.36 and the row CLEARS it by RM27.64. A flag is a reading taken at a moment, and this book changed its pricing basis twice between the draft and the fold. The row note says so rather than repeating a figure that has moved.

THE SHELF ROLLS 50 TO 37.5 on the 12.5 unit that actually left. A ROLL AND NOT A COUNT, so COUNT_ON stays at the 20th: nobody has looked at the shelf since the morning. 13.88 unit are still owed out to CE4-CHE, CE4-AD and CJ4-BJ, leaving 23.62 free to sell. If both pending rows move, 8.25 unit go with them and both are covered. QUEUE_COMMITTED moves to 2026-08-20T11:14:56.780Z, the newest of the three ids folded.

t: THE PHONE WAS QUOTING THE RETIRED TIER BOARD, AND UNDER THE DESK AT EVERY SIZE THAT MATTERED
n: THE PHONE WAS STILL QUOTING THE RETIRED TIER BOARD, AND IT WAS QUOTING IT UNDER THE DESK. phonePayload built its board out of PRICE_TIERS, which cappedBoard() solves with its own anchors, its own grid and its own interpolation. v326 made the desk quote one derived ladder and v327 gave that ladder the supplier’s taper; neither touched that line. So for two commits the desk and the phone were two engines again, which is the exact fault this payload exists to prevent, and it was introduced by the commit that removed the first engine rather than by anything the phone does.

THE GAP, MEASURED, AND IT RAN ONE WAY. Salt disagreed at eight of ten sizes and the phone was always the cheaper: RM140 against RM150 at 1.5 unit, RM410 against RM430 at 5, and RM900 against RM960 at 12.5. Oil disagreed at every size and by more: RM440 against RM750 at 50 unit, where the tier price also sat RM158 BELOW oil’s own floor, so the phone was showing an ask it would have flagged as under floor in the same panel.

ONE LADDER MEANS ONE ROW. The board the phone carries is now priceLadder() per size, per product, priced with that product’s own book selected. It stays an ARRAY because that is the shape the app maps over, and because a future second row should have to be a real second thing rather than a tier that is no longer one. The app reads row zero rather than hunting for the tier coded T2 and falling back: the fallback is what kept the panel alive and wrong through two commits, and a fallback that quietly carries a panel hides a fault instead of showing it.

AND THE SAME CHECK CAUGHT A SECOND FAULT, ON THE OIL BOARD, THAT NOBODY HAD LOOKED FOR. The desk asserts that the rate per unit may never RISE with size, and rounding the ask UP to the ten broke it: at about RM15 a unit the grid is a twentieth of an order, so 20 unit landed on RM300 at RM15.00 while 25 unit rounded RM375 up to RM380 at RM15.20, and a customer taking a quarter more oil paid more for every unit of it. Salt never showed it because its rates are seven times larger and the same step is a much smaller share, and the v326 and v327 checks only ever walked salt. ladderWalk() now walks the board forward and, where rounding up would lift the rate above the size below, steps the ask down one ten and no further, and only while it still clears the floor. Oil moves at six sizes, RM750 to RM720 at 50 unit; SALT DOES NOT MOVE AT ALL. The test added with this commit walks both books, which is the part that stops it coming back.

AND A CLAIM IN v327 IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN LEFT TO AGE. That entry said the collected and delivered floors are now the same number because cogs carries no delivery. True above 1 unit and not below it: floorTotal still lifts the floor to what SERVING the lot costs where that bites, so at 0.5 and 1 unit the delivered floor is RM40.99 and RM65.32 against a collected RM30.59 and RM61.18. The delivery saving survives at exactly the sizes where a delivery is the largest share of the order.

t: THE VOLUME DISCOUNT GIVEN IS NOW PROPORTIONATE TO THE VOLUME DISCOUNT RECEIVED
n: THE TAPER IS NO LONGER A NUMBER SOMEBODY PICKED. IT IS THE SUPPLIER’S OWN. His instruction: the markup must be proportionate to the purchase rate. v326 slid the ask from a stated 2.00x to a stated 1.33x and nothing tied the SHAPE of that slide to anything. Now the rate at which the ask falls with size is the rate at which SA5-BTR’s quoted rate falls with size, fitted by least squares over every tier of the live quote and refitted the moment he requotes. buyTaper() does the fit and reports its r-squared on the tab rather than hiding it.

THE MEASUREMENT IS CLEAN AND IT CONVICTS THE OLD BOARD. SA5-BTR quotes 6.25 unit at RM56 and 100 at RM43, and across all five tiers the rate falls as size to the power of -0.100, r-squared 0.96. The lots actually bought fit -0.107, so the quote and the history agree. His own selling ladder fits -0.119, meaning he has been handing back volume discount about a fifth faster than he receives it. The v326 board was far worse at -0.253, two and a half times the supplier’s taper, and the 2.00x to 0.65x variant considered on the way was -0.186. Both are now ruled out by measurement rather than by argument.

ONLY THE LEVEL IS TYPED, AND IT IS HELD. anchorX pins the curve at 0.958x at 2.5 unit, chosen so the ladder returns what this book has actually been charging. So this commit changes the DISTRIBUTION of the price across sizes and not the amount: under 2 unit falls about 2%, 2 to 5 unit falls about 3%, and over 5 unit rises about 4%, which is exactly the over-discounting the fit found. Charging more is a separate decision and it is this one number.

FLOOR AND CEILING BECOME BOUNDS RATHER THAN RUNGS. 0.33x and 2.00x now clamp the curve instead of being the points it must reach. On this cost neither binds at any board size, the ask running 1.301x at 0.5 unit down to 0.666x at 12.5. The old arrangement, where the ask slid all the way onto the floor at the largest size, quoted the refusal price to the biggest customer, which is not what a floor is for.

THE BOOK’S AVERAGE PRICE WAS MISSTATED AT v325 AND v326 AND IS CORRECTED HERE. Both entries said RM93.51 a unit. That figure is revTotal over soldKg, which divides revenue net of pending by the quantity PHYSICALLY DRAWN, and the two are not the same base: soldKg is 209.7 against 229.52 unit of priced quantity, so the average came out 9% high. On one base it is RM85.44. Nothing in the arithmetic of either commit depended on it, but it was quoted in the reasoning for both, and a figure used to argue a decision has to be right even when nothing computes from it.

t: ONE LADDER, GRADED BY SIZE: 2.00x AT HALF A UNIT DOWN TO 1.33x AT TWELVE AND A HALF
n: FOUR RUNGS BECOME ONE, AND THE ONE IS GRADED BY SIZE. His instruction of 20 Aug: a floor of 1.33x, an average of 1.67x and a ceiling of 2.00x, with the ask sliding from the ceiling at the smallest size to the floor at the largest. Floor, Good, Great and Ceiling are gone from the board. What prints now is the size, the cogs, the markup that size is asked, the ask, and the floor underneath it. These are markups on cost the way he states the measure, (sales less cogs) over cogs, so 2.00x is THREE times cogs and 1.33x is 2.33 times.

IT IS INTERPOLATED IN THE LOG OF SIZE, AND THAT IS NOT A PRESENTATION CHOICE. Log spacing puts the stated 1.67 average exactly at 2.5 unit, the geometric middle of the range, and it holds gross margin between 50% and 55% from 1 unit all the way to 12.5. A linear gradient does neither: it lands 1.67 at 6.5 unit and lets margin sag in the middle. Outside the two anchors the markup is CLAMPED rather than extrapolated, so a 50 unit lot is asked the 12.5 markup and not a markup the policy never stated.

THE BASIS MOVED FROM LOT COST TO COGS, AND THE FLOOR HAD TO MOVE WITH IT. The old rungs were struck on the lot cost, the salt after the leak plus one delivery. The ladder is struck on cogs, the landed RM46. Leaving floorTotal on the old basis put the 12.5 floor at RM1,455.90 against an ask of RM1,340, which is a board that refuses its own price. One basis, one ladder. The collected floor is the same number as the delivered one now, because cogs carries no delivery; the saving shows up in the margin instead.

ASKS ROUND UP TO THE TEN, ON HIS INSTRUCTION, AND THE FLOOR IS NEVER ROUNDED. Up rather than down, so the ladder is never quoted under itself: 1 unit solves at RM131.36 and asks RM140. The floor stays exact, because rounding a refusal line down puts the floor under itself and rounding it up makes it dearer than the policy states.

59 OF 76 LIVE ROWS NOW SIT UNDER FLOOR, AGAINST 16 BEFORE, AND NOTHING WAS REPRICED TO SAY SO. That is what a floor at 2.33 times landed cost means on a book whose priced rows have averaged RM85.44 a unit. The desk reports and does not clamp, so every one of those rows stands exactly as it was traded. Read it as a statement about the new policy rather than about the trades: they were struck against a floor a quarter of this one.

THE STATED 1.67 AVERAGE IS NOT WHAT THIS BOOK WOULD REALISE, AND THE DESK SAYS SO ON THE TAB. ladderRealised() weights the curve by the salt actually traded and returns 1.54, because the average sits at 2.5 unit and roughly half the volume here goes out in lots over 5 unit where the gradient is thinnest. It is computed rather than asserted so it follows the mix instead of going stale. Re-anchor the curve if 1.67 is wanted as the realised figure rather than as a point on it.

EVERYTHING THAT QUOTES NOW QUOTES THE LADDER, WHICH IS THE POINT OF DOING IT THIS WAY. enginePrice returns the ladder ask, so pxQuote, the board, the charts, the any-size panel and the saved sheet all follow one definition. The frozen tier cards no longer win in pxQuote and the sheet no longer prints them: three tier buttons became one Save the ladder, because a printed card and a derived ladder are two prices for the same lot and the card is the one the customer keeps. The tier multiplier is not applied and the tier select is gone from the panel. The ask the retired engine would have made is still returned and shown beside the ladder, so the day the two disagree is visible rather than argued about.

t: THE CHEAPEST LOT ON THE BOOK LANDS, AND THE COST BASIS IS REBUILT ON THREE STATED ASSUMPTIONS
n: 50 UNIT AT RM44 LANDED, PAID AND RECEIVED, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST SALT THIS BOOK HAS EVER BOUGHT. RM2,200 for 50 unit settles the row that stood pending since the morning, RM3 under the RM47 hundred-unit lot of 28 Jul that held the record. It is now the newest received lot, so replacement cost falls RM56 to RM44. STOCK_COST rolls to 44 and STATED_STOCK from 0 to 50, because the shelf was counted at ZERO that morning and the lot arrived after the count. A roll is not a count: COUNT_ON is untouched and nobody has looked at the shelf since. 13.88 unit are owed already, 3 to CE4-CHE, 5 to CE4-AD and 5.88 to CJ4-BJ, so free to sell is 36.12.

THREE COST ASSUMPTIONS WERE STATED AND ALL THREE ARE NOW IN THE BOOK, WHICH IS THE PART TO READ TWICE. Freight goes from RM20 a lot to RM100. Delivery goes from RM5 an order to RM50 for every three orders, RM16.67 each. SHRINK_ATTRIB goes from a half to 0.33, so the cost basis carries a third of the observed leak and margin absorbs the other two thirds. None of these was measured here; each is his stated figure, and each is one constant that can be moved back.

THE NET IS A COST BASIS DOWN RM10.51 A UNIT, AND IT IS NOT ONE MOVE. Effective cost goes RM65.92 to RM55.41. Goods alone go RM63.89 to RM48.65: the rate fell RM12, the 50 unit lot spreads freight four times thinner than a 12.5 lot does even at five times the cost, and the leak charged into the price falls from 9.85% to 5.46% on the lower attribution. Pulling the other way, delivery goes RM2.03 to RM6.76 a unit. A ladder is not a single lever and this commit moved four of them.

THE FREIGHT ASSUMPTION RESTATES HISTORY AND IS THE ONE TO CHALLENGE FIRST. freightPerLot is spread over every lot ever received rather than traced to one, so cost of sales freight goes from RM194.86 to RM974.30 across the whole book and reported gross profit falls RM779.44 with it. Nothing about the past changed; an assumption about it did. If RM100 was the cost of collecting THIS lot rather than the standing rate, this is the line to move and the figure to put back to 20.

WHAT THE BOARD NOW ASKS, AND WHAT IT WILL NOT REACH. A 2 unit Tier II order goes from RM180 to RM170. Asked what average rate returns 1.5x on cost of goods, the answer is RM115 a unit against RM46 landed, and the book has averaged RM85.44 a unit, being revenue net of pending over the quantity that revenue was struck on. It is above the desk’s own ceiling, which is double the lot cost, at every size from 2 unit up: RM113.98 at 2 unit and RM99.98 at 12.5. Small orders can carry it and bulk cannot, and 48% of the volume on this book has gone out in lots over 5 unit at RM75.56 a unit.

t: A RATE IS NOW CHECKED WHERE EVERY ENTRY PASSES, AND THE PHONE CAN RESTATE OR CANCEL AN ORDER
n: THE CHECK MOVED TO THE ONE PLACE EVERY ENTRY PASSES: THE MOMENT IT IS TYPED. Two rate faults reached this book on the same day and only one was caught. The RM115 oil unit was stopped by the approval screen, which is what that screen is for. The Modification that restated an order to 5 unit for RM50 was not, because a Modification does not go through the gate: no drafter put a rate beside it, no approval screen showed RM10 a unit next to RM56 of cost, and the only thing between it and the ledger was a person reading it. It got as far as the fold. So the check now runs on the phone, before anything is queued, whatever road the entry takes afterwards.
