IT SAYS WHAT IT SEES AND DECIDES NOTHING. It divides a total just typed by a quantity just typed, and compares that against rates already in data.json which the desk computed. It sets no price, writes nothing into the entry, and blocks nothing: an unusual rate is often a real decision and this book has deliberately sold below cost before. It is also SILENT almost always, which is the harder half. A check that speaks on every entry is a check that gets tapped through, so it says nothing unless the rate is outside everything the book has ever seen for that product, or a quarter off what that party actually pays.

PROVED AGAINST BOTH FAULTS AND AGAINST AN ORDINARY SALE. Half a unit to CA4-DAM for RM50, his standing RM100, passes in silence. The same order typed as 5 unit for RM50 reads "RM10/unit. Salt on this book has never gone below RM46.99. CA4-DAM averages RM103.33/unit; this is 90.32% below that." A unit of oil at RM115 reads "against a high of RM13 anywhere on this book". Both of today’s faults, caught before they leave the phone.

THE PHONE CAN NOW RESTATE AND CANCEL AN ORDER, WHICH COMPLETES THE AMENDMENT SET. The CA4-DAM restatement had to be made at the desk because the app offered only the three fulfilment kinds. Restate seeds its fields with the order as it stands, so a change is a change from something visible rather than from a blank, and Cancel takes no figures at all. Neither touches the cash and unit boxes, which are hidden rather than merely ignored.

AND THE FORM TELLS THE TRUTH ABOUT WHICH ROAD EACH ONE TAKES. A Fulfilment and a Cancellation are drafted and come back for a tap. A Modification is refused by the drafter BY DESIGN, because what changed is a judgement rather than which row, and is folded by a person. The road note changes with the kind and says so in terms, including the part that matters: nothing will put a rate beside a restatement before it is folded, so read the figures before sending it. Saying "goes through the gate" over a Modification would have been the more comfortable copy and the more dangerous one.

t: THREE CORRECTIONS ON HIS WORD, AND THE IMPOSSIBLE FIGURE WAS THE FOLD RATHER THAN THE SHELF
n: CJ4-BJ PAID RM400 AND TOOK NOTHING, WHICH IS WHAT HIS ENTRY SAID ALL ALONG. v322 folded it as 6.25 unit delivered, took the shelf to minus 6.25, and wrote a long comment about an irreconcilable contradiction between the count and the ledger. THERE WAS NO CONTRADICTION. The entry read "marked paid in full" in the line a person sees and carried 6.25 unit in the payload the ledger reads, because the app built those two from different sources and never checked they agreed. The shelf is back to the count of zero, where it never stopped belonging.

THE LESSON IS NOT THAT A FIGURE WAS WRONG, IT IS WHICH DIRECTION IT POINTED. An impossible number appeared and every word written about it reasoned about the SHELF: which stock might be missing, whether a lot had landed unrecorded, whether the count was mistimed. The impossible number was evidence about the FOLD. Salt cannot go below nothing, so a negative shelf was never a fact about salt; it was a fact about the last thing that touched the figure. Read a number that cannot exist as a question about its most recent writer, and check that before reaching for the world.

THE APP CAN NO LONGER SAY TWO THINGS AT ONCE. The amendment form built its human-readable line from the selected kind and its payload from the input boxes, which is two sources for one statement and the exact shape of fault this desk keeps writing tests about. The kind now decides the figures: Paid moves no salt and Handed over moves no cash, whatever is left sitting in the other box, and that box is greyed so the form shows what the kind means rather than only enforcing it on submit. Three assertions guard it.

CA4-DAM E111 IS RESTATED TO HALF A UNIT FOR RM50, AND THE ENTRY SAID FIVE. Five unit for RM50 is RM10 a unit against a book whose salt has never left the RM60 to RM120 band; half a unit for RM50 is RM100, his rate for the tenth order running. Corrected on his word before folding. A MODIFICATION IS THE ONE AMENDMENT THE GATE DOES NOT COVER, because what changed is a judgement rather than which row, so no drafter put a rate beside it and no approval screen showed RM10 a unit next to RM56 of cost. The RM115 oil unit was caught exactly that way; this one was caught by a person reading it, which is the fallback the gate exists to lean on less, not to replace.

THE SA5-BTR LOT IS RE-AGREED AT 50 UNIT FOR RM2,200, AND HE TOOK THE TIER THE LADDER ACTUALLY REWARDS. It replaces 25 unit at RM1,300: RM44 a unit against RM52, twice the salt for RM900 more, and RM3 under what the 100 unit lot of 28 Jul really cost. v321 said where the discount had moved and this is the answer to it: the new ladder gives RM2 a unit at the 25 step and RM6 at the 50, so taking the 25 would have spent RM1,300 to save RM50 against a size that saves RM400. It is still PENDING and still books nothing: no cash has moved and no salt has landed, so every floor still reads off the 18 Aug lot at RM56 until it arrives. When it does, the 8 unit owed to CE4-CHE and CE4-AD are the first call on it.

t: TWO FULFILMENTS FOLDED THROUGH THE GATE, AND THE SHELF IS LEFT AT MINUS 6.25 ON PURPOSE
n: THE FIRST AMENDMENTS EVER TO REACH THIS LEDGER THROUGH THE GATE. Both were tapped on the phone, drafted against the desk’s own ovKey, approved, and folded here. Until this week an amendment was refused on the ground that which row it amends is a judgement, which was true of an entry arriving as free text and stopped being true the moment the phone made him pick a specific open order. Fulfilment is the commonest entry this book takes and it was the last thing that still needed the laptop. It does not any more.

CJ4-BJ TOOK HALF HIS ORDER: RM400 AND 6.25 UNIT ON THE 20TH. The 12.5 unit at RM850 that had stood pending since 07 Aug is now half done on both sides, with RM450 and 6.25 unit outstanding. THE PRICE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED FOR A FORTNIGHT WAS ANSWERED BY MOVING IT. The note asked whether to hold the relationship at RM68 a unit or take it to RM955 and find out; he held it. The same reasoning applies unchanged to the half still to come, and it is still recorded rather than repriced.

CE4-AD PAID RM435 IN FULL AND TOOK NOTHING, SO FIVE UNIT ARE NOW OWED IN SALT. That is the second deferred delivery on the book beside CE4-CHE’s three, and it takes the total owed out to EIGHT UNIT AGAINST A SHELF THAT COUNTED ZERO THAT MORNING. It is the stronger position and the weaker one at once: the cash is banked at RM87 a unit against a lot agreed at RM52 and re-quoted hours later at RM50, so the margin improves whichever of those actually arrives, and five unit is a larger promise than three with nothing behind it. The cost is carried at RM56, the last RECEIVED lot, and it is EXPECTED to be wrong. Those units will draw whatever lands, which is the same reason v321 left the RM1,300 lot at RM1,300.

THE SHELF NOW READS MINUS 6.25 AND IT IS LEFT THAT WAY DELIBERATELY. Salt cannot go below nothing, so this is not a quantity: it is a contradiction between two records, and both of them are his. Either the SA5-BTR 25 unit lot has landed and its fulfilment was never written down, which is much the likelier and would put the shelf at 18.75, or the count was taken after those units went out. THE DESK WILL NOT GUESS WHICH AND WILL NOT PLUG IT. A plugged figure is a question that has stopped being asked, and this book has spent two versions learning that a gap left visible gets closed and a gap papered over does not. Mark the lot received and it squares by itself. COUNT_ON stays at 20 Aug, because this is a roll and only a count moves that.

THIS FOLD WAS BUILT ON v320 WHILE THE CLOUD AGENT WAS BUILDING v321 ON THE SAME BASE, AND BOTH SURVIVED. The agent folded the SA5-BTR re-quote and pushed; this session had the two fulfilments in hand locally. They touch different parts of the book, purchases and quotes against sales, so nothing was lost: the local work was rebuilt ON TOP of v321 rather than merged over it, and the re-quote, its flag on the RM1,300 lot and its dated clause are all intact. THE VERSION NUMBER WAS THE REAL CASUALTY. Three commits earlier in the day carried v323 and v324 in their SUBJECT LINES while never bumping evolution[0], so the book stayed at v320 and the build kept saying so. Those numbers never existed in the ledger and are not reserved; the changelog runs v316 to v321 unbroken and this is v322. A version is what the book says it is, not what a commit message claims.

t: SA5-BTR RE-QUOTES EVERY TIER DOWN, AND THE LOT AGREED THIS MORNING IS ALREADY RM50 ABOVE HIS OWN LADDER
n: A NEW LADDER FROM SA5-BTR, AUTHORITATIVE FROM THE 20TH, AND IT IS CHEAPER AT EVERY SIZE THIS DESK BUYS. 6.25 unit at RM350, 12.5 at RM650, 25 at RM1,250, 50 at RM2,200 and 100 at RM4,300, which is RM56, RM52, RM50, RM44 and RM43 a unit. A 6.25 UNIT TIER APPEARS FOR THE FIRST TIME, at the RM56 the 12.5 unit step used to cost, and the 50 unit tier goes back to exactly the RM2,200 quoted on 10 Jul before it moved dearer. RM43 at 100 unit is cheaper than any rate this desk has ever been quoted or has ever paid. WHERE THE DISCOUNT SITS HAS MOVED, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT CHANGES A DECISION. The old ladder gave RM4 a unit at the 25 step and RM4 again at the 50. This one gives RM2 at the 25 step and RM6 at the 50, so 50 unit is where it pays and 25 has stopped paying much.

NOT ONE FLOOR ON THIS DESK MOVES, AND IT LOOKS AS THOUGH IT SHOULD. Replacement cost is read off the newest lot actually RECEIVED, which is still the 12.5 unit that landed on 18 Aug at RM56; pxCost falls back to the quote only when no lot exists. A quote is what salt WOULD cost and a floor is built on what the shelf DID cost, so nothing here reaches a price until a lot is recorded as a buy. pxQuoteRate DOES NOT MOVE EITHER, and that is a coincidence rather than a bug: it takes the DEAREST tier, which was RM56 at 12.5 unit and is now RM56 at 6.25. The ladder got cheaper everywhere while its ceiling stood still. Proved rather than asserted: replacement cost, effective cost, every floor, boardHeadroom at 17 under floor and 0 under cost, and parityScan at no rows all read identical before and after.

THE 25 UNIT LOT AGREED THIS MORNING IS NOW RM50 ABOVE HIS OWN QUOTE, AND ITS FIGURES WERE LEFT ALONE. v320 folded 25 unit at RM1,300 against the 14 Jul ladder, approved on the phone; the re-quote prices that size at RM1,250. The row keeps RM1,300, because that is what was agreed and approved, and a quote arriving after a handshake does not rewrite it. What is added is a flag on the row saying so, and the clause in the v320 note that read the old ladder as a live fact is now dated to that morning. NOTHING IS LOST BY RE-OPENING IT: the lot is PENDING, so there is no payment to claw back and no stock to return, and the same salt at the new 50 unit tier is RM44 against the RM52 on the row. Re-agree, replace or let it stand: his call, and the desk states the gap rather than closing it.

THE 150 UNIT PLAN FOLLOWS THE RULE, NOT THE OLD NUMBER. SOURCING_PLAN is costed at the largest tier quoted, and that tier fell from RM47 to RM43, so the assumed rate follows it down and the stated lot goes from RM7,050 to RM6,450. The second half of the old wording had to go with it: RM47 was also the rate actually paid on 28 Jul, and those two facts have now parted company. RM43 has been quoted and never paid, so the plan now says a rate on offer rather than a rate achieved.

t: THE 25 UNIT TIER IS AGREED AND THE BOOK MOVES BY NOTHING, FOLDED BY THE FIRST RUN WITH NO LAPTOP ON IT
n: 25 UNIT AGREED WITH SA5-BTR AT RM52, AND NOT ONE FIGURE ON THE DESK MOVES. RM1,300 for 25 unit, approved on the phone and folded here as a PENDING purchase with no date, because nothing has been paid and nothing has arrived. PENDING COUNTS NOWHERE AND THAT IS THE POINT: poCash and poRecvKg both return nought for it, so it raises no payable, moves no cash, adds no stock and stays out of the weighted average. Stock, cost, margin, receivables and every floor read exactly as they did at v319. IT IS THE QUOTED 25 UNIT TIER, TAKEN FOR THE FIRST TIME. RM1,300 is the step standing on the 14 Jul ladder to the ringgit, RM100 cheaper than the same salt bought as two 12.5 unit lots at the RM56 both August lots carried, and dearer per unit than the 50 and 100 unit tiers beneath it.

NOTHING ROLLED, AND A DAY ON WHICH NOTHING MOVED SHOULD LOOK LIKE ONE. STATED_STOCK stays at the ZERO counted by hand on the 20th, COUNT_ON stays at that date because a fold never moves it, and STOCK_COST holds at 56 on the 18 Aug lot. An agreed lot is not a receipt, so replacement cost is still read off the newest lot actually RECEIVED; when this one lands it takes that job over at RM52 and every floor on the desk falls with it, which is a change to watch for rather than one to write early. The shelf it is coming to is empty and still owes 3 unit to CE4-CHE, paid for on the 18th with nothing behind the obligation.

THE FIRST FOLD RUN WITH NO LAPTOP ANYWHERE ON THE PATH. The row was drafted by the Worker on arrival, approved on the phone, and folded here by the scheduled cloud agent reading master/_to_fold.json. The agent holds no credential, by design: it cannot reach D1, the queue or Cloudflare, so GitHub Actions stages the approved rows in front of it and deploys, verifies and marks them committed behind it. What stays with a person is the half that is a judgement, which is this prose and the note on the row.

t: THE PHONE STOPS BEING A NOTEPAD: EVERY ENTRY THAT BELONGS ON IT, THE LEDGER TO READ, AND THE COUNT LEADING THE PAGE
n: RECONCILIATION IS A DAILY DISCIPLINE FROM TODAY, AND THE APP LEADS WITH IT. The count banner sits above the action list on the first screen, one line per product, and says whether the shelf was looked at or merely rolled forward. IT IS THE ONLY THING ON THAT PAGE THAT GOES WRONG BY BEING IGNORED. Every other panel is wrong only when a figure is wrong; a shelf is wrong the moment nobody looks, and it stays wrong QUIETLY, because the roll reports whatever the arithmetic last said. Twelve days of exactly that cost 5.05 unit of salt and 19 of oil in the week to the 20th. COUNT_ON IS NOW MACHINE-READABLE, one date per product, and a roll never moves it: only a count does. That distinction is the whole value of the field, because STATED_STOCK changes on most commits and this changes when somebody looks.

THE COUNT FORM RECONCILES BEFORE IT SENDS. Three cells: what the book says, what you counted, and the drift between them. The drift is the one subtraction this app performs and it is deliberately not a price, so it breaks no rule that matters: it exists so the gap is a thing you SAW rather than a thing you discover a week later. The desk still decides what the drift means when the count is folded, and a count still always wins there.

FOUR RECORD MODES INSTEAD OF ONE. A trade, an amendment against any open order, a party registration, and the three stock entries: count, loss and lost demand. THE AMENDMENT IS THE ONE THAT WAS MOST MISSING. Fulfilment is the commonest entry this desk makes, thirty-nine on the book, and until today it needed the laptop; that is why two of the three entries queued on 17 Aug took the old road. The phone now lists every open order with what is unpaid and what is still to move, pre-fills the outstanding amounts, and sends the desk’s own orderKey untouched rather than composing one. EVERY FORM SAYS WHICH ROAD ITS ENTRY TAKES. A trade is drafted and comes back for a tap; the other three are refused by the drafter BY DESIGN and folded by a person. Saying so on the form is the difference between a queue that looks broken and one you understand.

THE LEDGER IS READABLE ON THE PHONE, AND IT CARRIES NO COST AND NO MARGIN. All 111 rows, newest first, filterable by product, party and state, with pending rows at the top because a phone is read from the top. The omission is deliberate and it is the leak gate’s doing: phonePayloadLeaks() bans every per-unit cost from this payload because the page is public by decision, and a margin is a cost stated backwards. So the phone answers what was traded and what is owed, and the laptop answers what it earned. /desk STAYS, and the reason is the same one data.json exists for: the moment the phone prices anything itself there are two engines and they drift.

THE STATE OF EACH ROW IS DECIDED BY THE DESK, AND THE FIRST VERSION PROVED WHY. Written in the app from raw fields, it was wrong three times on the first look at real rows. It read a PURCHASE with a seller’s ruler, so a lot paid for and not yet landed said "you owe stock" when they owe it to you. It read receivedQty raw, which is ABSENT on most lots and means fully received, inventing 68 unit of obligations from lots that landed in July. Then it read cash raw, which is absent on the older lots where status:’paid’ is what says they were settled, reporting RM4,650 of supplier debt paid off in June. Three goes at one mistake in an afternoon, and all three are the same mistake: looking at the desk’s fields instead of calling the desk’s helpers. txPaid, txEffDeliv, txDeferKg, txAdvance, poCash and poRecvKg now decide it, in the master, and the phone only puts a word to the answer.

t: BOTH SHELVES COUNTED AT ZERO, THE COUNT FOUND THREE UNIT THE LEDGER HAD LOST, AND THE THIN MARGIN IS THE LEAK AND NOT THE TRADING
n: THE COUNT PAID FOR ITSELF THE MOMENT IT WAS TAKEN, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR TAKING ONE. Asked what had become of the 8.05 unit the roll claimed, he said CE4-CHE had taken 3.25 of his 6.25 rather than the 0.25 the book carried. Three unit had moved and nothing had recorded it. IT IS WRITTEN UP AS AN AMENDMENT TO HIS ROW, WHICH IS WHAT IT IS. A new row would have double-counted the RM500 he settled in full on the 18th, and that distinction is the whole reason the drafter refuses amendments rather than guessing at them. The trail now carries both tranches, a quarter unit on the 18th and three on the 20th. ASSUMPTION, STATED: no date was given for the three, so they are booked on the 20th, the day the shelf was counted and the delivery came to light.

SO THE SALT HOLE IS 5.05 UNIT AND NOT 8.05, AND THREE OF THOSE FIVE ARE SOMEBODY ELSE’S. Once his three come off, the roll should have read 5.05 and the shelf holds nothing. THREE UNIT ARE PAID FOR, UNDELIVERED, AND NOT THERE TO DELIVER. The desk owes them to a man who has settled in full and has nothing behind the obligation; that is the sharpest single line on this book today. The remaining 2.05 is the ordinary gap and it is what the plug is for. Twelve days and six roll-forwards since the 12 Aug count, flagged on each of the last two commits. The flag was right.

OIL IS COUNTED AT ZERO TOO, ON THE SAME LOOK, AND IT COSTS 19 UNIT. The roll said 19 and the shelf holds nothing. OIL’S HOLE IS CLEANER THAN SALT’S AND WORSE. Cleaner because nothing is owed on oil, no order is pending on it and nobody has paid for a unit of it that is not there. Worse because there is nothing to explain it with: the last count was 12 Aug and the last oil row was 14 Aug, so nineteen unit left in six days without a single line recording any of it. A SHELF NOBODY LOOKS AT REPORTS WHATEVER THE ARITHMETIC LAST SAID, and both products have now proved that in the same week.

THE THIN MARGIN IS THE LEAK, NOT THE TRADING, AND THE TWO COUNTS ARE ABOUT TO MAKE THAT PLAIN. He asked why the margin is so little when the next lot is 25 unit for RM1300. That is RM52 a unit, and it is a good buy: RM4 under the RM56 every 12.5 unit lot has cost since 08 Jul, seven per cent cheaper, and it covers the 21.5 unit of promises with 3.5 to spare. ON LOT COST THE TRADING IS HEALTHY. At RM52 the standing rates return 48.0% to CA4-DAM’s RM100, 52.7% to CM4-MK’s RM110, 43.5% to CE4-CHE’s RM92 and 35.0% to CR3-DAM’s RM80, each about four points better than the same rate on the RM56 shelf. THE BOARD DOES NOT MEASURE AGAINST LOT COST, IT MEASURES AGAINST EFFECTIVE COST, which is the lot loaded with the shrinkage plug, and that is why the desk names RM1417.29 to refill 21.5 unit: RM65.92 a unit, RM13.92 above what he is actually about to pay. THAT RM13.92 IS THE LEAK, PRICED. Twenty-four unit went missing across the two shelves today and the cost of them does not disappear; it is spread across every unit sold. Buying better will not fix it, because the loss is happening after the buying. The margin question and the empty shelf are the same question.

WHAT THE BOOK NOW SAYS, PLAINLY. Salt: nothing on hand, three unit owed out and paid for, so free to sell is minus three; 21.5 unit of promises against zero; RM80 owed in by CR3-DAM. Oil: nothing on hand and nothing owed either way. Every pending order on the book is now unmeetable, CJ4-BJ’s 12.5, CE4-AD’s 5 and CA4-DAM’s 1, and so is the deferred delivery that is already paid for. The 25 unit lot clears the salt side of that at a stroke. Nothing on order clears the oil side, and no oil restock is on the book at all.

t: THE SHELF IS COUNTED AT ZERO, AND SIX OF THE MISSING EIGHT UNIT ARE ALREADY PAID FOR
n: COUNTED BY HAND AT ZERO, AND A COUNT ALWAYS WINS ON THIS DESK. The roll said 8.05 and the shelf holds nothing, so this count costs 8.05 unit. IT IS NOT ORDINARY SHRINKAGE AND IT SHOULD NOT BE READ AS SPILLAGE. Six of those units were CE4-CHE’s paid-for deferral: he settled RM500 in full on the 18th, took a quarter unit, and the other six were the desk’s to hold. They are not there. Either they went to him and the fulfilment was never written down, which is the likeliest reading and would be an AMENDMENT to his row rather than a new one, or they left some other way. The desk does not know which and will not guess. What it can state is that the book owes 6 unit against a shelf of nothing, and that 24.5 unit of promises now stand against zero. The remaining 2.05 is the ordinary gap and it is what the plug is for.

NOTHING WAS INVENTED TO CLOSE THE HOLE, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY WORTH READING. The instruction was that the shelf is empty so a few transactions must have gone unrecorded, and that is almost certainly right. It is still a hypothesis, and a row written from a shortfall is a row written from a hypothesis. THIS BOOK HAS BEEN HERE BEFORE FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: the oil unit that stood at RM115 for a day was caught because the correction came from him and not from the arithmetic, and the desk booked what it was told rather than moving the figure into the range it expected. The same rule cuts both ways. So the count is recorded, the hole is visible and measurable, and the rows that explain it get written when their figures are known. A desk that fills its own gaps is a desk whose gaps you can no longer see.

THE READS THAT CARRY THE BOOK NOW NEED THE WRITE KEY. The posture was reads open, writes gated, and the gap in it was found by reading the responses rather than the policy. GET /drafts returned every proposed row WITH ITS COST AND ITS MARGIN. GET /ledger returned the mirror. GET /queue returned every device’s pending entries. So the three figures this desk works hardest to keep off the public payload, the ones phonePayloadLeaks() bans from data.json by name, were being served in full to anyone holding the URL. All three now require the same X-Salt-Key as a write, checked before the routes rather than inside each handler so a route added later cannot quietly miss it. /rev and /queue/ping stay open: a build id and a liveness probe carry no trade. This is not Zero Trust coming back; the site is still public in the sense that was asked for on 11 Aug. It is the write key covering the reads that are as sensitive as a write. The Approve tab now says so when it cannot read, because an empty panel and a panel that cannot see are different states and only one means you can stop thinking about it.

THE SCHEDULED RUN HAS BEEN READING A FOLDER THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The project moved 01_Dashboard to 30_Published and 06_Data to 10_Data, and nothing that reads those folders was told. Nine files in the repo were repointed on the last commit; salt_sync.ps1, salt_daily.ps1 and salt_launch.ps1 are corrected here. THE FAILURE MODE IS THE POINT: a run that reads a queue file from a folder that is not there finds no entries and reports a clean pass. It does not error. Master and root paths were already safe because both scripts resolve them from PSScriptRoot, which moved with them; only the sibling data folder was named outright.

THE v316 SORT DESTROYED FORTY-SEVEN SALES ROWS AND IT SHIPPED. Recorded here rather than quietly repaired. The new sorter opened a record at any line beginning with a brace, and sales rows carry NESTED amendment records, nineteen of them, each on its own line beginning with a brace. It tore those rows in half and reordered the halves by the AMENDMENT’s date. 96 sales rows became 49 and revenue fell from RM21,167.76 to RM12,186.50, a loss of RM8,981.26. It parsed, it built, it passed 254 tests and it deployed, because every check asked whether the file was valid JavaScript and none asked whether the book was still the same book. Restored from the pre-sort backup and re-sorted correctly; the extract is identical to the original as a set, to the sen. THREE THINGS NOW STOP IT. A record opens only at the array’s own indent. The sorter asserts its output is a PERMUTATION of its input and refuses to write otherwise. And the nested-amendment case is a unit test. Brace counting was considered and rejected: 128 note lines carry a brace inside their prose, so a depth counter fires on the text rather than the structure.

t: CR3-DAM HALVED ON HIS WORD, TWO PENDING ORDERS ASK 6 UNIT AGAINST 2.05 FREE, AND THE BOOK IS PUT IN DATE ORDER
n: CR3-DAM IS AMENDED FROM 2 UNIT TO 1, AND THE AMENDMENT MOVES THE SIZE AND NOTHING ELSE. His 18 Aug row was cut to 1 unit for RM80 on his word, so the receivable falls from RM160 to RM80 and a unit that had been counted as delivered comes back to the shelf. RM80 a unit is his standing rate on either reading and the margin on the price is untouched at 30.0%: on the RM56 shelf a unit returns RM24, so the order returns RM24 where it returned RM48. THE FLOOR ANSWER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL THE UNFAVOURABLE ONE. At 1 unit the delivered floor stands at RM85.66 and the collected at RM79.41, and it was DELIVERED, so it is measured against the harder line and sits RM5.66 under it; it would have cleared the collected line by RM0.59. Same answer the 2 unit reading gave, for the same reason. THE CREDIT READING IS WHERE IT ACTUALLY BITES. 2 unit out against a 1 unit retail cap was a breach; 1 unit out sits exactly AT the cap. Nothing further goes out until it clears, but the book is no longer carrying a breach. It remains the only balance on the book.

TWO PENDING ORDERS ARE AGREED AND NEITHER CAN BE MET OFF THE SHELF. CA4-DAM takes 1 unit at RM100 and CE4-AD takes 5 unit at RM435, RM535 and 6 unit between them, both undated because nothing has been paid and nothing has moved. CA4-DAM IS THE NINTH ORDER AT EXACTLY RM100 A UNIT, a rate that has not moved through a cost basis that went from RM64 to RM47 to RM56, and it is a full unit after four halves running, his largest since 06 Aug. CE4-AD IS PAYING RM7 A UNIT MORE THAN LAST TIME AND THE DESK STILL EARNS LESS ON IT. His 28 Jul order was the same 5 unit at RM80 off the RM47 lot and returned RM165 at 41.3%; RM435 against the RM56 shelf would return RM155 at 35.6%. The rate rose RM7, the cost rose RM9, and about six points still went to the supplier. CA4-DAM, CY2-NIL and CM4-MK each tell that story at an unchanged rate, and this one tells it through a rise, which is the harder version of it. Both clear their floors comfortably: RM100 against RM85.66 at 1 unit, RM435 against RM403.30 at 5.

THE SHELF ROLLS 7.05 TO 8.05 AND ONLY 2.05 OF IT IS FREE TO SELL. The CR3-DAM unit returns and nothing else moved, so the standing figure rises by one. Of that, 6 unit are CE4-CHE’s paid-for deferral and cannot be sold to anyone else. AGAINST 2.05 FREE THE BOOK NOW CARRIES 18.5 UNIT OF PENDING ORDERS, being CJ4-BJ’s 12.5, CE4-AD’s 5 and CA4-DAM’s 1, plus the 6 unit already owed and paid for. THE NEXT RESTOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THAT HAS BEEN TRUE OF A RATE-CLEAN ORDER. CE4-AD’s obstacle is stock rather than price, which is a different problem from every pending row of the past fortnight. AND IT IS STILL NOT A COUNT. Nobody has looked at the shelf since 12 Aug: this is the sixth roll-forward in nine days, and the plug has been carried on trust for all of them. v290 is explicit that a roll and a count are different things. Closing that gap is the one piece of housekeeping the book has been deferring.

THE BOOK IS PUT IN DATE ORDER, AND A TEST NOW KEEPS IT THERE. 37 sales rows and one purchase were sitting out of date order, because rows are appended in the order they are FOLDED and that is not the order things happened: a row agreed on the 17th and fulfilled on the 18th lands after rows dated the 18th, and an amendment can date a row into the middle of the book long after its neighbours were written. NOT ONE FIGURE MOVED. The desk sorts by date wherever the order matters, so this was never a computation fault; it made the FILE unreadable, and the file is what a person audits. PENDING ROWS CARRY NO DATE AND SORT LAST, which is the desk’s own rule showing through: an undated row has not happened, so it cannot be placed among the things that have. The sort is stable, so nothing moved that did not have to, and positions are NOT remapped because nothing on this desk keys off a row index. npm test now fails on an out-of-order book, so the tidy cannot quietly undo itself.

THE TOOLING WAS POINTING AT FOLDERS THAT NO LONGER EXIST, AND THE BUILD COULD NOT FIND THE MASTER. The project moved 01_Dashboard to 30_Published and 06_Data to 10_Data, and every hardcoded default in the repo still named the old ones. The build failed outright and the drain would have created a phantom 06_Data folder and read an empty queue from it rather than the real one. Nine files were repointed. TWO ARE STILL WRONG AND THEY ARE NOT IN THAT REPO: salt_sync.ps1 and salt_daily.ps1 both still name 06_Data, so the daily run reads the wrong queue path until they are corrected. Stated here rather than fixed quietly, because a scheduled task that reads an empty queue reports a healthy run.

t: THREE APPROVED ROWS FOLDED, AND THE BOOK NOW OWES 18.5 UNIT AGAINST 7.05 ON THE SHELF
n: THREE APPROVED ROWS FOLDED, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM CAME THROUGH THE GATE. The queue held exactly three entries, the drafter had turned all three into rows, and all three were tapped approved on the phone before this run began. Nothing was pending, nothing was refused and there was no amendment, so for the first time since v305 the whole commit is gate traffic and not one row was folded on a run judgement. The watermark moves to the newest id folded, 2026-08-18T22:26:37.778Z, which is the entry own timestamp and therefore sits at or after everything committed here.

CE4-CHE PAID FOR 6.25 UNIT AND TOOK A QUARTER OF ONE, SO THE BOOK NOW CARRIES A DEFERRED DELIVERY. RM500 collected in full on the 18th with 0.25 unit handed over, which puts 6 unit into deferred and nothing into receivables. It is the mirror image of CR3-DAM, who has the salt and owes the money, and the two sit on opposite sides of the same book on the same day. The rate is RM80 a unit against the RM92 he has paid five times, 13% below, and it clears the collected floor while missing the delivered one, so how the remaining 6 unit are handed over still decides which floor this row is measured against.

CA11-SEN OPENS AT RM60 A UNIT AND IS NOW THE WORST LIVE PRICE ON THE BOOK. 3 unit for RM180 returns RM12 at 6.7%, thinner than the 13.8% CM3-OKR set two days earlier, and the record has now been broken twice in three days by two new names. It is short of its floor by more than any other live price in proportion, and it joins CS6-PER as the second price under replacement cost. It is not under cost. RM60 is above the RM56 lot it drew, so the trade made money; what it does not cover is what replacing that unit now costs once freight, shrinkage and delivery are in. Both flags were on the phone before the tap, so this is a priced decision and the desk records it as one.

THE SHELF ROLLS 12.30 TO 7.05 AND ONLY 1.05 OF IT IS FREE TO SELL. 5.25 unit came off on this commit, and 6 of what is left are already paid for by CE4-CHE. Against 18.5 unit owed out, being that 6 plus the 12.5 agreed to CJ4-BJ, the book is 11.45 unit short on its own promises and 13.95 under the 15 unit reorder trigger. The walk goes 0.20 unit negative overnight on the 17th, because 5 unit went out against a 4.80 shelf and the 12.5 unit lot did not land until the 18th; the same 0.20 v314 recorded on the 18th, moved one day earlier by these rows and closed by the same lot. It is a roll and not a count. Nobody has looked at the shelf since 12 Aug, which is eight days and five rolls ago, and the unexplained plug of 46.4 unit is being carried on trust for all of it.

HEADROOM IS NEGATIVE AT MINUS 1.8%, WHICH IS THE WEEK PRICING FACT. The buying rate stands at RM56 and the first live price breaks at RM55, so the desk is already RM1 past the point where CS6-PER 08 Jul package stops covering replacement. Sixteen live prices sit under floor, two under replacement and none under cost. Salt margin eases from 39.20% to 38.76% on the three rows, oil is untouched at 27.65%, and observed shrinkage holds at 17.77% because nothing was bought.

t: FOUR FULFILMENTS FOLDED, THE SHELF TRIPLES, AND THE LOT LANDED ON THE DAY IT WAS NEEDED
n: FOUR AMENDMENTS FOLDED, AND NOT ONE OF THEM WENT THROUGH THE APPROVAL GATE, WHICH IS CORRECT. The gate of v305 governs NEW ROWS. The drafter refuses an amendment outright because it cannot say which row is being amended, so each of these was read against the row it settles and folded by hand, exactly as the rule says it should be. The three sales agreed pending at v311 are now dated and the SA5-BTR lot agreed alongside them has arrived. The one thing waiting on the phone is untouched: a 6.25 unit sale to CE4-CHE at RM500, drafted and PENDING, which no run may fold until it is tapped.

THE LOT LANDED ON THE DAY THE BOOK NEEDED IT, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED BEFORE. The shelf stood at 4.80 unit and 5 unit went out on the 18th, so the book was 0.20 unit short of its own promises until the 12.5 unit arrived the same day. Every restock since 28 Jul has landed on an empty shelf a day or more after it was wanted. It is now the newest received lot and therefore sets replacement cost, the job pending:true was holding it out of at v311; at RM56 it carries the same small-lot rate as the 13 Aug lot, so it takes that job over without moving a single floor. The shelf rolls 4.80 to 12.30 and STOCK_COST holds at 56. It is a roll-forward and not a count. Nobody has looked at the shelf since 12 Aug.

THE LEAK LOOKS SMALLER AND NOTHING WAS FOUND. Observed shrinkage falls from 18.66% to 17.77% and effective cost with it, RM65.53 to RM65.24, purely because 12.5 unit more have been handled and the plug is a rate measured over everything handled. No salt was recovered and nothing was explained: 46.4 unit are still unattributed, worth about RM2,419 at the average, which is a third of every ringgit of gross margin this desk has earned. A large receipt always flatters this figure, and the honest reading is that the same loss is now spread thinner rather than that the shelf is tighter.

CR3-DAM IS THE ONLY DEBTOR ON THE BOOK AND HE IS AT DOUBLE HIS CAP. 2 unit handed over on the 18th with nothing paid, so RM160 is the whole of receivables where yesterday there was none, against a 1 unit cap for a retail customer. The floor question v311 left open is answered, and answered the unfavourable way. That row said the manner of hand-over would decide it: DELIVERED rather than collected, so the delivered floor applies and the price sits under it, and the collected floor it would have cleared does not. Under floor is not under cost. On the RM56 shelf it returns RM48 at 30%, real money on a rate agreed before the restock lifted the basis by a fifth. Reported, not repriced.

THE BOARD-UNPRICED BREACH IS THE SAME ONE, NOW POINTING AT A NEWER LOT. It read 12.5 unit at RM56 landed 13 Aug and now reads the 18 Aug lot; the locked basis is still the 100 unit lot of 28 Jul either way. Nothing here is new and nothing is blocked. It is named because a breach that changes its wording without changing its cause reads like a fresh finding to the next person, and it is not one. Housekeeping, stated so it is not mistaken for loss: evolution had grown to sixteen entries because v299 to v313 were never moved to 04_Docs/changelog.json. They are moved here, the array is one entry again as it is meant to be, and no text was dropped.

t: THE TWO LINES THAT PUT NAMES IN THE QUEUE ARE GONE, AND A QUANTITY THAT HAD BEEN WRONG SINCE 11 AUG IS CORRECTED
n: THE ASSOCIATE SELECTOR MINTED PARTIES FROM A TEXT BOX, WHICH IS HOW A NAME REACHED THE QUEUE. Its + New associate option read a free-typed “name (location)” and queued it as the identifier; the downstream bucket then appended -Gen to that same string. The end-customer selector had the identical fault. Both broke the rule written twelve lines below them, that the queue file is plaintext and carries codes only, and both broke v174, which moved party creation into Names & IDs precisely so a code is minted from a name and a place ONCE, in the only panel that holds names. Nothing replaces them: create the party where names live, then pick the code from the list.

AND A SECOND LEAK WAS FOUND ONLY BY BOOKING A NORMAL RESELL AFTERWARDS. With the free-text paths shut, an ordinary R2 through an existing associate still wrote (R2 via <name>) into the entry’s raw line, because that sentence used ID(), which resolves a code to the real name whenever the directory is revealed. So EVERY associate transaction recorded with names on screen put a name on disk, not merely the new-associate path just fixed. It is codeOf() now, and the fix was verified with names revealed: the entry reads (R2 via CN6-WM). Testing the removal alone would have missed it; the happy path is what showed it.

CY2-NIL’S OPENING ORDER WAS 2.5 UNIT, NOT 2, AND IT HAS ALWAYS BEEN. On his correction. The row booked 2 unit for RM230, which made his rate read RM115 and its note claim the best retail margin on the book at 59.1%. Restated: RM92 a unit, RM112.50 at 48.9%, an ordinary good opening. The shelf does not move and the plug does, as at v298: the extra half unit went out on the 11th but the hand count of 1.30 was taken on the 12th, after it had gone, and a count always wins. The cost of carrying it was not the half unit. v311 read his second order at the correct RM92 as a 20% CUT from a rate he had never charged, and wrote a paragraph about a drafter blind spot that was not there. A wrong quantity does not stay a quantity error; it becomes a pricing story, and this one is withdrawn.

t: A REAL NAME REACHED THE QUEUE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THE QUEUE MAY NEVER CARRY
n: AN R2 RESELL WAS QUEUED WITH THE ASSOCIATE’S NAME IN IT INSTEAD OF HIS CODE. The entry carried assoc set to the DISPLAY LABEL, name and locality and all, and a downstream bucket built by appending -Gen to that same label. Its party field was null, so it named no code anywhere. The standing rule is absolute and is written beside nextNewId: only codes travel in the queue, never names. The queue is plaintext, salt_queue.json sits on disk unencrypted, and anything folded from it lands in a file that is built, committed and served publicly.

IT WENT NO FURTHER THAN THIS LAPTOP, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The name is absent from the cloud queue, absent from data.json, absent from the built desk and the phone app, and git log -S across every branch finds it in no commit that has ever existed. So there is no exposure to undo; what there is, is a path that will do it again. The registration was folded and the sale was NOT. CA11-SEN joins the roster because that entry is clean and carries only a code; the sale stays above the watermark, unfolded, because folding it would put the name in this file.

THE GATE WOULD HAVE HELD ANYWAY, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING. The drafter refuses any entry carrying assoc or stream fields, on the grounds that whose bucket a resell books to is a judgement, so this one could never have been drafted or approved. The protection was accidental rather than designed: it refused the entry for being a resell, not for carrying a name. Two things to settle before the sale can be booked. The bucket wants to be CA11-SEN-Gen, and the party was registered as a CUSTOMER while the entry treats him as an ASSOCIATE with an R2 downsell, which a customer cannot be. Both are his to answer, and neither should be guessed.

t: FOUR ORDERS BOOKED THAT COUNT NOWHERE, AND A PURCHASE THAT WOULD HAVE PRICED THE BOOK BEFORE IT ARRIVED
n: ALL FOUR ARE PENDING, SO NOT ONE FIGURE ON THIS DESK MOVES. Three sales, CA4-DAM at RM100 a unit, CY2-NIL at RM92 and CR3-DAM at RM80, and a 12.5 unit purchase from SA5-BTR at RM56. Nothing is paid and nothing has moved on any of them, so each takes NO DATE, draws no stock and books no revenue: the shelf stays at 4.80 and the cost basis is untouched. They are on the book so they can be seen, not because anything happened.

THE PURCHASE WOULD HAVE SET THE FLOOR FOR A LOT THAT HAS NOT ARRIVED. The drafter wrote it as status:"part", which is wrong twice, and without pending:true, which is the only thing poLive() actually tests. A live lot adds no stock while receivedOn is absent, so the error would not have shown in the shelf; what it WOULD have done is qualify as the NEWEST LOT, and the newest lot sets the replacement cost that every floor on this desk is built on. An order agreed and not delivered would have been pricing the book. Caught by folding it, fixed on the row and fixed in the drafter, and the check afterwards confirms the newest lot is still the one of 13 Aug.

AND CY2-NIL CUT 20% WITHOUT A WORD FROM ANYONE. He opened on 11 Aug at RM115 a unit, the best margin any retail order had returned; this one is RM92. The drafter stayed silent because its party check needs at least TWO prior orders before it will measure a rate against the median, so a SECOND order can move as far as it likes from the first and never be questioned. Being cautious with one data point is right and saying nothing about it is not: the check should name the parties it cannot judge rather than pass them in silence. Written on the row, because a limit nobody records is a limit nobody fixes.

t: A NEW CUSTOMER OPENS RM64 UNDER FLOOR, APPROVED WITH THE FLAG IN FRONT OF HIM
n: CM3-OKR OPENS AT 4 UNIT FOR RM260, AND IT IS THE THINNEST SALT MARGIN THE BOOK HAS EVER CARRIED. RM65 a unit against a RM56 shelf returns RM36, 13.8% on the price and a 16.1% markup on cost, beneath the 25% the floor asks. The delivered floor at that size is RM324.24 and the collected one RM317.99, so it misses both by about RM64. The next thinnest is CC5-OKR’s RM80 unit at 30.0%; every other retail row since the restock sits between 44% and 49%. Shelf falls 8.80 to 4.80, the tightest since the 13 Aug lot landed.

IT WAS APPROVED WITH THE FLAG SHOWING, WHICH IS WHAT THE GATE IS FOR. The drafter said in terms that RM260 was under both floors and that the party was not on the roster, and both were on the phone when he tapped approve. That makes it a priced decision rather than an accident, and the desk books it as one instead of arguing with it. The concession rests on expectation, not on record. Size has bought a discount here before, CM4-MK took 4 unit at RM90 once his cumulative buying passed RM1,000, but this buyer has no history at all. If his second order also comes in at RM65 then RM65 is his price and the book should say so; if it comes in higher, this was an opening.

AND THE TWO ENTRIES WERE COUPLED, WHICH v309 IS THE REASON ANYONE COULD SEE. Registering CM3-OKR was queued a minute before the sale, refused by the drafter because registering a party is not a trade, and surfaced on the phone in the refused panel built hours earlier. The sale could not be committed until that registration was folded into the roster. A sale waiting on a registration it cannot see is precisely the invisibility that produced the duplicate earlier the same day, and this run is the first evidence of the fix doing its job on real trade.

t: WHAT THE DRAFTER REFUSES IS NOW VISIBLE ON THE PHONE, BECAUSE INVISIBLE IS HOW THE SAME ORDER GOT QUEUED TWICE
n: AN ENTRY QUEUED ON THE LAPTOP WAS INVISIBLE FROM THE PHONE, AND THAT IS WHAT CAUSED THE DUPLICATE. The CC5-OKR fulfilment of 17 Aug was entered on the laptop and again from the phone three hours later, byte for byte. Re-entering it was the natural thing to do, because nothing on the phone said it was already in hand: an amendment is refused by the drafter by design, so it never reaches the Approve tab where it would have been seen. Only the watermark stood between that habit and a double count. Refused entries now appear there, in their own panel, with the drafter’s reason and where it saw them.

SEEN, NEVER APPROVABLE, AND THE SCHEMA IS WHAT ENFORCES IT. They live in a table of their own rather than as a fourth draft status, because a draft is required to carry a proposed ROW and a refusal by definition has none; making those columns nullable to fit would discard that guarantee for every row. The table has NO decision column at all, so there is nothing to approve even by accident, and the panel renders no buttons. The tab badge still counts only what a tap can clear, because sending someone to a tab with nothing to press on it is its own kind of noise. It is self-cleaning: anything the watermark has passed is deleted on the next drafter run, so a stale refusal cannot pile up into a list people stop reading.

THREE FAULTS FELL OUT OF BUILDING IT, ALL FOUND BY RUNNING IT AGAINST REAL ENTRIES. The drafter answered “amends an existing row” for every mode it did not handle, so registering a NEW PARTY was reported as an amendment, which reads as a fault in the entry rather than a category the drafter has no row shape for; each mode now names its own case. The name-leak gate existed in TWO copies, in the extract tool and in the suite, and the fix for the General collision had gone into one of them, so the other went on failing: one definition now, in book.mjs, asserted. And a party whose name is also an ordinary word the desk prints in a column heading cannot be checked for at all; that is a real hole rather than a tidy-up, so it is kept in a separate list and printed on every run, because a pass that means “no name appears except these” must never read as “no name appears”.

t: THE FIRST COMMIT RUN THROUGH THE GATE: ONE ROW APPROVED ON THE PHONE, TWO AMENDMENTS ROUND THE SIDE, AND A RECEIVABLE THAT NEVER EXISTED
n: THE APPROVAL STEP CARRIED REAL TRADE FOR THE FIRST TIME. CA4-DAM’s half unit at RM50 was typed on the laptop, drafted into a proposed row by the same drafter the phone uses, shown with its RM56 cost and its 44.0% margin, and approved on the phone before it reached this file. Every figure was in front of him before the row existed. The two amendments in the same queue took the older road, because an amendment is a judgement about WHICH row and the drafter refuses them by design, so this run is also the first evidence of where the gate’s edge actually falls: one of three entries went through it.

AND THE DESK WAS WRONG ABOUT CR3-DAM FOR THE SECOND TIME, IN EXACTLY THE SAME WAY. His 14 Aug unit was booked at v299 as delivered and unpaid, named the ONLY receivable on the book and said to put him at his credit cap. The RM80 had in fact been paid on the 14th, the same day the salt went out; only the report of it was late, by three days. His 08 Aug row made the identical mistake and spent four days marked past due. The fault is not in the reading, it is in the instrument. This desk sees what has been QUEUED, never what has HAPPENED, and it cannot observe the gap between the two. Where that gap is a few days it will invent a receivable every time, so the right reading of an unpaid row on a trusted account is “not yet reported”. The book now carries no receivable at all.

CC5-OKR MOVED AT THE RM80 THE DESK QUESTIONED, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION. The row stood pending and undated since the 14th precisely so it could be looked at: RM10 under the RM90 he has paid on every trade he ever made, and under the delivered floor the 13 Aug restock had just lifted. It is now paid and delivered at RM80, which clears the RM79.50 collected floor by fifty sen, misses the RM85.75 delivered one by RM5.75, and returns 30.0% against the 44% and 49% the other two orders of this run made. Recorded, not corrected. He saw the figure and traded anyway, which is a decision; a desk that quietly repriced it would destroy the only evidence the question was ever put. Shelf rolls 10.30 to 8.80, and the watermark moves to the newest entry folded rather than to the clock.

AND A FOURTH ENTRY ARRIVED MID-RUN THAT WAS THE SAME FULFILMENT A SECOND TIME. The CC5-OKR amendment was queued on the laptop at 08:54 and again from the phone at 11:30, with a BYTE-IDENTICAL payload and the same orderKey. That order held one pending unit and can be fulfilled once, and it had just been folded, so booking the second would have put 1 unit and RM80 through a completed row twice. It was WITHDRAWN rather than folded, from the file and from the cloud queue both, and it is recorded here because otherwise the only trace is an entry that silently ceased to exist. The cause is worth more than the incident. An entry queued on the laptop is invisible from the phone, so re-entering it is the natural thing to do and looks safe. Nothing stands between that habit and a double count except the watermark, which is the v287 fault approaching from the opposite direction. The drafter cannot help here either: an amendment is refused by design, so it never reaches the Approve tab where it would have been seen.

t: THE LEDGER READS ON A PHONE, AND THE RESTYLE IT WAS SCOPED FOR TURNED OUT TO BE DONE ALREADY
n: THE DESK HAS BEEN IN THE PHONE APP’S LANGUAGE SINCE v213, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THE WHOLE PORT COSTS. This began as the first tab of a restyle: take the Ledger and put it in the lite language the app uses. There was nothing to restyle. The tokens are already identical to the hex, glass at white 10%, hairlines at white 13%, the 14px radius, gold #e8c66b, ice #7fd7e8, violet #b3a6f5; the register ground is the app’s ground, three washes over near-black. A first attempt restated all of it and was correctly beaten by the v213 last-wins layer, which is how the redundancy was found. It was deleted rather than made to win. The two surfaces never disagreed about colour or material. They disagree about WIDTH.

AND THE WIDTH IS A REAL GAP, NOT A TIDYING JOB. A ledger row is a flex line carrying 74 + 84 + 118 + 126 pixels of FIXED numeric columns: 402px committed before the party, the date and the badges are placed at all. On a 375px screen that cannot reflow, only scroll. What stood there wrapped the row and let the columns shrink, which cleared the overflow and left the figures running together as bare numbers, because the headings that named them are off the top of a wrapped row. Below 560px the row now stops being a row: the identity takes the full width and the four figures sit in a labelled two-by-two grid, the pattern the app’s Approve card already uses. It is CSS only. No figure, render function or class name is touched, the labels are drawn in CSS so the desktop DOM gains nothing, and the wide layout is unchanged to the pixel: 74, 84, 118, 126, right-aligned, headings on.

TWO CASCADE TRAPS, BOTH SILENT, BOTH WORTH THE NOTE. The rules were first written as a new 640px block and were beaten at 375px by an existing 560px rule of equal specificity sitting later in the file, so they simply never applied; they now live in that 560px block and the ledger has one breakpoint rather than two fighting. Then flex:1 1 calc(50% - 5px) was rejected as a shorthand, which invalidated that one declaration and left the rest of the rule applying: the boxes and their labels drew correctly while the widths quietly kept their desktop values. Set as three longhand properties it is accepted. Both failures look like a rule half-applied rather than one broken, which is the kind that survives a glance.

t: ADDING A CUSTOMER WAS BROKEN IN TWO PLACES AT ONCE, AND BOTH WERE INVISIBLE
n: THE BUTTON REFUSED, AND IT REFUSED FOR A REASON THAT STOPPED BEING TRUE. Add ID would not mint a code unless the passphrase was held in memory, which was right when the encrypted vault WAS the directory. It is not any more: names live in BIO and Save writes them to salt_bio.json, and the vault is seeded from that file afterwards. Worse, the two ways of opening the directory disagree. The Names panel’s own Unlock keeps the passphrase; vaultReveal(), the ordinary show-me-the-names path, deletes it on purpose because it is not needed again. So after the reveal anyone would actually use, the button answered Unlock the vault first to a man staring at the unlocked directory. Nothing in there needs a passphrase, so nothing in there asks for one now.

AND HAD THE GUARD PASSED, THE NAME WOULD STILL HAVE BEEN THROWN AWAY. addParty wrote the name into vaultNames alone. The box beside each code renders from BIO, and Save reads those boxes back into BIO and DELETES any entry left empty. So a name typed into Add ID appeared nowhere and was discarded by the very next Save: the code survived, the person did not. It writes BIO now and lets vaultNames follow, which is the direction the rest of the panel already runs in.

PROVEN ON A COPY, NOT ON THE BOOK. The desk, both servers and a 06_Data holding the real directory were copied to a scratch folder and served there, because a POST to /bio on the real folder writes for real. Two parties were created through the actual panel, CT5-CHE and CB2-SET: both minted, both filled the name box, both survived Save into salt_bio.json, both queued an ADDID. The live directory was checked afterwards and carries neither. One false alarm is worth recording: the Save button looked unbound after a party was created, which turned out to be renderReveal returning early while the panel is CLOSED, exactly as it should. The test was wrong, not the desk.

t: THE APPROVAL STEP IS THE ONLY ROAD INTO THE LEDGER NOW, BECAUSE THE TWO THAT WENT ROUND IT ARE SHUT
n: TWO ROADS WERE STILL OPEN AND BOTH ARE CLOSED. The first was serve_desk.py’s sixty-second drain, which pulled the phone’s queue onto disk and left it in a file the daily run folded straight into this book; while the laptop was on, a phone entry reached the ledger without anyone reading the row. That pull is removed outright, not made optional, and the environment variable that tuned it is left unused rather than repurposed so an old setting is inert. The second was the desk’s OWN queue, which never went near the cloud at all: node tools/drafts.mjs --from-queue now puts those entries through the same table the phone reads, PENDING, using the same drafter rather than a second copy of it.

THE DAILY RUN NOW FOLDS APPROVED ROWS AND NOTHING ELSE. Its instruction used to be read every queue file and fold it, which is the behaviour that made the gate optional; it is rewritten to run --approved, fold the row AS WRITTEN, and mark each id committed afterwards. A row that looks wrong is reported rather than quietly corrected, because what he approved was that row and not somebody’s improvement of it. The watermark rule gets simpler as a side effect: a draft’s id IS the entry’s own at, so the mark is the newest id folded, which cannot sit before anything committed nor after anything left pending.

WHAT IS STILL NOT GATED, SAID PLAINLY. Editing this file by hand. That is not a hole to close, it is the desk itself, and the whole arrangement rests on it: the gate governs QUEUED transactions, which are the ones typed in a hurry at the point of sale and the ones that produced the RM115 oil unit. A row written deliberately into the master by someone reading the book is a different act and needs no tap.

t: THE DRAFTER DRAFTS ON ARRIVAL, BECAUSE THE CRON LOST A RACE IT WAS NEVER GOING TO WIN
n: A TEST ENTRY WAS PUT THROUGH THE QUEUE AND THE CRON NEVER SAW IT. serve_desk.py drains the cloud queue to disk every sixty seconds while the laptop is on, and that drain is a DESTRUCTIVE read: it moves the entries into the file and clears the cloud keys. So a fifteen-minute cron was competing with a sixty-second sweep and lost every time. An entry posted at 14:41 was on disk and gone from the cloud by 14:52, with nothing left to draft. The row is now written the moment the entry arrives, deferred so the phone still gets its acknowledgement immediately, and the cron drops back to being the safety net it should always have been.

THE TEST ROW ALSO CAUGHT A FAULT IN THE APPROVAL SCREEN ITSELF, AND IT IS THE RM115 MISTAKE IN COLOUR. The entry was 1 unit at RM900, a fat-fingered RM90, and the drafter flagged it twice: more than double the highest salt rate this book has ever carried, and RM900 from a party who has paid RM90 on every order he has made. Directly underneath those two warnings the margin cell painted 93.8% in green, because a fat margin bands as good. The eye was being told ’excellent’ on the exact row the words were telling it to check. Green means nothing needs looking at, so a flagged row cannot have one.

AND ONE HOLE IS NAMED RATHER THAN CLOSED. That same sixty-second drain still writes into the queue file the daily run folds into this book, so while the laptop server is running the OLD path still reaches the ledger WITHOUT passing the approval step. Shutting it means changing serve_desk.py and the daily-run task, neither of which lives in the cloud repo, so the approval step is not yet the only road in. It is written down rather than left to be discovered, because a guard everyone believes is total is worse than one whose gap is known.

t: THE DRAFTER RUNS IN THE CLOUD NOW, SO A ROW IS WAITING ON THE PHONE BEFORE THE LAPTOP IS OPENED
n: THE LAPTOP IS OUT OF THE LOOP FOR DRAFTING. A Worker cron reads the queue every fifteen minutes, reads the book from the D1 mirror, writes the proposed ROW into the draft table and stops. Nothing is approved, nothing is committed, nothing touches this file: an entry queued at the point of sale is a row waiting on the phone a few minutes later rather than the next morning. The commit itself is still a person and still the laptop, which is the correct division: writing a row is arithmetic, folding it into the book is a judgement.

IT IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT A LANGUAGE MODEL, WHICH IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A LIMIT. Everything an approval screen is read for is a number: the cost the row draws, the margin it makes, whether the rate sits on the party’s own ladder. A model on that path would put nondeterminism on exactly the figures that must be right, in a desk whose whole discipline is one engine and no drift. So the desk computes and the cloud reads: a PRICING SNAPSHOT is taken by the extract, through this desk’s own floorTotal, replCost and stockCostFor, and the drafter prices from it rather than recomputing anything. What a model could usefully write is the note, which is prose and which nobody approves; that is left off this path on purpose.

THE FLAGS ARE THE PRODUCT, AND THREE FAULTS IN THEM WERE FOUND BY POINTING IT AT THE REAL BOOK. Run against the RM115 oil unit it says, correctly, that the rate is more than double the highest oil rate this book has ever carried. But it also called a RM700 restock “RM300 under floor”, a floor being a SELLING line that means nothing on a purchase; it judged SA5-BTR, who has supplied nearly everything on the shelf, for having no BUYING history; and it went quiet on CC5-OKR’s RM80 because his own pending RM80 row was being counted as evidence of what he pays. All three are fixed: a purchase is not measured with a seller’s ruler, a supplier is known by having supplied, and only rows that actually MOVED count as history. A flag that fires when nothing is wrong is worse than no flag, because it teaches the reader to tap through.

t: A QUEUED ENTRY NO LONGER BECOMES A LEDGER ROW UNATTENDED: THE ROW IS DRAFTED, AND APPROVED ON THE PHONE
n: THE APPROVAL STEP IS BUILT AND THE ROW IS WHAT IS APPROVED. A drafter writes the proposed ledger row, it is stored as pending, the phone shows it with the cost it draws and the margin it makes standing beside the price, and a tap approves or rejects. Only approved rows are offered to the commit run. Rejected rows never reach it, and a row already decided cannot be decided again, because a double tap on a phone is the normal case rather than the odd one. Reads stay open and decisions are write-gated, which is the posture the rest of the cloud surface has held since 11 Aug: an approval reaches the master, so it is a write in the fullest sense.

IT EXISTS BECAUSE OF THE RM115 OIL UNIT, AND THE ARGUMENT IS WORTH KEEPING SHORT. That entry was faultless as an entry: a product, a party, a quantity, a price, all well formed, nothing in it that could be checked against anything. It was the ROW, carrying RM7 of cost and a 93.9% margin, that made it obvious on sight. So an approval screen that showed the entry back would have caught nothing, and this one leads with cost and margin instead. It computes neither: both are read from the draft exactly as written, because a second opinion computed on the phone would be a second pricing engine and two engines drift.

AND A BASIS ERROR IN THE v301 NOTE IS CORRECTED HERE. That note read the oil row’s 39.1% against the new 25% floor, which compares a margin on PRICE against a markup on COST: the same pair of bases that v300 had to reconcile in PRICE.floorPct, mixed again one version later. The sale is 39.1% margin on price and 64.3% markup on cost, and on the ladder that puts it between the good rung and the great one rather than just above the floor. Both rows now state both figures, because the ledger quotes one basis and the ladder the other and the two are easy to compare by mistake.

t: THE OIL UNIT WAS RM11.50, NOT RM115, AND THE FLAG THAT CAUGHT IT IS THE CASE FOR DRAFTING ROWS
n: RM103.50 OF REVENUE THAT NEVER EXISTED COMES OFF THE BOOK. CH4-MLR’s oil unit was booked at RM115 on his instruction at v300 and is corrected to RM11.50 on his instruction now. On the RM7 lot it returns RM4.50, 39.1% margin on the price and a 64.3% markup on cost, which puts it between the good rung and the great one; RM115 had shown a 93.9% margin no row on this book has ever come close to. The row states both bases because the ledger quotes margin on price while the v300 ladder is markup on cost, and the two are easy to compare by mistake. Nothing else moves: 1 unit left the shelf either way, so the count, the cost basis and every floor are untouched.

THE RATE NOW SITS ON THE LADDER, WHICH IS THE TEST IT FAILED BEFORE. RM11.50 lands between the RM11 CS6-BS paid for 30 unit direct and the RM13 his downsell fetched, and one unit costing more per unit than thirty is the right ordering. RM115 sat on no ladder at all, above a RM10 quoted ceiling by a factor of eleven. The desk booked it anyway and that was correct. It records what it is told and does not move a number into the range it expected, the same rule that booked the RM6 below-cost resell of 11 Aug without argument. What it did instead was name the one-digit alternative and put a figure on being wrong.

AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE APPROVAL STEP NOW BEING BUILT. The queued entry looked entirely ordinary: a product, a party, a quantity, a price. Nothing in it could be checked against anything. It was the ROW, with RM7 of cost and 93.9% of margin standing next to it, that made the fault obvious on sight. A pipeline that turned entries into rows unattended would have shipped this one; a pipeline that drafts the row and waits for a tap does not. The fault was caught in a day because the row was written down and read, and the point of the coming change is to make that reading a step rather than a habit.

t: HALF THE LEAK IS ABSORBED AGAIN, THE LADDER IS RAISED AND EVENLY SPACED, AND A NEW NAME OPENS ON BOTH PRODUCTS
n: TWO LEVERS MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, WHICH IS WHY NEITHER NUMBER IS ASSERTED HERE. SHRINK_ATTRIB goes from 1 back to 0.5, so half the leak is carried in the price and half comes out of margin as the cost of not having fixed it; that pushes every rung DOWN. The floor markup goes from 15% to 25% of cost, which pushes it UP. The v205 argument for absorbing half was never deleted when v244 reversed it, so it is live again as written, and the v244 case against it now sits beside it. Read the net off the board rather than working it out here.

THE LADDER IS A QUARTER OF COST APART THE WHOLE WAY UP. Floor 25, good 50, great 75, ceiling unmoved at 100, where it ran 15, 33, 67, 100 and the gap from floor to good was half the gap from good to great. Nothing in the arithmetic demanded it; a ladder a trader can hold in his head at the point of sale is the entire argument, and that is the only place it is used. A SECOND FLOOR WAS FOUND AND MADE TO AGREE. PRICE.floorPct is the older lever and it is a margin on PRICE, not a markup on cost, so it cannot take 25 without meaning something else; it goes to 20, which is the same line (0.25/1.25). It was never quite consistent with REF even at 15, floorPrice dividing by 0.85 for a 17.6% markup while floorTotal multiplied by 1.15. They now agree exactly.

CH4-MLR OPENS ON BOTH PRODUCTS ON THE SAME DAY, AND ONE OF THE TWO ROWS NEEDS ANSWERING. 1 unit of salt at RM110, the same opening rate CR3-PUD took, though against the RM56 shelf it now returns 49.1% where his returned 57.3%: eight points went to the restock, not to the customer. Then 1 unit of oil at RM115, which is ten times any oil rate this book has ever carried, against a RM7 lot, an RM10 quoted ceiling and prior sales at RM6, RM11 and RM13. It is booked exactly as given, because this desk does not quietly correct a figure into the range it expected. But RM11.50 is one digit away and would sit precisely between the RM11 and RM13 already on the book, so either the oil book is overstated by RM103.50 or something was sold that is not the RM7 oil. The row says so in terms.

t: THE SHELF IS RESTOCKED AT RM56, AND EVERY FLOOR ON THE DESK MOVES WITH IT
n: FOUR QUEUED ENTRIES COMMITTED, AND ONE OF THEM CHANGES THE PRICE OF EVERYTHING. A 12.5 unit lot from SA5-BTR on the 13th at RM700, 1 unit to CR3-DAM on credit and 1.5 to CN6-WM-R paid on the 14th, and a 1 unit CC5-OKR order left pending because nothing has moved for it. The shelf rolls from 1.30 to 11.30 and the book carries one receivable again.

RM56 A UNIT IS THE SMALL-LOT TIER, AND IT IS NOT A WORSE DEAL. Every 12.5 unit lot since 08 Jul has cost RM56; the RM47 quoted on every row since 28 Jul was the BULK rate and it takes 100 unit to reach. What the restock does is move replacement cost, which the desk reads off the newest received lot, so from the 13th every floor is built on RM56 rather than RM47 and sits roughly a fifth higher. The pending rows should be re-read against the live floor and not against the figures written beside them last week, CJ4-BJ’s 12.5 unit at RM850 first: it was RM2.40 short of a RM47-era floor and the floor has since risen under it again.

THE FIRST BLENDED COST ON THE BOOK, AND WHY IT IS SAID OUT LOUD. CR3-DAM’s unit takes the last of the RM47 remnant bar 0.30, and CN6-WM-R’s 1.5 draws that 0.30 plus 1.20 of the new lot, so its cost is RM54.20 a unit and belongs to no single lot. That also empties the shelf of its old rates: STOCK_COST goes from a 47.47 blend of an RM64 tail and the 28 Jul lot to a flat 56, and the standing caveat about not knowing where the shrinkage plug fell stops bearing on it. CC5-OKR is the one to look at rather than the arithmetic. RM80 would be RM10 under the RM90 he has paid on every trade he has made, on a smaller order, in the week the floor went up. It is left pending and left visible rather than repriced, because only he can say whether that was a decision.

t: The count is read from the end of its day, and the exception is written down where it will be read (13 Aug). The CR3-PUD unit is dated 12 Aug on his word, and on his word it went out BEFORE he counted the shelf at 1.30 that same day. This desk's standing convention is the opposite way round, a count being as at the START of its date so that same-day deliveries come off it, and the 29 Jul roll was built on exactly that. So this count is an EXCEPTION and both rows now say so in terms. Why a one-word correction earned a version of its own. Nothing in the arithmetic moved: the shelf is still 1.30, the leak still 19.86%, the floor at 12.5 unit still RM852.40, and the FIFO lot is RM47 whichever August day it is. What moved is the record, and the risk it guards against is real rather than theoretical. Apply the usual start-of-date rule to a 12 Aug sale and a 12 Aug count and the unit comes off the shelf twice, the shelf reads 0.30 and the leak is overstated by 0.42 points. That is precisely what v296 shipped before he caught it, and a rule that has already been misapplied once will be misapplied again unless the exception is written where the next reader is standing. It is written twice: on the row and on STATED_STOCK.

The count already had it: a unit comes out of the plug, and a floor moves under a live order (13 Aug). A correction to v296, made the same day. THE CR3-PUD UNIT MOVED BEFORE THE 12 AUG HAND COUNT OF 1.30, so the count had already absorbed it and v296's roll of STATED_STOCK down to 0.30 took the same unit off twice. The count is restored to 1.30 and the sale re-dated from the 13th to the 11th, a count being read as at the START of its date on this desk, which makes the 11th the latest day that sits inside it. The shelf is 1.30 and the shortfall on promises is 11.2 unit, not 12.2. WHAT BOOKING IT ACTUALLY DID WAS NARROW THE LEAK. Until this row existed the plug was carrying a unit that had already gone as unexplained loss; recording it moves that unit from loss to sale, and the leak falls from 20.28% to 19.86% with the effective cost from RM61.15 to RM60.84 a unit. Same mechanism as the CJ4-OKR four earned units on 10 Aug, and the quiet argument for booking every movement however small: an unrecorded sale is indistinguishable from theft. AND IT MOVED A FLOOR UNDER A LIVE ORDER. CJ4-BJ's pending 12.5 unit at RM850 was written up as clearing a RM824.95 floor by RM25.05. The 12 Aug count pushed that floor past it and this correction pulled it back a little, so it now stands at RM852.40 and RM850 is RM2.40 short, read live off floorTotal(12.5) rather than computed by hand. That order is the obvious source of most of the cash for the next 50 unit lot, so the RM2.40 is not academic.

A name brought in by an associate, a debt that was never late, and the shelf at 0.30 (13 Aug). Three entries and no engine change. A NEW CUSTOMER AT CR3-PUD, AND CN6-WM IS CREDITED WITH BRINGING HIM. 1 unit for RM110, paid and delivered on the day, tagged R3 to CN6-WM in full. The introduction rides on the FIRST order and on no later one, which is the rule the CM4-MK row of 10 Aug was booked direct to observe. RM110 sits RM10 under the T3 ask and RM10 over the RM100 anchor, so a small introductory concession was given; CY2-NIL took RM115 on the 11th, so two new names in three days have both opened above the anchor. On the RM47 lot it returns RM63 at 57.3%. The date is assumed to be today, because the instruction gave none. CR3-DAM WAS NEVER LATE, AND THE DESK SAID HE WAS. The RM80 advance of 08 Aug was settled on Wednesday 12 Aug, the day it was promised for. The row had read PAST DUE and named him the only receivable on the book, because the Wednesday had passed with nothing queued. A promise kept and a promise broken look identical to a desk that can only see what has been reported, and the gap here was one day of reporting, not four days of silence. The book now carries no receivable and no open advance at all, CC5-OKR having cleared on the 11th, and his 1 unit credit cap is free rather than at the line. THE SHELF IS AT 0.30 UNIT AGAINST 12.5 PROMISED. STATED_STOCK is ROLLED from the 12 Aug hand count of 1.30, not recounted: one unit moved on this commit and nobody has looked since the 12th, so the plug and the 20.28% leak do not move with it. Cover is a matter of hours at 4.48 unit a day. The buy is no longer a judgement about price, it is the constraint on every order taken from here, and the sale above was made off the last unit but one.

The book goes into a database, read only, and comes back byte for byte (13 Aug). Step two of one source of truth. A D1 database in APAC now holds the whole book, 99 records across six collections and 17 state keys, seeded from this desk by tools/d1.mjs and served read-only at /ledger. This desk remains the source of truth and every response from that endpoint says so: the desk still computes from its own arrays, the daily run still folds the queue into the master, and the Worker carries no insert of any kind, which is asserted by a test rather than left to good intentions. Adding a write path before the store is proven would create precisely the second source of truth this exercise exists to remove. The schema was derived from the rows rather than guessed. The census taken at v292 found sales carrying 26 distinct fields of which only five appear on every row, a nested amend array on 19 of them, and three fields that appear exactly once. A 26 column table with 21 nullable columns would have been mostly empty and would have needed an ALTER every time the book recorded something it had not recorded before, which it demonstrably keeps doing. So each record is stored as its own JSON document with only the columns worth querying lifted out beside it: date, party, product, status, qty and total, indexed on date and party. It is D1 rather than KV because KV rewrites a whole blob and last write wins, so two devices posting at once would silently lose a row; a queue can survive that and a ledger cannot. The round trip is proven, not assumed. The whole book is read back out of the store and compared key by key and row by row against the JSON that went in: all 25 keys and 139 records come back identical. Two faults were caught in the writing of it. Wrangler given a --file uploads it and returns an execution summary instead of the rows, so a SELECT run that way comes back looking successful and carrying nothing; reads now go through --command. And an empty collection disappeared from the store altogether, which meant selfUseLog and lostDemand could not be distinguished from a book that has no notion of self-use; the collection names are now recorded so an empty list survives as an empty list. The endpoint answers /ledger with the snapshot and a count per collection, /ledger/<collection> with the rows, and /ledger/state with the singletons. An unseeded store says so rather than answering an empty book, a known but empty collection answers 200 with no rows rather than 404, and a POST is refused with 405.

A duplicate key eats three ledger steps, and two notes stop telling the time (13 Aug). The CI4-OKR order of 03 Aug carries TWO amend keys in a single row object. JavaScript keeps the last and discards the first in silence, so the three Fulfilment steps that hand the salt over on 04 Aug and take the RM90 on 05 Aug were never in the trail: only the clerical Modification of 31 Jul survived, which moves nothing and leaves the order reading Pending. That is why the Order book counts an item that closed nine days ago. No figure is wrong and none ever was, because the stated deliveredOn, paidOn and cash carry the movements and txPaid reads the full RM180; what was lost is the record of how it happened. A scan of all 148 row objects finds this one and no other. The merge is NOT done here, on purpose: the discarded trail values the redeemed unit at RM95 and the row values it at RM90, so restoring the steps is a RM5 ruling rather than a repair, and it is the owner's. The row now says so on its face, which beats a correct total with a silent hole behind it. Separately, two notes had stopped telling the time. The CR3-DAM advance of 08 Aug said settlement was promised for Wednesday 12 Aug, 'which is TODAY', written on the 12th and read on the 13th: the money did not come, so the note was promising today what was already late. It now reads PAST DUE and adds what matters, that being late does not widen the 1 unit credit cap he sits exactly on. The CI4-OKR note said the order 'remains PENDING and counts nowhere until Monday', ten days after that Monday and eight days after it settled. Last, the read-only chip stopped calling itself the mirror, which was retired on 12 Aug and no longer exists; the state it reports is that no queue server answered, which is what its own tooltip always said, so it now reads 'no server, read only'. Nil trading activity: both queues empty, verified against the live Worker.

The map becomes a heatmap, and ten names come out of the file (12 Aug). The Map tab was a pin map: one labelled circle per party, fanned around its locality, with the place name printed beneath it and repeated in the tooltip, sitting above a gazetteer table that gave every locality by name with coordinates to four decimal places and a sentence on why each was believed. That is a customer directory drawn as a picture, on a desk that is served publicly by decision. It is now a heatmap. Parties are summed to their locality, each locality is one blob whose radius and heat band are its share of the book, and the blobs are composited with screen blending so two near neighbours brighten where they overlap and the picture reads as concentration. There is no text on the canvas beyond the scale bar and the compass, no per-party mark and no tooltip. The fan-out is gone with them: fanning existed to separate individuals and a heatmap has no individuals in it. The gazetteer now holds coordinates and nothing else, rounded from four decimal places to two, from about eleven metres to about 1.1km, which a heatmap blurs over in any case and which no longer points at a street. The table keeps the suffix, the party count, what the locality is worth and its heat band; the suffix is already inside every party code so it discloses nothing further. The names, the original precision and the provenance moved to 06_Data/salt_bio.json under "places", on the laptop and gitignored, beside the real names, which is where they should always have been and where they can still be read when a new suffix needs siting. Ten names were still in the file after the map was fixed, and a scan found them rather than a careful reading. Five were in explanatory comments accumulated over many versions, including one that spelled out where a customer lived while explaining what his code used to reveal. Two were real first names quoted verbatim inside the very comment that explains the payload leak gate, which had been describing a past leak by reproducing it. And three were in the v292 changelog note, which named all three places while describing their removal: the clearest possible argument for checking a file mechanically rather than trusting whoever last edited it.
