That scan is now part of the suite and runs on every build: every name and place in the directory is searched for in the built desk, with the party codes stripped out first because a code embeds its own place abbreviation by design and searching without that step reports every code as a leak. It reads zero. Hard rule 3, that no real name may ever be committed, is enforced rather than trusted.

Three customer locations come out of the ledger notes, and the book is extracted for the first time (12 Aug). Three sales rows spelled a real place into their own prose: a new direct customer at KLCC on 17 Jul, one at Petaling Jaya on 22 Jul and one at Cheras Selatan on 25 Jul. public/desk.html is committed and publicly served, so those three neighbourhoods were readable by anyone holding the URL. Each is replaced by the first three digits of the postcode, 504, 460 and 432: the area survives, the neighbourhood does not, and a three digit prefix covers a great deal more ground than the name it replaces. The prefixes are derived rather than recorded, since the directory holds no postcode field; correcting one is a one word edit and nothing downstream moves. They were found by a gate, not by reading eighty notes. tools/ledger.mjs extracts the book out of the desk and refuses to write the extract if it carries any name or place from the directory. It checks against salt_bio.json on the laptop, which never leaves it, and strips every party code from the text first, because a code embeds its own place abbreviation by design and searching without that step reports every code as a leak. It also learned that TBC is not a place: two parties carry it in the directory as an admission that the location was never known. The larger exposure is PLACES, and it is untouched. The desk carries a map of every party locality with latitude and longitude, built up over many versions. It is configuration rather than ledger, so the extract never reads it, but it ships inside the public desk and it is a good deal more revealing than the three notes just scrubbed. It is left alone deliberately: thinning it is a decision about what the map is for, not a scrub. The extract is step one toward one source of truth. The book is read out of the desk own runtime in jsdom rather than parsed out of the text, so what is captured is what the engine sees, and it is then proven four ways: every data-shaped declaration in the master is accounted for, every value survives JSON, the whole extract round-trips unchanged, and no name appears. Three faults surfaced in the writing of it. The committed book is BASE_SALES, not sales, because applyOverlay rebuilds the live arrays with the uncommitted queue folded over them, so extracting sales would write provisional rows into a store as committed. selfUseLog and lostDemand are ledger arrays declared with let and were invisible to a const-only sweep. And QUOTES holds functions rather than data, so it would have arrived in a store as two nulls without a word. It writes ledger/ledger.json and changes nothing else: this desk remains the source of truth until a store is proven against it.

The phone gets its own app, and the desk moves to /desk (12 Aug). The root was the whole laptop desk, 900 KB, loaded on a phone to read three things. It is now a 25 KB app written for the phone: what needs doing, where the book stands, and recording a transaction. The desk is unchanged and still reachable at /desk, so nothing the app has not rebuilt becomes laptop-only. The app computes nothing. Every figure it shows is read from data.json, which the build produces by running the master in jsdom and calling its own phonePayload(), so a price on a phone is the price this engine computed and the two cannot drift. It is the contract v284 established, now actually consumed by something. The only thing the app originates is a queued entry, written in the exact shape the Whiteboard writes so the daily run folds it with no special case. It holds an entry when there is no signal and pushes on the next connection, and it self-clears against QUEUE_COMMITTED exactly as the desk does. That is why data.json now carries the watermark and the build id: a device key in KV is a REPLACE of that device’s whole queue, so without the mark the app would re-post committed rows for ever, which is the v287 fault wearing a new coat. Two service worker faults were found and fixed on the way, both of which this move would have exposed rather than caused. It cached EVERY navigation as the offline shell, so a single visit to /desk would have made the desk the thing you get offline instead of the app. And data.json was not on the never-cache list, so it would have fallen into the cache-first branch and shown one build’s figures for ever while the freshness poll cheerfully reported the phone current. The freshness id now hashes the app as well as the desk, or an app-only change would have been invisible to that poll. Liquid Glass in the Ledger tuning, the cold, calm, formal end of the language and the right one for a trading book. Registers in house order, Do before Watch: what needs doing sits above what there is to look at. A note on the numbering. v290, the double stock count, was committed to the master by another session while this work was in progress, so the app takes v291. The evolution array holds only the current version by design, so v290’s entry lives in this file and nowhere else, exactly as every superseded entry does.

Both shelves counted on the same day, and the board falls through its own floor in five places (12 Aug). Salt was counted at 1.30 against a stated 8.64 and a ledger of 49.20, so the plug widens from 40.56 to 47.90 and the leak from 17.18% to 20.28%. Oil was counted for the first time ever, at 20, against a ledger of 35, so 15 unit are missing and oil's leak stops reading nil at 14.29%. It never had no leak; nobody had ever looked. The 35 it had been carrying was a v267 roll-forward of an 06 Aug count, a derived figure wearing a count's clothes, and the desk had been calling it stated. THE PRICE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT. Effective cost rises with the leak it carries: salt from RM58.91 to RM61.14 a unit and oil from RM7.69 to RM8.92. Five board prices now sit under their own floor: salt T1 at 12.5 unit, RM850 against RM857; and on oil, T1 at 10 unit, RM100 against RM105, and all three tiers at 50 unit, RM420, RM440 and RM470 against RM502. Headroom on both books reads minus one, and salt's safe buying rate is now RM46 against the RM47 it actually pays. Nothing has been repriced. A count is a fact and a price is a decision, and the second is his. What the desk will not do is quietly widen a floor to keep a price legal.

The oil shelf closes, a pending order settles and a new customer opens at the best margin on the book (12 Aug). Four transactions, two of them committed from the phone queue. The missing oil lot is on the book: 50 unit from SP7-PUD for RM350 on the 11th, RM7 a unit, the same top tier of his ladder as the first lot. Oil now walks 5 unit of opening plus 50 bought on the 6th and 50 on the 11th, less 20 sold on the 6th and 7th and 50 on the 11th, which leaves 35 unit on the shelf instead of the minus 15 v286 had to state. Nothing in the cost basis moves, and the 15 unit that had been carried at RM7 with no lot behind them now have one. Oil’s stated count stays null, because recording a purchase is not the same as counting a shelf and nobody has looked since the 7th. CE4-CHE’s 2.5 unit is settled. It had stood undated and counted nowhere, drawing no stock and raising no revenue, because an agreed-on date is an intention rather than a movement; the money and the salt both moved on the 12th. It dates from the agreement on the 11th with its movements stamped on the 12th, the same shape as CC5-OKR’s advance. RM230 at RM92 a unit is his standing price, matching 23 Jul and 31 Jul, and on the RM47 lot it returns RM112.50 at 48.9%. Its 2.5 unit come off the shelf for the first time. A new customer opens at CY2-NIL: 2 unit for RM230 on the 11th, paid and delivered on the day. RM115 a unit sits above CA4-DAM’s RM100 anchor and CE4-CHE’s RM92 standing price, and just under the RM116.67 a unit CA4-DAM paid on 26 Jul, so a first order took a full rate and no introductory discount was given. RM68 a unit on the RM47 lot is RM136 on the order at 59.1%, the best margin any retail order has returned. He is booked as ordinary retail rather than an associate, so he carries the 1 unit credit cap, and nothing is owed against it. The name and location are in the directory only and appear nowhere in the desk. CA4-DAM takes another half unit at RM50, his seventh order at exactly RM100 a unit, which is the steadiest rate on the book. No date was given and the order was reported complete, so it is booked on the 12th and the assumption is written on the row rather than left in a conversation. The stated salt count rolls from 13.64 to 8.64 for the 5 unit that moved, and the queue watermark moves with the commit, which is the v287 lesson made routine: update.mjs now refuses to ship when anything still above the mark already looks committed.

Writes are gated by a key, reads stay open (12 Aug). The desk is public to read by the owner’s decision, and that was never the whole exposure. Anyone with the URL could POST into the cloud queue; drain unions any POST into salt_queue_cloud.json and the daily run folds it into the master as real ledger rows with no review step between, so a stranger could write into the book rather than merely read it. A write now carries X-Salt-Key, checked against the SALT_WRITE_KEY secret and compared over the whole string so a wrong key cannot be found one character at a time by timing. The phone asks for the key once and keeps it in localStorage; a 401 asks again and retries exactly once, because a wrong key looping would ask for ever. The gate is dormant until the secret is set. With SALT_WRITE_KEY unset writeOk returns true and nothing changes at all. That is deliberate and it is the lesson of 11 Aug restated: the desk that can send the header must be live on the phone BEFORE the gate starts demanding it, or the owner locks himself out of his own queue exactly as the policy-less Access application did. Ship first, arm second. Reads are untouched, so Zero Trust stays off as instructed and the ledger is still world-readable on purpose. The laptop server ignores the header, so the desk behaves identically there, and drain and seed-vault push through wrangler rather than HTTP so neither is affected.

The v286 commit left the watermark behind, and the phone counted three orders twice (12 Aug). v286 folded four queued entries into the ledger and never moved QUEUE_COMMITTED, which is the one thing that stops a committed entry replaying. Three of the four stayed above the old mark, so the overlay booked them a second time on top of the rows that already carried them: the 30 unit CS6-BS order, the 20 unit resell and CE4-CHE’s 2.5 unit pending. That is 50 unit out and RM450 of cash counted twice, and one pending order drawn twice. Oil read minus 65 unit on the phone against the minus 15 the ledger states, and the ledger was right. Verified against the live Worker rather than inferred: it returned five queue entries, four of them above the old mark, and three of those four were already in the v286 ledger. The mark moves to 2026-08-11T21:33:18.232Z, which is salt_queue_cloud.json’s own updated. That is the v274 rule applied to the cloud file rather than the laptop one, and it is emphatically not the clock: it sits after all four entries that file held and before the SP7-PUD 50 unit buy queued at 08:47 today, so the four clear and the buy survives to be committed on its own run, which is what closes the minus 15. Nothing sits in the gap on the laptop side either: salt_queue.json still reads updated 2026-08-11T11:20:59.607Z with zero rows, and an entry queued there since would have moved that stamp. The residual risk is unchanged and is stated rather than waved away: a second browser holding entries stamped before this instant that has never posted loses them. The cloud build had never shipped either. The master went to v286 at 10:18 and public/index.html was still the v285 build seven hours later, so the phone was reading yesterday’s ledger while the laptop read today’s. Built with all nine patches anchored, 66 of 66 assertions passed, deployed, and the queue pruned to the one entry that is genuinely still pending.

Four from the phone, and the oil shelf will not bear two of them (12 Aug). The daily run folded four queued entries, all of them from the cloud queue and none from the laptop. CC5-OKR’s RM90 advance is settled: the unit went out on the 8th with nothing paid and the money landed on the 11th, three days out and inside terms. It was the only receivable on the book and it held him exactly at the 1 unit retail credit cap, so both readings clear at once and the sole open advance is now CR3-DAM’s RM80, promised for today. CE4-CHE took 2.5 unit at RM230, booked pending and therefore undated, because an agreed-on date is an intention rather than a movement; it is his fourth order at that exact size and price inside three weeks, which makes RM92 a unit his standing rate rather than a quote. THE OIL BOOK IS SHORT 15 UNIT. 50 unit went out on the 11th, 30 direct to CS6-BS at RM330 and 20 through his resell bucket at RM120, against a shelf of 35: five of opening plus one 50 unit lot, less the 20 already sold on the 6th and the 7th. An oil purchase made somewhere between 07 and 11 Aug was never queued. Both orders are booked because both happened, and no lot has been invented to make the arithmetic close. Oil’s stated count is withdrawn to null rather than rolled, because 35 less 50 is minus 15 and a count cannot be negative; null says nobody has looked since, which is the truth, and it lets the ledger stand at minus 15 so the desk states its own breach instead of asserting a shelf that cannot exist. This is the same breach v228 raised, in the same direction, and it clears the same way: record the purchase and the walk closes by itself. The two orders read very differently. The 30 unit direct order is the largest oil order on the book and the first bought for himself rather than resold, RM11 a unit for RM120 of margin at 36.4%, the best oil has returned, and it sits on the customer hurdle rather than the associate one. The 20 unit resell is the first order this book has ever sold below cost: RM6 a unit against a RM7 lot, minus RM20 at minus 16.7%, less than half the RM13 the same reseller fetched on the 6th and RM1 under the sharpest rate the supplier has ever quoted, so supply does not explain it. It was queued against a CS6-BS-Gen bucket, absorbed into CS6-BS-R at v280, so it is re-keyed rather than minting a retired code. FIFO takes the 30 off the RM7 lot in full and the first five of the 20; the remaining 15 have no lot behind them and are carried at RM7 as the last known rate rather than left uncosted. Two notes were repaired where the trade moved under them: the CC5-OKR row no longer claims to be the only receivable, and the CR3-DAM row no longer calls itself the second open advance.

Salt first, then oil, and it is now a rule rather than a coincidence (11 Aug). Standing instruction: every list, table and payload leads with salt. The order was already right, but only because that is the order PRODUCTS happens to be keyed in, and any alphabetical sort would have put oil first. PROD_ORDER states it and PROD_IDS derives from it, so the eighteen places that enumerate products inherit it from one line, and phonePayload, which had been calling Object.keys itself, now uses the same source. A product not named in PROD_ORDER is appended rather than dropped, so a third book still appears and simply has no stated position until it earns one. Proven against a PRODUCTS keyed oil-first, against an alphabetical sort and against a hypothetical third product: all three come back salt, oil. Recorded in the daily SKILL too, because the brief is written by hand and a rule that lives only in code would not reach it.

A contract for a phone app that renders separately, and the gate that stops it leaking (11 Aug). The cloud app is the laptop desk shipped whole: 900 KB loaded on a phone to show three things. A separate app cannot simply be written against the ledger, because the moment it prices anything itself there are two engines and they drift, which is the fault v205 spent its whole entry fixing. So the phone will compute NOTHING. phonePayload() is the entire contract: the board, the parties, the position per product and the action list, 1.6 KB against 900 KB, built by running the master in jsdom and calling its own functions, so a price on a phone is the price this engine computed. Then it tried to leak, twice, and both are worth recording. The first payload carried RM 58.88/unit effective in an action's reasoning, straight out of prose written for him at his own desk; the `why` text is gone and the phone gets the instruction without the arithmetic. The second was far worse: it carried Chase Chris and Chase Ron, real names, because `revealed` has defaulted to TRUE since v217 so ID() returns a name whenever the directory is loaded, and the app this feeds is public by decision with no sign-in. The payload now forces the lock for the duration of its own build and restores it after. phonePayloadLeaks() is the gate and it runs the leak_test vocabulary, every per-unit cost in the book in money form, and every real name the directory can currently see; the build REFUSES to write data.json if it returns anything. It is proven rather than assumed: a payload built without the lock is caught carrying Ron and Chris, and the locked one comes back clean. One false alarm was fixed on the way, because a check that cries wolf teaches you to skim past the real one: the generated ISO timestamp can read as the money form of a RM7 cost, so it is scrubbed before the scan.

The desk stops scrolling sideways on a phone, and it was one line (11 Aug). At a 375px screen the document scrolled to 1649px and sections measured anywhere from 353 to 796. Four wrong causes were chased and reported before the right one: the rail at 1647px looked like an overflow and is a deliberate scroller; a `1fr` KPI grid computing 274px columns looked like the trap and was merely splitting a parent that was already too wide; a `.rule` span at 735px was a `flex:1` filler growing into space, not making it; and a Chart.js canvas at 756px inside a 324px box was real but not the driver. The cause was `.shell` turning into a column flex at 860px. Its children `.main` and `.rail` then sized to their own content, and every heading, paragraph and card below simply filled the width it had been handed, which is exactly why they all measured wide and why none of them was ever the cause. `min-width:0` alone does not fix it, because in a COLUMN flex the automatic minimum applies to the main axis, which is height; it takes max-width:100% to cap the box and let the rail's own `overflow-x:auto` engage. The caps sit at the 860 breakpoint, where the column starts, not at 560 where they were first written and left 561-860px still broken. Result, measured: horizontal overflow across all fifteen tabs falls from up to 1274px to zero, at 375px and at 1265px alike, and the rail is now a 352px box scrolling 1728px of content as designed. Two smaller faults fixed on the way: a Chart.js canvas can no longer set the width of the document, and the Ledger row, a flex of no-shrink columns totalling 470px including a fixed 126px state column, now wraps.

An hour of his own time gets a price, and every lot size gets the minute it stops paying (11 Aug). RM150,000 a year over 2,080 contracted hours is RM72.12 an hour, now set in COST_BOOK. It is recorded as a CONVENTION rather than a measurement, in the comment beside it: the salt hours are evenings and weekends, so the true opportunity cost of one of them may sit either side of a salary rate. The cost panel gains one column and it is the sharpest on the desk. Contribution divided by what an hour of his time is worth gives the minute past which an order earns him nothing. On T1 a half unit and a single unit both stop paying at 13 minutes, end to end. On T2 the same sizes hold to 21 and 30, and on T3 to 38 and 47. That reframes what a tier is. It is not a loyalty discount, it is a decision about how many minutes of his own evening a customer is worth, and that is a reason a tier can be defended out loud where a missing unit never could. Delivery is no longer assumed: 69 logged trips put it at RM5 an order, so one of the three per-order lines is now measured and only packaging and handling remain null. And a false alarm, corrected. The Ledger's quick-mark buttons on the undated CJ4-BJ order render the word undefined, which looked like a dead control. It is not: the row's key really does contain that string on both sides, so ovFind matches and the button works. Only the readable queue line needed fixing, and it now says planned, undated rather than agreed undefined.
THE INTERACTION PASS: OIL DRAWS, AND THE DESK MOVES
n: Per-product charts draw per product at last. Every canvas now resolves inside its own product block with the book state set to match, so the oil analysis, sourcing outlook, inventory walk, monthly financials and pricing board charts exist for the first time; they had drawn into the salt canvas, or nowhere, since two books arrived at v262.
A chart is keyed to its canvas, never to a shared variable: a shared variable can only remember one book, so drawing the second used to destroy and blank the first.
One chart language, set once on the library: desk type, glass tooltips, round caps, and animation that switches itself off under reduced motion.

The pricing overrides no longer collapse the tab. A keystroke re-renders through the same per-product path as the first paint, and the controls in the second book respond too; they had never been wired.
The rail answers the keyboard (arrows, Home, End), tells assistive tech which tab you are on, and on a phone stays pinned to the top of the screen, so navigation is never a scroll away.
The address carries the tab, so a reload, including the cloud ten-second refresh, reopens where you were; the back gesture still leaves the desk in one step.

Every tab owns an accent now: Forward azure, Sourcing amber, Analysis violet, Map teal, and the six that had fallen back to gold are named. The headline, the table headers, the active tab and the third orb carry it, so the light follows where you are.
Sections settle in with a short stagger, buttons press, bars fill from zero, and tables hint at hidden columns behind you as well as ahead. All of it obeys reduced motion.

Filed on the 11 Aug daily run, not by the session that made the change. That session prepended its entry to `evolution` instead, which is the one-entry version chip and not the history; the duplicate v280 entry it left behind was removed and the watermark moved to the queue the version was published against. No ledger figure moved: every data constant is byte-identical to v280 and the engine returns the same twenty figures.

t: THE AUGUST AUDIT, AND THE FOUR THINGS IT CHANGED
n: Every August row walked one by one for confirmation, twenty six of them, and eleven corrected.

CJ4-BJ 15 Jul restated: revenue RM710 not RM850, because the 2.0588 unit withheld to settle two older balances was never sold. The RM140 becomes a collection on those orders rather than revenue here, and nothing was ever settled in kind for him.
FIFO throughout, on his instruction. The shelf reached zero on 28 Jul, so everything delivered from that date costs RM47.
Goodwill is an EXPENSE. It earns no revenue and carries no cost of goods, because no sale happened; the row stays so the salt still leaves the shelf.
CJ4-OKR's four earned units recorded at last. They had left the shelf with no row against them and were absorbed by the shrinkage plug, which falls from 44.56 to 40.56 unit.
The identifier is back on the old convention: C or S, the initial, the number of letters in the name, then the location. The short roster codes are purged with no translation table.

One reward scheme replaces the resell, refer and large-lot triggers. Hurdle is base lot times cheapest unit cost times 20 for a customer and 10 for an associate. Resale and referral are one stream; an associate's own buying takes the customer hurdle. Four margin bands decide how much, because turnover and margin rank almost nothing alike.

THE PRINTED BOARD IS GONE. A ladder derived from cost on every render replaces it: floor, good, great and ceiling at 15, 33.33, 66.67 and 100 per cent markup on the lot cost. It cannot go stale and there is nothing to reprint.
ONE FLOOR ACROSS EVERY SIZE. The retail and wholesale split made the floor FALL as quantity ROSE, from RM433.66 at 6.25 unit to RM425.73 at 6.5. A markup on a lot cost cannot invert.

Headroom walks the prices actually being charged rather than printed cards, and each hit says whether it is under floor, under replacement or under cost. Four live prices are under floor today and none is under cost.
The encrypted vault now re-keys itself whenever the directory changes, so a re-code reaches the phone with no further action.

THE COST IS UNLOCKED and moves live. Two freezes held it, not one: the lock returned a captured snapshot, and even off that path the shrink rate still preferred the stored figure, so unlocking the lot alone changed nothing.
Unlocking took prices under floor from four to one. Only CS6-PER's 12.5 unit loan settlement remains, and it is RM32.65 above replacement and not under cost.
CS6-PER settled the RM60 outstanding on his 07 Aug order. Nothing is owed on that account either way.

Prose warden pass: nine repairs, engine outputs identical before and after. Row notes no longer carry a hardcoded replacement cost, because a figure typed into prose goes stale the moment the buying rate moves.

THE PHONE HAD NO CHARTS BECAUSE OF A MISSING FILE. ensureChart loads assets/chart.umd.js from the same origin rather than a CDN, and the build copied the desk without it, so every chart 404'd and fell through to the text notice. The build now copies it.

Second prose pass: the walk-away is gone from every note, and every surviving card reference is marked as the retired vocabulary it is rather than restated with a figure that has since moved. Engine outputs identical before and after.

t: The phone can show names, and only by decrypting them
n: ONE CONTROL, TWO BEHAVIOURS, because the desk runs in two places. On the laptop the directory is plaintext in salt_bio.json, reaches the page over localhost, and Show is a screen-privacy toggle with editing as the whole point. On the phone the plaintext directory NEVER ships, the Worker answers /bio with an empty object, and only the AES-GCM envelope syncs to /vault. So there Show is a DECRYPT: it asks for the passphrase inline, uses it, discards it, and offers nothing to edit because there is no store to write back to.

THREE THINGS WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WRONG AND WERE CAUGHT BY TESTING THE STATES RATHER THAN THE HAPPY PATH. First, `revealed` defaults to TRUE, correct on the laptop and wrong on the phone, where the panel opened in a revealed state before any decrypt had happened: the button read Hide with nothing shown. It is DERIVED now via namesShown(), not assigned, because cloud mode is only known once the ping answers and setting revealed=false at that moment races whatever has already read it.

Second, with names locked the row fell through to the laptop's editable branch and drew 29 empty edit boxes over a directory the phone cannot save, reading from a BIO that is always empty there. Locked must mean locked.

Third, Hide on the phone was a toggle, which left the decrypted map sitting in vaultNames for anything that read it directly. It calls lockVault now, which drops the map as well as the flag. The build already wires visibilitychange to lockVault in cloud mode, so leaving the app does the same.

ACCESS IS OFF AND STAYING OFF, by his decision, and that changes what this button protects. The sealed file is reachable by anyone with the address, so the passphrase is the only thing between it and a real name. The panel says exactly that, in those words, next to the box where the passphrase is typed.

THE TWO BUILD STRINGS CLAIMING THE PHONE SITS BEHIND CLOUDFLARE ACCESS ARE GONE. They were true when written and false now. A desk that misdescribes its own protection is worse than one that says nothing, because it invites a decision made on a guarantee that does not exist.

THE KDF ITERATION COUNT NOW TRAVELS IN THE ENVELOPE. It was hardcoded at 150,000 in both the desk and tools/seed-vault.mjs, so raising it would have stranded every blob already sealed. Absent means 150,000, which is every existing blob, and a future seed can cost more without breaking anything.

A WRONG PASSPHRASE AND A CORRUPT BLOB ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE at the crypto layer, because AES-GCM only reports that the tag did not verify. Both are reported as 'that passphrase did not open it', which is the honest reading and the useful one.

Verified headlessly with real WebCrypto: seal, wrong passphrase refused, empty passphrase refused, correct passphrase opens and resolves a code to a name, lock clears the map and returns ID() to codes, and the iteration count round-trips. All fifteen tabs still render clean under both products, parityScan returns nothing, and the built bundle carries none of the 57 directory names.

t: Portrait
n: LANDSCAPE WAS ALWAYS FINE AND THAT IS THE CLUE. A phone on its side is 640 to 930px, which lands in the 860px rules, and those rules are a narrow DESKTOP layout rather than a phone one. Portrait is about 390px and had no rules of its own: the smallest breakpoint on this desk was 640px, so portrait got the desktop layout squeezed.

THE WHOLE PAGE SCROLLED SIDEWAYS. Every cell carries white-space:nowrap, which is exactly right for a figure and fatal at this width, and 56 of the 58 tables had no scroll container, so the overflow escaped to the document and took the entire layout with it. th.l and td.l were already position:sticky and had nothing to be sticky inside.

iOS ZOOMED ON EVERY TAP INTO A FIELD. Safari zooms the viewport whenever a focused input is under 16px; the fields were 15px. One pixel, and it left the page zoomed and off-centre after every entry, which made the Transaction tab unusable one-handed. The fields are 16px at narrow widths.

TABLES SCROLL INSIDE THEIR OWN CARD, WITH THE LABEL COLUMN PINNED. That is the right treatment for a dense numeric table, because reading down a column IS the job; reflowing one into stacked cards would destroy the comparison it exists to support. A fade on the right edge says there is more, because on a touch screen nothing else does.

THE WRAPPER IS APPLIED AT RUNTIME, TO EVERY TABLE, rather than by hand at the 58 render sites. A rule applied by hand in 58 places is a rule that will be missed in the 59th, which is the same reasoning that put deskctl and parityScan on this desk. It runs after applyNotes, which rewrites innerHTML and would otherwise orphan a wrapper made before it, and it is idempotent: verified across 100 rendered tables with no nesting after three consecutive runs.

THE RAIL IS ONE SCROLLING ROW instead of a wrapped block of fifteen buttons that cost most of a screen before any content began, and the chosen tab scrolls itself into view because on a scrolling rail it can sit off-screen. The mode switcher and the other control strips scroll for the same reason.
viewport-fit=cover WITH SAFE-AREA PADDING, so the page paints into a notch and pads itself back deliberately rather than being letterboxed.

NOT VERIFIED FROM HERE, AND SAID PLAINLY: there is no headless browser on this surface, so jsdom proved the structure, the CSS balance and the wrapper behaviour but nothing about how it LOOKS. The 560px rules and the type scale need an eye on a real phone.
Everything else unchanged: all fifteen tabs render clean under both products, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity.

t: The desk can record oil, and it now tests its own product split
n: IT COULD NOT RECORD OIL AT ALL, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER TO WHERE THE OIL TRANSACTION TAB WAS. tabWorkbench had no product control, no wbRecord payload carried a product, and ovNew pushed rows without one, so prodOf() read every entry ever made through the form as salt. The three oil rows on the book were written into the data by hand. A selector built from PROD_IDS now sits on the four modes that have a product, and is deliberately absent from the two that do not: an amendment inherits the product of the order it attaches to, and a follow-up is a conversation with a person.

A STOCK COUNT COULD SILENTLY OVERWRITE SALT'S SHELF, which is worse than any display fault. statedStock was one scalar: a count queued while oil was on screen was accepted, announced in the provisional bar, discarded for oil, and written over SALT's counted figure, the one number this desk documents as always beating the ledger. It is keyed by product now, and countedFor() answers for any book, returning null where none has been counted so the ledger stands rather than a count being invented. selfUseLog and lostDemand carry a product too.

AN AUDIT OF ALL FIFTEEN TABS FOUND THE v228 SPLIT WAS NEVER FINISHED. Six tabs were wrapped in perProduct and roughly forty reads behind them, and inside the helpers they call, still took `sales` and `purchases` WHOLE while being compared against figures recompute() had scoped to one product. The order book was caught at v272 by eye and the rest sat unnoticed for forty-seven versions.

forecast() WAS THE WORST OF THEM AND IS FIXED. Four whole-book reads walked against a scoped shelf, so Promised out printed the same 14.5 unit under both books: salt's promises measured against oil's 35 unit shelf. Salt now reads 14.5 and oil correctly reads nil.

cashFlow.dueIn MATCHED WHOLE-BOOK CASH OUT AGAINST ONE BOOK'S RECEIVABLE, so the object was not internally commensurable while Today printed the pair side by side. It is whole now, and computed from the primitives rather than by walking PROD and calling recompute() inside a function that forecast() calls mid-flight, which would have clobbered the caller's own globals. The obvious fix was the dangerous one.

TODAY, FORWARD AND OVERVIEW SAY WHICH BOOK THEY ARE SHOWING. All three draw one product while their leads claim the desk, and the v228 comment asserting the switcher scoped them was stale: the builders map never wrapped them, and v262 turned the switcher into a jump button. The label sits in its own row OUTSIDE the lead, because the prose fold truncates a lead to its first sentence and replaces the node's HTML: the first attempt put the badge at the end of the lead and it vanished behind Method and caveats. A label whose job is to stop a figure being misread cannot be the thing that folds away.

THE DESK NOW TESTS ITS OWN SPLIT. parityScan() states what must hold if scoping is right and reports what does not: two books cannot owe the same quantity by coincidence, a book with no orders cannot have commitments or receivables, an uncounted book must not borrow another's count, and the form must be able to reach every book. It returns clean on this book. The point is product three: declaring one should surface its own gaps on the Whiteboard within a load instead of waiting to be read out of the source, because knowing which globals are scoped is a rule that has to be remembered and this desk has learned twice what happens to those.

THE OBSERVATION ENGINE WAS INCOHERENT ON THIS AXIS AND IS NOT NOW. The rhythm was pinned to salt while the pricing and upkeep rules read pxCost() and tierBoard(), which follow the active product, so one tab mixed one book's demand with another's cost. Per-product ids carry the product, so hushing salt's shrinkage does not hush oil's. The customer families widened to the whole book, which is why one-and-done reads 28 names rather than 26.

C09'S 1 UNIT ADVANCE IS COMMITTED. RM90 at the Tier II ask, the unit handed over on the 8th and no cash, so it is the only receivable on the book and it puts him exactly at the 1 unit retail cap: Boundaries reads it as at the line rather than over it. Consistent with his own words on 06 Aug that he is reducing his intake. It books to salt, and it is the last row whose product was implied rather than chosen.

STILL OUTSTANDING, AND LISTED SO IT IS NOT LOST: roughly thirty scoping sites remain, the largest being stockHistory's mixed-scope shelf walk, pxSignals and pxRecentBuyRate feeding blended buy rates into the live board, riskRates, lotOutlook, sourcingPlan, tabAnalysis, tabInventory's in-transit list, tabFinancials valuing closing stock at salt's roll under every heading, and drawAnalysis and drawOutlookChart which resolve canvases by an id perProduct emits twice, so oil's charts never draw at all. Customers, Network and Map are documented as whole-business and read scoped figures. Statements add salt and oil into one unit column.

t: A version bump commits the queue, and deskctl now refuses one that does not
n: HIS RULE, MADE MECHANICAL, BECAUSE v273 BROKE IT THE SAME DAY IT WAS STATED. That push bumped the version and left QUEUE_COMMITTED exactly where it was. A rule that has to be remembered is a rule that gets missed, which is the same reasoning that put deskctl on this desk in the first place when a SKILL file failed to stop the mirror drifting seven versions behind.

THE WATERMARK NOW NAMES THE QUEUE FILE RATHER THAN THE LAST ENTRY IN IT. It had been set to the last entry's own 'at', a millisecond short of the file's 'updated'. That worked only by luck: the desk drops an entry on at <= QUEUE_COMMITTED, so it survived because nothing happened to sit in the gap. A queue file whose 'updated' fell between two entries would have replayed one of them, silently and on every load.

deskctl READS THE QUEUE NOW. status prints the file's row count, its 'updated' and the master's watermark, and says which of three states it is in: committed, watermark stale, or n uncommitted. stamp refuses outright while entries sit above the watermark, and refuses a VERSION BUMP while the watermark merely trails the file. The refusal comes before the manifest is written, so a refused stamp leaves no record claiming the bump was recorded.

BOTH REFUSALS WERE TESTED BEFORE BEING RELIED ON, against a scratch copy of the tree with its own DESK.json and a planted queue entry, never against the real folder: a checker nobody has seen fail is a checker nobody knows works.

THE ONE WAY THE RULE MUST NEVER BE SATISFIED IS BY MOVING THE MARK TO THE CLOCK. That would clear the check and drop everything written since the last snapshot, including browser-held entries no surface here has ever seen. It turns a loud failure into a quiet data loss, so the refusal message says so and the constant carries the reasoning beside it.

TODAY'S JUMP IS SAFE FOR A STATED REASON RATHER THAN A HABIT. The desk self-cleared at 11:46 KL and its server wrote a FULL SNAPSHOT of the browser queue back to 06_Data holding zero rows, so the authoritative queue at that instant was empty and nothing is discarded by moving to it. The residual risk, stated rather than waved away, is a second browser holding entries stamped before that instant that has never posted; that is inherent to a watermark and is the price of entries not replaying for ever.

DESK.json STATES paths.queue, so no surface has to guess where the queue lives after the folder was filed by function. Servers already resolved every write through a single DATA constant; deskctl now agrees with them explicitly rather than by coincidence.

A MISSING QUEUE FILE IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE, and status says so in those words. The desk holds its queue in the browser until a server writes it out, so absence of a file is absence of evidence and must never be reported as 'nothing pending'.
NOTHING ON THE BOOK MOVED. All fifteen tabs render clean, every headline figure is unchanged, and boardHeadroom(false) still returns RM0 with T1 breaching at RM48.

t: The Whiteboard derives itself
n: THE P-SERIES IS GONE AND Q1 IS ANSWERED. Seventeen hand-written plans came off the tab because every one of them was a reading of the book at a moment that had passed, and a stale plan on a desk is worse than no plan because it reads as current. P4 quoted shrinkage at 12.7% against today's 18.9%, P17 was struck on a 38.23 unit plug against 44.56, and P11 proposed a reorder trigger that has since been built into the Inventory tab. Q1 closes as the duplicate: the 05 Aug entry booking 2 unit through N19 for RM250 was the 06 Aug order re-entered, it was never committed, and closing it moves no figure, which is precisely the outcome raising it was meant to protect.

IN THEIR PLACE, observations() READS THE WHOLE BOOK ON EVERY LOAD. Six families, split by what you would do about the item rather than where the data came from: demand rhythm, integrity, customers, pricing drift, worth doing, and desk upkeep. Because every item is derived it cannot go stale and cannot disagree with the tab it came from, which is the failure the P-series kept repeating. What survives on the tab by hand is what the book genuinely cannot see: a promise made to somebody, a standing intention, a judgement with no figure behind it.

THE RHYTHM IS MEASURED ON ORDER DATES, NOT DELIVERY DATES. Demand arrives when somebody asks; when the salt moved is a fulfilment fact and belongs to the shelf walk. It reports orders a day beside units a day and judges itself on the former, because on a book this size a single 12.5 unit lot lands on one weekday and makes that weekday look like a phenomenon. Silent days are counted too: a day nobody ordered is evidence about that weekday, and dropping it would read only the days that worked.

EVERY FACTOR IS SHRUNK BEFORE IT REACHES AN INSTRUCTION, by n/(n+8) towards no effect, and confidence is judged on the THINNEST bucket rather than the total. Fifty-five orders sounds ample until they are cut seven ways and each weekday stands on six days, so anything leaning on a per-day split is labelled thin however many orders the book holds. Weekends run at 0.62 orders a day against 1.52 on weekdays; the pay window, the 25th to the 7th under the seven-day wage rule, runs BEHIND mid-month at 1.15 against 1.39, which was not the expected direction.

THE HOLIDAY FACTOR IS PINNED AT 1.00 AND THE TAB SAYS WHY. Not one Kuala Lumpur holiday falls inside 26 Jun to 08 Aug, so this book has never traded through one and there is no lift to apply. The table itself was verified against two sources, which disagreed on three dates; the tie was broken on internal consistency, so Aidilfitri reads 20 to 21 March and Awal Muharram 16 June. 2027 carries statutory fixed dates only, because a guessed festival date produces a confident and wrong restock instruction.

TWO RULES WERE TUNED AFTER THEY CRIED WOLF ON THE FIRST RUN. The duplicate rule flagged A10's two genuine 0.5 unit orders as urgent; it now shouts only where the book CANNOT tell the pair apart, which is the shape the N19 re-entry had, and murmurs where different dates or trails already separate them. The undated-delivery rule flagged 22 rows, almost all first-fortnight walk-ins paid in full on the day where the assumption cannot be wrong; it now fires only where the book itself says the day was not clean, which took it to none. A rule that cries wolf teaches you to skip it, which costs more than the rule earns.

HUSHES RIDE THE QUEUE AS mode:'obs' and applyOverlay now ignores that mode BY NAME. Plans and hushes already fell through the unknown-mode return, but silently, so the desk's guarantee that neither can touch a figure rested on an accident of ordering. Restore had to be made an entry that overrules rather than an absence, because the queue is append-only and cannot delete what came before it; without that the Bring back button wrote a record that read as another kind of hush.

THE RAIL SCROLLS ON ITS OWN and a back-to-top button appears once there is something to go back up to. At fifteen tabs on a short viewport the sticky rail could not be scrolled to reach the Actions group at all. TAB_LABEL was hoisted out of tabToday, which owned it while the Whiteboard needed the same map, because two label maps drift and the one that drifts is the one nobody is looking at.

NOTHING OUTSIDE THE WHITEBOARD MOVED. Every headline figure was extracted before and after and compared: stock 23.64 unit, free to sell 22.64, roll RM47.47, revenue RM15,373, collected RM14,362, margin RM5,921 at 38.5%, receivables nil, plug 44.56 unit at 18.9%, cover 5.9 days, and boardHeadroom(false) still RM0 with T1 breaching at RM48.

t: The order book reads one product at a time
n: IT WAS DRAWN TWICE AND READ EVERYTHING BOTH TIMES. tabReceivables took `sales` and `purchases` WHOLE while being rendered once per product, so an oil order appeared under the Salt heading and a salt order under Oil, and the total beneath each heading was the total of the whole book. The split at v262 gave it two headings and no scoping.

EVERY LIST ON IT IS NOW SCOPED: deferred salt owed to customers, pending orders, unpaid supplier bills and lots in transit. Salt carries five lines; oil carries none, which is correct, because nothing on the oil book is outstanding.

TWO EXCEPTIONS, BOTH DELIBERATE AND BOTH STATED IN THE SOURCE. A customer refund carries no product because it is a customer-level obligation, so it shows once on the default book rather than being duplicated under every heading. And the written-off supplier default stays salt-only by construction, because a default belongs to the book it happened on and must not follow the switcher onto another product's page.
S07'S ORDER NEEDED NO CHANGE. It already reads exactly as he describes it: 2 unit, nothing delivered, no cash received, one unit settled in kind by the reward and one unit still to pay for.

IT DRAWS AS TWO LINES ON THE ORDER BOOK AND THAT IS RIGHT. One unit is DEFERRED, because he has given value and received nothing, so the desk owes him salt. One unit is PENDING, because neither money nor salt has moved against it. A half-settled order cannot be one line without lying about one half of it.
NOTHING IS RECEIVABLE against that order, and nothing should be: he has not been handed anything, so there is nothing to be owed for.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; the Salt and Oil blocks on the order book no longer carry identical content; no boundary breaches.

t: An invented delivery reversed, and two orders collected
n: S07'S ORDER WAS BOOKED AS DELIVERED AND IT HAS NOT BEEN. He stated a price and a settlement and said nothing about handing anything over; I filled the gap. That is the second correction to the same row today and both were mine rather than his: first the cash was booked as received, now the salt as handed over.
SO 2 UNIT GO BACK ON THE SHELF and the RM 80 receivable disappears. You cannot be owed money for goods you have not handed over, so there is nothing receivable on the whole book again.

THE ORDER NOW READS OPEN, PAID AHEAD OF DELIVERY. The reward is drawn down and RM 80 of value is settled against nothing received, so the desk OWES HIM 1 UNIT. The reward stays applied: reversing a delivery does not un-earn a reward any more than reversing a payment did.

E16 AND Z20 ARE PAID AND COLLECTED, so the 3.5 unit the desk owed them go out on the 8th and only S07's single unit is left deferred. Both had paid on the 8th and collected the same day, so each draws as one line rather than three.
Z20'S IS HIS SECOND ORDER, so he leaves Tier III with it. From the next quote he is Tier II by the LEDGER rather than by concession, which is what the RM 100 he was charged already assumed.

THE SHELF IS 23.64 AND FREE TO SELL 22.64. Cover is 5.9 days against a 15 unit trigger, on a shipping rate that has climbed from 3.48 to 3.84 a day this week. The rate is rising because the week's trade has been dense, so cover is falling faster than the shelf alone would suggest.
REVENUE RM 15,373.26, collected RM 14,362, margin RM 5,921.40 at 38.5%, nothing receivable, 1 unit deferred. The plug holds at 44.56 and the leak at 18.87%.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; no boundary breaches; every reseller reads earned equals applied; the only deferred position is the one unit owed to S07.

t: Hugo requoted to RM260 and settled, and cover falls to 5.8 days
n: H29'S OPENING ORDER IS REQUOTED FROM RM 300 TO RM 260 and paid and delivered in full on the 8th.

RESTATED RATHER THAN AMENDED. A price re-agreed before any cash or salt moves is the price, not a movement, so the row carries the final terms and the history sits in its note. An amendment trail here would have drawn a Modification and a Fulfilment to describe an order that only ever happened once.

RM 86.67 A UNIT IS THE TIER II ASK given to a customer whose single order puts him in Tier III at RM 300. A RM 40 concession to open the account: RM 49 clear of the RM 211 floor, RM 119 of margin, and RM 26.67 a unit above replacement.

COVER IS NOW THE HEADLINE AND IT IS 5.8 DAYS. The shelf is 25.14 unit but FREE TO SELL is 21.64, because 3.5 unit are already owed to E16 and Z20 who have both paid. At the last fortnight's 3.73 a day that is under six days, against a reorder trigger of 15 unit which is roughly six days away.

THREE DELIVERIES IN TWO DAYS TOOK 8 UNIT OFF THE SHELF: 2 to S07, 3 to H29, and 1 to A10 before them. The shipping rate has risen from 3.48 a day to 3.73 with it, so cover is falling from both ends at once.
REVENUE RM 15,453.26, collected RM 14,362, margin RM 5,954.40 at 38.5%. Receivables are RM 80 from one name at one day. The plug holds at 44.56 and the leak at 18.87%.

ONE ORDER REMAINS PENDING: the J04 12.5 lot at RM 850. It is now HALF THE FREE SHELF and still under its floor, so it is no longer only a pricing decision; taking it would leave 9.14 unit and about two days of cover.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; no boundary breaches; the queue applies nothing.

t: Shafiq's cash half reversed to a receivable, and two paid-not-delivered orders committed
n: THE CASH HALF OF S07'S ORDER IS REVERSED. It was booked as RM 80 received and he has not paid it. Both unit are still handed over and one is still settled by the reward, so RM 80 stands as a RECEIVABLE and the order reads Open, delivered ahead of payment.

HE IS NOW THE ONLY DEBTOR ON THE BOOK, at RM 80 and one day old. Before this the desk carried nothing receivable at all, which is worth knowing: a single name at a day is not a problem, and it is the first time in a fortnight there has been one.
THE REBATE HALF IS UNTOUCHED. Earned 1, applied 1, nothing owed. Reversing a payment does not un-earn a reward, and the two halves of that order settle in different currencies for different reasons.
THE QUEUE IS RUN. E16's 2.5 unit at RM 230 and Z20's unit at RM 100 are both marked PAID IN FULL on 08 Aug with nothing yet handed over.

SO BOTH ARE DEFERRED, NOT RECEIVABLE, and the distinction is the whole point of that state: the money is in and the salt is not out, which is the opposite way round from an advance. The desk owes 3.5 unit against 28.14 on the shelf, so it is covered eight times over, but it is a commitment and it is now visible as one.
REVENUE RM 15,193.26, collected RM 14,102, margin RM 5,835.40 at 38.4%. The shelf is unchanged at 28.14 because nothing was delivered; the plug holds at 44.56 and the leak at 18.87%.
TWO ORDERS REMAIN PENDING: H29's 3 unit at RM 300 and the J04 12.5 lot at RM 850 that still sits under its floor.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; the queue overlay applies nothing; no boundary breaches; every reseller still reads earned equals applied.

t: A stated award for S07, spent the same day on a half-redeemed order
n: S07 IS AWARDED ONE FREE UNIT, on his direction that the oil turnover counts: RM 400 of salt plus RM 100 of oil is exactly the RM 500 step.

AND HE SPENDS IT THE SAME DAY. 2 unit at RM 160: RM 80 in cash and RM 80 settled by the reward, valued at the Tier I ask of RM 80 for a unit, which is the standing rule for a redemption with no price basis of its own. No separate handover: 2 unit leave the shelf and one unit of reward is drawn against them. Earned 1, applied 1, nothing owed.

IT BOOKS TO HIS OWN CODE, NOT S07-R, because the reward is his rather than his resell account's, and rebateApplied reads the plain code. It is the same shape as I18's 03 Aug order, where rebateKg names how many units of reward the row consumed.

THE GRANT IS A STATED AWARD RATHER THAN A RULE CHANGE, and that distinction is load-bearing. Making the rebate count oil would apply RETROSPECTIVELY to everyone: S11's R2 turnover would go RM 1,430 to RM 1,560, crossing a third step, and his 10 unit oil resell would ALSO trip the large-lot trigger at 5 unit, so he would gain one or two free units nobody intended to give him. Checked before acting rather than discovered afterwards.

AWARDS IS A NEW MAP BESIDE REBATE, holding rewards the desk DECIDED rather than computed. It adds into `earned` so the milestones panel still balances, and it stays separate so the reason survives the next person to read it. A reward the rules produce and a reward he chooses to give are different things, and a desk that adds them into one number cannot say which it is looking at.

WHETHER OIL COUNTS FOR EVERYONE IS STILL THE OPEN QUESTION IT WAS, and the margin-based rebate he is considering would settle it without a separate rule, because margin already weights a thin resell for what it is.

THE POSITION: salt revenue RM 14,863.26, collected RM 13,852, margin RM 5,669.90 at 38.1%, shelf 28.14 unit. The plug holds at 44.56 and the leak at 18.87%, because the reward settled in money rather than in a second handover.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; every reseller reads earned equals applied with nothing owed; no boundary breaches.

t: Two fulfilments committed, the third carried to the whiteboard as a question
n: BOTH S07 FULFILMENTS ARE COMMITTED, settled in full on 07 Aug: 2 unit of salt at RM 160 and 10 unit of oil at RM 100, paid and delivered. He marked them from the ledger cards and they carry their own lot cost, RM 47 and RM 7.

THE SHELVES ROLL. Salt 32.14 to 30.14, oil 45 to 35. The plug is unchanged on both, at 44.56 for salt and nil for oil, because salt that leaves against an order is not shrinkage; the leak holds at 18.87%.

OIL STILL TIES EXACTLY: 5 opening plus 50 bought less 20 sold is 35, and the counted shelf agrees with the ledger to the unit. That is what a product with no leak yet should look like, and it is worth watching as the number of oil orders grows.
SALT REVENUE RM 14,703.26, collected RM 13,772, margin RM 5,603.90 at 38.1%. Oil revenue RM 230, all collected, margin RM 86.67.

THE THIRD ENTRY IS STILL A QUESTION AND IS NOW ON THE WHITEBOARD AS Q1. A single watermark cannot commit two entries and hold a third, so moving it past the two S07 fulfilments would have taken the N19 duplicate with it. An entry that disappeared because of an arithmetic comparison is the worst way to lose one, so it is written down where it survives, with the whole argument and both ways to close it.

A DECISION HE HAS NOT TAKEN YET, AND IT IS WORTH A FREE UNIT. networkStats counts a reseller's turnover from the ACTIVE product only, so S07's R2 stands at RM 400 of salt with his RM 100 of oil beside it and not in it. Counting both puts him at exactly RM 500, which is the rebate step, and earns him a free unit. Left as it is and flagged rather than decided: whether oil turnover earns salt is his rule to make.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean under both products; the queue overlay now applies nothing; four orders remain pending; Q1 renders on the Whiteboard.

t: A row is costed in its own product, and the ledger says which product it is
n: MINUS 417% ON A LEDGER ROW. costOf fell back to wavgBuy, which is the ACTIVE product's weighted average, so a 10 unit oil order of RM 100 was costed at salt's RM 51.72 a unit and printed a margin of minus RM 417.20 at minus 417%. He spotted it on screen.

THE FALLBACK NOW READS THE ROW'S OWN PRODUCT, and computes it from purchases rather than from the globals, so it is safe to call while the desk is scoped to something else. That is precisely the case that was wrong: the ledger is consolidated, so it draws oil rows while scoped to salt. Salt RM 51.72, oil RM 7.06.

A PENDING ORDER HAS NO MARGIN AT ALL. Nothing is paid and nothing delivered, so there is no cost of goods against it, and printing a margin states a profit on a trade that has not happened. It reappears the moment the order moves.
AND A MARGIN OF EXACTLY NOTHING PRINTED AS 'RM -0.00 · -0%', on a rebate settled at cost. Rounded to zero before it is shown.

var(--cyan) HAS NEVER BEEN DEFINED IN THIS FILE. Salt's accent has pointed at it since the product split at v228, so salt's colour resolved to nothing everywhere it was used, on the product band and now on the ledger stamp. It is var(--ice), the cyan the rest of the desk actually uses. Found by reading the rendered markup rather than trusting the token name.
THE OIL ORDER IS A RESELL TOO. It books to S07-R beside his salt, so all three of his 05 and 07 Aug rows are R2 and his own buying is the two July orders alone.

EVERY LEDGER ROW CARRIES AN EMBOSSED PRODUCT STAMP, built like the Diamond badge with a lit top edge and a dark under-edge, in the product's own colour. The ledger is the one fully consolidated tab, so a row for 10 unit at RM 10 sat beside one for 10 unit at RM 68 with nothing to say why. It is embossed rather than flat so it reads as a stamp on the row instead of competing with Pending and Completed.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; 81 of 81 ledger cards carry a stamp; no negative margin is printed anywhere on the ledger; the oil row costs at RM 7.06.

t: The general bucket is retired and merges into the reseller's own account
n: S11-GEN, N19-GEN AND S07-GEN ARE PURGED, and everything they carried merges into the reseller's own -R account. It applies to R2 and R3 alike.

THE BUCKET WAS A SECOND CODE FOR A PARTY THAT WAS NEVER A PERSON. It was never named, never placed on the map, never issued a statement and never owed anything, and every figure it held already sat beside it on the -R row. One code where there were two, and the question it existed to answer, was that for him or for someone else, is still answered by which of his two codes the row sits under.
`downstream` SURVIVES FOR THE CASE IT WAS ALWAYS RIGHT FOR: an onward buyer the desk actually knows and delivered to. That is now M14 under S11-R and nothing else on the book.
isBucket IS KEPT AND ALWAYS FALSE rather than deleted. A dozen call sites ask it, and the honest answer now is that there are none; a missing function would have been a worse way to say so.
S07'S 05 AUG ORDER IS RE-BOOKED AS A RESELL. It was written as him buying 3 unit for himself and it is an R2 onward sale, so it moves to S07-R beside his 07 Aug one, at the same RM80 a unit.

IT CHANGES WHAT HE IS OWED. RM 240 moves out of his own buying and into his R2 turnover, which now reads RM 400 against a RM 500 rebate step. He is RM 100 of resell away from a free unit rather than RM 340, and his direct buying falls from RM 1,370 to RM 1,130.

THE PROSE WENT WITH IT. Three live row notes, the split rule, the Transaction tab's end-customer dropdown and the Map's siting note for Bandar Kinrara all described a bucket that no longer exists. Asserted rather than assumed: no rendered pane on any of the fifteen tabs contains -GEN or -Gen.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean under both products; the roster holds no bucket; exactly one row carries a downstream and it names a real customer; ownerOf and isPerson still resolve a resell account to its owner.

t: Four orders booked pending, a new customer, a new place and a new reseller account
n: ALL FOUR ARE PENDING, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A GAP. He gave sizes, parties and prices and did not say any of them was paid or handed over. Pending counts nowhere on this desk, so booking them settled would have overstated revenue, cost of goods, cash and the shelf at once. Every one of them now carries Paid, Delivered and Completed on its ledger card, so settling one is a click rather than a re-entry.

H29 IS A NEW CODE, minted on the standing convention: first initial plus the next global sequence, after M28. He is Tier III on his first order, which is what the board asks of a party with no history: RM 300 for 3 unit, RM 100 a unit, against a floor of RM 211.

KL SENTRAL IS A NEW PLACE. The desk carried KLCC as KLC and not KL Sentral, which is a different location three kilometres away, so it now has its own entry and H29 sits on the map rather than unplaced.

S07 OPENS A RESELLER ACCOUNT. His first onward sale creates S07-R as the counterparty and S07-GEN as the bucket the unknown end buyer sits in, exactly as S11 and N19 already work. The bucket is not a customer and is never issued a statement.

PRICED AT HIS OWN RATE, ON HIS INSTRUCTION: RM 80 a unit, what he pays when buying for himself. It clears the RM 143 floor at 2 unit by RM 17 and sits RM 60 under the Tier III card, so it is the thinnest resell on this book. It starts his R2 turnover at RM 160, RM 340 short of the first rebate step.

THE OIL IS THE BALANCE OF A RM 260 ORDER ACROSS BOTH PRODUCTS: RM 160 of salt and RM 100 of oil. RM 100 for 10 unit is Tier I on the oil board to the ringgit. It is only the second oil order this book has written and the first to a party who also buys salt.
Z20 AT RM 100 FOR A UNIT is Tier II where his single order puts him in Tier III at RM 120. A RM 20 concession he did not ask for, RM 26 above the floor. Stated by him, so it stands.

A BUG CAUGHT IN THE BOOKING, AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN QUIET. The scoping field is `product` and the row was first written `prod`, so the oil order scoped as SALT: it was floored against salt's ladder, raised a false boundary breach for pricing under floor, and left oil's pending reading zero while a live oil order sat on the book. Caught because oil pending was asserted rather than assumed.
THE POSITION NOW: salt 21 unit pending worth RM 1,640, oil 10 unit worth RM 100, six pending cards in the ledger, no boundary breaches.
THE N19 QUEUE ENTRY IS STILL NOT COMMITTED and still awaits his word on whether it duplicates the 06 Aug resell.

t: The queued entry looks like a duplicate, so it is not committed
n: THE QUEUE HOLDS ONE ENTRY AND IT IS NOT BOOKED. 2 unit to N19-GEN for RM 250, R2 through N19, dated 05 Aug, paid and delivered. The ledger already carries that transaction on 06 Aug: same reseller, same general bucket, same 2 unit, same RM 250, paid and collected on the day.

COMMITTING IT WOULD COST MORE THAN A WRONG FIGURE. RM 250 of revenue booked twice, 2 unit taken off a shelf they never left, and his R2 turnover pushed from RM 690 to RM 940, across a second rebate step, earning a free unit nobody earned. A duplicate that pays someone is worse than one that does not.

SO QUEUE_COMMITTED HAS NOT MOVED. The entry stays in the queue and stays on screen, which is exactly what that watermark is for. If the 05 Aug sale is real and separate, say so and it goes in; if it is the 06 Aug one re-entered, clear it from the desk.

THE TIER I RULE IS NOW APPLIED EVERYWHERE IT BELONGS. His instruction of 07 Aug was general rather than a one-off: a redemption with no price basis of its own uses Tier I. The 04 Aug half unit was corrected at v260 and the 06 Aug free unit was missed; it still carried RM 0 against RM 47 of lot cost, so the ledger read a total loss on a reward the man had earned by selling.
IT IS VALUED AT RM 80, the Tier I ask for a unit, and settled in kind. No rebate row on this book is priced at nothing now, checked by assertion rather than by eye.

THE EFFECT ON THE BOOK: revenue RM 14,543.26, margin RM 5,537.90 at 38.1%. N19 is no longer the worst margin on the revenue-against-margin chart; the bottom three are now R21 at 15.7%, J02 at 20% and S07 at 23%, all of which are real trades rather than an artefact of a reward priced at nothing.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean under both products.

t: The filter goes, both books appear on every page, and nothing is below floor
n: THE SWITCHER WAS A FILTER AND THAT WAS THE FAULT. Half the desk was always hidden and the half on screen was easy to read as the whole. It is gone.

MONEY CONSOLIDATES, BECAUSE MONEY ADDS UP. Financials and the Order book open with both products totalled and each figure split beneath it: revenue RM 14,593, being salt RM 14,463 and oil RM 130; collected RM 13,742; margin RM 5,515; spent on stock RM 13,000.

PHYSICAL THINGS DO NOT CONSOLIDATE, because 32 unit of salt plus 45 of oil is not 77 of anything. Inventory, Sourcing, Pricing and Analysis are REPEATED once per product, each block headed by its own name and colour. Nothing is hidden and nothing is nonsense.
LEDGER, CUSTOMERS, NETWORK, MAP AND TODAY ALREADY READ THE WHOLE BUSINESS and were left alone. `sales` and `purchases` have been whole since v228; only recompute() is scoped.

THE WRAPPER RESTORES WHAT IT BORROWS. PROD is a global recompute() reads, so perProduct() sets it, builds, and puts it back with a final recompute. A builder that left the desk scoped to the last product in the list would silently reprice every figure drawn after it; asserted that PROD and the shelf read salt after a full fifteen-tab render.
THE PRODUCT BUTTONS JUMP RATHER THAN FILTER, scrolling to that product's block on the current tab, and on a tab that reads both books together they say so instead of appearing to do nothing.
THE 50 UNIT TIER I OIL ANCHOR GOES TO RM 420, clearing the 10% wholesale floor of RM 416.67 that RM 410 sat under. NOTHING ON EITHER BOARD IS BELOW ITS FLOOR.

PRICES END IN FIVES OR TENS AND NOTHING FINER. The RM 1 step introduced at v262 solved oil's flat floor and produced RM 582 and RM 746 on a printed card, which is not a price anyone reads out. Where a five will not fit, the price goes UP: above its floor and breaking a taper is defensible, below its floor is not.
SALT'S BOARD IS NOW ENTIRELY ON FIVES with no ties, no rising rates and nothing under floor. The 4 unit cell moved RM 280 to RM 285 to keep the 5 unit cell at a round RM 350.

ONE THING OIL CANNOT DO, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A BUG. Above 60 units its floor rate is flat to within three sen, RM 8.32 at 60 against RM 8.30 at 100, while one five-ringgit step at 70 units moves the rate by seven sen. The window is narrower than the step, so Tier I rises from RM 8.33 a unit at 60 to RM 8.43 at 70. The taper is over and the grid cannot express what is left of it. A 100 unit anchor, or a wholesale floor below 10% on oil, is what would give it room.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; six carry both products and two of those carry a consolidated block; PROD and every scoped figure read salt after the render completes.

t: Oil gets its own ladder, prices and floor; the scatter stops saying the same thing twice
n: THE SIZE LADDER IS PER PRODUCT. Salt runs 0.5 to 12.5; oil starts at a 10 unit minimum, steps by 5 to 50, then by 10 to 100. Quoting oil on salt's sizes had produced a board whose smallest lot was a twentieth of the minimum order.

OIL'S SIX ANCHORS ARE STATED, so nothing on that tab is derived any more: RM 100 / 115 / 130 at 10 units, RM 410 / 440 / 470 at 50. That is RM 10.00, RM 11.50 and RM 13.00 a unit at 10, and RM 8.20, RM 8.80 and RM 9.40 at 50.
IT AGREES WITH THE ONE TRADE WRITTEN. The single oil sale was 10 units for RM 130, which is Tier III at 10 units to the ringgit. The ladder is consistent with the book rather than merely plausible.
BEYOND 50 THE RATE HOLDS FLAT, because the anchors stop there and the curve is clamped rather than extrapolated. If 100 units should be cheaper per unit than 50, that needs a third anchor.

SALT'S FLOOR CURVE IS NOW SALT'S ALONE. Its 33%-to-15% markup was anchored at 1 unit and 12.5, so on a 10-to-100 ladder every oil size clamped to the far end, and a product carrying RM 5 of delivery on a RM 375 lot inherited a floor built for RM 5 on a RM 63 lot. A product without its own curve now falls back to the band percentage, which is the desk's own refusal line.

ONE BREACH SURVIVES AND IT IS HIS TO SETTLE. RM 410 for 50 units at Tier I is under the desk's 10% wholesale floor of RM 416.67, by RM 6.67. Because every larger size must clear that same floor, oil cannot quote below RM 8.33 a unit above 50, so the rate RISES from RM 8.20 at 50 to RM 8.50 at 60 instead of falling. Reported rather than engineered away: raising the 50 unit Tier I anchor to RM 420 clears it, and so does stating a 100 unit anchor.

THE SCATTER'S TWO AXES WERE THE SAME FACT TWICE. x carried total revenue and the bubble carried volume, so a big customer was big twice over and the chart could not distinguish a party who buys often in small lots from one who buys rarely in large ones. x is REVENUE PER ORDER now and the bubble is TOTAL REVENUE.
THE BUBBLE SCALES BY AREA, NOT RADIUS. Doubling revenue should double the ink; radius-proportional bubbles overstate a large customer by the square.

VERIFIED ON BOTH PRODUCTS: all fifteen tabs render clean under salt and under oil; salt's board is unchanged to the ringgit; oil's board is stated, strictly ordered across tiers, on the five grid, with the single rate inversion above named above.

t: Anchors go per product, the RM0 reward gets a price, and the scatter becomes revenue against margin
n: THE PRICING TAB WAS SHOWING SALT'S PRICES FOR OIL. PRICE_ENGINE.anchors was flat, so switching the desk to oil kept the board and changed the cost underneath it: RM 80 for a unit of oil that lands at RM 7.40, a 545% markup, and RM 850 for a 12.5 lot. The single oil sale on the book cleared RM 13 a unit. A price list keyed to nothing is worse than no price list, because it looks authoritative.

ANCHORS ARE NOW KEYED BY PRODUCT. Salt keeps his nine stated prices exactly. A product with none does not borrow another's prices: it borrows the SHAPE, the markup salt takes on its OWN lot cost at each anchor size, applied to this product's own lot cost from its own frozen basis. Oil reads RM 15 / 20 / 25 at a unit and RM 115 / 120 / 125 at 12.5.

AND IT SAYS SO ON THE PAGE. A derived board carries a banner naming the product it took its shape from, why, and what has actually traded against it. Oil's derived Tier II at 12.5 works out at RM 9.60 a unit against the RM 13 he actually got, so the placeholder is CONSERVATIVE and is flagged as one rather than presented as a recommendation. Three prices per tier and it becomes a stated board like salt's.

DERIVED ANCHORS ARE DE-COLLIDED AT DERIVATION. On a cheap product three markups can round to the same five, and oil did: Tier I and Tier II both came out at RM 15 for a half unit. The solver would normally break that tie but it treats an anchor as immovable, and these are arithmetic rather than his numbers, so they are separated where they are made.

THE RM0 DOT WAS A REWARD PRICED AT NOTHING. N19's half unit on 04 Aug carried total RM 0 against RM 47 of lot cost, which is minus 100% margin and exactly why that dot sat alone on the floor of the chart. Every other rebate row on this book already carries a price and settles it in kind; this one did not. It is valued at the Tier I ask of RM 50 and settled in kind, per his rule that a redemption with no price basis of its own uses Tier I.

THE SCATTER IS NOW REVENUE AGAINST MARGIN. The average is DRAWN rather than described, as a dotted line at the WEIGHTED average of 37.7%, total margin over total revenue: a simple mean of the dots would let a RM 50 order pull the line as hard as a RM 1,600 one.
EVERY DOT CARRIES ITS PERCENTILE, because 42% margin means nothing on its own and '42%, the 62nd percentile of this book' says whether it is a good trade here.

AND THE TWO TAILS ARE NAMED, because they are the only two that imply an action. Top quartile in gold: high value CUSTOMERS, seven of them. Bottom quartile in violet: high value RELATIONSHIPS, seven, which is not a list of mistakes but what he keeps for reasons other than margin. The middle twelve are one neutral colour so the tails read at a glance.

VERIFIED ON BOTH PRODUCTS: all fifteen tabs render clean under salt and under oil, salt's board is unchanged to the ringgit, oil's is derived from its own cost, and the banner appears only where the board is derived.

t: The tier pill gets its air back, and a Liquid Glass conformance pass
n: THE PILL SAT AGAINST THE NAME. .sbadge has carried margin-left:8px since it was written and .tierpill did not, so 'Martin' and 'TIER III' read as one word. Eight pixels, and two more on the right where a state badge follows.

AND IT BROKE IN TWO. Inside the narrow sticky customer column on Reconnect the pill folded onto a second line, doubling every row's height to say the same thing. It holds one line now. Liquid Glass is explicit that labels wrap and figures do not, and a two-word pill is a label in name only.

A CONFORMANCE PASS, NOT A RESKIN, and that is the language's own instruction: when editing something that exists, match the document's styling and its token names, and change only what was asked. The desk keeps its Ledger tuning, its --gold, --ice and --vio, and every name it already uses.

CHECKED AGAINST THE CURRENT SPEC RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The aurora, the three glass tiers, the focus-visible rings, prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-reduced-transparency are all present and were left alone. Reporting a reskin as an improvement when nothing was wrong would be the worse outcome.

WHAT WAS GENUINELY OUT was the tap target on the ledger quick buttons: 26px against the language's 40px rule. They are 34px now, which is the most a ledger row can carry without the mark bar swamping the card above it. Stated rather than quietly left at 26 or quietly taken to 40.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; the pill computes 8px of left margin and nowrap; the quick buttons compute 34px.

t: Five revive cards become one line, measured against each customer's own rhythm
n: TODAY PRINTED A CARD PER QUIET NAME: five of them, each with a headline, a sentence of history, a quote, a value and a button, to say a thing that is one sentence long. Today is the tab that answers what to do now, and 'four people are overdue' IS the answer. Which four, by how much and at what quote is the next question and it already has a tab.

IT NOW READS: 4 customers have not ordered within their own cadence, worth about RM 170 at today's board if each reorders at his usual size, furthest behind G01 at 33 days past his own 4-day rhythm. The button opens Customers.

AND THE TEST NOW MEANS WHAT IT SAYS. Overdue was a flat 21 days, which called a man who buys monthly quiet and let a weekly buyer go silent for a fortnight unremarked. It is measured against the party's OWN median gap, so a name appears when it is late by ITS habit rather than by the calendar.
A PARTY WITH ONE ORDER HAS NO HABIT AND IS NOT COUNTED. The desk has always refused to hand a single-order customer the book average and it does not start here.
OUT OF AREA IS COUNTED SEPARATELY AND NAMED in the same line, never silently dropped.
THE RANKING NOTE ONLY PRINTS WHEN THERE IS A RANKING. A sentence explaining how the list was sorted is boilerplate when the list is one line long, which it now usually is.

A REPAIR WORTH RECORDING. The first attempt at conditioning that note matched the wrong element: it wrapped the empty-state card of the block helper instead of the note, crossed a template boundary and took the whole file's backtick balance with it. deskctl check caught it before anything was published, which is the entire reason that check runs before every stamp.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean, the Watch block carries one item, and the figure on it matches the sum of what each overdue party would earn at today's board.

t: The close button follows the screen
n: PINNED TO THE VIEWPORT, NOT TO THE PAGE. In the header it scrolled out of sight, so on a long tab the way out was wherever you had last scrolled from. Fixed at the top left it is in the same place from every tab and every scroll position.

A QUARTER OPACITY UNTIL WANTED. Enough to find when you are looking for it, little enough to ignore when you are not. Hover brings the whole button up rather than changing a colour on a solid one, and it carries a blur behind it so it stays legible over a chart or a table.
focus-visible LIGHTS IT EXACTLY AS HOVER DOES, so tabbing to it does not land on something the eye cannot see.

BUILT ONCE, OUTSIDE ANYTHING THAT RE-RENDERS. Every other header control lives inside #meta, which is rewritten whenever the stamp, the role or the reveal state changes. A button that disappears between the mouse going down and coming up is worse than no button, so this one is appended to the body at startup and never touched again. Asserted: exactly one exists, and it survives a tab change and a forced header re-render.
z-index 70, UNDER THE IDENTITY PANEL AT 80. A modal that could be dismissed round its edges is a worse fault than a modal that covers the exit.
SMALLER UNDER 860px, because at that width the rail is already close to the corner.
VERIFIED: fixed at 10px by 10px, opacity 0.22, one instance, survives re-render, and the click still flushes the queue, calls /bye by both routes and attempts to close the window.

t: The queue was flushed and not committed, which are different things
n: THE FILE WAS WRITTEN AND ALWAYS HAD BEEN. 06_Data\\salt_queue.json carried one AMEND entry stamped 05:25 KL. Flushing means the browser wrote the file; it does not mean the entry is in the books.

WHAT KEEPS AN ENTRY ON SCREEN IS QUEUE_COMMITTED. The desk drops a queued entry only once that watermark passes its timestamp, and only a run moves the watermark. That is the design and it is the right one: it is what stops an entry being booked twice, and it is why nobody is ever asked to press Clear. It also means a queued entry sitting in the Transaction count is not evidence of a fault.

THE A10 FULFILMENT IS COMMITTED. 1 unit at RM 90, agreed 06 Aug, paid and delivered in full on the 7th. It carries its own RM 47 lot cost rather than falling back to the weighted average, which would have back-dated cheap salt onto an old order.
THE ROW'S NOTE IS CUT TO THE FACT. It carried a paragraph about why the price moved from RM 100 to RM 90 an hour after it was quoted, which was desk history rather than anything about this order.

THE SHELF FALLS TO 32.14 UNIT. A count is read as at the START of its date, so the 06 Aug count of 33.14 stands for the 6th and a unit handed over on the 7th comes off on top of it. The plug is UNCHANGED at 44.56 and the leak stays 18.87%: salt that left against an order is not shrinkage, and rolling the count without saying so would have quietly made the leak look worse.
REVENUE RM 14,413.26, COLLECTED RM 13,612, margin RM 5,407.90 at 37.5%. Nothing is receivable and nothing is deferred. Cover is 9.9 days on 32.14 unit free to sell.
TWO ORDERS REMAIN PENDING: E16 at RM 230 and the J04 12.5 unit lot at RM 850, which still sits RM 102 under its floor and is a decision rather than an arithmetic problem.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; the A10 order reads Completed with cash and delivery both on the 7th; the queue watermark matches the file it consumed.

t: A Close desk button that writes the queue, stops the server, and fails honestly
