n: THE BUTTON SITS IN THE HEADER, right of the version stamp. It is grey until hovered and crimson only then: a button that shouts all day gets pressed by accident, and this one stops the server.

THE QUEUE IS FLUSHED FIRST AND THE CLOSE WAITS ON THE WRITE. Everything typed into this desk lives in memory until salt_queue.json is written, so closing the window before that lands would lose it without a word. qFlush already returns the write, so the close hangs off its promise rather than off a timer and a hope.

IT COUNTS WHAT IS UNCOMMITTED BEFORE IT ASKS. The confirm names the number of queued entries and says plainly that they are written to the queue file and picked up on the next run, so closing with work outstanding is a decision rather than a surprise.

IT CALLS /bye, WHICH THE SERVER ALREADY UNDERSTANDS. That is the route the pagehide beacon uses, so the server stops on the next watchdog tick instead of idling out its timeout. sendBeacon first because it survives the window going away, fetch with keepalive behind it for browsers without it.

AND IT FAILS HONESTLY. window.close() is refused by every browser for a window the user opened themselves, so it works from the launcher's app window and not from an ordinary tab. Rather than appear to do nothing, the page replaces itself with a plain statement that the server has stopped, how many entries were saved, and that the tab and the black window behind it can be closed.

VERIFIED against a stubbed browser: the confirm names the right count, the queue is flushed, /bye is called by both beacon and fetch, window.close() is attempted, and the fallback panel renders with the entry count in it. All fifteen tabs still render clean.

t: A pending order is a note to self, and the captions are derived rather than typed
n: AN ORDER AGREED ON MONDAY AND SETTLED ON WEDNESDAY WAS THREE LINES: Opened, a Fulfilment, Closed. The middle two say the same thing twice and the first records a state that never had a consequence, because PENDING COUNTS NOWHERE on this desk. It is a reference, not a movement. Settled orders now draw as one line.

THE EXCEPTION IS REAL CREDIT, AND ONLY REAL CREDIT. Where the order sat in Advance or Deferred for more than TWO days, someone was carrying the other and that is a fact about the relationship rather than a rounding of the calendar. Those keep their steps. Dwell is measured to the next step, or to today where the position is still open, so nothing hides by never being closed.

THE TEST IS THE CREDIT PERIOD, NOT THE OPENING STATE. The first version also required the order to have opened Pending, which kept the steps on eight rows that opened straight into Advance or Deferred and closed within a day. Multi-line cards fall from 12 to 7.

NO BOILERPLATE, AND THE CAPTION IS NOW DERIVED. Carrying the written notes up to the collapsed line replaced three lines of noise with one: 'as booked', 'agreed at RM100/unit, nothing moved on the day'. What prints instead is computed from the ledger and compares this order with the SAME PARTY'S median settle time, so it says nothing when someone behaved exactly as he always behaves. A caption that fires on every row is boilerplate however true it is. One card carries one today.

THE WRITTEN NOTES ARE NOT DELETED. They stay on the row, in the file, and on any card that keeps its steps. What they no longer do is print on a card that collapsed precisely because nothing happened worth three lines.

THREE THINGS CUT FROM PRICING, all flagged by him. The standing paragraph re-explaining the 30 Jul rate correction, which never changed with the data and is now the fact alone. The line reading 'Absorbed and not recovered: RM 0/unit', which has reported nothing since attribution went to 1 and now only shows when there is something absorbed.

AND SIZES OFF THE BOARD, REMOVED ENTIRELY. A whole section quoting a price, a rate, a margin, a profit and a walk-away for five lot sizes nobody has ever ordered, on a tab whose first control already quotes ANY size against the same engine. His complaint was that every section wanted to decide the right price; this was the clearest instance.

THE LAUNCHER OPENS FULL SCREEN. Three flags rather than one: --start-fullscreen does the work, --start-maximized is the fallback for builds that ignore it on a profile with no saved window state, which is exactly a fresh .desk-profile, and --window-position pins it to the primary display so app mode cannot restore it onto a monitor that is no longer attached. App mode is kept, because the tie between the desk window and the server needs a process id to watch.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity; 70 of 77 ledger cards draw as one line and every card that keeps its steps has more than two days of credit behind it.

t: Paid, Delivered and Completed, on the pending order's own card
n: THREE BUTTONS ON A PENDING LEDGER CARD. A pending order has paid nothing and moved nothing by definition, so Paid is its whole total, Delivered is its whole quantity and Completed is both. There is nothing to type and therefore nothing to mistype.

IT QUEUES, IT DOES NOT WRITE. Every other entry on this desk rides salt_queue.json and is committed on the next run; a button that edited the ledger directly would be the single path that bypassed that. The payload is byte-for-byte what the Transaction tab pushes for a Fulfilment, so the entry shows as Provisional and clears on the next commit like anything else.

OFFERED ONLY ON A PENDING ORDER, and only when that order is not already provisional. A part-paid or part-delivered row carries a real arithmetic question, how much, and that belongs on the Transaction tab where a figure can be entered and checked.

THE FIRST VERSION LOOKED PERFECT AND BOOKED NOTHING. render() recomputes; it does not rebuild the rows from BASE and re-apply the queue, so calling saveQueue and render put the entry in the Transaction count, repainted the card, and moved not one figure on the books. applyOverlay now runs first, exactly as wbRecord has always done.

IT WAS CAUGHT BY ASSERTING ON revTotal AFTER THE CLICK rather than on the card, which repainted convincingly either way. Worth remembering: on this desk a card changing state is not evidence that anything was booked.

ALL THREE LAND ON THE DESK'S OWN STATES, verified against a 2.5 unit order of RM 230. Paid: revenue and cash both up RM 230, deferred up 2.5 unit, state Open Deferred, because he holds money for salt not yet handed over. Delivered: revenue up RM 230, cash unchanged, receivable up RM 230, state Open Advance. Completed: both, state Completed. Pending falls by 2.5 unit in every case.

STOCK DOES NOT MOVE ON A DELIVERY, AND THAT IS CORRECT. The shelf is a counted figure and a count beats the ledger; what changes is the plug between them, exactly as the count rule has always required.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; three pending cards carry the bar and no non-pending card does; the queued payload matches the Transaction tab's shape field for field.

t: A solved cell clamps up to its floor, and the 12.5 anchor argues against his own intent
n: R4 NOW CLAMPS UPWARD, BUT ONLY ON A SOLVED CELL. The old rule reported and refused to clamp, and it was right to: on a board of PRINTED cards a tier deliberately under its floor was a policy statement, and silencing it hid the thing the desk most needed to show. These cells are solved from an interpolation, so one landing under the floor is not a policy, it is the curve passing through a price the desk would refuse to trade at.

TIER I AT 5 UNIT GOES RM 345 TO RM 350, as instructed. The rate law then carries 4 unit to RM 285 and 6.25 to RM 435, because lifting one cell without its neighbours would put the rate up as the lot grew.
NOTHING SITS UNDER FLOOR ANYWHERE ON THE BOARD, verified by assertion rather than read off.

A CORRECTION MAY NO LONGER PUSH A CELL UNDER ITS FLOOR. The rate law used to be free to cut the larger lot to restore order; if the only way down is through the floor it now leaves the pair alone and lets the board show it, so the clamp cannot be undone by the very pass that follows it.
A PINNED PRICE IS STILL NEVER MOVED, in either direction. A stated price below the floor is a decision he has taken and it stays visible; only solved cells are lifted.
26 OF 30 CELLS ARE ON TENS. Four need fives, all Tier I, at 2, 3, 4 and 6.25 unit.

HIS STATED INTENT IS TO SELL LESS 12.5 AND MORE 0.5 TO 6.25, AND THE BOARD ARGUES THE OPPOSITE. At Tier I a 12.5 lot at RM 850 earns RM 100 of contribution. The same 12.5 unit sold as twelve singles and a half earns RM 260; sold as two 6.25 lots it earns RM 120. So every large lot at the stated anchor forgoes RM 160 against selling the same salt small, and RM 360 at Tier II where the gap is wider.

THE ANCHOR THAT WOULD MAKE HIM INDIFFERENT IS RM 1,010 AT TIER I, RM 1,260 AT TIER II. Below that the board is paying customers to take the size he says he wants to sell less of. Stated rather than applied, because the anchors are his to set.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; all nine anchors exact; no ties across any row; no rising rate down any column; no cell under its floor.

t: Nine stated prices, and a solver between them
n: HE NOW SETS THE BOARD DIRECTLY at 0.5, 1 and 12.5 unit for each tier: Tier I 50, 80, 850; Tier II 60, 100, 900; Tier III 80, 120, 950. Nothing is derived from cost any more except the floor that tests the result. All nine anchors hold exactly, asserted rather than eyeballed.

THE SOLVER INTERPOLATES THE RATE, NOT THE TOTAL, in the log of size. Interpolating totals draws a straight line through a curve and puts the middle sizes above both ends on a per-unit basis, which is the opposite of a taper. Outside the stated range the rate is held flat rather than extrapolated.

NEAREST TENS ALL ACROSS IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE ON TIER I, and the desk says so rather than quietly bending a number. His 1 unit anchor fixes the rate at RM 80. On a ten grid the only 1.5 unit prices are RM 110 and RM 120: RM 120 ties the rate, which the strictness rule forbids, and RM 110 crashes it to RM 73.33. From RM 73.33 a strictly falling rate reaches RM 66.67 by 3 unit and can never climb back to the RM 68 his 12.5 anchor states.

SO THE SOLVER TAKES THE COARSEST GRID EACH CELL CAN HOLD. 27 of 30 cells land on tens. Exactly three need fives, all on Tier I, at 2, 3 and 5 unit. Tier II and Tier III are entirely on tens. The grid used is recorded per cell rather than inferred.

TWO EARLIER FAULTS, BOTH FOUND BY ASSERTION AND BOTH FIXED. The strictness pass was overwriting his 12.5 anchor at RM 775, because it did not know a stated price is immovable; anchors are now pinned and a colliding solved neighbour gives way instead. And a rounding tie at 1.5 unit was avalanching down the whole Tier I column, handing every later size a rate RM 9 below the interpolation and putting seven cells under floor; corrections are now local and made at the finest grid, because a correction is already an exception and coarse steps overshoot the thing they repair.

TWO CELLS SIT UNDER THE FLOOR: Tier I at 5 unit, RM 345 against RM 348, and at 6.25, RM 430 against RM 434. Three and four ringgit. REPORTED, NOT CLAMPED, which is what R4 has always required, and they follow from the anchors rather than from the solver.

CONTRIBUTION ON THE EXISTING BOOK FALLS 10.2%, revenue 3.1%, because these anchors price Tier I well below where the markup ceilings had it: RM 8 a unit at 12.5 against RM 20 at a single unit, on 9.5 days of cover.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; all nine anchors exact; no ties across any row; no rising rate down any column; no cell off its own grid.

t: The markup curve is a cap, and the cap is the board
n: A FLOOR AND A CAP ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUCTION, and reading his four numbers as the first was my error. As a minimum, the regressed margin curve was free to price above them and did: Tier I quoted 50.4% at a unit where he had said 33%. As a maximum they ARE the board.

EVERY CARDED PRICE IS NOW lot cost times one plus the tier's markup at that size, rounded DOWN to the five grid so a cap is never breached by rounding. The regressed curve no longer sets a carded price; it stays alive for off-board sizes and the analysis panes.

THE STRICTNESS PASS FLIPS DIRECTION WITH IT. While the curve was a floor, a tie had to be broken upward or a price fell under its own minimum. Now it is a ceiling, so breaking upward would breach the number he set: every collision is resolved by pushing the cheaper side DOWN. Both passes now only ever lower, which still terminates.

THE TIER CURVE NO LONGER LIFTS THE FLOOR. What remains under the board is the band percentage, 15% retail and 10% wholesale, which is the absolute refusal line. A cap that fell below it would be a real conflict and is REPORTED on the board rather than resolved silently, which is what R4 has always required. None does today.
DELIVERED AGAINST ASKED, checked at the four stated points: Tier I 26.6% at 1 unit and 14.7% at 12.5, Tier III 97.9% and 44.8%. Each sits under its ceiling.
THE SPREAD IS NOW 26% TO 56% ACROSS THE TEN SIZES, against 21% before any of this and 26% to 38% when the curve was read as a floor. That is the wide range he asked for.

TIER I AT 1 UNIT IS RM 80. That is the exact price he said he could sell at and could not find on the board three versions ago, when the RM 20 ringgit minimum put the floor at RM 83.18. It is there now because he set the ceiling himself.

ROUNDING DOWN COSTS UP TO RM 5 A LOT. At 1 unit that is the entire gap between the 33% he set and the 26.6% delivered, because the cap computes RM 84.03 and the grid takes it to RM 80. A finer grid at the small sizes is the fix if the gap matters; at RM 1 steps Tier I would read RM 84 and 33.0%.
TIER I AT 12.5 EARNS RM 7.20 A UNIT against RM 20 at a single unit, on 9.5 days of cover. That is what a 15% ceiling asks for and it is stated rather than adjusted.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; no ties across any row, no rising rate down any column, every price on the five grid, no cell under the band floor, and no cell above its own cap. Repricing the book gives revenue up 1.9% and contribution up 6.1%.

t: The floor becomes a curve per tier, stated as markup on cost
n: READ AS MARKUP ON COST, WHICH IS THE ONLY READING THAT PARSES. A 100% margin on revenue is undefined; a 100% markup is twice lot cost. His four numbers are therefore Tier I 33% at 1 unit falling to 15% at 12.5, and Tier III 100% falling to 45%.
TIER II IS THE MIDPOINT AT EVERY SIZE rather than a third pair of typed numbers, so the middle of the ladder cannot develop a kink that nobody chose.

INTERPOLATED IN THE LOG OF SIZE, because that is how the fitted margin curve already behaves and how a discount is actually felt. CLAMPED outside the two anchors rather than extrapolated: nobody stated a price for a 20 unit lot and a curve is not entitled to invent one.

IT REPLACES minPerUnit, WHICH IS NOW ZERO. The two cannot both be the floor. A flat RM 20 a unit forces the 12.5 lot to a 31% markup, which would have silently overruled the 15% he asked for at Tier I. The mechanism stays live at zero so it is one number to restore.

THE FLOOR IS PER CELL NOW, NOT PER ROW, because it is per tier. Each price is tested against its own tier's line; the Floor column still prints one figure and that figure is the band floor with no tier applied, the absolute refusal line under everything.
THE ANCHORS ARE HONOURED EXACTLY: the floor computes 33%, 15%, 100% and 45% at the four stated points, checked against the interpolator rather than assumed.

THE SPREAD WIDENS FROM 21% TO BETWEEN 26% AND 38% across the ten sizes. It is NOT the 50% the anchors imply at 1 unit, and that is the honest consequence of asking for a FLOOR: a floor is a minimum, and the fitted margin curve prices Tier I above its own floor at RM 95 rather than at the RM 85 that 33% would permit. Pricing each tier AT its floor is a one-line change if the stated curve is meant to be the board rather than its lower bound.

TIER I AT 12.5 NOW EARNS RM 10.40 A UNIT against RM 35 at a single unit, on a shelf with 9.5 days of cover. That is what the 15% anchor asks for and it reopens the scarcity gap that the RM 20 minimum had closed. Stated rather than adjusted.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render clean; no ties across any row and no rising rate down any column; every price on the five grid; no cell under its own tier floor. Repricing the book gives revenue up 5.9% and contribution up 19.4%, RM 3,424 to RM 4,089.

t: One pricing basis, the watch list learns distance, and three replies folded in
n: THERE WERE TWO ENGINES AND THE DESK QUOTED BOTH. pxQuote anchored on ladderRate(), a curve predating the tier board, then applied a demand signal and a party adjustment. At 1 unit it said RM 130 where the board said RM 95; at 12.5 it said RM 1,010 where the board said RM 1,105. It fed the revive cards, the reseller table, the cover analysis, the earnings chart, the 12.5 commentary and the walk-away column, so every rule added since v245 bound one engine and not the other.

pxQuote NOW COMPUTES NOTHING. On a carded size it returns the board cell; off the board it calls enginePrice, which is the engine that built the board, under the same floors and the same laws. Asserted identical at all 30 cells, not eyeballed.

THE PARTY ADJUSTMENT IS RETIRED, not disabled. A per-customer nudge sitting on top of a tier is by definition a second basis, and the tier is already the desk's statement about that relationship. sigNet and partyNet remain as ignored arguments only so nine call sites did not have to be rewritten to prove they no longer matter; the signal engine itself was found dead at v241, computing a -5% that useDemand discarded.
THE WALK-AWAY SURVIVES AND IS NOT A QUOTE. The board carries no refusal line, so one is still derived, but straight from floorTotal rather than from any ladder of its own.

OUT OF AREA IS NOT QUIET. v243 dropped distant parties from Reconnect on Overview and left them on the Today watch list, which is the one surface meant to say what to do today, so the same two names were put in front of him every morning. They now come off and are summarised in a single row naming them, because a list that got shorter should say why.

THREE REPLIES FOLDED IN. Two contacts stand at no reply. C09 has answered that he is reducing his salt intake; recorded as 'later' with the substance in the note rather than as 'no', because what has changed is the size and rhythm of what he takes, not whether he buys. The log has no outcome for buying LESS and probably should.
THE WATCH LIST NOW CARRIES THE LAST WORD SPOKEN with each name, so a card says both that someone has gone quiet and what they said when last asked.
VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity; pxQuote and the board agree at every cell; the watch list is down to the three metro names plus one summary row.

t: No two numbers the same: the board is strictly ordered both ways
n: TWO RULES, BOTH ABSOLUTE. Across a row the price strictly RISES from Tier I to Tier III. Down a column the rate per unit strictly FALLS as the lot grows. No ties in either direction, at any size or tier. A tie is not a price; it is where two answers collided and the solver shrugged.

BOTH TIES CAME FROM THE RM 20 RINGGIT FLOOR, not from the tier maths. Once a tier sits on the floor its rate is cost plus twenty plus the delivery spread, which falls so slowly with size that a five-ringgit grid rounded 3, 4 and 5 unit to the same RM 80 a unit on Tier I. At 12.5 the floor caught Tier I and Tier II together at RM 985.

THE DIRECTION OF THE FIX WAS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. The existing within-tier rule pulled prices DOWN to make the rate fall, on the sound argument that lowering never raises an ask already quoted. With a floor binding at the bottom that option is gone: cutting the large lot puts it under its own floor. So enforceStrict() walks from the LARGEST size UPWARD and raises the smaller lot instead, which is also the right commercial direction while cover is 9.5 days.
BOTH PASSES ONLY EVER RAISE, so iterating them to a fixed point terminates. The guard allows twelve rounds; it settles in two.

IT RUNS IN buildPriceTiers, NOT IN THE SOLVER. engineBoard() builds the cards and solveLadder() is a separate path with its own R5 ordering rule, so putting the pass at the point where PRICE_TIERS is assembled makes it the last word for every surface that reads the board: the quote panel, the menu, the cards and the drift analysis all inherit it.
THE BOARD NOW READS, Tier I per unit: 110, 95, 86.67, 85, 82, 81.67, 81.25, 80, 79.20, 78.80. At 12.5 unit the three tiers are RM 985, RM 990 and RM 1,105.

VERIFIED BY ASSERTION RATHER THAN BY EYE: zero ties across any row, zero non-falling rates down any column, zero duplicate prices in any row, zero prices off the five grid, zero cells under floor. Repricing the 44 priced orders gives revenue up 4.5% and contribution up 14.7%, RM 3,424 to RM 3,929.
All fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity.

t: The board drawn, and a time series of what the model has actually charged
n: THE SHAPE CHART: rate against size, one line per tier, with the floor and the effective cost drawn beneath them. A table of thirty prices cannot show that a ladder has gone flat, and flat is the whole finding once the ringgit floor binds. Tier I falls RM 110 to RM 78.80 a unit across the board while the floor falls only RM 88.20 to RM 78.60, so the two converge at size and the gap that is left is all the room there is.

THE HISTORY CHART: every priced order plotted at the rate actually paid, on the date it was agreed, grouped into three lot bands, with today's Tier II ask for that band drawn as a dashed reference. This is the first time the desk has shown what it charged over time rather than what it charges now.

IT FINDS SOMETHING THE TABLES DID NOT. Under 2 unit, 22 orders: ask RM 100 a unit against a median paid of RM 100, dead level. Over 5 unit, 9 orders: ask RM 78.80 against a median paid of RM 68, which is the squeeze the ringgit floor was meant to apply. But the MIDDLE band, 18 orders between 2 and 5 unit, asks RM 90 against a median paid of RM 100. The desk is quoting BELOW what that band has actually been paying, across more than a third of the book.

NOTHING IS FITTED ON EITHER CHART. Observed points and one horizontal reference line, because 44 priced orders cannot support a demand curve and drawing one would let the desk talk itself into a price nobody has paid. The dashed line is today's ask, not a forecast.

BOTH CHARTS FALL BACK RATHER THAN BREAK. Where Chart.js cannot load, chartEmpty replaces the canvas with the standing line that every figure drawn is in the tables on the same tab, which is how the other five charts on this tab already behave.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity; both canvases wire into the two existing redraw paths; and both chart configurations were captured against a stubbed Chart constructor to confirm five datasets of ten points on the shape chart and six on the history chart, rather than inferred from the code.

t: Three tiers, a ringgit-per-unit floor, and a ladder that stops discounting the scarce thing
n: FIVE CATEGORIES BECOME THREE, NAMED TIER I TO TIER III. Measured before cutting: the engine was already solving Associate and Loyal to the same 29.8% target, and Regular held 2 customers against a book of 24, so two of the five distinctions were nominal before any constraint bound. Membership now reads Tier I 2, Tier II 10, Tier III 12.

AN ASSOCIATE NEVER FALLS TO THE FULL ASK. Folding Associate away first dropped the principal reseller to Tier III on his single direct order, which is exactly backwards: what he is worth is what he brings. The standing is now a FLOOR, so it stops him paying the no-history price without buying him a discount the engine priced identically to Loyal anyway.

REL NO LONGER PAYS TWICE. Tier I sat at 0.82 AND took zero credit days, so one fact bought both a discount and a cost saving. rel is 0.92 and the zero days deliver the rest, which is cost recovery rather than a second gift.

A PERCENTAGE FLOOR CANNOT EXPRESS SCARCITY. At 20% it let a 12.5 lot go for RM 13.59 a unit while a single unit earned RM 40, on a shelf with 9.5 days of cover. A minimum of RM 20 A UNIT now sits beside the percentage, whichever bites harder. Contribution per unit at 12.5 goes RM 13.59 to RM 18.80, and the taper across the board flattens from 40-to-13.6 to 50-to-18.8.

THE STEP INCENTIVE SWITCHES OFF BELOW 14 DAYS OF COVER. A 3% discount per size step is a policy for spare capacity; paying customers to take units that cannot be replaced is the one move that reliably costs money. incentiveNow() reads coverStats() and returns zero while the shelf is short. It is zero today at 9.5 days.

THE PERCENTAGE FLOOR DROPS TO 15% RETAIL AND 10% WHOLESALE, because a floor should be a refusal line and never the price. With the ringgit minimum doing the real work, the percentage no longer needs to bind, and the tier targets are free to set the board.

THE GRID IS FIVES. At tens the band between a size's floor and its no-rate-rise ceiling was falling through and the engine dropped to exact ringgit; halving the step keeps every printed price round. Zero prices are off the five grid at any tier or size.

THE CHOICE OF RM 20 IS BOUNDED, NOT MAXIMISED. Contribution rises monotonically with the minimum, because the desk has no demand curve and never will from 49 orders, so an optimiser would raise prices forever. Swept 15 to 45: RM 20 is the largest value that keeps every tier distinct at nine of ten sizes while leaving the board under the best rate ever cleared at each size. At 30 and above all three tiers converge at 12.5 and the ladder collapses again.

MEASURED AGAINST THE BOOK, NOT ASSERTED: repricing all 44 priced orders at the new board gives revenue up 4.4% and CONTRIBUTION UP 14.5%, RM 3,424 to RM 3,919. Six orders would rise more than 20%, five of them at 12.5 unit, which is the intended effect and the commercial risk in one sentence.

TWO CELLS SIT ABOVE THE BEST RATE EVER CLEARED at their size, both Tier III, at 3 unit and 5 unit. Flagged rather than clamped: Tier III is the full ask for someone with no history, but it is a real risk of no sale and it exists at every setting of the minimum, so it comes from the tier relativity and not from this change.

EACH CUSTOMER CARRIES A GLOWING TIER PILL, built like the Diamond badge he already uses for associates: a lit chip with the tier's own colour at two radii. Tier I is brightest and Tier III dimmest, so brightness carries the same information as the numeral. The recency badge still shows beside it, because how recently someone bought is a different question from what they pay.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol and no kilo or kilogram, nothing under floor, every price on the five grid, and boardHeadroom(false) finite at RM 0 with Tier I giving first at RM 48.

t: The total shrinkage is booked into the pricing model, and the ladder closes at size
n: SHRINK_ATTRIB GOES 0.5 TO 1 ON HIS INSTRUCTION. The v205 reasoning for attributing half is kept above the constant rather than deleted, because it is the case AGAINST this setting and it is what to re-read when the leak is fixed. Put it back to 0.5 and the whole board follows.

THE LOCK IS REBUILT ON THE SAME LOT. Nothing about the 28 Jul purchase changed; what changed is the leak behind it and the attribution in front of it. Basis now carries 18.87% observed at full attribution rather than half of 16.19%.

THE NUMBERS IN THE LOCK ARE CAPTURED, NOT HAND-COMPUTED. The lock was deleted in a scratch copy, pxCost() run down its full unlocked path at attrib 1, and the result written back: sampleLoad 10.9778, absorbed 0, eff 60.008, effEx 58.1778. Hand-arithmetic into a frozen snapshot is how a basis silently diverges from its own engine.
EFFECTIVE COST RM 53.19 TO RM 60.01, up RM 6.82 a unit or 12.8%. Absorbed goes to zero by definition: at full attribution the desk carries none of the leak itself.

THE CARDS ARE NOT FROZEN, AND A COMMENT ON boardHeadroom STILL SAYS THEY ARE. buildPriceTiers() runs inside recompute(), so PRICE_TIERS is re-solved on every render and the whole board moved with the cost. The 'frozen numbers, moving floors' language predates v234 and is now wrong; flagged rather than rewritten.

THE LADDER CLOSES AT SIZE, AND THIS IS THE FINDING. Above 4 unit the tiers converge: SP, AS, LO and RE all quote RM 370 at 5 unit, RM 460.76 at 6.25 and RM 920 at 12.5, every one of them on 18.5% margin. A Special customer now pays a Regular's price at every size that matters. Small sizes still separate properly, 25% to 45.4% across the five tiers at 1 unit, so the squeeze is entirely at the top.

SEVEN CELLS ARE NO LONGER MULTIPLES OF TEN: RM 225 at 3 unit on three tiers, RM 460.76 at 6.25 on four. This is engineLadder's v238 fallback working as written, where the band between the floor and the no-rate-rise ceiling is under RM 10 it steps to RM 5, and under RM 5 it prices exactly. It is the band closing, not a rounding fault, but it does breach the multiple-of-ten rule the printed cards are built on and the card generator will need a decision before the next print.

NOTHING SITS UNDER FLOOR and headroom holds at RM 0 a unit with SP giving first at RM 48, but 22 cells give at that rate where 3 did. The board is now flat against its own floor rather than comfortably above it.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no occurrence of the retired mass symbol or of kilo or kilogram, boardHeadroom(false) finite with pxOver.cost restored to null, and the board re-read after recompute rather than before it, which is the error that made the first measurement of this change say the cards had not moved.

t: Stock counted at 33.14, the contact log opens, and out of area stops reading as lapsed
n: COUNTED 33.14 UNIT on 06 Aug, stated by him. A count beats the ledger outright, so the 6.33 unit against the rolled 39.47 books as self-use: the plug goes from 38.23 to 44.56 and the observed leak from 16.19% to 18.87%. First count since 03 Aug, so it is three days of handling landing at once.

THE BOARD DOES NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS THE LOCK WORKING. PRICE_LOCK froze the basis on the 28 Jul lot, so pxCost returns the snapshot verbatim and still prices off the 16.19% recorded in it. Effective cost holds at RM 53.19 and headroom at RM 0 a unit, SP giving first at RM 48.

WHAT THE COUNT ACTUALLY DID IS MAKE THE NEXT REPRICE WORSE. Measured at the new leak rather than asserted: effective cost RM 53.95, headroom minus RM 1 a unit at minus 2.1%, and the cells under floor go from three to ten. When the next lot lands and the lock releases, the board moves against him by that much unless the leak comes down first.
COVER FALLS WITH THE COUNT: 33.14 unit free to sell, 9.5 days at the fortnight rate of 3.483 a day, dry on 15 Aug rather than 17 Aug, against a reorder trigger of 15 unit.

THE CONTACT LOG OPENS. contacts[] was built with the machinery around it and left empty, so the Reconnect follow-up column read 'not yet' against every name on the desk. First three entries: M12, G01 and C09, messaged 06 Aug, outcome noreply. Channel is recorded as message because that is the ordinary one here and only 'said hello' was stated; correct any that was a call or a visit.

A HELLO IS NOT AN ORDER. The Reconnect rule is unchanged: a name stays until it BUYS, so all three are still listed, now with the follow-up column filled and the silence attributable to them rather than to him.

OUT OF AREA IS NOT LAPSED. Reconnect was listing a customer in Ho Chi Minh and one up-country beside metro customers who had simply gone quiet. A party whose place is KNOWN and falls outside the Klang Valley frame now drops off: M13 at 1,017km and N06 at 217km, both measured with the existing farFrom() and inMetro() rather than judged.

AN UNKNOWN PLACE IS NEVER GROUNDS FOR DROPPING ANYONE. The desk excludes on evidence, not on the absence of it, and the card now says '2 out of area not shown', because a list that quietly got shorter is a list you stop trusting.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no occurrence of the retired mass symbol or of kilo or kilogram in any pane, and boardHeadroom(false) finite with pxOver.cost and pxOver.shrink both restored to null after the reprice probe.

t: A dashboard is not a report: the quote panel becomes three fields, six sections fold
n: THE QUOTE PANEL IS THREE THINGS. It said '6 unit to a One-time customer quotes RM 490, RM 81.67/unit, earning RM 176. The 5 unit beside it is RM 410 at RM 82/unit for RM 147.' Six figures in a sentence that had to be read to be used. The .qrow grid was already three columns wide and only two were filled, so the answer now sits in the third: how much, to which category, recommended price. The figure carries at 20px in gold, and goes crimson with its border lit when the quote is under its own floor, because the panel no longer has a sentence to put a warning in.

THE RATE AND THE EARNINGS ARE NOT LOST. They are on the board table below, which is what a table of a figure per size is for. The standing paragraph under the panel, 'The board carries ten sizes. This one answers the eleventh...', is deleted outright: it never changed with the data, so it was documentation sitting on a dashboard.
THE SAME QUOTE WAS RENDERED TWICE. anyRow appeared in the top card and again under 'Sizes off the board'. The second copy is gone.

SIX SECTIONS NOW FOLD as details.obsec, closed on load: how a price is built, what each size earns, wholesale under review, if shrinkage comes down, against the market, price response. NOTHING IS DELETED, every one opens verbatim, and each summary carries its own answer, so 'How a price is built' reads 'Regular, 2 unit, line by line, RM 180' when shut.

WHAT STAYS OPEN IS WHAT THE TAB IS FOR: the four cost KPIs, the quote panel, the board, sizes off the board, the reseller menu, what a unit costs, and salt supply. Open headed sections fall from ten to five. Visible prose on Pricing falls from 924 characters to 619; across the desk, 4,687 to 4,382.

THE RULE IS NOW A SKILL, dashboard-storyboard, so it applies to every surface built from here. Assign every block a register before writing it: Ask (what do I do now) open and largest, Watch (what could change it) open and figures only, Do (what action is here) open, Study (why is it this way) folded. A tab carries one to three open sections; ten means a report wearing a dashboard's clothes.

SURVEYED BEFORE ACTING RATHER THAN GUESSED. Every tab was measured for visible prose with the notes fold shut. Pricing was the outlier at 924 characters over 11 blocks and 10 open sections; the next worst was Analysis at 475, and most of that is the 'chart unavailable' fallback which does not render when Chart.js loads. The other fourteen tabs already comply, so nothing was changed on them.

VERIFIED: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no occurrence of the retired mass symbol or of kilo or kilogram in any pane, every disclosure closed on load, and boardHeadroom(false) finite with pxOver.cost restored to null.

t: Feature audit, first pass: the provably dead ones are out
n: EVERY TAB WAS INVENTORIED FROM THE RENDERED PAGE rather than from memory: 15 tabs, their KPI cards, headed sections, card headers, tables, charts and controls. What follows is only what could be PROVEN dead by asking the desk itself; the judgement calls are written up for him rather than acted on.

THE SIGNAL ENGINE MOVES NOTHING, AND SAID SO IN A TABLE. pxSignals computes a net demand adjustment of -5%, and PRICE_MODEL.useDemand is FALSE, so enginePrice multiplies by a lift of exactly 1. 'Why the board reads as it does' and the 'Live adjustment' KPI were therefore publishing a figure with no effect on any price, which is worse than publishing nothing: it invites a decision from a number that does not act. Both removed. Switching it on was the alternative and it is the wrong one, because a live demand signal would contradict the v233 freeze that stops the board drifting between purchases.

POLICY ANCHORS WERE ORPHANED AT v234. PRICE.aRetail and aWhole are not read by enginePrice, engineLadder or marginCurve: since the margin became a regression on the book's own trades, the anchors anchor nothing. The KPI is gone.

THE LADDER-CAP TESTER IS GONE. capLot() returns null, SALES_POLICY.maxLot is null, and it was a harness for a policy that was proposed and never adopted. It was also the same shape as the override panel he had just had removed, and for the same reason: it tested a hypothetical the desk has no way of committing to.
PRICING GOES FROM SIX KPIs TO FOUR AND FROM TWELVE HEADED SECTIONS TO TEN. It was by a distance the most overloaded tab: eleven tables against one on the Order book.

ONE OF MY CUTS TOOK A CLOSING BRACE WITH IT and the tab would not parse. Caught by deskctl check before publishing, restored, and reported here rather than quietly fixed. That is the third time in this session that removing a section has taken a neighbour with it, which is an argument for cutting one thing at a time and checking between, and that is how the rest will be done.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit, headroom RM0, all three pricing laws holding on all five tiers, and all fifteen tabs rendering clean and non-empty under both products.

t: He was right, that panel was useless, and pulling it out found two real bugs
n: IT WAS NOT MERELY USELESS, IT WAS MISLEADING, and for three separate reasons that had all accumulated in the last few hours. The board is FROZEN between purchases since v233, so an override that reprices the basis simulates something the desk has deliberately decided not to do. Its quick-set chips still offered RM56 and RM41.56, the 30-day averages that v232 replaced with the latest lot rate of RM47. And its 'Quote for' party selector was superseded at v237 by five categories read off the ledger, so it could contradict the classification it sat next to.

WHAT SURVIVES IS THE ONE USEFUL THING IN IT. The board carries ten sizes; a customer will eventually ask for an eleventh. That box stays, now with a category beside it, and it answers on the same engine and the same three laws as everything else.

FOUND WHILE REMOVING IT, AND IT IS THE v232 DOUBLE COUNT AGAIN: tierBoard and solveLadder were handing c.eff to floorTotal. eff already carries the per-unit delivery, and floorTotal adds one per lot, so the floor charged delivery twice. Every floor tierBoard drew was too high, and tierBoard is what boardHeadroom reads, which is why the headline headroom figure had gone NEGATIVE.

AND A SECOND ONE UNDERNEATH IT: the cost walk re-derived the leak and the average delivery LIVE while probing. boardHeadroom asks how far the buying rate can rise before a FROZEN price breaches its floor; recomputing everything else while walking answered a different question in the same words and compared frozen prices against floors they were never built on. Only the lot rate moves now; the lock holds the rest.

HEADROOM NOW READS RM0, WHICH IS NOT A BUG BUT IS THE WEEK'S PRICING FACT. At RM47 nothing breaches. At RM48 eleven cells do. The board has no room at all: one ringgit on the buying rate puts Special, Associate and Loyal under their floors at the larger sizes, because a fitted margin of 33% at 12.5 unit multiplied by an 18% Special discount lands below the 20% the floor asks. The discounts are not affordable on bulk at this cost base, which is a decision for him rather than something to engineer away.

ALSO FIXED: the any-size quote spliced its size into the ladder and rebuilt the chain around it, which broke the profit law at the inserted point. It is now judged against the largest board size at or below it, which is the same test without disturbing anything.

AND MY OWN MESS, SAID PLAINLY: removing the panel took out three declarations that lived in the same block and had nothing to do with it, and the Pricing tab rendered EMPTY twice before I noticed. The emptiness check added at v236 is what caught it both times.

POSITION UNCHANGED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit. All fifteen tabs render clean and non-empty under both products, and all three pricing laws hold on all five tiers.

t: The launcher opens instantly, and the desk and the window are tied together
n: IT WAS SLOW FOR THREE REASONS AND ONLY ONE WAS THE SLEEP. It ran deskctl published, then deskctl status, then slept five seconds so they could be read, and only then opened anything. The reports now run AFTER the desk is on screen: they are worth reading and they are not worth waiting on.

IT ALSO OPENED THE BROWSER BEFORE THE SERVER. Line 67 opened the URL and line 68 started the server, so every launch was a race the browser could win, which is why a first load sometimes came up empty and wanted a refresh. The server now starts first and the port is POLLED every 40ms until it actually answers, so the desk opens the moment it is genuinely ready rather than after a guess at how long that takes.

TIED BOTH WAYS, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF WHAT HE ASKED. Close the desk and the window closes at once. Close the window and the desk closes at once. The old behaviour was a heartbeat with a ten second delay, and closing the window by hand left the desk open against a dead server: live to look at and quietly unable to save.

A BROWSER TAB HAS NO PROCESS TO WATCH, which is why this was not done before. Open a URL while Chrome is already running and the new process hands off to the existing one and exits immediately, so there is nothing to wait on. The desk therefore opens in APP MODE against a profile of its own, which gives it a real process with a real lifetime. Two watchers then face each other: one waits on the browser and kills the server, the other waits on the parent window and kills the browser. Whichever goes first takes the other with it.

THE PROFILE IS PERMANENT AND DELIBERATE, in .desk-profile beside the launcher rather than in TEMP, so the desk's own settings survive between runs and stay apart from everyday browsing. It costs nothing, because the queue, the directory and the menu are read from 06_Data through the server: the desk's real state was never in the browser.

THE LAUNCHER MOVED TO salt_launch.ps1. Batch cannot hold a process id or wait on one, and both requirements need exactly that. The .bat is now a wrapper that finds Python and hands over. It also drops the wmic call that would have found the window's own process id: wmic is deprecated and absent on current Windows 11, and the parent id is available directly from the PowerShell side.
GRACEFUL WITHOUT CHROME OR EDGE: it falls back to the default browser, says plainly that the two cannot be tied together and why, and keeps the old behaviour of stopping when the window is closed.

NOT TESTED BY ME AND SAID SO. This sandbox is Linux; no part of a Windows launcher can be run here. The PowerShell parses and its quoting and brackets balance, but the first real test is his double-click.
ALSO REMOVED: a probe file of mine, pc.js, that had leaked into 01_Dashboard during an earlier run and had no business being in the project folder.
NOTHING IN THE DESK MOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit, and all three pricing laws still hold on all five tiers.

t: No more breaks in the ladder, and the thing breaking it was a typed floor
n: EVERY TIER NOW RUNS EVERY SIZE. The v237 rule that a tier stops where its laws collide is withdrawn, and the per-tier size caps go with it: a cap is a break by another name.

THE COLLISION WAS NEVER ARITHMETIC. Write cost as goods times quantity plus one delivery. The lowest lawful price at a size is the larger of its floor and the price that earns what the size below earned, and BOTH of those fall as a rate when the lot grows, because each sheds the fixed delivery charge over a bigger quantity. So the lowest lawful rate is always below the rate of the size beneath it and the band is never empty.

WHAT EMPTIED IT WAS ROUNDING AND A LEFTOVER. The band's bottom was rounded UP to ten and its top DOWN to ten, which on a narrow band crossed them over. The band is now held exactly and only the chosen price is rounded, to five where ten will not fit.

AND THE REAL CULPRIT: A HAND-TYPED FLOOR OF RM825 ON THE 12.5 UNIT LOT. Set when effective cost was RM60.93 and the computed floor there was RM952. On today's basis the computed floor is RM808.70, so the typed figure sat RM16 above it and, at RM66/unit, ABOVE the rate of the 6.25 lot. It forced the two cheapest tiers to quote a bigger lot dearer per unit than a smaller one. It is not a margin, it is a leftover from a cost base that no longer exists, and his rule is that only the margin may move a price. PRICE.lotFloor is now empty.

FIXED, AND IT MADE A CATEGORY REAL IN NAME ONLY: prices were rounded to the NEAREST ten, which pushed a discount tier up into the one above it. Loyal at 0.5 unit wanted RM56.80 and Regular RM60.40, and both became RM60; every larger size then inherited the tie and Loyal and Regular quoted identically all the way to 12.5 unit. Rounding DOWN separates them and favours the customer, and it also realises the volume discount that rounding up had been cancelling: Regular now carries a real cut at all nine steps instead of six.

A10'S PENDING UNIT MOVES FROM RM100 TO RM90 as a direct result, which is the honest consequence of the fix rather than a second decision. He has paid RM100/unit on four of his five orders, so it is a RM10 cut he did not ask for: what his standing is worth on the board rather than a concession.

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: all three laws hold on all five tiers across all ten sizes. Profit never falls, the rate never rises, and every step carries a real discount on Regular, One-time and Loyal. The discount tiers converge at the top not because of a floor but because the profit law forbids them earning less than they earned at the size below, which is the constraint doing its job.
NOTHING BANKED MOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit.

t: Identity rebuilt, and five categories that earn themselves
n: THE OLD CODE CARRIED TWO THINGS THAT MOVE. C or S, the first initial, the LENGTH of the name, then the location. It made sense while the vault was locked and the code was the only readable handle anyone had. v217 unlocked the directory and from that moment the code was baking mutable attributes into an identifier: correct a spelling and the length changes, move house and the suffix changes, and either breaks the one-identifier rule.

THE NEW CODE IS THE FIRST INITIAL AND A GLOBAL SEQUENCE in joining order: G01, J02, F03. One letter of signal, which is enough for him and not enough for anyone else, which is what he asked for. No name, no length, no place. The sequence never repeats and is never reused. 28 people re-keyed across the ledger, the roster, the gazetteer, the network, the plans and the directory, with the old ids purged outright and no translation table, per the standing rule.

ACCOUNTS HANG OFF A PERSON; PEOPLE NEVER HANG OFF A PERSON. S11-R is the same man's reselling account and S11-GEN is his bucket, so those carry his number. A BUYER may not: the party filed as CS6-BS-1-MK was a person kept under someone else's name and is now M14, with a code of his own.

TWO PROBLEMS DISSOLVED RATHER THAN WERE FIXED. The TBC codes are gone, because a code no longer needs a place and a party whose location is unknown is simply that. And the party with a location but NO NAME could not be a person under his rule, so it folds into the bucket; it had never traded, so nothing moved.

THE BUCKET IS NOT A PERSON ANYWHERE NOW. It was excluded from the map at v222 but still counted as a customer everywhere else: it drew badges, sat in the approach calendar, took a place in the concentration ranking and had a buying cadence computed for it. isPerson() is the single test and every per-person view asks it.

FIVE CATEGORIES, READ OFF THE LEDGER EVERY TIME, never typed against a name, so a customer moves up by trading and down by stopping. Special (spend and orders), Associate (resells or refers, a standing rather than a spend), Loyal (three orders and active), Regular, One-time. On this book: Special 2, Associate 4, Loyal 4, Regular 2, One-time 12. A reselling account is folded into its owner, so nobody is counted twice or lands in two categories at once.

THE LADDER NOW OBEYS THREE LAWS AND THEY ARE ENFORCED IN ONE FORWARD PASS. Profit may not fall as the lot grows. The rate may not rise. And every step up must cut the rate by at least 3%, because profit rising and the rate merely not rising are both satisfied by a FLAT rate, and a flat rate gives a customer no reason to take more: Regular sat at RM100 at both 1 and 1.5 unit.

THREE PASSES FOUGHT EACH OTHER AND WERE REPLACED BY ONE. Enforcing profit, then rate, then the incentive let the last undo the first: pulling 6.25 unit down for the discount left 12.5 unit quoting a HIGHER rate than the size below. Each price is now chosen once inside a band whose ends are both known first.

WHERE THE LAWS CANNOT ALL HOLD, THE TIER STOPS. Special and Associate are the cheapest ladders so their floors bind first; rather than break a law their boards simply end, at 3 unit and 5 unit. A short honest ladder beats a long one containing a step where taking more costs more per unit. Verified: all three laws hold on all five tiers.

A 1 UNIT PENDING ORDER FROM A10, PRICED BY CATEGORY. He classifies Loyal off the ledger, five orders with the last five days ago, and the Loyal ladder quotes RM100. He has paid RM100/unit on four of his five orders, so the engine landed on his own rate without being told it.

NOTHING BANKED MOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, collected RM13,522, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit. Pending is now 16 unit worth RM1,180 across three orders. All fifteen tabs render clean and non-empty under both products.

t: No, profit must never fall as the lot grows, and on one pane it was
n: HIS QUESTION, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The 'What each size earns' table showed profit on the lot running RM193, RM190, RM183, RM175 from 6.25 to 12.5 unit: a stretch of the board where selling MORE salt earned LESS money. No board should ever contain that.

THE CAUSE WAS TWO ENGINES, WHICH IS THE WORSE FAULT. v234 replaced the quote board with enginePrice, but this pane still ran the old pxQuote over its own size list, so the desk was quoting two different prices for the same lot depending on which pane you looked at. One ladder now serves both.
THE LADDER OBEYS TWO LAWS AND ONLY ONE WAS EVER ENFORCED. The rate may not rise with size, which was enforced. The profit may not fall with size, which was not.

THEY LOOK LIKE THEY FIGHT AND THEY DO NOT. Holding profit merely EQUAL to the size below sets price = profit + goods x quantity + delivery, so the rate becomes profit/q + goods + delivery/q, and both of those terms shrink as q grows. Equal profit therefore always lands at a strictly LOWER rate than the size below. The equal-profit price is the floor of the allowed range and the previous rate is its ceiling, and that range is never empty. Proven, not asserted: both laws now hold across all fifteen sizes.

THE BUY SIMULATOR IS REMOVED at his instruction, with every local that existed only to feed it: the quantity and rate overrides, the arrival day, the what-if forecast, the quick-set chips, the shrinkage level switch and the re-priced board. srcOver, srcSet, srcReset, wireSourcing and srcRedraw are gone with it.

THE SUPPLIER TABLE WAS MIXING PRODUCTS, which is what he meant by asking what the table even was. supplierStats() read the whole purchase book, so an oil supplier at RM7/unit sat beside a salt supplier at RM50, and 50 unit of oil counted against 206 unit of salt as though a unit were a unit. Share, weighted rate, best rate and fill were all computed across two commodities that share nothing but a column heading. Sourcing sits under the product band, so it now shows the selected product alone: salt reads SA5-BTR at 100% of the last 30 days again, which also restores the concentration warning the oil lot had been diluting away.

MY OWN TEST HARNESS MISSED SOMETHING AND HAS BEEN FIXED. Removing the simulator left a reference to a deleted local and the whole Sourcing tab rendered EMPTY. The syntax check passed and the tab sweep passed, because a blank section contains no bad text. The sweep now fails a tab that renders almost nothing, which is how this was caught.
POSITION UNCHANGED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit, trading cash RM572 net. All fifteen tabs render clean and non-empty under both products.

t: The paid-up capital plan is removed
n: IT SAT IN TWO PLACES. PLANS_CASH entry K1, 'capital cut to RM250, remainder taken as owner's dividend', which fed a Forward-tab scenario behind a switch. And whiteboard plan P15, 'Cut paid-up capital to RM250 and draw the rest', stated 28 Jul and marked committed. Both removed.

NEITHER EVER TOUCHED A FIGURE, so nothing in the books moves. cashAdjust is empty and always has been, meaning no drawing was ever recorded; the plan only ever existed as an intention and as an optional scenario. Revenue, margin, cash, stock and every receivable are identical.
THE FORWARD TOGGLE DISAPPEARS BY ITSELF, being guarded on PLANS_CASH being non-empty. Nothing had to be unwired.

THE DRAWING MACHINERY STAYS, DORMANT. A leaveRM or fixed-amount drawing plan added to the array still resolves during the cash walk, sized against the balance standing on the day. It is about twenty guarded lines and a future drawing is plausible, so it is kept rather than deleted and re-derived later. If the intention is that this desk never models a drawing again, it comes out of the walk too.

ONE REFERENCE SURVIVES AND IS DELIBERATE: a code comment explaining why a plan's worth is an explicit field rather than a regex over its prose cites P15 as one of the two cases that got it wrong. It documents a real fault in the code it sits above and is not rendered anywhere.

VERIFIED: whiteboard now runs P1 to P17 without P15, PLANS_CASH is empty, and neither the Forward tab nor the Whiteboard mentions capital or a dividend anywhere. All fifteen tabs render clean under both products. Revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit, trading cash RM572 net.

t: The quote board is gone, and nothing types a price any more
n: FIVE PRINTED LADDERS RETIRED OUTRIGHT. SS, S, R, M and P are gone with no translation table, because a price is not an identity and nothing needs to look the old ones up. Three tiers replace them and they are RELATIONSHIPS, not sizes: Loyal, Regular, Acquaintance.

THE OLD BOARD WAS A LIST OF NUMBERS SOMEBODY DECIDED ONCE. Solved against cost at v205, then frozen, so it aged: every price answered a question about a cost base that had since moved. Worse, tierTargets() worked BACKWARDS from those typed anchors to infer the margin, so the margin was an accident of an old decision.

THE MARGIN IS NOW REGRESSED FROM THE LEDGER. Every priced sale is a data point: what it sold for against what it cost to serve at that size. Ordinary least squares of margin on ln(quantity) over 49 orders gives 46% at 1 unit falling to 33% at 12.5. Rebate and zero-value rows are excluded, because a free unit is not a price anyone accepted. It refits as the desk trades, with no decision taken by anyone.

BELOW EIGHT PRICED ORDERS IT REFUSES TO FIT and uses a stated fallback instead, rather than regressing three sales into a pricing policy. The fitted slope is also barred from going positive: on a thin book one large well-priced order could tilt the line upward and quote bulk dearer per unit than retail.

A PRICE IS BUILT FROM THE BOTTOM, and every input is measured except one. Goods at the locked landed cost grossed for samples. Delivery at RM5 once per ORDER. Credit for the days each tier actually takes, at 12% a year. Bad debt at the rate the book has actually lost. Then the fitted margin. The only typed number left is a shift applied to the whole curve, and it is at zero.

SIZE NEEDS NO CARD OF ITS OWN. A fixed RM5 an order dilutes as the lot grows, so the rate taper falls out of the arithmetic rather than being typed into five ladders by eye. That is why three tiers can do what five were doing.

FOUND AND FIXED, AND IT WAS MINE FROM v232: the delivery cost was counted twice. eff spread RM5 over an average 2.73 unit order to give a per-unit headline, and solveLadder then multiplied that by the quantity AND added RM5 per lot on top. A 6 unit floor carried six deliveries. pxCost now returns effEx, goods only per unit, and every price and floor adds delivery exactly once. Every floor on the board has moved as a result.
THE FLOOR WAS BUILT THE SAME WRONG WAY and is now built per lot: (goods x quantity + one delivery) over one minus the floor percentage.

A SANITY CHECK THE BOARD PASSED ON ITS OWN: CJ4-BJ's pending 12.5 unit at RM850 lands exactly on the new Loyal price of RM850. Nobody arranged that; he is a loyal high-volume customer and the engine priced him where he already sits.

HEADROOM IS NOW NIL AND THAT IS INFORMATION, not a fault. The Loyal price at 12.5 unit sits RM19 above its floor, so a single ringgit on the buying rate breaches it. The old board read 27.7% only because its top-end prices were set well above what the evidence supports.

PRICE_TIERS SURVIVES AS A SHAPE, NOT A DECISION. It keeps sizes and tiers with prices parallel, so the menu, the sheets and thirty other call sites carry on unchanged, but every number in it is generated by engineBoard() and rebuilt with every recompute.

THE DYNAMIC LADDER PANE AND ITS DRIFT ANALYSIS ARE DELETED. They existed to compare the printed cards against the model; the board and the model are now the same object, so drift is structurally zero and a pane reporting it would be theatre.
NOTHING IN THE LEDGER MOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit. All fifteen tabs render clean under both products.

t: The board is frozen between purchases, and it had been drifting daily
n: HIS INSTRUCTION: reprice only when a lot is bought, and until then do not move. It was moving every day and nothing announced it.

TWO OF THE FOUR COMPONENTS DRIFTED ON THEIR OWN. The leak is self-use over everything handled, so it changes with every count and every unit that goes out. The average delivery changes with every order shipped. A floor quoted to a customer on Tuesday was not the floor on Thursday without a single decision being taken in between. On a desk where the cards are printed and carried on a phone that is worse than a wrong price, because nobody knows which one is live.

THE BASIS IS NOW A SNAPSHOT, taken when a lot lands and held as DATA rather than recalculated. PRICE_LOCK carries the lot, the freight, the leak, the average delivery and the resulting basis, per product. The board reads those and nothing else.

THE TRIGGER IS THE LOT, NOT THE DATE. pxCost compares the locked lot against the latest received lot. Same lot and the snapshot stands however old it is. A newer lot and the desk reprices immediately, marks the Pricing panel 'Repriced' instead of 'Frozen', and raises a breach until the figures are written back into PRICE_LOCK. A purchase is exactly when a price SHOULD move, and it is now the only time it can.

THE SIMULATOR STILL BYPASSES THE LOCK, because testing a hypothetical lot is the one occasion a fresh number is wanted. The panel marks that state 'Simulated' so it cannot be mistaken for the live basis.

LOCKED TODAY: salt at RM53.19 on the 100 unit lot of 28 Jul, oil at RM7.90 on the 50 unit lot of 06 Aug. Tested by pushing a hypothetical newer lot: the state flipped to stale, the basis repriced to RM56.69 and the breach fired, exactly as intended.

FIXED, AND IT WAS HIS CATCH: an empty chart replaced its CANVAS with a sentence but left the .chartbox and its inline height, so a chart with nothing to draw still reserved up to 250px of empty space under a heading describing a chart that was not there. The Order book showed one line floating in a 190px void. chartEmpty now removes the whole CARD where the card exists only to hold a chart, and collapses the box otherwise. Seventeen guards rewritten; no empty chartbox anywhere now reserves height.

NOTHING IN THE LEDGER MOVED AND NO PRICE MOVED. Salt revenue RM14,323.26, cost of goods RM8,958.36, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, shelf 39.47 unit, floors unchanged, headroom RM13/unit at 27.7%, no tier under its floor. IFRS statement unchanged: gross profit RM5,220.46 at 36.4%, operating profit RM2,170.15 at 15.2%. All fifteen tabs clean under both products.

t: The pricing basis was wrong three ways, and the floors moved with it
n: IT PRICED OFF AN AVERAGE, NOT A LOT. The basis was pxQuoteRate(), a 30-day weighted buying rate of RM56, which blends in what salt used to cost. A price set today has to replace today, so the basis is now the rate on the latest lot actually received: RM47, the 100 unit lot of 28 Jul.

IT CARRIED NO COST OF COLLECTING A LOT. RM20 a pickup, stated by him, spread over the lot it arrived on: RM0.20/unit on 100 unit. A big lot carries it thinly and a small one does not, which is part of what buying in size is for.

IT CARRIED NO COST OF DELIVERING AN ORDER. RM5 an order for delivery, packaging and handling, divided by the average delivery of 2.73 unit measured over 58 actual deliveries: RM1.83/unit. It ADDS rather than divides, because it is spent per order whatever the salt cost, and it is why a half-unit order is a different business to a bulk one.

THE LEAK NOW HAS A REASON RATHER THAN JUST A NUMBER. Half of it is samples, testers and advertising, so those units are spent winning sales and the sales they win must carry them: RM4.16/unit. The attribution was already 50%; what changes is that it is now a stated cost rather than an arbitrary split. The other half, RM4.96/unit, is still absorbed and is shown as absorbed.
THE BASIS IS RM53.19/UNIT AGAINST RM60.93. Lower, despite adding two costs that were never there, because the RM56 average was RM9 above the rate actually paid.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS LIVE AND IT REVERSES A DECISION. Every floor falls about 12.7%. The 12.5 unit floor goes from RM952.06 to RM831.05, so CJ4-BJ's pending 12.5 unit at RM850 now CLEARS it by RM18.95. The 'Pending under floor' breach raised at v225 is gone, and the order that looked like a relationship problem was an arithmetic one. Board headroom rises from RM6/unit at 10.7% to RM13/unit at 27.7%.

IFRS: THE SAME FOUR COSTS SORT TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, and conflating them is how a desk capitalises its marketing. IAS 2.11 puts the lot rate and the collection cost into INVENTORY. IAS 2.16(d) excludes selling costs, so delivery and packaging are period. IAS 38.69 expenses advertising and promotion, so samples and testers are period. IAS 2.16(a) expenses abnormal waste, so the unexplained half of the leak is period. Pricing basis RM53.19, balance-sheet cost RM47.20, and they are meant to differ.

NEW STATEMENT OF PROFIT OR LOSS on the Financials tab, per product. Salt: revenue RM14,323, cost of sales RM9,103 (goods RM8,958 plus freight in RM144), GROSS PROFIT RM5,220 at 36.4%. Then selling and distribution RM290, marketing RM1,005, abnormal loss RM1,005, IFRS 9 credit loss nil, and the RM750 SF6-KLC prepayment impairment. OPERATING PROFIT RM2,170, 15.2% of revenue.
THAT 15.2% IS THE NUMBER THE DESK HAS NEVER SHOWN. The headline margin of 37.5% was never wrong, but it is gross of every cost of actually selling, and the gap between the two is RM3,050.

INVENTORY AT THE LOWER OF COST AND NRV (IAS 2.9). Salt: RM1,908 at landed cost against RM3,973 NRV, so cost is lower and carried. Oil: RM333 at cost and NRV NOT TESTED, because oil has a supply quote and no selling card, so there is no price to estimate NRV from. Reported as untested rather than passed.

FIXED WHILE BUILDING: the SF6-KLC prepayment write-off was guarded on the active product rather than on salt, so selecting oil put a RM750 salt loss into oil's statement and turned a RM48 operating profit into a RM702 loss. Also pxShrinkRate() used salt's opening quantity whatever product was selected.

NOTHING IN THE LEDGER MOVED. Revenue RM14,323.26, collected RM13,522, shelf 39.47 unit, receivables nil, pending 15 unit. All fifteen tabs render clean under both products, no tier sits under its floor, and pxOver.cost restores to null after the headroom walk.

t: The rail explains the products, so the prose does not have to
n: HIS COMPLAINT WAS RIGHT AND IT BROKE A STANDING RULE. The product work shipped with paragraphs explaining how and why the switcher scopes what it scopes. Prose economy is a hard rule on every surface, and I wrote explanation instead of building something self-evident.

THE RAIL NOW CARRIES THE ANSWER. Two bands: one headed with the selected product's name in its own colour, holding Command, Position and Trading; one headed All products, holding Relationships and Actions. Sourcing and Pricing moved into the product band where they belong, Transaction and Whiteboard stay outside it. Switching recolours the band and renames it. You can see which nine tabs follow the product, so the sentence saying so is deleted.

THE OVERVIEW PARAGRAPH BECOMES A TABLE: one row per product with revenue, margin, shelf, shelf value and spend, the active row highlighted, a combined row beneath, and an 'open' button on the inactive one. It replaces a paragraph that said the same thing in ninety words.

THE SUPPLY PANEL LOSES ITS HISTORY. A Buying chip in the heading replaces the paragraph explaining that a supply quote is not a selling card. The account of what v226 got wrong belongs in this file, not on the page.

FOLDED, AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST CUT: .insight blocks never collapsed. .dsc notes have folded behind Method and caveats since v210, but insights were exempt, so the longest prose on the desk was the prose that always showed. Network alone carried 1,976 permanently visible characters. They are now treated as the lead already is: first sentence stays, because that is the finding; the rest folds.

VISIBLE INSIGHT PROSE FALLS FROM 4,477 CHARACTERS TO 593. Nothing is deleted or summarised: expanding restores the original HTML verbatim, and it was tested rather than asserted. Every number on all fifteen tabs under BOTH products was extracted before and after and compared: the only differences anywhere are the Method-and-caveats counters, which rose because insights now count toward them.

COMMITTED FROM THE QUEUE: CN6-WM redeems the free unit earned at v223 when his R2 turnover crossed RM500. No advance to offset, so it is handed over as salt exactly as his 04 Aug half unit was. RM0 of revenue, 1 unit off the shelf at RM47 of cost. Earned 2, applied 2, nothing owed either way. Shelf 40.47 to 39.47 unit, margin RM5,411.90 to RM5,364.90, 37.46%.

FIXED, AND THE REDEMPTION EXPOSED IT: nextBest() took the median of every order's rate including rebate rows. CN6-WM has three direct orders of which two are free units, so his median rate read RM0 and the uplift against it rendered as +Infinity per cent. A free unit is not evidence of a price anyone accepted; rebate and zero-value rows are now excluded, and where nothing priced is left the rate reads as a dash rather than a number.

POSITION: salt shelf 39.47 unit, revenue RM14,323.26, collected RM13,522, margin RM5,364.90 at 37.46%, receivables nil, pending 15 unit, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%. Oil 45 unit at RM7, revenue RM130, margin RM56.67 at 43.6%, plug nil. All fifteen tabs clean under both products.

t: The opening oil has a rate, and finding it caught a worse bug
n: THE OPENING 5 UNIT ARE CARRIED AT RM7.667. They came off a 30 unit lot bought for RM230, which is the 30 unit tier on SP7-PUD's ladder. Written into the desk as the division rather than a rounded 7.67, so the arithmetic shows its working and no rounding is baked into a cost basis. The other 25 unit of that lot were gone before this book opened and are not on it.

FIFO NOW APPLIES TO THE ONLY OIL SALE, and it moves the margin. The shelf held 5 unit of opening oil at RM7.667 when the 50 unit lot landed at RM7 on the same day. Oldest first, so the 10 unit order took the 5 opening unit and 5 new ones: RM73.33 of cost and RM56.67 of margin, 43.6%. v229 showed RM60 at 46.2%, costing the whole order at the new lot because the opening rate was unknown. RM3.33 is a small number and the discipline is not: costing a sale at the cheapest lot on the shelf flatters every margin it touches.

FOUND WHILE CHECKING THE SHELF VALUE, AND IT IS THE MORE SERIOUS FAULT. STOCK_COST is the rate of the lots on the SALT shelf, and five places read it unconditionally: the Overview stock-cost card, the stock valuation, the Financials line and replCost(), which feeds the PRICING ENGINE. With oil selected they valued 45 unit of oil at RM47.47 and reported a shelf of RM2,136 that is worth RM315.

IT PRODUCED NO NaN AND NO THROW, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS. Every sweep since v228 passed clean because the number was well formed; it was simply wrong by a factor of seven, and it would have been wrong on screen in a card headed 'Stock value'. The tab sweep tests for malformed output and cannot test for plausible output, so this class of fault has to be looked for deliberately whenever a global is read across a product boundary.

SHELF VALUE IS NOW PER PRODUCT: salt RM47.47, oil RM7. Oil's 45 unit are all off the 50 unit lot, since the opening 5 were consumed first by the only sale, so RM7 is the rate of what is actually on the shelf rather than an average of what has been. That is the same test STOCK_COST answers for salt.

OIL'S WEIGHTED COST IS RM7.0606 across 55 unit, being the RM350 lot plus RM38.33 of opening. The book still ties exactly: opening 5 plus 50 bought less 10 sold is the 45 counted, plug nil, boundary list empty.

SALT IS UNMOVED: revenue RM14,323.26, cost of goods RM8,911.36, margin RM5,411.90 at 37.78%, shelf 40.47 unit valued at RM1,921.11, replacement RM47.47, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%. All fifteen tabs render clean under both products.

t: Oil is measured in tens, and that was the last thing wrong with it
n: THE BASIS OF MEASUREMENT WAS A TENTH OF WHAT IT SHOULD BE. SP7-PUD's ladder is 10, 20, 30 and 50 unit at RM100, 180, 230 and 350, so the rates are RM10, RM9, RM7.67 and RM7 rather than RM100 to RM70. Every oil quantity and every oil rate on this desk was wrong by a factor of ten from v226 until now.

THREE READINGS OF ONE ROW, AND ONLY THE THIRD IS THE TRADE THAT HAPPENED. The sale is 10 unit at RM130 drawn from a RM7 lot: RM60 of margin, 46.2%. v226 and v227 called it 1 unit at RM130 with margin unknowable, because the ladder was read as a selling card. v228 fixed the side of the trade and reported RM30 at 23.1%, still on tenth-size quantities. It took both corrections to get a true figure, which is worth remembering the next time a single number looks settled.

THE OIL BOOK NOW TIES EXACTLY. Opening 5 unit, plus 50 bought, less 10 sold, is the 45 unit he counted. Ledger and count agree to the unit, so the shrinkage plug is nil, which no product on this desk has ever managed before: salt's is 38.23 unit.

FIRST OIL LOT RECORDED: 50 unit for RM350 from SP7-PUD, the top tier and the sharpest rate on his ladder at RM7/unit, so the first oil ever bought was bought at the best price offered. Stated assumptions, since neither was given: dated 06 Aug, the day the product was declared and the sale went out, and treated as paid and received in full because it was reported as a completed purchase rather than an order.
THE v228 BREACH IS CLEARED. Oil no longer shows units sold with nothing bought, and the shelf no longer reconstructs to minus one. The oil boundary list is now empty.

THE OPENING 5 UNIT HAS NO STATED COST, so it stays out of the weighted average rather than being guessed. The oil cost basis is therefore RM7/unit on the 50 unit lot alone, which is honest but thin: one lot is not an average.

FIXED, AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN UGLY ON SCREEN: the uncarded-size check walked whole units. On oil, measured in tens, that proposed 46 sizes nobody would ask for; on salt, whose tiers are 12.5 apart, it proposed 96. It now steps by the highest common factor of the tier sizes, computed on hundredths so a fractional tier like 12.5 survives an integer gcd, and shows at most four. Oil steps by 10 and reports one real gap at 40 unit; salt steps by 12.5 and reports four.
WORTH KNOWING AT THE POINT OF BUYING: 40 unit of oil built off the ladder costs RM330, while 50 unit costs RM350. The last 10 unit cost RM20, which is RM2/unit against a RM7 lot rate.

SALT IS UNMOVED TO THE RINGGIT: revenue RM14,323.26, collected RM13,522, cost of goods RM8,911.36, margin RM5,411.90 at 37.78%, shelf 40.47 unit, plug 38.23 unit, bought 231.25 unit at RM51.7197 weighted, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%. All fifteen tabs render clean under both products.

t: The desk becomes multi-commodity, and the oil ladder was a supply quote all along
n: ONE LEDGER, TAGGED. Every sale and purchase carries a `product`, and absent means salt, so not one of the sixty-odd existing rows had to be edited to say what it already was. A row that forgets is treated as salt rather than dropped.

ONE BOOK PER PRODUCT, AND THE SPLIT BITES IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE. recompute() now reads pSales(PROD) and pPurch(PROD) instead of the whole arrays. Everything downstream is untouched, because every product-scoped tab already read the globals recompute sets. Adding product three means adding a PRODUCTS entry, not editing fifteen tabs.

WHAT SWITCHES AND WHAT DOES NOT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Switching scopes the nine tabs that are ABOUT a product: Today, Forward, Overview, Order book, Inventory, Financials, Analysis, Sourcing, Pricing. Each has its own shelf, cost, leak and ladder, and mixing them would give a stock figure in no unit at all. It does NOT scope Customers, Network, Map, Ledger, Transaction or Whiteboard, because there is one bank account, one roster and one map, and a customer who buys both should appear once with both purchases against his name. He was unsure; this is the reversible choice, since consolidated views can be scoped later but a desk split end to end cannot be recombined without re-keying the roster.

CORRECTED, AND IT INVERTED THE PRODUCT: the 1/2/3/5 unit ladder at RM100/180/230/350 is SP7-PUD's SUPPLY QUOTE, what oil costs, not a selling card. v226 and v227 read it as a sell card. Consequences: oil has a real cost basis, the first sale made RM30 at 23.1% rather than an unknown margin, and the observation that a reseller paid RM30 over the card is WITHDRAWN for oil, because there is no oil selling card at all. The equivalent salt observation about CN6-WM stands, being RM15/unit over the R card.

QUOTES ARE NOW ONE THING IN ONE PLACE. A QUOTES registry keyed by product, rendered by a single panel that labels itself a BUYING ladder in its first sentence. The v226 error was possible because oil's ladder lived in a structure of its own with no label saying which side of the trade it was on; that cannot recur.

THE LADDER CHECK IS NOW SHARED AND RUNS ON EVERY PRODUCT'S QUOTE. Rate must not rise with size, and no lot may be beaten by buying the same quantity in smaller lots. Both of Patrick's pass: rates fall RM100, RM90, RM76.67, RM70, and nothing is beaten. The uncarded 4 unit size is reported rather than filled, and it is worth knowing: 4 units bought off the ladder is RM330 while 5 units is RM350, so the fifth unit costs RM20.
TWO OIL SUPPLIERS MINTED: SM4-KEP at Kepong and SP7-PUD at Pudu, derived by the standing rule rather than invented, with both places added to the gazetteer. Roster goes to 33, sited 25, drawn 23.

NEW BREACH AND IT IS REAL: oil shows 1 unit sold and delivered with NOTHING ever recorded as bought, so the reconstructed shelf is minus one. The margin is only right because the row states its own cost. A new check reports it for whichever product is active, and it also distinguishes a shelf NEVER COUNTED from one counted at nought, which are different claims.

FIXED WHILE TESTING: the pending-under-floor check walked every product's rows, so selecting oil judged a SALT order against oil's cost base and produced a confident, meaningless breach. And the free-to-sell breach both duplicated the no-purchases finding and said 'salt' while oil was selected. Both scoped.

SALT IS UNMOVED TO THE RINGGIT. Revenue RM14,323.26, collected RM13,522, cost of goods RM8,911.36, margin RM5,411.90 at 37.78%, shelf 40.47 unit, plug 38.23 unit, receivables nil, pending 15 unit, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%, and the same two boundary rows. All fifteen tabs render clean under BOTH products with no throw and no bad figure.

t: The oil card is fine. I had the size wrong
n: THE TOP OIL TIER IS 5 UNITS AT RM350, NOT 4. Recorded as 4 at v226 on my mishearing. The correction is to the SIZE, not the price, and it removes both faults v226 reported.

ON THE REAL FIGURE THE CARD PASSES BOTH TESTS THE SALT BOARD ENFORCES. Rates run RM100, RM90, RM76.67, RM70, falling at every step, so nobody pays more per unit for taking more. And no tier can be beaten by splitting the order: 5 units at RM350 beats 3+2 at RM410 and every other combination.

WHAT v226 SAID WAS TRUE OF A TIER THAT DOES NOT EXIST. At 4 units for RM350 the rate really would have risen from RM76.67 to RM87.50, and 3+1 really would have bought the same oil for RM330 against a RM350 tier. Both findings were sound arithmetic on wrong input. The v226 entry is left standing rather than edited, because the desk records what it did; this entry is the correction.

THERE IS NO 4 UNIT TIER AND THAT IS NOT A HOLE. A skipped size is dropped rather than filled, which is the rule the salt ladder already follows. The panel now reports the uncarded sizes and what they cost anyway: built from the card, 4 units is RM330, and 5 units is RM350, so the fifth unit costs RM20 and the 4-to-5 step is the cheapest oil on the card. That is a quoting fact, not a defect.

HARDENED WHILE IN THERE: the split-check was a naive recursion over the tiers. It is now memoised and rounds to two places at each step, so a future card with fractional sizes or many tiers cannot hang the Pricing tab.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED. Salt revenue RM14,323, collected RM13,522, margin RM5,412 at 37.8%, shelf 40.47 unit, plug 38.23 unit, receivables nil, pending 15 unit, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%. Oil revenue RM130 on one sale, margin and stock still null because no oil has been recorded as bought or counted.

t: A second product, and its card has a fault the salt board could not produce
n: OIL ARRIVES, AND THE FIRST SALE IS ON THE BOOK. CS6-BS resells 1 unit to an end buyer with no name, so it books to his general bucket with CS6-BS-R as counterparty, exactly as a salt downsell would. RM130, paid and delivered on the day. The party was given as a name shared by TWO codes on this book; the '(Bangsar South)' in the instruction is what resolved it, which is the split rule doing its job.

IT IS HELD ENTIRELY OUTSIDE THE SALT BOOKS, AND THAT IS NOT TIDINESS. This desk is single-commodity in its bones.
