An oil sale booked as an ordinary row would have been destructive three ways: ledgerStock sums every sale, so one unit of oil sold would read as one unit of SALT gone, raising the shrinkage plug and every floor on the board; cogs falls back to wavgBuy where a row has no cost, so oil would have been costed at the salt average of RM51.72 and reported a margin that is pure invention; and every band, ladder and concentration figure would silently mix two commodities.

MARGIN AND STOCK ARE NULL AND STAY NULL. No oil has ever been recorded as bought, so there is no cost to subtract and none is estimated. No oil has been counted, so there is no oil shelf, no oil cover and no oil leak. The panel says what is missing at least as loudly as what is known.

THE CARD IS CHECKED THE WAY THE SALT BOARD CHECKS ITSELF, AND IT FAILS BOTH TESTS. At 1, 2, 3 and 4 units for RM100, 180, 230 and 350 the rates are RM100, RM90, RM76.67 and RM87.50. The rate RISES between 3 and 4 units by RM10.83, so a customer taking more oil pays more per unit for it.

WORSE, THE 4 UNIT TIER IS ALREADY BEATEN BY YOUR OWN CARD. The same 4 units bought as 3+1 costs RM330 against the RM350 tier, so anyone who orders twice saves RM20. That is the same fault as the 100 unit salt quote that sat at RM4,800 after the lot was bought at RM4,700: a price the customer can already beat. A tier nobody should ever take is worse than no tier.

NOT AUTO-CORRECTED. The salt ladder cannot produce either fault, because solveLadder rounds and then an explicit pass walks the ladder pulling prices down until the rate stops rising. This card was typed rather than solved. What the 4 unit tier should earn is a decision, not an arithmetic slip, so the desk reports it and leaves it.

RM130 ON A RM100 CARD IS THE SECOND TIME THIS WEEK A RESELLER HAS PAID OVER THE CARD, after CN6-WM at RM125/unit against a RM110 card on 05 Aug. Either the market bears more than the cards assume or the cards are set low. Two sales on two products is not evidence, but it is worth watching.

NO SALT FIGURE MOVED. Revenue RM14,323, collected RM13,522, margin RM5,412 at 37.8%, shelf 40.47 unit, self-use plug 38.23 unit, receivables nil, pending 15 unit, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%: all identical to v225. Oil shows on Overview as an explicit exclusion so it cannot be mistaken for part of them.

THE PROPER END STATE IS A product FIELD on every row with the aggregates filtered by it. That is a real refactor and was not done on the strength of one sale; this holds the record faithfully until it is worth doing.

t: Two pending orders, and one of them no longer clears its floor
n: CE4-CHE, 2.5 unit at RM230, agreed today. His THIRD order at exactly that size and price, matching 23 Jul and 31 Jul, so it is a settled habit rather than a negotiation. Clears the RM190.41 floor by RM39.59 and the RM195 walk-away by RM35, sitting between the S card at RM220 and the R card at RM270, which is where his rate has sat every time.
CJ4-BJ, 12.5 unit at RM850, PLANNED for 07 Aug rather than agreed on it: the date is the intention, not a movement. An exact repeat of his 15 Jul order, same size, same total, same RM68/unit.

AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM: THE PRICE HAS NOT MOVED AND THE COST HAS. The floor at 12.5 unit is now RM952.06 and the engine quotes RM955, so RM850 is RM102 under floor. It was NOT under floor in July. The 03 Aug count found 12.18 unit gone with nothing recorded against it, which lifted the leak from 11.03% to 16.19% and raised every floor on the board. The order did not get worse; the cost base did.

WHAT IT STILL DOES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. At RM68/unit against the RM47 lot actually on the shelf it makes RM21/unit, RM262.50 on the lot, so it is cash-positive and well above what the salt cost. It does not cover the RM60.93 it costs to REPLACE that salt plus the 20% the wholesale band asks. Margin on replacement is 10.4%. Left visible and left pending rather than quietly repriced: he is the second largest customer on the book and the lot is 31% of the free shelf, so it is a relationship decision, not an arithmetic one.

BOTH COUNT NOWHERE. Neither paid nor delivered, so no revenue, no cost of goods, no stock movement, no receivable. They show in the Order book and in Boundaries only, and the 15 unit is still on the shelf and still free to sell.

FIXED, AND IT WAS A REAL BLIND SPOT. boundaryScan's margin-floor check walks pricedSales, and pricedSales excludes Pending by definition, so the ONE state in which a price is wholly repriceable was the one state the check could not see. Its own comment says an open sale still breaches because it can be acted on; a pending one can be acted on completely. New 'Pending under floor' rule closes it.

IT IS MEASURED DIFFERENTLY ON PURPOSE. The existing check compares against the row's own lot cost, which is right for salt already drawn. A pending order has drawn nothing, so there is no lot to charge it to and the only honest comparison is replacement: floorTotal() over effective cost, the same floor the quote board and walk-away are built on. Judging it against a cheap old lot would have passed a price the board itself would refuse, which is exactly how this order slipped through on lot cost at 30.9% while failing on replacement at 10.4%.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED. Revenue RM14,323, collected RM13,522, margin RM5,412 at 37.8%, shelf 40.47 unit all free, receivables nil, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%. Pending now reads 15 unit worth RM1,080 across two orders.

t: Nothing is owed, in either direction
n: CD4-CS PAYS THE RM150 IN FULL. It was the last open position on the book. Delivered 25 Jul on an advance with nothing paid, settled 06 Aug: 12 days out against a 10-day term, so 2 days over and 50% provisioned when it landed. Recorded by stating cash, deliveredOn and paidOn on the row rather than inventing an amendment trail, since the row never carried one.

RECEIVABLES GO TO NIL, GROSS AND NET. The RM75 of provisioning is released and riskRates() now reads a bad-debt rate of zero on RM14,323 of revenue. Due in is nil and due out is nil: no trade receivable, no supplier bill, no unpaid refund. The RM750 lost to SF6-KLC is not counted as expected cash, having been written off on 31 Jul.

THE BOOK IS FULLY SETTLED, WHICH IS A STRONGER STATEMENT THAN CURRENT. Revenue RM14,323 against RM13,522 collected in cash and RM801.26 settled in kind across ten rows: the two together are the whole of revenue to the ringgit. Nothing is outstanding anywhere on the book.
HIS CREDIT CAP IS CLEAR AGAIN. The order sat exactly ON the 1 unit retail cap rather than under it, so the cap has been fully drawn since 25 Jul and is now free.

TRADING CASH IS POSITIVE FOR THE FIRST TIME: RM13,522 in against RM12,650 of purchases and the RM80 refund paid to CZ6-WM, a net RM792. STATED AS A FLOW, NOT A BALANCE. There is still no cash count on this desk, so what the desk knows is what trading has generated, not what is held.

THE ONE THING STILL OUTSTANDING IS NOT A DEBT. CN6-WM is owed one free unit, earned when his R2 turnover crossed RM500 at v223 and not yet redeemed. It is a claim on the shelf rather than money, and free-to-sell reads 40.47 unit with 1 of them spoken for.

POSITION: shelf 40.47 unit all free, deferred and pending nil, margin RM5,412 at 37.8%, board headroom unchanged at RM6/unit and 10.7%. Cover 11.9 days at the fortnight rate of 3.41 unit a day, so the shelf still dries 17 Aug and the next-lot section is unmoved on its recommendation.

t: The best resell rate on the book, and it earns a free unit
n: CN6-WM RESELLS 2 UNIT FOR RM250, paid and collected on the day. The end buyer is a stranger, so it books to CN6-WM-Gen with CN6-WM-R as counterparty, exactly as his 03 Aug downsell and the CS6-BS ones do. The bucket is not a customer and is never issued a statement. Settlement on the order date, so it folds into the opening line and carries no amendment trail.

RM125/UNIT IS THE BEST RATE THIS DESK HAS TAKEN ON A RESELL AND IT IS NOT CLOSE. His own 6.5 unit resell on 03 Aug gave RM67.69/unit: same reseller, same bucket, nearly double the rate three days later. It is also RM15/unit ABOVE the R card, which quotes RM220 at 2 unit, and RM95 above the RM155 walk-away.

THAT IS WORTH UNDERSTANDING RATHER THAN CELEBRATING. A reseller paying over the retail card has to clear more than retail downstream to earn anything. Either he is selling into a pocket that bears more than this book has tested, or the 03 Aug rate was the anomaly and this is the correction. Stated, not resolved: one order is not a pattern.

IT CROSSES THE R2 REBATE STEP. His indirect turnover goes RM440 to RM690, past the RM500 threshold, so earnedR2 goes from 0 to 1 and total earned from 1 to 2 against 1 already applied. HE IS OWED ONE FREE UNIT. Nothing is handed over here: there is no advance outstanding for it to offset, so it stands as a claim until he asks, exactly as the first one did.

CONFIRMED BEFORE BOOKING RATHER THAN ASSUMED: that the RM250 was settled and collected, and that it is what the DESK receives rather than what the end buyer paid. On an R2 row the total is desk revenue, so reading it the other way would have overstated the rate and the margin together.

POSITION: shelf 42.47 to 40.47 unit, all free to sell, deferred and pending nil. Revenue RM14,323, collected RM13,372, cost of goods RM8,911, margin RM5,412 at 37.8%. Receivables unchanged at RM150 gross and RM75 net. Board headroom unchanged at RM6/unit and 10.7%: no cost input moved.

t: The map is finished, and the data was always there
n: THE GAZETTEER IS FILLED FROM NAMES & IDS. Thirteen suffixes were unplaced: SEN, SB, BJ, DAM, PER, CHE, SK, BS, KER, AD, BTR, TAI, HCM. Not one of them was unknown. Every party has carried a location in the parenthetical of his directory entry all along, and until the vault came off at v217 the desk could not read it. PLACES goes from 7 entries to 20.

TWO SOURCES, KEPT APART ON THE PAGE. The NAME of a place is the directory's, quoted as he typed it. The COORDINATE is not, because the directory holds none: each pair is a published centroid for the named locality, cited in src. Everything stays exact:false, which is the truth rather than modesty.

SITED 25 OF 31, DRAWN 23. Six are off the map and NOT ONE IS A GAP. Two are reseller trading accounts, which are the same people as their parent codes and would have drawn one man twice. Two are general downsell buckets, which are accounting destinations rather than persons. Two were entered as TBC, which is an admission rather than a location. The Map tab now says which of those two things it is instead of lumping them together as missing.

FIXED: -R READ AS MISSING DATA. The reseller-account suffix was not in NON_PLACE, so CS6-BS-R and CN6-WM-R sat in the unplaced list reading 'suffix R is not in the gazetteer', which invited someone to go and find a location that does not exist. Excluded for the reason it is excluded for.

THE FRAME IS THE KLANG VALLEY AND STAYS ONE. CN5-TAI is 217km NNW and CM6-HCM is 1,017km NNE, in another country. Plotting them would have stretched the bounding box across a thousand kilometres of sea and compressed every metro pin into a single smudge: arithmetically honest and visually useless. They are listed with great-circle distance and compass bearing instead, which carries more than a dot pinned to a corner.

DAMANSARA IS THE ONE GUESS LEFT AND IS LABELLED AS ONE. Two parties give it, and the name covers Damansara Heights in KL, Damansara Utama in PJ and Kota Damansara in Petaling, up to 12km apart. Sited at Damansara Heights as the nearest reading to the rest of the book, with the ambiguity written into the gazetteer row rather than hidden behind a pin.

KERINCHI AND BANGSAR SOUTH ARE THE SAME PLACE under two names, the second being the first renamed by its developer. Kept as separate entries because the directory keeps the names apart, offset about 400m so they do not overlap, and the offset is declared presentational rather than surveyed.

A REFERRAL RECORDED: CA5-KER was introduced by CS6-PER. His R3 stream goes from RM230 to RM350 across two referred customers. No rebate is triggered: the threshold is RM1,500 and the single-order lot trigger is 5 unit against an order of 1. NOTHING ELSE MOVED. Revenue RM14,073, collected RM13,122, margin RM5,256 at 37.3%, shelf 42.47 unit, receivables RM150 gross and RM75 net, board headroom RM6/unit at 10.7%: all identical to v221.

t: Two sold and paid, and one of them is not a card
n: CS6-BS-1-MK, 2 unit for RM220. An exact repeat of his 23 Jul order, same size and same price, and RM110/unit IS the R card at 2 unit to the ringgit. Floor RM152.33, walk-away RM155, so it clears both with RM67.67 to spare. Paid and delivered on the day, so it folds into the opening line and carries no trail.

BOOKED DIRECT, DELIBERATELY, AND THE CREDIT STILL REACHES CS6-BS. He is a named buyer under that reseller and the queue offered no assoc. Both earlier orders to him were booked direct, so this follows them rather than inventing a third treatment, and assocOf() resolves him through the 15 Jul R2 row that carries him as its downstream. The named-code trap does not bite here because that row already anchors him.
CS6-PER, 3 unit for RM240. His first order as an ordinary customer since the ban lifted on 30 Jul. Paid and delivered together, nothing owed.

RM80/unit IS NOT A CARD, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY WORTH READING. The SS ladder skips 3 unit rather than filling it, so the lowest card actually offered at that size is S at RM260, and this went out RM20 under it. It is NOT a breach: floor RM228.50 and walk-away RM230, cleared by RM11.50 and RM10, earning 21.3% on the RM60.93 effective cost. A sale under the bottom card is a decision rather than a quote, and it is recorded as one rather than smoothed into the ladder.

SHELF 47.47 TO 42.47 UNIT, all free to sell. Deferred nil, pending nil, in-transit nil. Both lots drawn from the RM47 salt, so the remnant is unchanged and STOCK_COST stays at RM47.47. No count since 03 Aug, so the plug stays at 38.23 unit.

THE NEXT-LOT SECTION MOVED ON ITS OWN, WHICH IS THE POINT OF BUILDING IT DERIVED. The shelf now dries 19 Aug rather than 17: the fortnight window rolled past a heavier week and the sell rate fell from 3.84 to 3.27 a day, which more than offsets the 5 unit that just left. The gap to end August narrows from 13.6 days to 12, the bridge from 55 unit to 40, and the pull-forward date slips from 13 to 14 Aug. Nothing was retyped.

POSITION: revenue RM14,073, collected RM13,122, margin RM5,256 at 37.3%, receivables RM150 gross and RM75 net on one debtor 12 days out. Board headroom unchanged at RM6/unit and 10.7%, since no cost input moved.

t: The next lot, stated, and the date that does not survive the shelf
n: SOURCING NOW CARRIES THE NEXT LOT. His plan, put where he asked for it: about 150 unit, end August, on the reading that next week is already covered. Typed: quantity, date, reasoning. Derived at render time from coverStats() and the live sell rate: every date, every gap and every ringgit, so a stated date cannot go stale while the shelf moves under it.
NEXT WEEK IS COVERED AND THE SECTION SAYS SO FIRST. 47.47 unit free, reorder mark of 15 unit not reached until 13 Aug. Nothing needs buying this week and the desk agrees with him on that.

THE DATE IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE SIZE. At 3.84 unit a day the shelf empties 17 Aug, 13.6 days before end August: 52.22 unit of demand meeting an empty shelf. On the four-week rate of 4.73 a day it empties 15 Aug, earlier still, so the sceptical read is the harsher one here rather than the softer.

TWO ROUTES, PRICED, AND NOT PRESENTED AS EQUAL. Pull the 150 forward to about 13 Aug: one lot, one trip, cover to 18 Sep. Or hold end August and bridge 55 unit: 205 unit inside a month against 115 of demand, RM9,635 committed in four weeks, and 137.26 unit sitting on the shelf on 31 Aug.

WHAT THE FIRST DRAFT GOT WRONG, FIXED BEFORE IT SHIPPED. It claimed pulling the lot forward puts the cadence back at month end by itself. It does not: 36.1 days of cover and a month are different lengths, and the honest re-buy date is 18 September. The bridge-route shelf figure also omitted the salt already on the shelf and the selling between now and then; it is now worked from free stock less the run rate plus both lots usable.

RM47/unit IS AN ASSUMPTION AND IS LABELLED ONE EVERYWHERE IT APPEARS. The ladder stops at 100 unit and there has never been a 150 unit lot. At RM47 the lot is RM7,050, effective RM50.81 after expected shrinkage, and pulls the weighted average from RM51.72 to RM49.89. The panel says to get a quote at the size before treating any of it as real.

THE RISK IS THE COUNTERPARTY, NOT THE PRICE. SA5-BTR is 100% of every unit bought in the last 30 days across 8 clean lots. RM7,050 to one name is 9.4 times the RM750 already lost to SF6-KLC, who was also reliable until he was not. Stated as a figure, with splitting the lot or paying against delivery as the answer, not as a warning against buying.

NOTHING IS BOOKED AND NOTHING MOVED. No stock, no payable, no in-transit, no cost and no board effect. Verified: all fifteen tabs render, no throw, revenue RM13,613, collected RM12,662, margin RM5,031 at 37.0%, receivables RM150 gross and RM75 net, shelf 47.47 unit, headroom RM6/unit at 10.7% and pxOver.cost restored to null. Every one identical to v219.

t: The book ties out, with one position left open on purpose
n: CH5-KLC cancelled. It was pending, so it counted nowhere and nothing moves; the row stays as the record that it was agreed and dropped.
CS6-BS-R collected the half unit paid for the day before. That was the last deferred salt on the book, so deferred goes to nil and the shelf rolls 47.97 to 47.47 unit.
CI4-OKR paid the RM90. With the RM95 already settled in kind by his rebate, E64 is closed at its agreed RM185, two days out and well inside his term.
WHAT IS LEFT: one open position, CD4-CS at RM150, 11 days out and 50% provisioned. Everything paid is delivered and everything delivered is paid.

FIXED, AND IT WAS QUIETLY WRONG: a zero-value row could never be marked paid in full, because the test required a total above zero. The first free unit ever handed over therefore read as Open - Advance, salt out with nothing in, so the desk showed a debt that was never owed. A free unit has no price to meet, so the test is met. Without this every future rebate redemption would have sat on the books for ever.
POSITION: shelf 47.47 unit all free to sell, revenue RM13,613, collected RM12,662 cash and RM551 in kind, receivables RM150 gross and RM75 net, margin RM5,031 at 37.0%.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs, no rendering leaks, consistency assertions hold, stock walk foots, board headroom unchanged at RM6/unit. Dates for the three movements are 05 Aug, being today on the desk clock; he gave none.

t: Three committed, and the first free unit exposes two faults
n: E64, CI4-OKR. Both units handed over on 04 Aug with no cash. On his call the agreed RM185 STANDS and the free unit settles RM95 of it in kind, the way CN6-WM's advance was cleared, rather than repricing the order to RM90. The second unit is unpaid, so RM90 is an advance. His rebate is now fully drawn.
CN6-WM redeems the last 0.5 unit as salt. No advance outstanding to offset against, so it is handed over: RM0 of revenue, 0.5 unit off the shelf at RM47.
CS6-BS-R paid RM60 on the day it was agreed and has not collected, so it is DEFERRED, not pending. The money counts, the half unit stays on the shelf and is owed out.

FIXED: A REBATE COULD ONLY APPLY A WHOLE ROW. rebate:true applied the entire quantity, which held while every rebate row was wholly a rebate. E64 is one free unit inside a two unit order. New rebateKg states the applied part; the whole row is still assumed when it is absent.

FIXED, LATENT SINCE THE LEDGER WAS BUILT: the first RM0 line ever written to this book took the whole Ledger tab out. marPct is null on a zero-value row and the margin subtext guarded on margin alone, so it called toFixed on null. A free unit still has a margin in ringgit; what it has no meaning for is a percentage of nothing.
POSITION: shelf 50.47 to 47.97 unit, 47.47 free to sell against 0.5 deferred. Revenue RM13,613, collected RM12,572, in kind RM551, receivables RM240 gross and RM165 net. Margin RM5,029.
Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs, no rendering leaks, all consistency assertions hold, stock walk foots to the counted figure, board headroom unchanged at RM6/unit.

t: The lock comes off and the vault becomes a directory
n: ONE BOX PER PARTY, on his instruction. BIO[code]={raw,photo}. He types whatever he knows in any order, and the structured fields get built later out of what actually turns up rather than from a schema guessed today. 27 people get a box; the four -R and -Gen accounts still do not, because they are not people.

bioScan() IS THE SEED OF THOSE FIELDS. It reads the free text back and reports what it recognised: name, location from the parenthetical, Malaysian phone, email, @handle, postcode. Shown as chips under the box and deliberately not editable, because they are a reading of the text and there must only ever be one copy of a fact.

THE OLD NAMES ARE NOT STRANDED. 24 of them sit inside an AES-GCM blob this desk can no longer read by design, so removing the lock without a route out would have lost them. Import old vault takes the passphrase once, decrypts IN THE BROWSER, and writes into the directory. He offered the passphrase in chat and it was declined: a secret pasted into a transcript stays there, and the button needs nothing from outside his machine.

PLAINTEXT, STATED ON THE PANEL ITSELF. salt_bio.json holds real names, numbers and addresses in the clear. The desk file stays clean because the directory is fetched at runtime from its own file, so salt_command.html can still be shared or screenshotted, and the published mirror carries no directory at all.

PHOTOS ARE DOWNSCALED TO 320px IN THE BROWSER before storage. A phone photo is two megabytes and this file is read on every load. The server's body cap is now route-aware, 8MB for the directory and the old tight 2MB for everything else.

vaultNames BECOMES A VIEW, not a store: bioName() reads the first line back as the old Name (Location) contract, so ID(), the statements and the entry parser carry on unchanged. revealed now defaults to true, since with no lock there is nothing to unlock; the Hide button survives as screen privacy, not encryption. With the directory empty the desk still shows codes, so nothing leaks before he fills it.

Verified: parse OK, serve_desk.py parses, fifteen tabs, no rendering leaks, all consistency assertions hold. Panel renders 27 boxes, 27 photo controls, 4 account rows, the plaintext warning, and the import control only when an old vault is on file. No ledger figure moved.

t: Accounts stop asking to be people, and the ID convention is measured
n: FIXED: CS6-BS-R, CS6-BS-Gen, CN6-WM-R and CN6-WM-Gen were each offering a 'name (location)' box and a first-seen hint in the Names & IDs panel. A -R is an account and a -Gen is a bucket; neither has a name to give. They now state what they are and carry their own role, so the vault stops collecting four permanent blanks.
MEASURED, NOT FIXED, because the convention is his to choose. The code is [C|S] + name initial + NAME LENGTH + location. Three faults follow from that.

ONE, IT LEAKS THE NAME IT IS MEANT TO PROTECT. Names live only in an AES-GCM vault, but every code states the initial and the exact letter count in plaintext. CS6-BS narrows to a six-letter S name in Bangsar South.

TWO, ONLY HE CAN MINT OR CHECK A CODE. The name half is unverifiable from outside the vault, so the desk cannot generate one, cannot validate one, and cannot catch a wrong one. Five stems already collide on initial and length: CA5, CJ4, CS6, CE4, CN6.

THREE, TBC IS A PLACEHOLDER SHAPED LIKE A PLACE. CH6-TBC and CZ4-TBC share it, so a to-be-confirmed location reads as a real one and two different people appear to share an address. Confirming either forces a re-key, which the one-identifier rule then has to absorb. Separately, ten suffixes have no PLACES entry at all: DAM, CHE, HCM, SK, BS, TBC, KER, AD, BTR and SEN, so most of the book cannot be placed on the Map.
Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs, no leaks, consistency assertions hold, no ledger figure moved.

t: Resell gets its own account, and a pending resale opens on it
n: RESELL BOOKS TO <ASSOCIATE>-R. He spotted that a resell was arriving as the associate's own purchase. Seven rows re-keyed: six CS6-BS, one CN6-WM. CS6-BS now reads RM432 of own buying against RM1,370 resold; CN6-WM RM50 against RM440. The -R code is an ACCOUNT, not a person and not a place: no vault name, no PLACES pin.

ONE RESOLVER, ownerOf(). Everything that asks whose stream a row belongs to goes through it: associateIds, networkStats direct and indirect, downstream links, the lot trigger, the resell ledger, the map. Miss one and the associate silently loses credit for his own resells. assocOf now resolves -R, -Gen and named -n-XX suffixes to the same owner.
R2 AND R3 STAY SEPARATE, on his call. The distinction is not the mechanism, it is whether the end buyer is known.

OPEN GAP HE IDENTIFIED, NOT YET BUILT: end-buyer knowledge has four states, name and location, name only, location only, neither. The desk has homes for two of them. A code needs a name AND a location (v144), so a buyer known by name but not location, or by location but not name, has nowhere to sit and falls into -Gen with the wholly anonymous.
NEW PENDING: CS6-BS-R 0.5 unit at RM60, RM120/unit, end buyer unknown so downstream -Gen. Exactly the S card at a half unit, clearing the RM38 floor and RM40 walk-away. Pending counts nowhere.
Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs, no leaks, all consistency assertions hold. Revenue RM13,368, collected RM12,512, AR RM150, margin RM4,927, stock 50.47 unit, every figure unmoved by the re-key.

t: CI4-OKR appointed, and the rebate gains a lot trigger
n: CI4-OKR joins the associate bench. The 30 Jul CZ4-TBC sale, 5 unit at RM435, is tagged as his referral (ref + refKg).

NEW LOT TRIGGER: any single R2 or R3 order of 5 unit or more earns 1 free unit. Three calls settled, all reversible. Scope: associate streams only, since all sales would have caught 11 direct orders from non-associates worth about RM517 at lot cost. Basis: alongside the RM500 and RM1,500 thresholds, not instead, because replacing them would push CS6-BS and CJ4-OKR negative on a rule written after they drew. Stacking: one per order however large, so it cannot be gamed by splitting.

OFFSET IS AUTOMATIC, REDEEM IS NOT. An earned unit meeting an outstanding advance clears it in kind with nothing to press; handing salt over leaves the shelf and stays behind the button. Booked into the row (settledRM + rebate:true), not derived at render, so an offset cannot be counted twice.

EFFECT. CS6-BS earns a third unit on his 7 unit resell and it clears his RM110 advance on the spot: advances out fall RM260 to RM150, AR net RM158 to RM75. CN6-WM 0.5 unit and CI4-OKR 1 unit sit waiting on Redeem. CJ4-OKR and CS6-PER unchanged.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs, no leaks, all consistency assertions hold. Revenue RM13,368, collected RM12,512, margin RM4,927, stock 50.47 unit, all unmoved: the offset is in kind and touches neither revenue nor cash.

t: Liquid Glass, Ledger tuning, and the desk gets focus rings for the first time
n: APPLIED AS A LAST-WINS LAYER, NOT A REWRITE. Every one of the class names across 630KB of markup is untouched; only the material and the light change. The desk was already most of the way there: v108 frosted the panels and the palette had been pinned to 'register', a steel-and-violet aurora with cyan and gold accents, which sits within a few degrees of the Ledger tuning now adopted properly. Ledger is the right tuning for this desk on the skill's own terms: financial, cold, precise.

FOCUS RINGS EXIST FOR THE FIRST TIME AND THIS WAS THE WORST FAULT FOUND. The file contained zero occurrences of :focus-visible against 28 buttons, a form on every tab, fifteen keyboard-reachable tab controls and a calendar of focusable chips. The desk was unusable by keyboard without sighted guesswork. Every control now takes a 2px ice ring at 2px offset, with the mouse-click ring suppressed via :focus:not(:focus-visible), and controls carry a 40px minimum tap target.

THE FROST HAD NO FLOOR UNDER IT. backdrop-filter is unsupported in some renderers and there was no opaque fallback declared anywhere, so on those engines text landed directly on the raw aurora. Added @supports not (backdrop-filter) raising every pane to rgba(24,29,41,.96), and prefers-reduced-transparency, which was not honoured at all, now drops the blur and hides the orbs.

THE LIGHT. Aurora gains its third anchor, an abyss wash at 45% 118%, because two washes leave the lower half of a tall page flat and a flat dark page is not this language. Three orbs added, ice at the top right, violet at the lower left, gold dimmed to 15% mid-page, all fixed, blurred 64px, behind the content and pointer-inert.

THE MATERIAL. Pane, Veil and Well are now real tokens rather than per-component improvisation, which is why radii and fills had drifted. Panes take 22px, nested items 14px, pills round. The nesting rule is explicit: children of a pane never frost again, so there is one blur layer per stack rather than compounding GPU cost and visual mush. Tooltips and sticky table headers moved to the Veil, dark-tinted so content scrolling beneath cannot fight the label.

112 CHART COLOUR LITERALS RETINTED, by hand, because Chart.js reads JavaScript objects and cannot see CSS custom properties: the chart palette had silently stayed on the old violet scheme while the panes moved. Grid strokes to the material's own hairline, ticks to ink-2 and ink-3, and the series to Ledger ice, gold, violet with good, warn and bad keeping their semantic families.

--dim RAISED FROM 3.4:1 TO 5.0:1. It is decor-grade contrast and the desk was using it for 9px labels on the calendar and plan rows. Measured against the worst-case pane, the glass fill blended over the brightest aurora corner at roughly #1a2130, every token now passes: ink 14.8, mut and ink-2 7.2, ice 9.8, gold 9.8, violet 7.4, good 10.5, warn 11.1, bad 6.4.

KEPT DELIBERATELY: the ten per-tab accent hues. The skill asks for a warm lead, a cool counter and a bridge, and this desk carries ten. They are wayfinding chrome rather than data, they are already in-family pastels, and flattening ten sections to three colours would destroy information to gain tidiness. Also fixed: lang was 'en' and is now 'en-GB'.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, zero rendering leaks. All fifteen still carry an h1, a lead line, a title matching the rail and classed KPI grids. Three orbs render, the third aurora anchor is present, and the fallback, reduced-transparency, reduced-motion and print blocks all exist. Calendar, board headroom, plan cards and the notes toggle intact. No ledger figure moved.

t: A source comment was printing itself on the Forward tab
n: HE SPOTTED IT ON SCREEN: '/* v180: the counted-balance panel is gone with the balance itself */' rendering as body text under the cash-line callout on Forward. The comment sat immediately AFTER the closing brace of a template expression, which put it inside the template literal rather than inside the function, so it was never a comment at all and the browser printed it. Moved into JS context inside the IIFE, where it reads as intended and where the note about why it broke now lives beside it.

THE WHOLE DESK WAS SWEPT FOR THE SAME CLASS OF FAULT rather than just the one he could see, because a leak of this kind is invisible in the source and only shows on the rendered page. Checked across all fifteen tabs: leaked block comments, unevaluated ${} expressions, stray backticks, double-escaped entities such as &amp;, raw entity text such as — printed literally, 'null' as text, and '[object Object]'. One fault, now zero.
THE SWEEP IS A STANDING CHECK. It joins the render verification, so any future comment or expression that escapes into a template literal fails the run instead of waiting to be noticed by eye.

LINE ENDINGS: the fix initially wrote four bare LFs into a uniformly CRLF file. Caught by the byte check and normalised in the same run. Every edit to this file is byte-checked for that now, because a whole-file ending flip shows as a total diff and would bury a real change.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol. All fifteen still carry an h1, a lead line, a title matching the rail and classed KPI grids. One chart-fallback wording, zero fractional font sizes, zero rendering leaks. Calendar, board headroom, plan cards and the notes toggle intact. 7,077 line endings, all CRLF. No ledger figure moved.

t: A consistency pass over all fifteen tabs, audited rather than eyeballed
n: FOUR TABS HAD NO h1 AT ALL. Overview, Inventory, Order book and Ledger opened directly on an h2, so the page carried no title and the heading hierarchy started one level down. Ledger was the worst of it: its first heading read 'Statement of account, what a customer may be given', a sub-panel caption standing in as the name of the tab.

TWO TABS BOTH CALLED THEMSELVES CUSTOMERS. The rail said Order book and the page said Customers, while a different tab, reached from a rail entry actually labelled Customers, also said Customers. Clicking one and reading the other is the kind of fault that survives for months because each tab looks right on its own. Order book now says Order book. Financials said Financial statements against a rail reading Financials. All fifteen rail labels now match their page titles exactly, and that is asserted on every verification run rather than left to the eye.

SEVEN KPI GRIDS CARRIED NO COLUMN CLASS. The base .kpis rule is three columns, so an unclassed row of four rendered 3+1, six rendered 3+3 by luck, and the eight-card row on Overview rendered 3+3+2. Every grid is now explicit: Overview 6 as k3 and 8 as k4, Inventory 6 as k3 and 4 as k4, Order book two rows of 3 as k3, Whiteboard 3 as k3. There is no longer a single .kpis without a k-class anywhere on the desk.

ELEVEN WORDINGS OF ONE SENTENCE BECOME ONE. The chart-unavailable line existed as 'These charts need Chart.js, which did not load', 'This chart needs Chart.js; the table above carries every figure', 'the supplier table carries every rate', 'the ledger itself is directly below', and seven more, across 13 places in the source and 22 on screen. All now read 'Chart unavailable. Every figure it draws is in the tables on this tab.' Shorter, and one thing to change if it ever needs changing.

THE TYPE SCALE HAD NO SCALE. Twenty-three distinct inline font sizes including six half-pixel steps at 9.5, 10.5, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5 and 14.5, across 49 declarations. Half steps are rounded up to the nearest whole pixel, leaving seventeen sizes and no fractional type anywhere.

WHAT WAS MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: 566 inline style attributes, and 148 raw hex colour declarations against 613 var() uses. Most of the hex sits in the second theme block and in Chart.js option objects, which cannot read CSS custom properties, so it is not the inconsistency it looks like from a count. Table header alignment was checked and is already uniform: 42 of 42 tables left-align their first header cell. Empty states read '—' inside tables and 'None.' inside cards, which is a distinction worth keeping rather than a collision.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol or kilo/kilogram. Asserted per tab and clean on all fifteen: an h1 exists, a lead line exists, the h1 matches the rail label, and every KPI grid carries a column class. One chart-fallback wording remains, zero fractional font sizes remain. Calendar, board headroom, plan cards and the notes toggle all still render. No ledger figure moved: stock 50.47 unit, revenue RM13,368, margin RM4,927.

t: Key message split from database, and a money column that was twice a guess becomes a field
n: MEASURED FIRST, THEN CUT. Across all fifteen tabs the desk rendered 95,577 characters, of which 49,699 were explanatory prose: 52%. Whiteboard was 93% prose, Pricing 65% over the largest tab on the desk, Sourcing and Forward 72%. Ledger, the most data-dense tab, was 8%. The pattern was that the tabs which REASON were drowning and the tabs which merely list were fine.

DEMOTED, NOT DELETED, on his instruction. Several of these blocks exist only because a figure was once wrong, so removing them invites the same error back. Every tab now carries ONE lead sentence, always visible, truncated to its first sentence; every .dsc over 140 characters is marked .note and hidden until asked for; and a 'Method and caveats (N)' control sits under the lead saying exactly how much is folded away. 43% comes off the default view. Pricing sheds 60%, Sourcing 67%, Analysis 55%, Whiteboard 82%.

WHY A LENGTH THRESHOLD AND NOT A TAG ON EVERY BLOCK. There are 120-odd prose blocks; tagging each is 120 chances to mis-tag and a fresh chance on every later edit. The two kinds are not close in length: method paragraphs run 200 to 900 characters while the short ones are load-bearing scraps, 'None.', a chart fallback, a figure restated. Measured before adoption: the rule hides 92% of prose by character and leaves 72 short blocks on screen, each checked by hand.

FIFTEEN LEAD SENTENCES, SIX OF THEM NEW. Overview, Inventory, Receivables, Ledger, Sourcing, Pricing, Transaction and Network had no lead at all: they opened straight into a KPI row, so a cold open said nothing about what the tab was for. Auto-detecting the lead was tried and abandoned, because on seven tabs the first prose block is a caption sitting further down and the rule picked that instead.

THE WHITEBOARD IS ONE LINE PER PLAN. Seventeen plans printed in full, every visit, 16,863 characters. Each is now a summary row carrying its code, title, worth and whether it has slipped, with the full write-up behind a click and anything overdue opened for you. All 15,575 characters of reasoning remain in the page. The detail deliberately does NOT carry class dsc, or the notes rule would hide it a second time and the click would open an empty box.

THE MONEY COLUMN SHIPPED WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT SHIPPED HONEST, and this is the part worth remembering. First it took the FIRST RM figure in the plan's text: P17 then read RM62.94, a unit cost it quotes in passing, when the plan is worth RM973. Then it took the LARGEST: P15 read RM8,950, a cash count it mentions while proposing to draw RM250. Both looked computed, sat in a money column, and were neither checked nor checkable. That is precisely the failure the desk refuses everywhere else. There is now no inference at all: worth is an explicit optional field with an input on the form, and an unpriced plan shows a dash. Every plan shows a dash today, which is honest and is itself the finding, because it means not one of the seventeen has been costed.

t: The cost of doing business, mapped by how each cost scales (03 Aug)
n: The desk knew two costs, the salt and the leak. Everything else that has to happen before a unit reaches a customer sat outside the model, so every tier was judged against a cost that was only part of the story. Costs are now grouped by
how they scale, because that and not the total is what decides which order is worth taking:
per unit doubles when the order doubles,
per order lands whole on a half unit and whole again on six,
per month carries whether anything sells, and
risk is derived rather than typed.

Every unmeasured line stays null and says so. A figure invented here would move every price on the board and be indistinguishable from one that was counted, so the panel reports what is missing and what it is worth instead. Two of the three per-order lines are unmeasured today, and the third, delivery at RM10, is the tier basis rather than anything observed: deliveryLog is still empty.

The finding is the shape. Against the M card, per-unit contribution falls from RM99.06 at half a unit to RM68.67 at 6.25, which is the taper working. Per ORDER it rises from RM50 to RM429, because the trip and the bag cost the same either way. Which column decides depends on what is scarce: when the shelf was empty a unit was scarce and per-unit was right, but the shelf now holds 50.47 and trips and hours are the constraint, which makes per-order the one that governs. One more ringgit of per-order cost takes
2.0% off a half-unit order and 0.2% off a 6.25, so every line still unmeasured hurts the small end about nine times harder.
And the risk figures invert an assumption. Read off the book rather than assumed, supplier default has cost
5.93% of everything paid out, RM750 of RM12,650, against
0.77% provisioned on customer credit. The desk carries a one-unit credit cap, an ageing ladder and a provisioning schedule for customers, and the money that actually went missing went to a supplier.
SHAPE REPAIRED at v210: this entry was filed with no 'd' and no 'n[]', as a single HTML blob, where every other entry carries a date and a list. Split on its own headings; not one word changed.

t: The approach table becomes a calendar, and two pictures of one fact become one
n: HIS STANDING INSTRUCTION, STATED THIS RUN AND WORTH KEEPING: when a feature is added, something should be removed, revamped, combined or simplified, or the desk accretes into a tab nobody acts on. This is the first pass under that rule and it DELETES more than it adds.

WHO TO APPROACH NEXT IS NOW A MONTH GRID. The old table was ten columns wide and sorted by lateness, so answering the only question being asked, who do I message today, meant holding a date, a cadence, a lot size, a quote and a margin delta in the head for every row, with the answer in the last column. A name now sits on the day his OWN median gap says he is next due, and everything else moves into a card that opens on hover, or on tap: the chips carry tabindex so :focus-within fires on a touch screen, where :hover does not exist and the board would otherwise be dead on the one device he carries. Not one figure changed, only the shape.

OVERDUE NAMES GET A RAIL ABOVE THE GRID, and this is the part that had to be decided rather than assumed. Their due dates are in PAST months: CG5-SB is 29 days over, so his date was 5 July and an August grid would not show him at all. The rail holds everyone past due, the grid holds today onward, and days before today are dimmed rather than filled so the same work is never printed twice. Audited: 10 names carry a cadence, 3 on the rail, 7 in the grid, none lost off the end.

JULY AND SEPTEMBER FLANK IT IN SUMMARY, and July answers the question the desk had never asked: does the cadence read actually predict anything. Replayed from the order dates rather than asserted, every order but a party's last implies a due date at that order plus his median gap, met if his next order landed on or before it. 22 due dates fell in July and 18 were met, 82%. That is the line that says whether the habit is a signal or a story, and it is worth the ten lines it costs.

THE OVERDUE BAR CHART IS DELETED. It plotted days past cadence, which the calendar now says by position, and the Customers tab was carrying the same fact as a chart, a table column and a KPI. The two-up beside the scatter collapses to a single wider card; ccDueObj, its canvas and its draw block are gone, leaving one tombstone comment.

THE 13 NAMES WITH ONE ORDER ARE OFF THE BOARD AND THE BOARD SAYS SO. One order is not a habit and giving them a due date would mean handing them somebody else's cadence and then acting on it. The caption states the count and where they are instead, because 13 of 23 names disappearing silently is how a simplification turns into a data loss.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol or kilo/kilogram in any pane. 36 cells for a 31-day month on a Monday-first grid with 5 leading blanks, 10 chips each carrying a card, every chip focusable, popups anchored left in columns 1 to 2 and right in 6 to 7 so none is clipped off the board. Every figure spot-checked against the retired table: CG5-SB RM305 earning RM122 at +2%, CS6-PER RM955 earning RM193 at -11%, CC5-OKR RM135 earning RM74 at +50%, CS6-BS still reading collect RM110 first. boardHeadroom unchanged at RM6/unit. No ledger figure moved.

t: A test that could not fail is replaced by a number that can
n: HE ASKED WHETHER THE QUOTE-BOARD INVARIANTS WERE WORTH RUNNING AND THE ANSWER IS MOSTLY NO. The daily run asserted three things at four replacement costs: every total a multiple of five, the rate never rising with lot size, and nothing under its floor. Swept across 366 cost and leak combinations, RM20 to RM140 against six leak levels, 14,274 prices, the first two did not break ONCE. They cannot. solveLadder rounds with Math.round(cost/(1-m)*lift/10)*10, so the multiples test tests Math.round; and an explicit R3 pass walks the ladder pulling any price down until the rate stops rising. Asserting a property the code enforces two lines earlier proves only that the code ran.

THE THIRD ASSERTION WAS NOT MERELY WEAK, IT WAS UNSOUND. R4 reports and does not clamp: SS sits under its floor DELIBERATELY above a half unit because it carries no per-lot delivery, and cards.py insists that stays visible. A flat check for price at or above floor would therefore have fired on the desk being honest. It returned zero only because RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56 all happen to be clean; over the wider sweep 5,740 of 14,274 solved rows sit under floor and every one of them is correct behaviour.

NEW boardHeadroom(), NEXT TO tierBoard(). The cards are frozen numbers and the floors move with cost, so every printed price is one purchase away from losing money. It walks the replacement rate up one ringgit at a time from the live rate and reports the last rate at which every card still clears, which tier gives first, at what size and by how much. SS is excluded by default, because including it makes the figure fire on policy rather than on cost; pass true to see the whole board.

TODAY IT READS RM6/unit OF ROOM, 10.7%. The cards clear to a replacement rate of RM62 and S gives first at RM63, on the 4 unit price of RM340 against a RM342.74 floor, short by RM2.74. Including SS the room is RM2 and SS breaches at all five of its sizes from RM59, which is the deliberate breach and not news. Live replacement is RM56.

ON THE PRICING TAB as a sixth KPI, coloured: green above 20% of the live rate, amber between 10 and 20, red under 10. It is the early warning the invariants pretended to be, and unlike them it moves every time the buying rate, the leak or the delivery rate moves. The kpis grid gains a k6 column rule and the 860px breakpoint was extended to match, or the six cards would not have wrapped on his phone.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol and no kilo or kilogram in any pane. boardHeadroom saves and restores pxOver.cost, confirmed null on both keys after the walk, so probing the board cannot leave an override behind and silently reprice the desk. No ledger figure moved: stock 50.47 unit, revenue RM13,368, margin RM4,927.

t: The oldest pending order closes, and the cost basis admits what it cannot know
n: E52 IS PAID AND DELIVERED. The CA5-KER 1 unit agreed on 28 Jul sat pending for six days and cleared on 03 Aug, RM120 and the unit moving together. It was the oldest pending row on the book. Committed from the queue entry written at 14:42 KL; the row now carries cost 47, cash 120, deliveredQty 1, deliveredOn and paidOn of 03 Aug, and a two-step amend trail whose first step is the 28 Jul opening at nothing moved. That opening step is NOT stripped: replayAmend accumulates from zero, so removing it would understate the close by the whole order.

THE PRICE IS THE WEAK PART AND THE DESK SAYS SO. RM120 clears the RM90 walk-away but sits RM30 under the RM150 the R board quotes at 1 unit, and under the RM150/unit actually achieved from CD4-CS. It earns RM73 at 61% on the RM47 lot, which is a good margin on a bad price: the lot was cheap, not the quote strong.

WHAT MOVED. Revenue RM13,248 to RM13,368, margin RM4,854 to RM4,927 at 36.9%, cash collected RM12,392 to RM12,512 and trading net RM-338 to RM-218. Pending falls from 3.5 unit and RM385 to 2.5 unit and RM265, leaving CH5-KLC and CI4-OKR. Receivables are untouched at RM260 gross and RM158 net, because this order never became one.

THE SHELF ROLLS 51.47 TO 50.47. The 03 Aug hand count was read at about 09:00 KL and E52 moved at 14:42 KL, so the unit went out AFTER the count and is deducted rather than already inside it. Cover tightens from 10.7 to 10.4 days at 4.88 unit a day, and Today and Inventory now agree that the shelf empties on 13 Aug, where at v205 they disagreed by a day on the same 10.7 through opposite rounding.

STOCK_COST STAYS AT RM47.47 AND NOW ADMITS WHY THAT IS APPROXIMATE. The unit came off the RM47 lot so the remnant is untouched and the constant does not move. But the 47.47 was solved on a 101.32 unit shelf of 2.82 at RM64 against 98.50 at RM47, and the hand count cut the shelf to 51.47 with a 38.23 unit plug that has no lot attached to it. If the whole plug came off the RM47 lot the blend would be RM47.94 and the shelf RM24 dearer. The comment stated the old composition as fact; it now states the caveat instead. Nothing is guessed and no figure moves.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol and no kilo or kilogram in any pane, quote board invariants hold at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56 with no price under its own floor, and the stock walk foots 4.9 opening plus 231.25 received less 147.45 delivered and 38.23 shrinkage to the counted 50.47.

t: The board and the ladder stop disagreeing, and the customer stops paying for the whole leak
n: HALF THE LEAK IS CHARGED, HALF IS ABSORBED, on his instruction, through a single new constant SHRINK_ATTRIB. Until now every unit lost was recovered in the price of the units that survived, so a 16.19% leak was passed on whole. That is defensible arithmetic and a poor commercial instruction: it hands the cost of an unsolved problem to customers who did not cause it, and it raises prices hardest exactly when the leak is worst, which is when prices should be steadiest. The customer now carries 8.09% and margin carries the rest. Effective cost falls from RM66.82 to RM60.93/unit, and RM5.88/unit is absorbed by choice. Set the constant to 1 to pass the whole leak on again, or to 0 to absorb all of it; everything downstream moves with it.

THE CARDS ARE NOW THE LADDER. He asked for the quote board and the dynamic ladder to agree, and they do: all 39 prices identical, where 26 of 39 differed before. Every printed price is the solver's own output at the new cost. THIS WAS ONLY EVER POSSIBLE ONCE THE COSTS MATCHED: the cards had been costed at RM51.96/unit with NO leak in them at all, then tested against an effective cost that had the whole leak in it, so the two boards could not agree by construction no matter what prices were typed. Fixing the basis is what made agreement reachable; retyping prices alone never would have.

IT IS A REAL PRICE RISE AND IT LANDS AT THE TOP, WHICH IS WHERE THE ANALYSIS SAID THE MONEY WAS LEAKING. R, the only card that leaves his phone, is UNCHANGED to 2.5 unit and then rises: 3 unit RM310 to RM320, 4 unit RM390 to RM420, 5 unit RM460 to RM520, 6.25 unit RM540 to RM650, a fifth dearer at the biggest size. M and P rise further, to RM240 and RM280 more at 6.25 unit. The hand-solved taper had been generous precisely in the band that earned RM7.60/unit, so the correction lands on the problem. Small sizes barely move and SS at 0.5 unit falls from RM50 to RM40.

SS COMES OUT FLAT AT RM80/unit AND THAT IS NOT A SOLVER FAILURE. SS carries no per-lot delivery, so nothing in its cost gives the ladder a reason to taper. The old SS taper was a commercial choice dressed as arithmetic, and forcing the two boards to agree is what exposed it. If the taper is wanted back it now has to be argued for rather than assumed.

AGREEMENT IS A SNAPSHOT, NOT A PROPERTY, and the desk says so in the source. The ladder recomputes from live cost on every load; the cards are frozen numbers. The moment the leak, the replacement quote or the delivery rate moves, the two part again and the drift column shows by how much. This is worth re-running rather than assuming the boards stay married.

05_Pricing\cards.py UPDATED TO THE SAME GRID, so the printed card and the desk cannot disagree either. Its header now records that the cards are no longer hand-solved and states the cost basis behind them.

FIXED WHILE HERE: the Pricing tab's headline read 'Shrinkage load 8.1%, live from the count', which understated the real leak by half and would have let a reader conclude the problem had halved overnight. Both shrinkage KPIs now show the charged figure against the observed one, '8.1%, 16.2% observed, 50% of it charged'.

Verified: all 39 card prices match the solver exactly; every total a multiple of ten; no rate rises with lot size within a tier; tiers strictly ordered cheapest to dearest at every shared size; NOTHING under the 20% floor, so the six SS and S breaches of v204 are gone because the cards moved onto the model. Parse OK, fifteen tabs, no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, quote board invariants hold at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56. Stock 51.47 unit, revenue RM13,248, margin RM4,854 at 36.6%, untouched: a price list governs what happens next and must not restate the past.

t: The floor comes down to 20%, and the single-floor principle survives it
n: FLOOR LOWERED FROM 30% TO 20%, still one floor at every size. 30% was set an hour earlier and its consequence was immediate and unacceptable: it put the R card under its own floor at 5 unit and 6.25 unit, and R is the card that actually goes to customers. A floor that forbids your own published price is not a floor, it is a recall.

AT 20% THE CARDS SURVIVE. R, M and P clear at every size they run to. Breaching prices fall from 12 to 6, and all six are SS and S at the small and middle sizes, which have been deliberately under the floor since the tiers became policy: SS carries no delivery in its cash and earns on its own basis. Closed sales under the floor come back from 9 to 4.

THE PRINCIPLE IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERED. There is still ONE floor rather than 25% retail and 2% wholesale. The 2% was never a floor: it permitted RM68.18/unit while retail was protected, and it created a cliff at exactly 6.25 unit where a customer taking a quarter of a unit more could legitimately pay RM100 less. That arbitrage is gone whether the number is 30 or 20. At 20% the floor rate is RM83.52/unit against the RM66.82 effective cost, and the 6.5 unit lot sold yesterday at RM67.69/unit would now be refused rather than waved through.

The 30% reasoning is kept in the source beside the 20%, because the reasoning is the asset and a number that moved twice in one morning should show why. Nothing else changed: stock 51.47 unit, revenue RM13,248, margin RM4,854 at 36.6%, receivables RM260 gross and RM157.50 net, no breaches.
Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, quote board invariants hold at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56.

t: One floor at 30%, delivery becomes a real number, and a rebate drawn before it was earned
n: ONE FLOOR, 30%, EVERY SIZE, on his instruction. It was 25% retail and 2% wholesale, and the 2% was never a floor: it permitted RM68.18/unit while retail was protected at RM89.09, which is exactly how the 6.5 unit lot went out at RM67.69 on 03 Aug while breaching nothing. Worse, the split put a CLIFF at 6.25 unit, so a customer taking a quarter of a unit MORE could legitimately pay RM100 LESS. A single 30% floor removes the cliff and the arbitrage together, and because 30% is above the old retail 25% it bites on small lots too rather than being a wholesale patch.

TWELVE CARD PRICES NOW BREACH, and they are reported rather than suppressed. The ones that matter: R at 5 unit is RM460 against a RM477.26 floor, and R at 6.25 unit is RM540 against RM596.58, RM56.58 short. M at 6.25 unit is RM16.58 short. R is the card that leaves his phone, so at those two sizes the printed card is now below the desk's own refusal line and needs reprinting before it is handed to anybody. The rest are SS and S at the small and middle sizes, which were already known to sit under the floor by design. Closed sales under the floor rise from 3 to 9 for the same reason: the floor moved, not the prices.

DELIVERY IS RM10 PER ORDER, stated by him, replacing the RM17.50 assumption the desk had been carrying and labelling as a guess. The Pricing tab stops calling it an assumption and now says it is his stated rate, still inviting logged runs to replace it with an observed mean. The 49 priced lots therefore carry RM490 of delivery rather than RM857.50, so the number is smaller than yesterday's estimate but real for the first time, and it now flows into every modelled price through the ladder.

CN6-WM'S ADVANCE SETTLED BY A PRE-EARNED HALF UNIT. He had resold RM440 against a RM500 milestone, so the half unit is drawn EARLY on his instruction. It is applied against the advance rather than handed over as salt, per the standing offset rule: the 0.5 unit he already holds from 21 Jul is what the rebate pays for, RM50 against RM50, so the receivable clears exactly. Nothing physical moves and nothing is waived. Receivables fall from RM310 to RM260 gross and RM182.50 to RM157.50 net, and the credit-age breach clears with it, so the desk now reports NO breaches for the first time in this record.

THE NEXT AWARD IS SMALLER BY EXACTLY WHAT WAS TAKEN, AND NOTHING HAD TO BE TYPED TO MAKE THAT TRUE. freeKg is earned minus applied, so when his resold total crosses RM500 the milestone earns 1 unit, 0.5 is already applied, and he receives 0.5. The arithmetic enforces the loan on its own.

FIXED, PRE-EXISTING: the Overview milestone table could not express a rebate drawn early. Its Reward cell read `earned`, not what had actually been applied, so a party who had taken half a unit before reaching the milestone showed a bare dash, as though nothing had happened. It now reads the applied figure and says '0.5 unit drawn early' in amber, with the reason on hover. The Network tab was already correct, which is why the two panes disagreed.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, quote board invariants hold at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56. Stock 51.47 unit, revenue RM13,248, margin RM4,854 at 36.6%, all unchanged by these three edits, which is the point: a floor and a delivery rate govern what happens NEXT and must not restate what already happened.

t: The leak doubles on a hand count, and two things break honestly as a result
n: HAND COUNT, 03 Aug, 51.47 unit. It supersedes the rolled 63.65 outright, because the count always wins. Confirmed with him first that it was taken AFTER the day's two deliveries had left the shelf, the CS6-BS 2.5 and the CN6-WM 6.5, so those 9 unit are already inside the figure and are not deducted twice. Read at the start of the day, as the standing convention assumes, it would have meant 42.47 on the shelf and a 20.00% leak. The two readings differ by 9 unit and RM3.18/unit of effective cost, which is why it was asked rather than assumed.

THE NEWS IS BAD. 12.18 unit has gone with nothing recorded against it since 29 Jul, about RM630 at the RM51.72 average. The plug goes 26.05 to 38.23 unit and the leak 11.03% to 16.19% of the 236.15 unit handled. Effective cost rises RM62.94 to RM66.82/unit, and RM600 of measured margin leaves the book with it. Shrinkage now stands at RM1,977, which is 41% of every ringgit of gross margin the desk has ever earned. Nothing is attributed.

TWO THINGS BROKE, AND BOTH ARE THE DESK BEING HONEST RATHER THAN FAULTS INTRODUCED HERE. First, the R card at 6.25 unit, RM540, now sits RM16.81 UNDER its own floor of RM556.81. It is the only R, M or P price that breaches, and it breaches because the cost moved, not because the price did. The Pricing tab says so on its own, unsuppressed. Second, the reconstructed stock walk now dips to -6.04 unit on 12 of 39 days, where it previously never went below zero. Negative salt is impossible: it is the dating fault the desk already names, since 23 orders still carry no recorded delivery date and fall back to their order date, and a plug 12.18 unit larger drags the whole reconstructed line down. Recording deliveredOn against those 23 orders is what fixes it. NO DATE WAS INVENTED to make the line look right.

NEW PLAN P17, four levers on margin, each priced. ONE, fix the leak: 16.19% back to the 7.5% he called achievable cuts effective cost RM6.28/unit, worth RM973 across the 154.95 unit sold to date, and costs nothing but weighing lots in and out. TWO, raise the wholesale floor, which is where the hole actually is: above 6.25 unit the floor is 2%, permitting RM68.18/unit while retail is protected at RM89.09. The six lots over 6.25 unit sold 83.25 unit at RM74.41; a 15% floor earns RM349 more, 20% earns RM758 more, 25% earns RM1,222 more. THREE, cap the ladder at 6.25 unit, which is P16 and is now arithmetic: that band earns RM7.60/unit before a delivery assumed at RM17.50 a lot. FOUR, record and charge delivery: 49 priced lots at RM17.50 is RM857.50 never booked anywhere, 29.1% of what the book earns over effective cost, and the largest unmeasured number on this desk.

WHAT THE SHELF IS WORTH, bootstrapped over the 49 real priced orders with 40,000 runs, units reaching a customer taken as shelf times one minus the leak. Selling as he has been selling: RM3,737, 90% interval RM3,226 to RM4,271. Capping at 6.25 unit: RM4,279, 90% interval RM4,071 to RM4,484, so the cap is worth about RM542 on this shelf alone and more than halves the spread. Retail only at 3 unit and under: RM4,392. Cap plus a repaired leak at 7.5%: RM4,723. The arithmetic ceiling, every surviving unit sold in half-unit lots at the P card, is RM7,765, but it needs 87 separate buyers and is not a plan. Against those, the surviving salt costs RM2,882 at effective cost and the shelf cost RM2,443 to buy.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs render with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, quote board holds at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56. The stock walk deliberately does NOT pass its usual test and is reported rather than papered over.

t: The downsell moves to the bucket where it belonged, and the ledger is audited for double counting
n: CN6-WM-1-TBC WAS WRONG AT SOURCE AND IS PURGED OUTRIGHT. The end buyer of the 03 Aug 6.5 unit sale is a stranger, so the trade belongs in CN6-WM's GENERAL BUCKET and not under a code of its own. The split rule is explicit that a named downstream is earned only where you delivered to the person yourself and therefore know who he is, and the queued code gave its location as TBC, which is an admission that the place was not known. A code was minted on the strength of a placeholder. The row now carries downstream CN6-WM-Gen, the named code is purged rather than kept as an alias, and no translation table is left behind, per the standing one-identifier rule.

NOT ONE FIGURE MOVED. Verified by extracting every money amount, every unit quantity and every percentage from all fifteen tabs before and after, with party codes stripped first so the code string itself could not masquerade as a change: the lists are identical. Stock 63.65 unit, revenue RM13,248, collected RM12,392, margin RM4,854 at 36.6%. A re-key that moves a figure has a bug in it; this one does not.

IT ALSO CLOSES THE GAP FLAGGED AT v200 rather than leaving it open. assocOf() returns null for a named <associate>-n-XX code but resolves a -Gen code back to its reseller, so with the trade in the bucket CN6-WM earns the credit BY CONSTRUCTION rather than because I happened to notice and rewrite the counterparty by hand. He stands at RM490 brought, RM60 from his first free unit. The resolver gap itself is still open for any future named downstream booked direct.

LEDGER AUDITED FOR DOUBLE COUNTING, on request. Ten checks: identical rows, rows paying or delivering more than they sold, amendment trails claiming more than their row, revenue rebuilt from scratch, the downsell counted once or twice, delivered units against soldKg, the v150 loan double-deduction, the network attribution, cash carried as both a field and a split, and received purchase units. NO DOUBLE COUNTING FOUND. Three checks raised a flag and all three were the check being naive rather than the desk being wrong, which is worth recording so the next audit does not re-raise them.

The two 22 Jul lots of 6.25 unit at RM350 from SA5-BTR are identical in every field except receivedOn, 22 and 23 Jul. They are the two halves of one 12.5 unit lot within the 25 unit paid that day, as both notes say. Genuine, not a duplicate.

Revenue rebuilt naively came to RM13,633.26 against the desk's RM13,248.26. The RM385 difference is EXACTLY the three pending orders, CA5-KER RM120, CH5-KLC RM80 and CI4-OKR RM185. Pending counts nowhere, so the desk is right and the naive sum was booking intentions as revenue.

Delivered units summed to 155.01 against soldKg of 146.45. The 8.56 unit difference is EXACTLY the two set-offs, CS6-PER's 6.5 unit against the 12 May loan and CJ4-BJ's 2.0588 unit against his unpaid 28 Jun and 05 Jul balances. Salt settled in kind is counted as FULFILLED but not as DRAWN, so it cannot leave the shelf twice. That is the distinction between txDeliv and drawnKg doing its job.

One coincidence worth naming before it alarms somebody: CS6-BS's indirect figure and CS6-PER's direct figure are both RM1,370 and are entirely unrelated, the first being CS6-BS's five downsells and the second CS6-PER's two own purchases. Across all four associates total equals direct plus indirect exactly, and no ringgit appears under two of them.

Verified: parse OK, fifteen tabs with no throw and no undefined, NaN or Infinity, no retired mass symbol, no surviving reference to the purged code in any data field, stock walk lows at 1.63 unit and foots to the counted 63.65, quote board holds at RM40, RM44, RM48 and RM56.

t: A queue committed only after it was read back, and a quarter of a unit that cost RM100
n: Both queued entries committed, after being put in front of him first rather than booked on sight. That confirmation step earned its keep twice in one commit, which is the argument for keeping it.

CN6-WM-1-TBC added to the roster as CN6-WM's first named downstream. The TBC suffix has no gazetteer entry, so he stays UNPLACED on the Map rather than being guessed at, which is the intended behaviour and not an omission. No name reaches this file or the queue; the name lives only in the encrypted vault once Save is pressed.

THE SALE WAS QUEUED DIRECT AND IS BOOKED AS AN R2 DOWNSELL, on instruction. The form recorded 6.5 unit for RM440 with the end buyer as the top party and assoc null. Checked before committing: assocOf() resolves the -Gen pattern back to its reseller but returns NULL for a named <associate>-n-XX code. So had it stood as queued, CN6-WM would have earned nothing from his own first sale as an associate: not in R2 revenue, not toward his rebate, not on Network. Booked instead with CN6-WM as the counterparty and CN6-WM-1-TBC as the downstream. It takes him from RM50 of business brought to RM490, so he is now RM60 from his first free unit.

GAP LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY, NOT FIXED: assocOf() still returns null for named downstream codes. The v195 safety net that books a downsell to its reseller whether or not the box was ticked covers -Gen only. t: A bucket for a buyer you know nothing about, and CN6-WM appointed
n: CN6-WM APPOINTED AN ASSOCIATE. He joins CS6-BS, CJ4-OKR and CS6-PER on the bench and can now trade on the R2 and R3 streams. STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS NOT COSMETIC: an associate carries a 2 unit credit cap against a retail 1 unit, so the appointment DOUBLES the credit he may run, and he is at the same moment the desk's only open breach, RM50 delivered on 21 Jul and unpaid at 13 days against a 10-day term. The cap is not what he is breaching, so nothing is concealed: the credit-age breach still reads on Boundaries and on Today, verified after the change. But the first thing the desk did for a man who has not paid in a fortnight was raise his limit, and that belongs in the record rather than in a footnote. No ledger row moved: revenue, margin and stock are untouched at RM12,808, 36.8% and 70.15 unit.

+ ADD ID CAN NOW CREATE A GENERAL BUCKET. Until now every party was created by NAMING it, because a code is derived from a name and a place, and the panel demanded both. A -Gen bucket is the one party that has neither by construction: it is where an associate's onward sale goes when you never meet the buyer, so requiring a name asked for exactly the information whose absence is the reason the bucket exists. The new kind takes the associate and nothing else, hides the name and location fields rather than leaving them on screen demanding the impossible, mints <associate>-Gen, and writes NO vault entry, so the vault goes on holding names only. It refuses to mint one twice and says which associate already has it.

This relaxes a stated rule, and deliberately. The split-rule note says a -Gen code exists only once it has been used and is never seeded onto the roster empty. That held while the only way to get one was to book a sale, but it also meant a newly appointed associate had no bucket until his first downsell, which is the moment you least want to be improvising. Creating one ahead of the sale is now allowed; the reasoning is here rather than left for someone to rediscover as a contradiction.

EVERY -Gen BUCKET NOW LISTS ON THE TRANSACTION FORM. The end-customer dropdown was built only from downstreams already seen in sales, so a bucket created before its first sale was invisible on the one form that needed it. It now unions the used downstreams with every -Gen code on the roster. The blank option still auto-routes to the ticked associate's bucket, so the old path is unchanged.

FIXED, AND PRE-EXISTING: creating a party destroyed its own confirmation. addParty wrote the success message and then called renderReveal(), which rebuilds the panel from scratch, so the <details> collapsed and the message was discarded with the node holding it. Creating a party looked identical to creating nothing, on the one screen where you most need to be told a code was minted. The re-render now happens first, then the box is re-opened, the chosen kind restored so the fields do not snap back to Customer, and the message written into the new node.

Tested by driving the real form rather than reading the source: the bucket kind hides name and location and shows the associate; CN6-WM-Gen mints, reaches the roster, writes nothing to the vault and queues one ADDID row; a second click refuses and says why; a second associate's bucket mints independently; both appear on the end-customer list; and the ordinary customer path still derives its code from name and place and still encrypts the name. t: The CS6-BS-Gen cancellation and rebooking, recorded after the fact
n: WRITTEN RETROSPECTIVELY AT v197. v196 shipped without a changelog entry: the evolution string inside the desk was rewritten but this file was never touched, so the version existed for an hour with no record anywhere. Reconstructed here from the file itself so the sequence is not left with a hole in it.

v196 did two things. It cancelled the 02 Aug pending CS6-BS order, 1 unit at RM120 to the CS6-BS-Gen bucket, by setting cancelled:true and adding a two-step trail, a Fulfilment dated 02 Aug recording the agreement and a Cancellation dated 30 Jul. And it added a new row dated 30 Jul for 2.5 unit at RM270 to the same bucket, paid and collected the same day, rolling STATED_STOCK from 72.65 to 70.15.

The dating did not hold together. The new row was dated 30 Jul, so RM270 of revenue and 2.5 unit of stock landed in JULY, lifting July revenue from RM11,327 to RM11,597 and July gross margin from 36.5% to 37.0%. Yet the row's own note called it a rebooking of an order agreed on 02 Aug, and the cancellation of that 02 Aug order was dated 30 Jul. An order agreed on the 2nd was therefore cancelled three days before it was agreed and replaced by a delivery made three days before it was agreed. replayAmend sorts by date, so the ledger card showed the cancellation first and the agreement after it.
Reverted in full at v197 on instruction. Recorded here rather than deleted, because a version that moved the July P&L should not vanish from the record.

t: A downsell books to its reseller whether or not the box was ticked
n: QUEUE COMMITTED: 1 unit at RM120 through reseller CS6-BS to a general downsell buyer, agreed 02 Aug, nothing paid and nothing moved, so PENDING. RM120/unit is exactly the 16 Jul downsell rate through the same reseller, so it is his established price rather than a concession. It sits against true-reseller terms of payment upfront and same-day delivery, which this one has not met.

AS QUEUED IT WOULD HAVE BEEN BOOKED WRONG. The Transaction tab sent it as a direct sale to a party called CS6-BS-Gen with no associate ticked. CS6-BS-Gen is not a customer: it is the bucket a sale falls into when the end buyer gives no name and no location, and the money comes from CS6-BS. Committed as queued it would have minted the bucket as a counterparty in its own right, owed money by nobody, and issued it a statement with no one to send it to. He caught it and said so.

THE CODE ALREADY KNOWS. A downstream code names its reseller by construction, so leaving the attribution to a tickbox means one missed tick books a downsell as a direct sale. New assocOf(code) answers it two ways, cheapest first: the ledger has already booked that code as somebody's downstream, or the code is a reseller's code plus a suffix. Only a parent that actually resells counts, so an ordinary customer whose code happens to prefix another is never treated as one. Verified against the whole roster: the three CS6-BS downstreams resolve to CS6-BS, the reseller itself and every ordinary customer return null.

Wired in at BOTH ends. ovApply fills a silence at commit and records what it inferred in the provisional notes, so nothing can be committed against a bucket again. The form no longer waits to be told: choosing a downstream in the Party list now ticks the associate box, names the reseller, sets R2, puts the buyer in End customer and says on screen what it did. An explicit tick still wins; this only fills a silence, and the correction is visible before it is queued rather than found in the ledger later.
